[McCulloch–Pitts](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02478259), [Rosenblatt](https://doi.org/10.1037/h0042519) | **Not simply too early.** Multilayer differentiable learning addressed a different and more expressive class; perceptrons remain useful units, not a general architecture revival. “XOR alone killed neural nets” is an oversimplification of the historical slowdown. |
| ADALINE / LMS | Linear adaptive filter updated by error correlation; cheap online learning but linear predictions and weak learned features. [Widrow–Hoff](https://isl.stanford.edu/~widrow/papers/c1960adaptiveswitching.pdf) | **Still useful, narrowly.** GPUs and encoders provide better features, but the mechanism is established adaptive filtering; modern hardware is not a novelty source. |
| Hebbian learning / Oja | Local co-activity updates can extract correlations and principal directions, but do not by themselves yield deep task-relevant abstractions. [Oja 1982](https://math.bu.edu/people/gkocker/ma769/oja_1982.pdf) | **Useful local rule, not a general learner.** Strong frozen features make the rule more practical, while local online adaptation is already widely studied. |
| Hopfield nets / bidirectional associative memory | Energy descent retrieves a stored pattern from a partial cue; classic dense storage has interference and spurious minima. [Hopfield 1982](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554) | **Substantially revived already.** Dense modern associative memories raise capacity, and modern Hopfield updates are mathematically tied to attention. [Dense associative memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01164), [Hopfield Networks is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02217). Do not claim “Transformer + Hopfield” as new without a different update rule or memory semantics. |
| Boltzmann machines | Stochastic energy models learn distributions through sampling; likelihood gradients require difficult partition-function estimates and mixing. [Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski 1985](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~fritz/absps/cogscibm.pdf) | **Compute helps parallel chains, not equilibrium mixing or estimator variance.** Contrastive divergence and score/diffusion methods modernized adjacent objectives; a generic BM comeback is not open architecture space. [Contrastive divergence](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~hinton/absps/tr00-004.pdf), [score matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07762). |
| Adaptive Resonance Theory (ART) / Fuzzy ART | Match–reset competition adds categories when a sample violates a vigilance threshold; designed to balance stable memory and plasticity. Threshold choice, category proliferation, and drifting input metrics limit scale. [Fuzzy ART](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/089360809190056B) | **Partly revived, with direct collisions.** DeepART (2025) places ART-style local updates into deep models; ART plus self-organizing reservoirs was published in 2022. [DeepART](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107580), [ART reservoir](https://mjcs.um.edu.my/index.php/MJCS/article/view/34808). “Deep encoder + ART head” is already occupied. |
| Self-organizing maps / neural gas / growing neural gas | Competitive prototypes organize a map or graph to preserve neighborhood/topology; fixed metric and neighborhood geometry become questionable in high-dimensional semantic spaces. [Kohonen SOM](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00337288), [GNG](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/1994/hash/d56b9fc4b0f1be8871f5e1c40c0067e7-Abstract.html) | **Practical online clustering/map components.** Better encoders and nearest-neighbor hardware help, but topology learning and RL state abstraction already exist; arbitrary growth is not a new class. |
| Radial basis function networks | Local kernels interpolate from centers; many centers or poor distance geometry make scaling hard. [Broomhead & Lowe](https://sci2s.ugr.es/keel/pdf/algorithm/articulo/1988-Broomhead-CS.pdf) | **Some compute relief.** Random features, inducing points, and learned embeddings address center cost; broad replacement of deep nets is not supported. |
| Cascade-correlation / constructive nets | Add a hidden unit when residual error remains, then freeze it, avoiding repeated global retraining. Greedy irreversible feature choice can overfit or lock in a poor basis. [Fahlman & Lebiere 1989](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/1989/hash/69adc1e107f7f7d035d7baf04342e1ca-Abstract.html) | **Growth is viable but not new.** Modern compute makes candidate search cheap; pruning, validation, dynamic sparse training, and network morphism are close baselines. |
| Cellular automata / artificial life | Local rule applications create large global patterns, but programming a desired computation through local interactions is difficult and distant information moves slowly. | **Differentiable CA/NCA are genuine modern revivals for growth and repair**, including trained asynchronous cellular rules, but pattern regeneration does not imply general intelligence. [Growing NCA](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/), [Lenia](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05433). |
| Cellular neural networks / analog arrays | Continuous local circuits perform parallel image-like operations with low latency; analog mismatch, wiring, precision, and task-specific design limited adoption. [Chua & Yang 1988](https://nonlinear.eecs.berkeley.edu/raptor/CNNs/CellularNeuralNetworks-Theory.pdf) | **Hardware may revive efficiency, not breadth.** Requires physical energy/latency measurements and calibration robustness, not only a software simulation. |
| Reservoir computing / echo-state nets / liquid-state machines | Fixed recurrent dynamics transform temporal input; only a readout is trained, avoiding full recurrent credit assignment. Fixed random dynamics may be irrelevant to the task and can be fragile to timescale/spectral choices. [Jaeger ESN report](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/215385037_The_echo_state_approach_to_analysing_and_training_recurrent_neural_networks-with_an_erratum_note), [Maass et al. LSM](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12433288/) | **Not just an old failed neural net.** Neuromorphic/photonic hardware and streaming uses help, but surveys still find integration and generality limitations; self-organizing ART reservoirs and reservoir robot control are already explored. [2024 perspective](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-45187-1). |
| Spiking neural networks / local eligibility learning | Event-driven neuron states and spikes offer temporal/event computation; nondifferentiable thresholds and long-delay credit made training difficult. | **Partly “too early.”** Surrogate gradients, e-prop, and neuromorphic processors directly address training/memory limits. [E-prop](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-17236-y), [SpiNNaker 2 E-prop](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9742366/). Local plasticity is known; general advantage still needs joules, latency, and matched accuracy on event-native tasks. |
| Kanerva sparse distributed memory | Hamming-addressed distributed locations implement noisy associative recall at large logical address sizes; random high-dimensional neighborhoods cross-talk and writes are costly. [NASA report](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/archive/nasa/casi.ntrs.nasa.gov/19890017031.pdf) | **Memory is cheaper, but geometry/cross-talk remain.** Later Kanerva-machine and HDC successors already revisit it; increasing RAM does not solve address concentration. [Kanerva Machine](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01756). |
| Learning classifier systems (XCS and relatives) | A population of condition–action rules is selected, updated, generalized, and sometimes evolved online; matching and rule populations can grow and credit can be noisy. [Wilson XCS](https://sci2s.ugr.es/keel/pdf/algorithm/articulo/wilson1995b.pdf) | **Useful for inspectable stream rules.** Deep features, replay, and layered systems exist, including XCSR; performance must beat equivalent rule learning, not just a linear head. [XCSR](https://www.fujipress.jp/jaciii/jc/jacii002100050856/). |
| Genetic programming / evolutionary computation / neuroevolution | Search candidate programs, weights, or topologies using fitness. Main cost is often sample/evaluation count, not arithmetic per candidate. | **Compute made massively parallel search practical** where gradients are absent or evaluations parallelize; it did not erase sample inefficiency, deceptive landscapes, or simulator exploitation. [Evolution Strategies](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.03864), [AutoML-Zero](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a.html). |
| NEAT / HyperNEAT / developmental encodings | Evolve topology/weights or generate regular connectivity from a compact geometric genome. Search can be costly; the encoding imposes inductive bias. [NEAT](https://doi.org/10.1162/106365602320169811), [HyperNEAT](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19199382/) | **GPU and tensorized variants help evaluation.** Regularity can scale to many connections, but modern GPU NEAT and evolving SNN topology already exist; encoding bias remains. [GPU-NEAT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01817). |
| Expert systems / production systems | Hand-authored rules yield traceable domain conclusions, but knowledge acquisition, exception coverage, and brittle perceptual predicates dominate. | **Modern perception repairs input quality, not rule completeness.** Differentiable logic and neuro-symbolic program induction already occupy this hybrid. [DeepProbLog](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2018/hash/dc5d637ed5e62c36ecb73b654b05ba2a-Abstract.html). |
| Blackboard architectures / HEARSAY-II | Asynchronous specialists post partial hypotheses to shared working memory; a scheduler picks work. Coordination and stale/conflicting hypotheses are hard. | **More capable specialists are available, but the organization is established.** Bayesian blackboards and value-of-computation scheduling make a generic “experts on a board” revival low novelty. [HEARSAY-II](https://mas.cs.umass.edu/pub/paper_detail.php/229). |
| Soar | Impasse creates a subgoal; its result can be compiled into a production (“chunk”) to avoid repeating the reasoning. Some missing negative conditions can overgeneralize. [Soar architecture](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/soar_manual/02_TheSoarArchitecture/), [procedural learning manual](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/soar_manual/04_ProceduralKnowledgeLearning/) | **Not primarily compute-limited.** Current manual confirms local-negation chunking can overgeneralize and documents filters. Simulator-generated counterexamples could help validate chunks, but explanation-based learning and counterexample-guided synthesis are close. |
| ACT-R | Explicit cognitive modules, buffers, declarative/production memory, and activation-based retrieval model bounded cognitive processing. | **Large-scale vector search may improve implementation scale, but core claims concern cognitive constraints and representations.** Neural ACT-R implementations predate modern GPUs; retrieval activation alone is not a new memory architecture. [ACT-R](https://act-r.psy.cmu.edu/), [ACT-RN](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6471s90n). |
| Copycat / Fluid Concepts | Many stochastic local codelets build and revise analogy structures in a workspace; an associative Slipnet shifts concept activations and a changing temperature controls exploration. [Copycat chapter](https://melaniemitchell.me/PapersContent/HofstadterMitchellCopycat1995.pdf) | **More parallel trials and better perception help run the mechanism, but not its hand-built concepts/codelets or microdomain dependence.** Neural analogy already exists. A remaining probe would learn *representation edits* (split/merge/regroup), not only map prestructured inputs. [Neural Analogical Matching](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16163). |
| Subsumption / behavior-based robotics | Concurrent sensor–action layers suppress or inhibit one another for fast reactive control. It deliberately avoids a central world representation. [Brooks 1986](https://people.csail.mit.edu/brooks/papers/representation.pdf) | **Still good for low-latency bounded control.** Strong perception helps; predictive planning can complement it, but learned arbitration and RL hybrids are known. Lack of long-horizon state is a scope limitation, not a hardware accident. |
| Dyna / early world models / model-based RL | Learn a dynamics model, plan on it, then use real experience to correct the model. Simpler early models and limited simulation constrained it. [Dyna](https://mlanthology.org/icml/1990/sutton1990icml-integrated/) | **Strong example of “early, not bad.”** Latent world models, GPU simulation, and imagined rollouts revived the family. Planning exploitation of model errors and compounding error remain. [PlaNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04551), [Dreamer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01603), [MuZero](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-03051-4). |
| Predictive state representations / OOMs / stochastic distinguishing experiments | Represent state as predictions of future action–observation tests rather than latent hidden-state variables; active tests can reveal aliased states. [PSR 2001](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2001/file/1e4d36177d71bbb3558e43af9577d70e-Paper.pdf) | **Partly too early for raw perception, already revived with gradient training and deep recurrent policies.** SDEs explicitly do surprise-driven active state discovery, so the broad modernization is not new. [RPSP](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/hefny18a.html), [SDE / sPOMDP](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005). |
| Bayesian networks / probabilistic graphical models / sum-product circuits | Factorized distributions support interpretable dependencies and sometimes exact inference; variable elimination can grow exponentially with treewidth. | **More memory and GPUs help sampling/parallel message passing; no general cure for treewidth or model misspecification.** Learned tractable circuits and neural parameterizations are established. [SPN](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~pedrod/papers/uai11a.pdf). |
| Fuzzy systems / ANFIS | Fuzzy membership rules express graded, human-readable input–output relations; rule count and choice of meaningful variables are limiting. | **Differentiable optimization improves fitting but does not make rule discovery free.** ANFIS is an established adaptive neural-fuzzy system. [ANFIS](https://doi.org/10.1109/21.256541). |
| Fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) | A signed, weighted concept graph propagates fuzzy node activations through feedback loops for scenario reasoning; expert-chosen concepts and graph/weight identification are the hard parts. [Kosko, 1986](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0020-7373(86)80040-2) | **Modern learning updates weights and edge functions, but does not make an FCM an identified causal model.** Nonlinear and delayed causal edges are established FCM prior art; 2026 KA-FCM uses a newer spline-edge parameterization. Cyclic causal graphs and active intervention design are also established. See AR-77/HY-60. [Extension review](https://doi.org/10.1145/3610771), [KA-FCM (IEEE TFS 2026)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TFUZZ.2026.3680681). |
| Hierarchical Temporal Memory | Sparse distributed representations and temporal memory aim at continual sequence learning. | **The permanence/sequence mechanism is already a defined architecture, not an untried generic idea.** Test it as a baseline against streaming recurrent models/reservoirs, not as novelty. [Cui et al. 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626963/). |
| Neural Turing Machine / differentiable external memory predecessors | A controller reads/writes an explicit memory through differentiable addressing; addressing and stable multi-step manipulation were difficult. | **Autodiff, GPUs, and larger memory directly improved trainability.** NTM/DNC/memory networks and transformer memory are well-developed successors. [NTM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5401), [DNC](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature20101). |
| Neural algorithmic reasoning / learned algorithmic interpreters | A learned message-passing system imitates algorithmic steps or program executions. Training instances often fail to extrapolate with input size. | **More synthetic data and simulation help, but execution is explicit in the closest baselines.** Require size/composition extrapolation over algorithmic baselines. [NAR review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02761). |
| Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH) / self-organizing polynomial networks | Generate candidate polynomial units/layers, select them by an external criterion, and grow a predictive network from data. Small computers made candidate search expensive, but short-sample model selection and validation noise were also central. [Ivakhnenko 1968 record](https://ndlsearch.ndl.go.jp/en/books/R100000136-I1574231875460562432), [self-organization in control](https://doi.org/10.1016/0005-1098(70)90092-0) | **Partly an early constructive-learning ancestor.** GPUs can evaluate many candidates, but validation leakage, polynomial explosion, and inductive bias remain. Later polynomial neural networks, pruning, AutoML, and cascade growth overlap. Not a new architecture revival by itself. |
| Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller (CMAC) | Hash/coarse-code a continuous control input to several memory locations and sum their values; local updates yield fast approximation and adaptation. Input dimension multiplies address combinations, and memory collisions/quantization limit scale. [Albus 1975, NIST record](https://www.nist.gov/publications/new-approach-manipulator-control-cerebellar-model-articulation-controller-cmac1) | **A useful control memory, still specialized.** Modern RAM/parallelism help table size, but tile coding, local function approximation, adaptive control, and CMAC variants are established. The dimensionality problem does not disappear. |
| Neocognitron | Hierarchical local cell layers self-organize shape-sensitive visual features and tolerate shifts/deformations. Its minicomputer-era scale and training data were tiny by current standards. [Fukushima 1980](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00344251), [1988 implementation](https://doi.org/10.1016/0893-6080(88)90014-7) | **Clearly too early as a broad vision direction, but already absorbed into the CNN lineage.** Modern compute/data transformed capability, yet the architecture family is not unoccupied; compare its local learning only against current CNN/ViT baselines. |
| Helmholtz machine / wake-sleep | A top-down generative network is paired with a bottom-up recognition network; wake and sleep phases train each side using samples from the other. This avoided intractable posterior inference but gave a biased recognition/generative learning procedure. [Hinton et al. 1995](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~hinton/absps/ws.htm), [Helmholtz Machine Through Time](https://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~dayan/papers/hdtn95.html) | **Not merely a hardware failure.** Large data and accelerators help stochastic learning, while variational inference, VAEs, flows, and diffusion/score models changed the objective and optimization. Wake-sleep is a historical precursor, not a new generative architecture class. |

### What modern technology really changes

- **Compute:** makes independent evolutionary rollouts, Monte Carlo chains, parallel codelets, and parameter sweeps cheaper. It does not fix a bad state representation, exponential treewidth, difficult mixing, or a reward that needs too many interactions.
- **Autodiff and optimization:** turn local circuits, continuous cellular rules, and differentiable memories into trainable systems. They do not automatically make discrete state growth, variable programs, rule exceptions, or long-horizon credit smooth.
- **Large self-supervised datasets and pretrained perception:** remove a historic sensory bottleneck for symbolic, ART, cognitive, and control backends. This may also hide the contribution: all comparisons must match front-end features and compute.
- **Simulation:** allows counterexamples, active experiments, evolutionary trials, and repeatable robotics tests. It cannot guarantee sim-to-real transfer and can make a learned planner exploit model errors.
- **Memory/hardware:** enables large rule populations, graph state, replay, and physical neuromorphic/analog tests. Sparse irregular operations may remain CPU/memory-bound, and hardware advantages require measured energy and latency.

## Architecture hybridization: coupling audit

The hybrid rule is: name each source mechanism, specify the information flow that changes behavior, then search for that coupling directly. A combination is demoted when the components merely sit side-by-side or the coupling is already canonical.

| ID | Source architectures and coupling | Complementarity / behavioral change | Closest prior art and current decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| HY01 | **PSR + GNG:** graph nodes store action-conditioned predictions of future tests, not observation centroids. Forecast residuals can add discriminator tests and split/link nodes; planning traverses action-labeled predictive edges. | GNG contributes online topology growth; PSR contributes a state coordinate tied to future controllable consequences. | SDE already grows/splits/refines/merges predictive tests; sPOMDP splits predictive state partitions; growing-SOM RL already couples topology growth with action/reward/transition estimates. A continuous graph over predictive vectors may be only an indexing choice. **Demoted pending an application-level advantage.** [SDE 2017](https://robots.isi.edu/prl/collins2017-a-robust-cognitive-architecture-for-learning-from-surprises.pdf), [sPOMDP 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005), [growing-SOM RL](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106723). |
| HY02 | **Soar chunking + counterexample-guided synthesis:** a learned chunk stays provisional; near-miss simulator states challenge its conditions, and counterexamples trigger a guard addition or split. | Soar compresses solved subgoals; CEGIS checks whether the generalization preserves behavior. If it works, learning becomes iterative “compile, challenge, repair” rather than one-shot chunk insertion. | Explanation-based learning, Soar filters, and CEGIS are each established; exact integration not verified. **Useful bounded experiment; low novelty.** [Soar chunking docs](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/soar_manual/04_ProceduralKnowledgeLearning/). |
| HY03 | **Copycat + learned representation edits:** codelets propose split/merge/regroup operations on a workspace; outcomes on analogy tasks train edit utility and preserve multiple candidate structures. | Copycat contributes stochastic local revision; a learned edit policy could carry useful representational moves between domains, unlike matching already-tokenized relations. | Neural analogy, SME/ACME, and learned program/structure search are near. Exact edit policy risks being RL over an ad hoc program space. **High-risk exploratory probe, do not promote yet.** [Copycat](https://melaniemitchell.me/PapersContent/HofstadterMitchellCopycat1995.pdf), [Neural Analogical Matching](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16163). |
| HY04 | **Bayesian blackboard + cost-aware VOI scheduler:** each specialist posts a calibrated belief update and estimated cost; scheduler runs the computation with greatest expected decision improvement per cost. | Could maintain unresolved alternatives and spend compute only where a specialist may change the action. | Opportunistic blackboards, Bayesian blackboards, and value-of-computation scheduling already provide this coupling. **Reject as novelty; retain as systems baseline.** [HEARSAY-II](https://mas.cs.umass.edu/pub/paper_detail.php/229). |
| HY05 | **Deep perception + ART category formation:** frozen/trainable encoder feeds ART/FuzzyART winner/reset and local category updates. | Learned sensory features address ART’s old raw-input geometry; ART provides immediate category creation and local updates. | DeepART (2025) already integrates ART learning in deep MLP/CNN; ART-reservoir combinations exist. **Reject generic form.** [DeepART](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107580), [SORN reservoir](https://mjcs.um.edu.my/index.php/MJCS/article/view/34808). |
| HY06 | **ART + reservoir dynamics:** ART/ITM clusters and organizes recurrent reservoir nodes; sequence state uses the adapted reservoir. | ART adds data-shaped topology; reservoir supplies temporal fading memory. | Direct self-organizing reservoir network for action recognition (2022). **Existing component combination; reject generic form.** [Paper](https://mjcs.um.edu.my/index.php/MJCS/article/view/34808). |
| HY07 | **LCS + deep features/replay:** XCS learns rules over a learned visual or latent representation; replay improves sampled experience. | Deep features improve perception; LCS gives inspectable action rules and niche-based adaptation. | XCSR, deep-feature LCS, and replay XCS already exist. **Not novel; use as comparison for event-rule candidates.** [XCSR](https://www.fujipress.jp/jaciii/jc/jacii002100050856/), [XCS replay](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05628). |
| HY08 | **Hopfield associative memory + attention:** attention performs content-addressed associative retrieval and updates a query with retrieved patterns. | High-capacity associative retrieval becomes a convenient differentiable layer. | The mathematical equivalence is explicit in modern Hopfield work. **Reject unless memory update semantics or online learning differs.** [Hopfield Networks is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02217). |
| HY09 | **Dyna/world model + evolved policy:** train a recurrent model, then search/evolve policies with imagined rollouts. | Model-based data efficiency plus gradient-free policy search. | Recurrent World Models Facilitate Policy Evolution and POET already cover these combinations. **Reject broad form.** [World-model evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01999), [POET](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01753). |
| HY10 | **NCA + autodiff/regeneration:** optimize local cellular rules by differentiating task-level growth/repair losses. | Local self-organization becomes target-directed and damage-tolerant. | This is the central known NCA revival; HyperNCA also grows weights. **Reject as novelty unless computation/control is qualitatively new.** [Growing NCA](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/), [HyperNCA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11674). |
| HY11 | **E-prop + neuromorphic processors:** compute local eligibility traces online and use hardware parallelism for event-driven recurrent learning. | Avoid BPTT state storage while preserving online adaptation; low memory may matter on edge devices. | Already implemented on SpiNNaker 2 with speech keyword spotting; no general capability win established. **Existing; benchmark energy/latency only.** [SpiNNaker 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9742366/). |
| HY12 | **NEAT / topology evolution + local synaptic learning:** use population fitness to change graph structure and e-prop/local rules to adapt weights between generations. | Evolution could search non-differentiable structure while local plasticity reduces weight-search burden. | Evolutionary SNN structure learning and GPU NEAT are active; likely known at mechanism level. **Hold pending exact search for local-rule/evolution coupling.** [Evolutionary SNN survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12552), [GPU-NEAT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01817). |
| HY13 | **Differential dataflow + learned dependency validity:** persistent claims keep signed/provenance deltas; candidate dependencies are learned from corrections and counterfactual edits, then used to choose the invalidation cone. | Differential dataflow cheaply reuses derived results when dependencies are known; learned dependency confidence could supply semantic validity where humans did not author a graph. | Truth maintenance, Bayesian-network relevance invalidation, self-adjusting computation, incremental probabilistic-program inference, and event-stream causal-dependency learning already cover much of this. **System engineering question, not a strong model-class candidate.** [Differential Dataflow](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/differentialdataflow.pdf), [TMS](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/77-1/Papers/035.pdf), [Bayesian update](https://sites.pitt.edu/~druzdzel/psfiles/ijprai99.pdf), [online causal dependency](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2013.09.022). |
| HY14 | **PSR + reactive subsumption:** each fast behavior proposes action plus short-horizon test predictions; arbiter uses forecasted risk/confidence, rather than fixed priority alone. | Reactive modules retain fast escape behaviors while predictions handle perceptual aliasing and route ambiguity. | RPSP, robot PSR control, and learned subsumption/arbitration are known; coupling may reduce to predictive control over a behavior library. **Demote to application probe.** [RPSP](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/hefny18a.html), [learned subsumption](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7506774/). |
| HY15 | **Fuzzy rules + neural adaptation (ANFIS-like):** differentiable membership functions and rule consequents are trained jointly. | Human-readable graded rules with smooth fitting. | ANFIS (1993) is direct prior art. **Reject as a new architecture.** [ANFIS](https://doi.org/10.1109/21.256541). |
| HY16 | **Neural algorithmic reasoning + GNN/message passing:** graph networks learn transition steps of classical algorithms and execute them over varied graph sizes. | Learned local transitions may generalize algorithmic operations. | Neural algorithmic reasoning is already this broad family; size extrapolation is the actual test, not hybrid novelty. [NAR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02761). |
| HY17 | **Probabilistic circuit + neural feature learner:** neural modules provide leaves/parameters while circuit structure supports tractable exact queries. | Perception learns features while circuit gives exact marginals for selected queries. | Deep probabilistic circuits and neural leaves already exist. **No novelty claim; possible calibrated-query baseline.** [SPN](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~pedrod/papers/uai11a.pdf). |

### Hybrid conclusions and surviving questions

- Many attractive old-modern pairs are already direct papers: ART/deep learning, ART/reservoir, LCS/deep features, Hopfield/attention, NCA/autodiff, world-model/evolution, and e-prop/neuromorphic hardware. The pair names themselves should not reappear as candidates.
- HY01 initially looked least-settled, but direct audit shows the adaptive predictive test/state lifecycle already exists in SDE/sPOMDP, while growing-SOM RL adds online topology and transition learning. No architecture-level survivor has emerged from the archaeology track yet. A PTM experiment would test only whether a continuous graph index is practically useful beyond those methods.
- **Counterexample-checked chunking** (HY02) may improve safe rule reuse but likely belongs as a learning mechanism within Soar/CEGIS, not an independent model class.
- **Learned dependency validity for incremental inference** (HY13) may have an opaque-model systems niche; prior work on TMS, Bayesian relevance, self-adjusting computation, incremental probabilistic programs, and event-stream causal learning lowers the novelty ceiling substantially.
- Copycat-style learned representation revision (HY03) remains too underspecified for promotion. A meaningful test has to show that split/merge/regroup operations yield held-out analogical transfer with fewer search steps, not just more stochastic trials.

## Deep-candidate docket

The broad slate remains active. These detailed dockets are experiments to disprove specific claims, not claims of novelty. Established components, near-duplicate architectures, and negative results remain in the notebook.

### New archaeology/hybrid candidates (C026–C029)

#### C026 — Predictive Topology Memory

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** grow a graph of state hypotheses whose nodes store predictions about future action–observation experiments; grow the predictive test vocabulary when a counterexample shows two situations need a new distinction.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** nodes encode predictive distributions over selected tests and action-conditioned outcomes; each action/observation updates test forecasts and node belief, then may add a test, edge, split, or merge. Input is an online controlled observation stream. Output is a predictive state belief, action forecast, and optional discriminating experiment.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** local Bayesian/online forecast updates plus residual-driven topology growth; infer current graph state by matching the history-updated predictive vector and plan on labeled edges; persistent graph/test memory grows and prunes under budget.
- **Use cases / proposed advantage:** partially observed environments with aliased observations and changed dynamics; state distinctions may be aligned with controllable future consequences instead of appearance.
- **Weakness / nearest work / possible novelty:** test discovery may be unidentifiable or costly; test/node growth may explode. SDE already splits tests, refines compound tests, and merges predictively similar tests; sPOMDP splits predictive states; online PSR discovery and CSSR also grow predictive tests/states. GNG state abstraction and trajectory inference are close. Residue is the use of a continuous prototype graph over predictive vectors, which may be only a memory/indexing choice. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.05)**.
- **Falsifiable prototype:** 5×5 symbolic aliased maze with a mid-run transition change. Compare against active SDE, fixed PSR, RPSP/GRU, GNG on observations, and oracle state planning under matched memory and interaction budgets. Reject if there is no sample-efficiency or post-change benefit, or if a fixed test bank matches it.

#### C027 — Counterexample-Checked Soar Chunking

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** propose a production rule from a solved Soar subgoal, challenge it on generated near-miss situations, then add guards/split/reject before permanent reuse.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** a provisional condition/action rule stores trace, positive cases, and counterexamples; repeated operation is compile → challenge → repair. Input is a symbolic reasoning trace and simulator state. Output is a verified rule, corrected rule family, or rejection.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** explanation-based chunking plus counterexample-guided refinement; ordinary indexed production matching at inference; persistent rule/trace/validation memory.
- **Use cases / proposed advantage:** safe speed-up in repeatable planning domains; preserve compression while avoiding overgeneral learned rules.
- **Weakness / nearest work / possible novelty:** exact domain simulator or verifier may be unavailable; guards could erase transfer and verification could exceed saved search. Soar already has chunking and correctness filters; CEGIS/EBL/ILP are close. At most this is a verified repair loop for a particular rule learner. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.1)**.
- **Falsifiable prototype:** randomized Blocks World with local-negation edge cases; compare vanilla chunks, built-in filter, and checked repair on repeat search cost, false firings, correctness, rule size, and verification time. Reject if the filter matches its curve or guards erase speed-up.

#### C028 — Learned Copycat Representation Revision

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** allow the system to change how it groups or relates the input while solving an analogy, and learn which local representational edits transfer across tasks.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** a workspace stores competing groupings/correspondences and codelet proposals for split, merge, regroup, or break; repeat edits, assess conflicts/results, and update edit utility. Input is a pair of structured or encoder-proposed situations. Output is a mapping plus revised segmentation/relations.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** stochastic local search with feedback-trained edit preferences; inference runs multiple partial revisions; persistent memory stores an edit inventory and successful analogies.
- **Use cases / proposed advantage:** analogies where the correct match requires changing granularity, not merely mapping fixed predicates.
- **Weakness / nearest work / possible novelty:** unspecified edit semantics can hide hand-coded intelligence; search may be expensive; SME, ACME, Copycat/Metacat, neural analogical matching, and program search are close. Potential residue is cross-task learning of edits that alter representation topology. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.1)**.
- **Falsifiable prototype:** controlled analogy grammar with ambiguous groupings and held-out rule combinations; compare learned edits, fixed-structure mapping, neural analogical matching, and hand-coded Copycat edits. Reject if transfer is absent or search grows without accuracy gain.

#### C029 — Learned Dependency-Validity Propagation

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** reuse prior conclusions after local edits by learning which upstream changes actually invalidate which derived claims, while attaching confidence/certificates and conservatively auditing uncertain cases.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** typed claims/provenance plus uncertain dependency edges are repeatedly updated by signed deltas and correction events. Input is a changing structured world/graph and queries. Output is a recomputed answer with dependency certificate, an uncertainty flag, or an audit request.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** infer candidate semantic dependencies from derivations and interventions; corrections calibrate edges. At inference, propagate changes only through affected edges, but audit/fully recompute uncertain regions. Persistent memory is the claim/provenance graph and edge-confidence history.
- **Use cases / proposed advantage:** interactive simulators, code/world state, or knowledge structures where expensive inferences face frequent local changes; reduce recomputation without hand-authored complete dependency maps.
- **Weakness / nearest work / possible novelty:** skipped true dependencies cause silent staleness; audit can eliminate speed gains. Truth-maintenance systems, Bayesian-network relevance invalidation, self-adjusting computation, incremental Datalog/probabilistic inference, online causal-dependency learning, and dataflow caches already cover most operations. Possible residue is learning semantic validity links from opaque-model corrections; this is more likely a systems contribution than a model class. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.05)**.
- **Falsifiable prototype:** mutable synthetic graph with known dependencies and 10^4–10^5 derived claims; compare full recomputation, oracle provenance, differential dataflow, and learned links across changed-cone sizes. Reject if unsound unflagged answers occur or audit overhead removes savings.

#### C030 — Outcome-Basin State Machine

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** identify a state by its bounded-horizon *control signature*: the set of goal regions reachable under available action sequences, with costs or risks, rather than a passive observation embedding.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** store set-valued action-conditioned reachability signatures; execute actions, update reachable basins, and merge/split histories when tested outcomes agree/disagree. Input is observations, actions, and goal sets. Output is an abstract control state, safe action, or reachability forecast.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** learn signatures from local trials and transition observations; inference selects actions whose reachable set covers the goal while respecting safe regions; memory is a partition of histories and set-valued outcomes.
- **Use / possible advantage:** sparse-reward and goal-conditioned control where passive observations look alike but controllable futures differ; abstract state may be reusable across multiple goals.
- **Weakness / closest work / possible novelty:** control bisimulation, MDP homomorphisms, PSRs, goal-conditioned RL, and reachability analysis already capture much of the core. Maintaining set-valued outcomes may be expensive. Residue would require measurable sample/memory gains over a learned transition model. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.1)**. [Goal-conditioned bisimulation](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/hansen-estruch22a/hansen-estruch22a.pdf), [formal MDP abstractions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14402).
- **Falsifiable prototype:** small POMDP with observation-aliasing and action-dependent reachability; compare against RNN state, fixed PSR, and transition-model planner on goal success, abstract-state count, and interactions. Reject if it reduces to a bisimulation quotient or gives no advantage.

#### C031 — Violation-Scoped Homeostatic Reorganization

- **Plain-English idea / primitive:** retain fast control loops that keep essential variables within viability bounds, but when one bound is violated, reorganize only the modules with measured causal influence on that variable.
- **Information, repeated operation, input, output:** store essential-variable bands, current controller modules, and a sparse intervention/sensitivity graph; control, detect violation, probe implicated parameters, accept changes that restore viability, and keep unaffected modules fixed. Input is sensor feedback plus safety bands. Output is action and occasional localized controller reconfiguration.
- **Learning / inference / memory:** online perturbation experiments estimate parameter-to-variable effects; search local gain/structure changes rather than global random retuning. Inference remains closed-loop control; memory stores modules, viability history, and sensitivities.
- **Use / possible advantage:** robotics/industrial control with localized actuator drift; may preserve previously successful control when one subsystem changes.
- **Weakness / closest work / possible novelty:** Ashby ultrastability/Homeostat, perceptual-control reorganization, adaptive control, extremum seeking, safe control, and modular fault diagnosis are close. Perturbation attribution can be unsafe or slow; essential variables are supplied by the designer. Novelty confidence **very low (~0.1)**.
- **Falsifiable prototype:** simulated coupled plant with three control loops and one mid-run actuator-gain shift; compare global homeostat search, violation-scoped updates, adaptive PID, and model-based re-tuning. Measure recovery time, constraint violations, and retained performance in unchanged loops. Reject if localization does not improve the recovery/violation Pareto frontier. [Ashby, *Design for a Brain*](https://www.ashby.info/Ashby%20-%20Design%20for%20a%20Brain%20-%20The%20Origin%20of%20Adaptive%20Behavior.pdf), [PCT hierarchy](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0149763419306220).

### Lead-verified prior-art updates

- The Soar user manual directly states that local substate negations can yield overgeneral chunks; Soar has a `allow-local-negations` setting that rejects chunks derived from such reasoning. Therefore the proposed verifier must beat this built-in safety/performance tradeoff, not only vanilla chunking. [Procedural learning](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/soar_manual/04_ProceduralKnowledgeLearning/), [chunk option](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/reference/cli/cmd_chunk/).
- “Surprise-based learning of state representations” (2018) already frames Stochastic Distinguishing Experiments as active predictive state tests and introduces sPOMDP. This directly narrows C026: new work would need the online topology/test-set interaction and an advantage over active SDE, not active predictive state alone. [Primary article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005).
- Growing Neural Gas already learns an incremental topology, and GNG has been used for trajectory inference (TinGa). These are close ingredients but not proof of a predictive-test graph. Targeted exact-phrase searches did not find a paper with the same co-adaptive test-bank plus graph-growth rule; this is not evidence of absence. [GNG](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/1994/hash/d56b9fc4b0f1be8871f5e1c40c0067e7-Abstract.html), [TinGa](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7355244/).
- ART + self-organizing reservoir is a direct 2022 hybrid. DeepART (2025) is a direct deep/ART collision. They are demoted regardless of whether our wording or motivation differs. [SORN reservoir](https://mjcs.um.edu.my/index.php/MJCS/article/view/34808), [DeepART](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107580).
- Copycat’s original description documents the coderack/workspace/Slipnet interaction, stochastic codelets, and temperature feedback. It provides direct prior art for an emergent local-search architecture; LCRR must claim only learned *revision operators*, not codelets, workspaces, stochasticity, or analogical mapping. [Copycat chapter](https://melaniemitchell.me/PapersContent/HofstadterMitchellCopycat1995.pdf).
- The PDL search found a large established field of dependency-tracked incremental evaluation. No direct “learned semantic invalidation” architecture was verified, but the absence of an exact search hit is weak evidence. Continue only if a soundness-aware mechanism can be stated beyond predicting cache hits.
- **Stronger direct collisions from the prior-art hunter:** Collins & Shen 2017's SDE learner explicitly splits a predictive test when one-step extensions improve prediction, refines compound tests when components behave differently, and merges tests with similar forecasts. The 2018 sPOMDP version associates each latent state with a predictive experiment and splits states when tests distinguish them. McCracken & Bowling (2005) already discovers core PSR tests online; CSSR (2004) grows causal predictive states from histories; growing-SOM RL (2020) combines online topology with reward/transition estimates. The new PTM's split/test lifecycle is therefore established; only its continuous predictive-space prototype graph remains, and that may be implementation detail. [SDE 2017](https://robots.isi.edu/prl/collins2017-a-robust-cognitive-architecture-for-learning-from-surprises.pdf), [sPOMDP 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005), [online PSR discovery 2005](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2005/file/c3008b2c6f5370b744850a98a95b73ad-Paper.pdf), [CSSR 2004](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0406011), [growing-SOM RL 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106723).
- **Further PDL collisions:** Doyle's Truth Maintenance System tracks justifications and revises beliefs after assumptions change; Bayesian-network relevance updating invalidates and updates only beliefs affected by new evidence/model revision; self-adjusting computation records dynamic control/data dependencies and notes change propagation is not always faster; incremental probabilistic-program inference reuses traces across program edits; event-stream causal-network work learns dependency edges online. These reduce the possible remainder to sound, calibrated dependency learning for opaque computations, which is likely a systems research question. [Doyle 1977](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/77-1/Papers/035.pdf), [Lin & Druzdzel](https://sites.pitt.edu/~druzdzel/psfiles/ijprai99.pdf), [Acar et al. 2009](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~blelloch/papers/ABBHT09.pdf), [Cusumano-Towner et al. 2018](https://pldi18.sigplan.org/details/pldi-2018-papers/37/Incremental-Inference-for-Probabilistic-Programs), [Acharya & Lee 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2013.09.022).
- **Further Copycat collision:** Metacat (2002) already records a temporal trace of cognitive events, notices repeated dead-end “snags,” keeps episodic analogy themes, and alters codelet urgencies or concept clamping to change later search. LCRR must claim transferable *edit semantics*, not a system that observes its own search and shifts attention. [Marshall, Metacat](https://science.slc.edu/jmarshall/papers/cogsci02.pdf).
- Additional cybernetics/control archaeology from the independent invention track produced a control-signature state quotient and a localized ultrastability proposal (C030–C031). The first is close to bisimulation and PSR; the second addresses Ashby’s documented slow, highly cross-coupled Homeostat by preserving unaffected modules, but overlaps adaptive control and fault isolation. Both are recorded as low-novelty probes, not new architecture claims.
- Other old control mechanisms screened and demoted: hierarchical Perceptual Control Theory/setpoint loops, iterative learning control (repeat-trajectory error correction), and phase-coded perturbation learning. They remain useful methods, but their primitives are established; notably, iterative robot trajectory learning dates to Arimoto et al. (1984), and perturbation-based black-box gradient estimates overlap SPSA/extremum-seeking. [Arimoto et al.](https://doi.org/10.1002/rob.4620010203), [PCT evidence review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0149763419306220), [Spall's SPSA paper](https://doi.org/10.1109/9.119632).

### Deep probe A — Predictive Topology Memory (PTM; HY01)

**Status:** Defer as an architecture claim (novelty confidence ~0.05). A CPU toy experiment is justified only if its question is empirical inductive bias—does a topology over predictive prototypes help continuous/noisy tasks beyond SDE's predictive state partition? The central state/test growth behavior already has close prior art.

1. **What it computes.** PTM maintains an online graph of state hypotheses where each node is a prototype over predictions of selected action–observation tests. It tries to answer “which future behavior state am I in?” rather than “which current observation vector looks nearest?”
2. **Basic unit.** A node contains (a) a probability vector over a finite bank of tests, (b) uncertainty/count statistics, (c) reward and transition estimates by action, and (d) sparse outgoing transition edges. A test is a short action sequence paired with its possible observation sequence.
3. **Communication.** The active state distribution routes each action to outgoing edges; an observed outcome updates node probabilities and forecast statistics. A disagreement or high residual posts a counterexample to the test-growth process. There is no all-to-all node communication.
4. **Where knowledge exists.** In the node/test table and action-labeled graph, rather than a fixed neural weight matrix. A shared observation encoder may be added later, but the initial test isolates the architecture with symbolic observations.
5. **Learning.** Initialize a small test bank. Maintain forecasts online with calibrated counts/updates. Grow a new test when two nodes make different action-conditioned predictions that matter for a decision; split a node when prediction residuals are persistently multimodal; merge nodes only when their forecasts and transitions remain statistically indistinguishable. Use GNG-like graph insertion as a structural proposal, not an automatic novelty claim.
6. **Inference.** Update a posterior over nodes using current history and predicted test outcomes. If two plausible nodes imply different actions, select a short distinguishing experiment by expected reduction in decision-relevant uncertainty divided by action cost. Then plan over the learned graph or act reactively when uncertainty is low.
7. **Post-deployment learning.** Yes: new streams update forecasts, append tests, and grow/split/merge nodes. Growth is bounded by a memory budget; low-value tests/nodes are archived or retired with a replayable version log.
8. **Scaling.** Naively O(number of nodes × tests × actions) per observation. A practical version needs sparse top-k node retrieval, shared test outcomes, capped graph degree, and test pruning. Graph update is likely CPU/memory-bound; a learned visual encoder may use GPU separately.
9. **GPU/CPU/hardware fit.** Small structured environments are CPU-friendly. If visual input is used, freeze the same encoder for every baseline in the first comparison. GPU use is then limited to representation extraction; the PTM core should stay under the shared 5.5 GB cap or use CPU.
10. **Data needed.** Online action/observation trajectories and optional rewards; no hidden-state labels. For a first test, procedurally generate aliased mazes with known transition structure. A second stage can use pixels with common frozen features.
11. **Strongest potential advantage.** State distinctions are driven by future action-conditioned consequences, which may be more useful than observation prototypes in partial observability. Growth could spend memory only on distinctions that change a control decision.
12. **Likely failure modes.** Inadequate actions make states unidentifiable; counterexample tests proliferate; noisy forecasts split one state repeatedly; a nearest-node metric hides multimodal belief; high-dimensional tests are expensive; apparent gains may come from a better planner rather than the representation.
13. **Closest work.** PSR/OOM state learning and predictive filters; SDE/sPOMDP surprise-driven active state discovery; RPSP; GNG/SOM state abstraction and TinGa trajectory inference. [SDE/sPOMDP](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005), [RPSP](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/hefny18a.html), [online PSR discovery](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2005/hash/c3008b2c6f5370b744850a98a95b73ad-Abstract.html), [TinGa](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7355244/).
14. **Potentially novel part.** SDE already grows/splits/refines/merges predictive experiments and sPOMDP uses predictive experiments to split a state partition. Online PSR discovery and CSSR independently grow predictive test/state structures; growing-SOM RL combines topology growth with action/reward/transition estimates. The residual—storing a continuous prototype graph over predictive vectors—may be an engineering choice. A new mechanism would need a clear operational behavior beyond state partitioning or nearest-node indexing. [Collins & Shen 2017](https://robots.isi.edu/prl/collins2017-a-robust-cognitive-architecture-for-learning-from-surprises.pdf), [sPOMDP 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005), [online PSR discovery](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2005/file/c3008b2c6f5370b744850a98a95b73ad-Paper.pdf), [CSSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0406011), [growing-SOM RL](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106723).
15. **Smallest worthwhile experiment.** A 5×5 symbolic maze with pairs of visually identical cells whose correct action depends on history, plus one mid-run transition change. Compare PTM with (i) fixed-test PSR, (ii) SDE active testing, (iii) observation-space GNG, (iv) GRU/RPSP with the same experience budget, and (v) an oracle state planner. Also ablate joint growth into tests-only and topology-only variants. Match memory bytes and planning compute; measure episodes to goal, predictive Brier score, state/test count, stale decision rate after the change, and update work. Use a pixel/frozen-encoder replication only if the structured test survives.
16. **Falsifier.** Current evidence says this may reduce to SDE plus an index. Drop the mechanism if joint growth does not improve over the best one-sided ablation and active SDE, if it does not improve sample efficiency or post-change recovery at equal memory/compute, if graph/test growth is unstable, or if any gain disappears with a strong fixed-test baseline.

### Deep probe B — Predictive Delta Ledger (PDL; HY13)

**Status:** Retain as a correctness/efficiency research question, not a promising new model class (novelty confidence ~0.05). Prior art covers explicit dependency recording, belief invalidation, probabilistic inference reuse, and online causal-edge learning; only opaque-model semantic validity may remain.

1. **What it computes.** It maintains a persistent set of derived claims and selectively updates claims when source facts change. The computation is organized around signed deltas and dependency cones instead of replaying every inference after each edit.
2. **Basic unit.** A typed claim/fact with value, confidence, source/version, and a provenance record. A dependency hyperedge connects inputs to a derived claim and stores whether the link is rule-authored, inferred, or uncertain.
3. **Communication.** A changed input emits a signed change event; downstream operators receive it and recompute affected claims. Conflicts create correction events that propagate backward to edge-confidence updates or guard checks.
4. **Where knowledge exists.** In the persistent claim graph, operation rules, and dependency/provenance structure. Model parameters may score candidate links, but the operational state is explicit and inspectable.
5. **Learning.** Candidate semantic dependencies are inferred from repeated derivations and interventions/edits. When a correction shows an output became stale—or remained valid despite a proposed cause—the system updates link confidence. Safe mode must conservatively recompute low-confidence regions; a learned edge must never silently stand in for a proof of validity.
6. **Inference.** Apply only the affected delta cone, answer a query from current claims, and attach the dependency certificate/version set used. If the certificate is uncertain, trigger selective audit or full recomputation before returning a high-stakes answer.
7. **Post-deployment learning.** Yes: corrections improve candidate dependency estimates. The risk is that the model learns regularities that fail under a rare intervention; a correction log and conservative fallback are necessary.
8. **Scaling.** If the affected cone has size k in a graph of N derived claims, ideal update work is near O(k) plus edge traversal, versus O(N) full replay. Learned link discovery itself may be O(N) and memory can grow with full provenance. Delta algebra / incremental view maintenance is CPU-friendly; embeddings or candidate link scoring can be batched on GPU.
9. **GPU/CPU/hardware fit.** Start CPU-only on synthetic graphs. GPU is optional for upstream multimodal encoding and candidate link scores; it should not be needed for sparse delta propagation. Before any GPU experiment, inspect current use and stay within the shared cap.
10. **Data needed.** Mutable graphs, event streams, or code-like worlds where local facts are edited and ground-truth dependencies are known for evaluation. Train/validate on some edits, hold out edit combinations and rare causes.
11. **Strongest potential advantage.** Reuse expensive conclusions across repeated small changes while learning the relevant semantic dependencies without requiring the user to author a complete dependency graph.
12. **Likely failure modes.** Unsound skipped invalidations return stale claims; conservative auditing removes the speed benefit; inferred dependencies are correlated but not causal; provenance storage dominates; broad learned dependencies cause over-invalidation; benchmarks may reward an intentionally weak recomputation baseline.
13. **Closest work.** Differential Dataflow, self-adjusting computation, incremental view maintenance, truth-maintenance systems, Datalog provenance, and cache invalidation. [Differential Dataflow](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/differentialdataflow.pdf).
14. **Potentially novel part.** Learning and calibrating semantic invalidation dependencies from corrections/edit outcomes when no explicit execution or causal graph is available, then using them to prioritize incremental recomputation with explicit soundness audits. But online causal-dependency learning already exists for event streams, while truth maintenance and Bayesian-network relevance cover belief invalidation; the dataflow machinery must not be called new. [Doyle 1977 TMS](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/77-1/Papers/035.pdf), [Bayesian incremental belief updates](https://sites.pitt.edu/~druzdzel/psfiles/ijprai99.pdf), [self-adjusting computation](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~blelloch/papers/ABBHT09.pdf), [incremental probabilistic-program inference](https://pldi18.sigplan.org/details/pldi-2018-papers/37/Incremental-Inference-for-Probabilistic-Programs), [online causal dependency learning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2013.09.022).
15. **Smallest worthwhile experiment.** Generate a deterministic synthetic rule graph with conditional branches, negation, and alternate derivations, 10^4–10^5 derived claims, and known dependencies. Apply local edits that vary changed-cone size, including held-out branch conditions and adversarial edits that activate unseen dependencies. Compare full recomputation, oracle dependency tracking, DRed/BF-style incremental maintenance, a standard dataflow system, and learned links with conservative audits. Measure exact-answer errors, silent staleness, audit rate, wall-clock work, recomputed claims, and dependency-memory growth.
16. **Falsifier.** Reject if the learned graph ever returns unflagged stale claims above the predeclared tolerance, needs hand-authored semantic edges, scales like full replay on small edits, or loses all latency gain once soundness audits are included.

### Deep probe C — Counterexample-Checked Soar Chunking (CCSC; HY02)

**Status:** Useful mechanism experiment, not a new architecture class. Novelty confidence ~0.1–0.2.

1. **What it computes.** Converts successful subgoal reasoning into a reusable production, then challenges the generalized production against nearby situations before allowing it to become permanent.
2. **Basic unit.** A provisional production rule with conditions, action/result, source trace, and a set of positive/negative validation examples.
3. **Communication.** Soar working-memory matches trigger candidate rules; a verifier receives counterexample states and sends back a missing-condition or split request. No dense neural messaging is required.
4. **Where knowledge exists.** Production memory, traces, and a small counterexample/guard set. The simulator is an external exact transition oracle in the first prototype.
5. **Learning.** Standard chunk generation proposes a rule; a counterexample-guided loop searches for states where the new rule fires but the original subgoal procedure would produce a different result. Add a discriminating guard, create a specialized sibling rule, or reject the chunk. Preserve correctness by default when the verifier cannot decide.
6. **Inference.** Rule matching and conflict resolution proceed as usual; verified chunks skip repeated subgoal search. Provisional/unverified rules may be tested in shadow mode but cannot control behavior.
7. **Post-deployment learning.** Yes. Each failed prediction supplies a new counterexample; the rule version is repaired or retired.
8. **Scaling.** Inference cost remains indexed rule matching; verification could be expensive and may require bounded search, solver assistance, or simulator sampling. Negation/continuous state increases the guard-search cost. CPU is appropriate for the first discrete benchmark.
9. **GPU/CPU/hardware fit.** CPU-only; a neural world model is unnecessary in the primary test. If later used to propose counterexamples, compare with exact simulator and never trust its unverified negatives.
10. **Data needed.** Deterministic or well-specified small transition system with repeat subgoals and generated near misses; no large corpus. A Blocks World or logistics simulator provides precise ground truth.
11. **Strongest potential advantage.** Prevent useful compilation from sacrificing correctness when ordinary generalization misses local negative conditions or context.
12. **Likely failure modes.** Counterexample search misses rare regions; guards make chunks too specific; verification costs exceed the saved subgoal work; one can reproduce the result with standard CEGIS or conservative Soar filters.
13. **Closest work.** Soar’s existing explanation-based chunking and correctness filters, explanation-based learning, inductive logic programming, and counterexample-guided inductive synthesis. The current Soar manual explicitly warns that local negations can create overgeneral chunks and documents `allow-local-negations` as a filter. [Soar learning manual](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/soar_manual/04_ProceduralKnowledgeLearning/), [chunk command](https://soar.eecs.umich.edu/reference/cli/cmd_chunk/).
14. **Potentially novel part.** At most, a verified feedback loop that synthesizes missing guards for a specific explanation-based rule learner. This is likely a useful integration detail rather than a new architecture. Any prototype must beat Soar's built-in `allow-local-negations` filter and a conventional CEGIS guard-synthesis baseline.
15. **Smallest worthwhile experiment.** Small deterministic Blocks World with repeated planning subgoals and local-negation edge cases; exhaustively enumerate states so chunk correctness can be decided exactly. Compare vanilla chunking, Soar’s conservative negation filter, a conventional CEGIS guard-synthesis baseline, and counterexample-checked chunks on repeat-task search cost, held-out correctness, false rule firings, rule size, and validation cost.
16. **Falsifier.** Do not continue if added guards eliminate most reuse, verification cost exceeds saved search, or Soar’s built-in filter reaches the same correctness/efficiency curve.

### Deep probe D — Learned Copycat Representation Revision (LCRR)

**Status:** Defer. High risk, low novelty confidence (~0.1), and insufficiently specified. A separate prototype is not justified until a finite edit grammar and feedback signal are stated independently of hand-coded Copycat codelets.

- **Mechanism:** a workspace stores competing object/relation/group hypotheses. Local “codelets” propose representation edits (merge, split, regroup, relabel, or break a mapping); edit selection depends on unresolved conflicts and task outcomes. Successful cross-task edits are retained as an edit policy or reusable codelet, while failed edits become local counterexamples.
- **What each source contributes:** Copycat supplies stochastic local construction and feedback from the current workspace/Slipnet; learned edit selection supplies reuse across tasks. The coupling changes the representational search actions, not just the input encoder.
- **Why behavior could differ:** The system may revise its input segmentation or relations when a current mapping conflicts, rather than choosing among fixed correspondences. This could support analogies with changing granularity.
- **Prior art:** Copycat/Metacat, structure-mapping engine (SME), ACME, neural analogical matching, and neural program/structure search. Metacat already monitors its own processing trace, detects repeated “snags,” stores analogy themes episodically, and clamps codelet/Slipnet activity to alter subsequent search. The remaining claim must be learned transfer of a finite representation-edit language, not self-monitoring, stochastic structure revision, episodic memory, or codelet scheduling. Current targeted checks found no exact same mechanism, but the definition is too broad to claim novelty.
- **Small experiment:** Generate analogy pairs from a small compositional grammar with controlled ambiguous groupings. Compare learned revision, fixed-structure SME-like mapping, neural analogical matching, and Copycat-style hand-coded local edits on held-out combinations. Measure exact mappings, edit count, search steps, and sensitivity to distractors.
- **Falsifier / continuation gate:** Stop if gains depend on hand-designed task-specific codelets, require more search than baselines, or fail on held-out transformations. Continue only if a small learned edit inventory transfers across grammars and reduces both error and search.

## Rejected / demoted ideas

- **Associative Fold (C009):** learned associative aggregation is meaningful for variable-order pooling, but Deep Sets, commutative monoids, and scan/prefix models occupy its central primitive. Keep as a component hypothesis; reject a distinct-class claim absent a new operation and test. [Deep Sets](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2017/hash/f22e4747da1aa27e363d86d40ff442fe-Abstract.html), [learnable commutative monoids](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08541).
- **Geodesic Atlas (C004):** graph geodesics and manifold embeddings are established through Isomap and successors; modern encoders can improve the metric but do not change the basic primitive. Retain only if a causal/decision-validity signal changes graph construction and beats manifold baselines. [Isomap](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.290.5500.2319).
- **Error-Correcting Belief Code (C007):** redundant error-correcting output codes are established; embedding beliefs into codewords is not new without a novel online code-growth or decoding rule. [ECOC](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9501101).
- **Generic deep encoder + ART, ART + reservoir, XCS + deep features, NCA + autodiff, Hopfield + attention, e-prop + neuromorphic hardware, world-model + evolution, fuzzy + neural, and neural-network + blackboard:** all have direct prior-art collisions in HY04–HY17; do not promote by naming them differently.
- **Predictive delta propagation with hand-authored dependency edges:** already a standard incremental computation approach. Only the learned validity/invalidation mechanism remains as a question; if learned edges are unsound or audits erase savings, reject.
- **SOM/GNG over modern embeddings; Oja updates over frozen features; ART novelty heads; Hebbian/RBF kernels; broader probabilistic circuits; extra-context or larger-memory versions of existing models:** useful baselines/components, no distinct architecture claim.
- **Constraint Crystal, Causal Mechanism Loom, Morphogenetic Tissue, Event Ecology, and Scale-Free Abstraction Reactor:** keep their adversarial audits above. Their respective cores overlap factor graphs/CDCL, SCM/VCD, NEAT/NCA, XCS, and IBP/Slot Attention/BLT/DreamCoder. They survive only as sharply bounded experiments, not broad novelty claims.

## Open questions

- No new architecture class has survived the combined collision audit yet. Which primitive can add a broad capability without reducing to a better index or a known learning/search system?
- Can a continuous predictive-prototype index outperform SDE's adaptive predictive state representation on noisy/high-dimensional streams, or is its graph purely an implementation detail?
- Is any learned dependency validity mechanism sound enough to save computation when execution/provenance graphs are unavailable, or does explicit symbolic tracking always win?
- What older architecture relied on technology that changed materially, rather than on a structural assumption already replaced by a modern successor?
- Which computational substrates (phase-coupled oscillators, analog/chemical systems, developmental encodings) provide a capability advantage measurable beyond energy or hardware novelty?
- Does broad usefulness require a scalable compositional representation, or can a fundamentally different unit avoid that assumption?
- Can any specified learner produce deterministic, non-vacuous validity sets from sparse dynamics data beyond Taylor-model bounds and invariant-measure or trajectory-level conformal prediction? The C012 pilot only reproduced a known recurrence; novelty confidence for a distinct solution is very low.

## Next research actions

1. Continue the separate prior-art, adversarial, and invention passes, then incorporate their findings only after lead verification.
2. Search neglected physical/dynamical and pre-2000 architectures against the numbered slate; keep rejections and clear “too early” cases.
3. Do not promote PTM, PDL, Soar chunking, Copycat revision, or outcome-basin/homeostatic control as architecture classes without a mechanism beyond their nearest predecessors.
4. If an architecture-level survivor appears, first run its smallest CPU falsification with matched baselines. PTM's proposed first test is a 5×5 aliased maze with a mid-run dynamics change plus tests-only/topology-only ablations, but SDE prior art is a gate.
5. Before any later GPU run, query live GPU memory/utilization and active processes; identify whether Claude/research is using it, stay near 5.5 GB VRAM or below, leave at least 1 GB headroom, and record runtime/peak memory/shared use. No GPU experiment is planned or running now.
6. Do not spend more on the C012 residual-plus-Lipschitz recurrence; imCP (2026) proves that method family directly. Reopen only for a distinct, specified sound/local validity learner and compare it formally against Taylor models, imCP, and trajectory-level conformal methods.
7. Continue archaeology beyond Ashby/DFT into second-order cybernetics, anticipatory systems, autopoiesis, and viable-system architectures; promote none without a lead-verified mechanism and prior-art check.

## Continuation log — second archaeology and hybrid pass (2026-09-27)

**State:** Candidate numbering remains C001–C031. This pass did not add a new architecture claim: the most interesting revivals below are either still active research or have direct modern implementations. No experiment was run. Work was literature-only and CPU-side; no GPU process was started. Before any future GPU work, take a fresh device/process snapshot because the earlier snapshot cannot attribute desktop VRAM use to a research agent.

### Old architecture revival audits

#### Dynamic Field Theory / Dynamic Neural Fields (Amari/Wilson–Cowan lineage)

- **What the old architecture computes:** A field is a continuous activity distribution over a feature coordinate such as position, color, velocity, or an action parameter. Local excitation and broader inhibition create stable peaks; recurrent dynamics select, retain, transform, and sequence those peaks. Coupled fields can bind attributes through shared index dimensions and coordinate-transform/gain fields. The unit of computation is the evolving field pattern, not a token or a static feature vector.
- **Historical strengths and limits:** DFT offered real-time, sensorimotor-grounded representations and was demonstrated for online object learning on a robot with very few views. The hard parts were choosing the dimensions and coupling kernels, manually tuning field parameters, and keeping the state space low-dimensional enough to simulate and interpret. These are design and scaling limits, not simply insufficient 1980s compute.
- **What changed:** Modern GPUs can simulate larger field banks and support differentiable parameter fitting; modern encoders can provide robust feature proposals; event cameras/robot simulators and self-supervised interaction can supply richer experience. Yet DNF-specific online intrinsic plasticity was already published in 2017, a sensor-to-motor cognitive neuromorphic architecture was described in 2013, and DFT work on grounded nested phrases appeared in 2023/2024. It is therefore inaccurate to call the architecture abandoned or merely “too early.” The newer language result demonstrates a constrained grounded process model, not a general learned language system: its paper states that the language-processing front end is not modeled and reports a hand-specified cognitive architecture for nested relational phrases. [Dynamic fields and neuromorphic architecture](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2013.00276/full), [intrinsic plasticity for DNF](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5583149/), [robot object learning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2008.03.007), [grounded nested phrases](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-023-10007-7).
- **Verdict:** The core field dynamics, localist peaks, gain-field transformations, field coupling, and online gain/resting-level adaptation are known. More compute does not remove manual ontology, binding design, feature-coordinate choice, or the gap from a small hand-authored model to open-domain perception. This is a living specialized architecture, not a failed general architecture waiting for GPUs.
- **Hybrid screen — DNF + learned visual representation:** This coupling is directly instantiated, not just adjacent prior art. Grieben & Schöner (CogSci 2022) map headless VGG16 feature maps into localist neural fields using a learned BCM mapping; the fields support scene memory, category concepts, and guided visual search. ROBOVERINE (IROS 2024) extends the DFT + pretrained VGG16 interface to a simulated robot, online few-shot learning of new object categories, overt/covert attention, scene grammar, working memory, and goal-oriented behavior. A 2003 NeurIPS model already coupled a growing self-organizing state layer, local Hebbian action-conditioned transitions, and dynamic-field planning. The exact “encoder → fields ↔ active search/action” hybrid and the world-model + field planner are therefore occupied. The remaining possible work is a materially new, specified uncertainty-aware sampling/update law, not a new DNF/encoder pairing. [Grieben & Schöner, 2022](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8k85s8nc), [ROBOVERINE 2024 preprint](https://dynamicfieldtheory.org/upload/file/1731322090_1a5745b05d2c973a7943/GriebenSehringEtAl2024IROS_preprint.pdf), [Toussaint, NeurIPS 2003](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2003/hash/28b60a16b55fd531047c0c958ce14b95-Abstract.html), [deep dynamic visuomotor network](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02444).
- **Smallest falsifier if revisited:** In a CPU simulator with symbolic object features first, then a common frozen vision encoder, test partially occluded target selection under a controlled feature-distribution shift. Compare fixed DNF, DNF with intrinsic plasticity, encoder+GRU policy, and encoder+field policy under matched observations/actions and latency budgets. Measure success, false bindings, adaptation examples, field stability, and action count. The claim fails if intrinsic plasticity does not recover faster than fixed fields, or if field feedback does not improve over a recurrent policy at equal compute. GPU encoder use is optional and must follow the shared-VRAM protocol; the first test needs no GPU.

#### Cascade-Correlation and other constructive networks

- **Original mechanism:** Start from a minimal network, fit output weights, then train candidate hidden units to correlate with residual error, add one unit, freeze its incoming weights, and continue. The cascade turns earlier units into fixed detectors for later units. The original motivation was avoiding the moving-target problem and backpropagation’s then-slow training. [Fahlman & Lebiere, NeurIPS 1989](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1989/hash/69adc1e107f7f7d035d7baf04342e1ca-Abstract.html).
- **Was it bad or early?** Faster matrix hardware and modern automatic differentiation remove some original optimization and implementation pressure, and parallel hardware can score many candidate units at once. But the serial add-one-at-a-time structure is still hard to batch; frozen feature detectors limit global refinement; each new unit may see all earlier units, so inference/storage can grow quadratically; and the old algorithm optimizes a supervised residual rather than a broad self-supervised objective. These are not all cured by a faster GPU. Recurrent cascade-correlation was also shown to have representational limitations, not just compute cost. [Giles et al., recurrent cascade-correlation limitations](https://doi.org/10.1109/72.392247).
- **Modern status:** Constructive and cascade variants remain in papers and specialized applications, but their central growth rule is established and does not appear to have displaced static deep networks.
