Modern relatives include AdaNet, which adaptively learns both network structure and weights with data-dependent generalization guarantees; Progressive Neural Networks, which freeze earlier task columns and add lateral-connected columns; and Deep Cascade Learning, which applies bottom-up cascade training to convolutional networks. These show that modern compute and optimization did revive parts of the constructive agenda, while also making structural growth an established field rather than an unoccupied architecture class. [AdaNet, ICML 2017](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/cortes17a.html), [Progressive Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04671), [Deep Cascade Learning, TNNLS 2018](https://doi.org/10.1109/TNNLS.2018.2805098).
- **Verdict / experiment gate:** Historical speed claims against 1980s backprop are not evidence of contemporary superiority. A fair CPU experiment would use a streaming function with changing smooth and discontinuous components, equal cumulative parameters and update FLOPs, and compare Cascade-Correlation, a growing RBF/GNG model, expanding MLP, and a fixed MLP with replay. Measure plasticity after long streams, old-function retention, growth cost, inference cost, and sample efficiency. Reject if frozen detectors force unbounded growth or if dynamic growth fails to retain an advantage after compute matching. Not worth a broad architecture claim now.

#### Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH)

- **Original mechanism:** Generate low-order polynomial candidate units from subsets of input variables, fit them, score on a holdout/regularity criterion, retain selected units, and repeat in layers. Structure selection is part of learning rather than a topology fixed before training. Early work could construct multilayer polynomial models on small computers. [Ivakhnenko 1968 record](https://ndlsearch.ndl.go.jp/en/books/R100000136-I1574231875460562432), [self-organization in control, 1970](https://doi.org/10.1016/0005-1098(70)90092-0).
- **Was it bad or early?** More compute makes candidate fitting and scoring cheaper, but the search over variable subsets still grows rapidly, and validation-driven growth can overfit a small or shifting sample. This is not only speculation: a 1988 statistical study reported sensitivity to data partition and regularity criteria, weaker performance than regression on some noisy/nonlinear/multivariate small-sample cases, and potentially divergent extrapolations. Polynomial cross terms are a strong bias for smooth low-dimensional regression but a poor default for raw images, language, or compositional programs. Modern feature encoders and differentiable architecture search help with some front-end/search cost, but then GMDH's distinctive polynomial selection is no longer doing the broad perceptual work. [Green, Reichelt & Bradbury 1988](https://doi.org/10.2307/2531895).
- **Modern status / verdict:** GMDH remains in domain-specific forecasting, engineering, and hybrid modeling. Modern GMDH variants are direct revivals, so “self-organizing network growth” is established. Its likely niche is interpretable low-dimensional system identification, not a replacement general model class. A cheap test is a synthetic dynamical system with known sparse polynomial interactions and varying sample size/noise; compare GMDH, sparse polynomial regression, symbolic regression, and a small MLP under equal model-selection data. The claim is falsified if selection instability or validation cost erases its sample-efficiency/interpretability advantage. [ML-based GMDH variant](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40747-021-00480-0).
- **Addendum:** See AR-79 for a 2026 source check of self-organizing polynomial descendants and a smaller first CPU probe on a favorable compositional interaction target. That probe does not complete the planned sparse-regression/symbolic-regression/MLP comparison, nor validate performance outside the selected synthetic function.

#### CMAC / cerebellar model articulation controller

- **Original mechanism:** Quantize overlapping regions of a continuous input/control space to a small set of memory addresses; sum the corresponding table values to approximate a function. Updating only active locations gives fast local adaptation and simple lookup. This was proposed for high-degree-of-freedom manipulator control. [Albus 1975, NIST archive](https://www.nist.gov/publications/new-approach-manipulator-control-cerebellar-model-articulation-controller-cmac1).
- **Was it bad or early?** More RAM and fast parallel reads help with table capacity and control latency. They do not remove the curse of dimensionality, address collisions, dependence on hand-designed tilings, or the locality/generalization tradeoff. A deep encoder may reduce the address dimension, but latent drift then invalidates stored addresses unless the encoder is frozen or memory is remapped.
- **Modern status / verdict:** CMAC is still used for fast adaptive control. Deep CMAC, recurrent CMAC, neural-network+CMAC controllers, and hierarchical mixture-of-experts + CMAC are established, so this obvious hybrid is not a new architecture. The narrow useful question is whether a stable learned latent address map can retain local online adaptation under plant drift with lower memory than CMAC's hand-designed tiling and less forgetting than a global controller. [Hierarchical CMAC for multi-task RL](https://doi.org/10.1016/0921-8890(95)00005-Z), [hybrid neural network–CMAC controller](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2020.00695).
- **Small CPU falsifier:** Simulate a multi-joint control problem with one joint’s dynamics changing mid-run. Compare fixed-tiling CMAC, adaptive CMAC, a small MLP, and a common-encoder/CMAC variant. Match memory bytes and observations; report tracking error, stability violations, samples to recover, and memory growth. Do not claim a new general architecture if the benefit is limited to low-dimensional control.

#### Sparse Distributed Memory (SDM) and the 2023 continual-learning revival

- **Original mechanism:** Kanerva’s 1988 SDM sparsely samples random hard locations from a huge binary address space. A query selects locations within a Hamming-distance radius; a write increments/decrements each selected location’s per-bit counters, and a read sums the selected counters and thresholds each output bit. Overlap makes retrieval tolerant of address and data noise, while also creating interference between unrelated patterns. This is not nearest-neighbor lookup: each item is distributed over many overlapping locations. The NASA/RIACS report is a contemporaneous implementation analysis of Kanerva’s book, not the book itself. [Rogers, NASA/RIACS Technical Report 88.32 (1988)](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19890017031/downloads/19890017031.pdf).
- **Modern revival:** Bricken et al. (ICLR 2023) translated an SDM-inspired circuit into a modified MLP (SDMLP). Its top-k activation forms sparse input-dependent subnetworks; L2 normalization, positive weights, no bias terms, an annealed broad-to-sparse competition schedule, and SGD without momentum address neuron specialization and stale optimizer updates. The authors report class-incremental learning without task labels or replay on their tested benchmarks. This is not a direct implementation of Kanerva's original enormous address table; it is a sparse activation/learning-rule adaptation. Main Split-CIFAR results use 256-dimensional embeddings from a frozen, ImageNet32-pretrained ConvMixer and train for long per-task epochs; the paper has pixel/no-pretraining ablations, but the main continual-learning result does not establish a general end-to-end perceptual learner. [ICLR 2023 paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=JknGeelZJpHP), [arXiv version and experiment details](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11934).
- **2026 update:** Selective Subnetwork Distillation (SSD) explicitly targets SDMLP's cross-task knowledge-transfer and representational-capacity bottlenecks by distilling across active subnetworks using neuron activations/connectivity. This is evidence that modernized SDM-style continual learning is an active family, and that task isolation trades off against transfer. It lowers novelty for any “sparse memory prevents forgetting” proposal. [Xue et al., AAAI 2026](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v40i32.39960).
- **Was it bad or early?** The hardware limitation was explicit: the 1988 NASA/RIACS report says SDM’s compute and memory demands made full-scale implementation impractical on ordinary sequential machines and describes the Connection Machine-2 as enabling near-full-scale experiments through massive parallelism. Modern CPUs/GPUs and bit-packed Hamming operations ease that throughput bottleneck. They do not remove the address-radius tradeoff: too few active locations give weak recall; a wide radius raises overlap and cross-talk; storage/write cost grows with address count and value width. Modern learned encoders can supply addresses, but embedding drift changes memory neighborhoods. Retrieval also supplies no compositional reasoning by itself. The SDMLP continual learner is a sparse MLP inspired by SDM principles, not a direct implementation or proof that classical SDM scales to broad intelligence. [Rogers, 1988](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19890017031/downloads/19890017031.pdf).
- **Related older/current prior art:** Dynamic Sparse Distributed Memory (ECCV 2022) is closer to Kanerva's associative-memory idea than SDMLP: it learns partially overlapping representation clusters online from nonstationary streams and prunes by local density, explicitly targeting task-free continual learning. A separate 2021 fruit-fly-inspired circuit combines sparse coding with partial freezing/local associative updates, another direct collision for sparse-address continual learning. SDMLP experiments also use frozen feature embeddings in key results, so its continual-learning mechanism should be judged separately from perception. [DSDM, ECCV 2022](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2022/papers_ECCV/html/8170_ECCV_2022_paper.php), [fruit-fly continual learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07617).
- **2026 follow-up caveat:** Selective Subnetwork Distillation (SSD) claims no replay or task labels, but its pseudocode takes a task-indexed dataset D_t, sweeps D_(t-1) to calculate teacher activation frequencies, and then trains on D_t. Unless those old examples are replaced by continuously maintained activity counts, this procedure has explicit task boundaries and revisits old data. SSD describes itself as structural routing; the concrete algorithm selects frequent teacher neurons and applies hidden-activation and output-logit distillation to a student. The pseudocode does not clearly specify whether it adds persistent cross-task edges or just distills selected activations, so call it a sparse-network continual-distillation method pending implementation-level clarification. Do not cite its abstract as proof of task-free or replay-free operation without resolving the protocol. [AAAI 2026 paper](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v40i32.39960).
- **Verdict / experiment gate:** The revival is technically substantive for continual learning, but the primitive and the 2022/2023/2026 variants are known. A reproduction would be useful only if it tests distribution shifts beyond static class-incremental benchmarks, with matched memory and genuinely task-free boundaries; compare DSDM, SDMLP, the fruit-fly model, SSD, replay, and sparse/expanding-network baselines. It is not a new class candidate here.

### Hybrid audit additions

| ID | Coupling | Why it looked complementary | Closest prior art / disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| HY18 | DNF recurrent selection and working memory ↔ learned perception encoder, with field state choosing the next sensory query | DNF offers stateful competition and embodied coordinates; encoder offers high-dimensional perceptual features. The feedback loop could make perception active instead of a one-way feature pipeline. | Direct collision: CogSci 2022 maps pretrained VGG16 into DNF fields with learned BCM links for scene memory/search; ROBOVERINE (IROS 2024) uses DFT + pretrained VGG16 in a simulated robot with online few-shot categories, scene grammar, working memory, and active vision. Toussaint 2003 already couples learned action-conditioned world models and field planning. **Reject as a new hybrid**; only a distinct online uncertainty/sampling rule could reopen it. |
| HY19 | Cascade-Correlation feature growth ↔ SDM/SDMLP sparse subnetworks | Constructive growth could add residual features while sparse routing isolates tasks, combining adaptation with reduced interference. | SDMLP already grows sparse task-specific subnetworks through top-k activation; DSDM directly grows/prunes semi-distributed memory clusters online; progressive/expanding networks and cross-task distillation are established, including 2026 SSD. The capacity-vs-transfer tension is known. **Demote**; do not fuse two known mechanisms by name. |
| HY20 | Chemical reaction network learning ↔ neural or digital feature extraction | Chemical dynamics might provide a compact online learner after an upstream feature encoder; digital perception could remove raw-pixel burden. | Chemical implementations of perceptrons, neural ODEs, and Boltzmann machines predate the new work. Jaffard & Sbalzarini (2026 arXiv preprint) prove a deterministic mass-action CRN without hidden layers can learn a classification setup with regret guarantees and report handwritten-digit simulation results better than a comparable hidden-layer SNN. Their model uses a selection phase over feature subsets and expert-weight species; it does not establish a physical chemical computer, broad perception, or lower wall-clock/energy once input preparation and readout are charged. **Interesting computational result; known substrate family, not a new architecture class.** [2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12060). |

### Unconventional-computation screen — verified negative results

- **Phase-coded/phase-locked oscillator memory:** established periodic-attractor and phase-pattern associative-memory work; overlaps the notebook's Resonance Binding. Do not rename oscillator synchronization as a new memory class. [Aoyagi & Nomura](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9812198), [Baird 1989](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1989/file/3644a684f98ea8fe223c713b77189a77-Paper.pdf).
- **Billiard-ball/conservative computation:** Fredkin–Toffoli conservative logic established reversible, collision-based computation. It overlaps Conservation Flow; search/layout optimization would be the learner and thus a separate search problem. [Fredkin & Toffoli](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01857727).
- **Heteroclinic itineraries / winnerless competition:** stable saddle-to-saddle sequences are an established computation and temporal coding mechanism; overlaps Temporal Braid/Multi-Clock. [Afraimovich et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/nlin/0304016), [perturbed heteroclinic computation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physleta.2005.08.013).
- **Diffractive optical networks:** experimentally demonstrated trainable diffractive layers are important hardware work but implement learned neural transformations optically; hardware medium alone does not change the learning architecture. [Lin et al., Science 2018](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat8084).
- **Chemical reaction networks, photonic reservoirs, excitable-media wave logic, and algorithmic self-assembly:** all have established computation/learning precedents. Their remaining question is a measured task-level advantage after counting reset/forgetting, I/O transduction, noise, physical training cycles, material complexity, and matched digital baselines. [Molecular-scale learning review](https://doi.org/10.1039/D2NR06202J), [chemical learning/reconfigurability](https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.202201866), [photonic reservoir](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.7219), [reaction-diffusion logic](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chaos.2004.07.021), [Tile Assembly Model thesis](https://thesis.caltech.edu/1866/).
- **Chemical-network paper scope caveat:** the 2026 result is a submitted preprint, its theoretical claim is about a particular deterministic mass-action construction, and its numerical evidence is simulated classification. It is a stronger proof-of-learning result than generic chemical-neuron analogies, but does not yet demonstrate a wet-lab learner or establish efficiency over modern digital ML. [Paper and version/date](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12060).

### Updated continuation gates

1. Two independent source-check reports on DFT/SDM modernization and constructive architectures have been integrated and lead-verified; keep their resulting rejections unless a new mechanism is found.
2. Continue archaeology in old architectures not yet analyzed in depth, emphasizing whether modern tools actually remove a historical bottleneck rather than merely making a known method faster.
3. Keep the 31-card slate stable unless a distinct mechanism is found; add screened old architectures as archaeology records, not falsely novel candidates.
4. No experiment is justified yet by this pass. If the DNF or CMAC control probe becomes worth running, make it CPU-only and benchmark against direct modern neighbors; do not use a GPU unless a learned image encoder becomes necessary.
5. Before every GPU run, inspect current VRAM and processes, account for another research workload without interrupting it, target at most about 5.5 GB VRAM, preserve around 1 GB of total headroom, and record utilization/sharing and duration. No experiment has used the GPU in this research.

### Lead-verified source-check correction

- DNF + deep vision and DNF + action-conditioned planning were already occupied more directly than the initial HY18 note suggested. In ROBOVERINE, a pretrained headless VGG16 feature extractor feeds a learned BCM map into 3D fields over spatial position and visual category; the fields handle active attention, goal search, scene grammar, and online category learning. The authors simulate it in Webots and acknowledge learning only a small number of categories, so the proof is a compelling specialized process model, not evidence of broad scaling. [ROBOVERINE, IROS 2024 preprint](https://dynamicfieldtheory.org/upload/file/1731322090_1a5745b05d2c973a7943/GriebenSehringEtAl2024IROS_preprint.pdf).
- The direct active-visual-search hybrid dates at least to Grieben & Schöner's 2022 DFT/DNN paper, where VGG feature maps are mapped into localist neural fields for scene memory and guided search. The older NeurIPS 2003 model directly learns action/perception relations in a growing self-organizing layer and uses a dynamic field for planning. Therefore HY18 is rejected as a novelty claim, not merely assigned low confidence. [2022 DFT/DNN paper](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8k85s8nc), [Toussaint 2003](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2003/hash/28b60a16b55fd531047c0c958ce14b95-Abstract.html).
- SDM revival has another direct architecture precedent absent from the first pass: ECCV 2022 DSDM grows/prunes overlapping representation clusters for task-free online continual learning. The 2023 SDMLP is a trainable sparse MLP recipe; its paper's stated results depend on a feature representation and do not make it a general end-to-end perceiver. This lowers novelty of sparse associative memory as a continual-learning class. [DSDM](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2022/papers_ECCV/html/8170_ECCV_2022_paper.php), [SDMLP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11934).
- The 2026 SSD method's “no replay/no task labels” claim must be qualified: Algorithm 1 uses a task stream and computes prior-task neuron activation counts from D_(t-1). This could be implemented by storing online counts during that task, but that alternative protocol is not what the pseudocode literally specifies; its replay/task-free status needs an apples-to-apples reproduction before being trusted. [AAAI 2026 proceedings PDF](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/39960/43921).


### Old architecture archaeology — Boltzmann machines and the sampling bottleneck

**Disposition:** Known model family with a meaningful hardware revival; no new architecture candidate added. This is a clear “partly too early, partly intrinsically difficult” case. The sampler-throughput bottleneck can be engineered away for certain sparse topologies, but good mixing, biased learning shortcuts, inference cost, and generalization remain.

1. **Original mechanism (1980s).** A Boltzmann machine is a recurrent network of stochastic binary units with symmetric interactions. Its state has an energy; asynchronous unit updates sample a distribution over states. Training adjusts weights so correlations under data-clamped states match correlations under the freely running model. Inference is iterative settling/sampling, not a one-way feed-forward pass. [Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1207/s15516709cog0901_7).
2. **Why it struggled.** Exact maximum-likelihood learning needs model-phase expectations under the equilibrium distribution, whose partition function and exact expectations are exponential in unit count. MCMC can mix very slowly, especially in multimodal energy landscapes, and learning repeatedly pays for sampling. Mean-field approximations reduce computation but add approximation error and can fail to converge in general; Kappen and Rodríguez’s 1997 mean-field plus linear-response method reduced the stated complexity from exponential to cubic for its formulation, but this did not make all models easy. [Kappen & Rodríguez (1997)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/1997/hash/0e4e946668cf2afc4299b462b812caca-Abstract.html).
3. **Modernizations already tried.** RBMs constrain the graph to make blocks conditionally independent and parallelizable. Contrastive divergence (CD) starts chains at data and truncates the run, trading sampling cost for estimator bias; Teh et al. explicitly note possible spurious fixed points. Persistent CD, mean-field inference, wake-sleep/recognition networks, and DBN/DBM pretraining or recognition passes all addressed parts of the training/inference expense. DBMs still faced expensive bidirectional inference: the 2010 method reports naive mean-field inference could be 25–50× a single bottom-up DBN pass, then adds a recognition network and a few mean-field corrections to reduce that cost. [Teh et al. (2003)](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume4/teh03a/teh03a.pdf), [Salakhutdinov & Larochelle (2010)](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/proceedings/papers/v9/salakhutdinov10a/salakhutdinov10a.pdf).
4. **What technology changed.** Faster digital logic, FPGA parallelism, and sparse graph hardware can produce many low-cost probabilistic updates, while larger datasets and accelerators make training runs less prohibitive. But the 2023 result does not show that an ordinary GPU removes the serial-update/mixing problem: it uses a hardware-aware sparse DBM on a probabilistic-bit FPGA, with a CPU computing correlation updates. Their graph permits concurrent updates to non-neighboring units; density and topology are chosen around Pegasus/Zephyr FPGA constraints. [Niazi et al. (2023; v2 2024)](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.10728).
5. **What remains hard.** Higher sample throughput does not guarantee independent/equilibrium samples: their 4,264-p-bit Pegasus graph needs roughly CD-10^4 sweeps to mix empirically; CD-10^2–10^3 degrades mixing. Sparse hardware-aware graphs may alter representational capacity, and topology/hardware limits remain. The paper’s CIFAR result uses 100 grayscale training images, 100 binary samples per image, and reports no successful generation; it is not evidence of broad-scale image modeling. Its MNIST result is more meaningful (full 60,000-image dataset; about 90% test accuracy with ~30,000 parameters, compared with an RBM needing millions for a similar accuracy), but its generative quality and task-level comparisons are narrow. Reported 50–64 billion flips/s is sampler throughput, not by itself end-to-end training cost including CPU updates and data transfer. These distinctions matter when judging the revival.
6. **Closest hybrid and exact coupling (HY21).** The existing hybrid couples a sparse Ising/p-bit sampler to a classical CPU: the sampler evolves the binary state and returns correlations; CPU code applies the positive-minus-negative phase weight update, then sends weights back. It creates a high-throughput Gibbs-sampling path, but the division of labor and architecture are directly published. It is a hardware revival of Boltzmann learning, not a novel model class. The paper’s headline comparisons also change topology, parameter count, and sampler budget, so they do not isolate a general representational advantage of DBM over RBM. [Niazi et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.10728).
7. **Potentially new part / novelty judgment.** No distinct algorithmic mechanism survives this review. “Use a faster sampler,” “use sparse hardware,” “use asynchronous p-bits,” “combine an energy model with an Ising machine,” and “use sampling for generative learning” are occupied. A future proposal would need a different, explicit learning or inference rule—not only a new physical realization or a sparser graph. Novelty confidence for the broad revival as an architecture: near zero.
8. **Smallest falsifiable experiment.** If the hardware question becomes actionable, first use a CPU toy distribution with known modes (e.g., a two-dimensional multimodal mixture and parity-like binary distributions). At matched parameter count and wall-clock/sample budget compare CD-1, persistent CD, longer Gibbs chains, and a tempering baseline; report mode coverage, effective sample size per second, held-out log likelihood where estimable, and sensitivity to graph degree. Then, only if sampler quality is competitive, compare a physical p-bit implementation with end-to-end I/O and CPU update costs included. The architecture-level claim fails if its apparent learning benefit disappears at matched compute, if mode coverage stays poor, or if extra sweeps raise time without improving held-out density or generation. **No experiment was run in this pass.**

**HY21 audit entry — CPU optimizer ↔ sparse Ising sampler.** Complementarity: ordinary digital arithmetic is flexible for parameter updates; asynchronous probabilistic hardware accelerates stochastic state evolution. The exact coupling is already the published CPU–FPGA loop above. The behavior differs from running Gibbs sampling purely in software mainly through sampler throughput/energy, while the objective and model remain Boltzmann learning. Keep as evidence that a historical hardware limitation can be relieved; reject as an architecture novelty claim.

**Source audit note:** Do not flatten “Boltzmann machines were abandoned because GPUs were too weak” into one story. The slow negative phase is both a hardware throughput problem and an algorithmic mixing problem. A custom sampler has demonstrated the former can improve dramatically on selected sparse graphs; it has not established that equilibrium learning, useful scaling, or modern perception/generalization is solved.

**Resource / experiment log (2026-09-27):** Literature review only; CPU/web research; no GPU experiment or local training run; runtime and peak VRAM not applicable; no Codex-owned GPU process. No current GPU snapshot was needed because no GPU work was started. For any future run, take a fresh process and VRAM snapshot first and keep within the shared-use target.

### Old architecture archaeology — predictive coding and wake-sleep

**Disposition:** Both mechanisms have modern continuations; neither is a new broad model class. The strongest historical lesson is that missing compute was only one obstacle. Predictive coding’s iterative settling can remain slow on ordinary accelerators, while wake-sleep’s inference/generative mismatch is an objective and approximation problem. Their modern forms already overlap with local learning, continual sequence models, generative replay, program synthesis, and uncertainty-guided rehearsal.

#### Predictive coding (PC)

- **Original computation:** Hierarchical generative units send predictions down; prediction-error units represent mismatches between predicted and observed activity, and those errors update latent states and synapses. Rao and Ballard’s 1999 visual-cortex model used this as an account of receptive-field responses; PC theory predates deep-learning dominance. [Rao & Ballard, 1999](https://www.nature.com/articles/nn0199_79).
- **Why it struggled:** It requires iterative state inference/settling, often for every input and training update. Small early demonstrations and limited compute narrowed the experiments, but modern compute alone does not make repeated settling cheaper than a feed-forward/backward pass on GPU hardware. Recent critical analysis finds contemporary PC variants have runtime lower bounds at least comparable to backpropagation, even where parameter updates can match backprop. Treat that as one published analysis, not a universal impossibility theorem. [Zahid et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02658).
- **Modernization already achieved:** Modern autodiff theory clarified the connection: PC can approximate exact backprop gradients along arbitrary computation graphs, and particular variants can recover them under their assumptions. That both validates PC as a local implementation route and lowers novelty for “local prediction errors replace global backprop.” [Millidge et al., 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04182), [Salvatori et al., 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7610561/).
- **Continual-learning prior art:** Annabi et al. compare online PC-RNN rules with reservoir/conceptor and replay methods on sequential trajectories, and explicitly test predictive coding for continual sequence modeling. This is an older direct precedent for PC-driven online learning, although replay and PC are compared as separate model branches in that study. [Annabi et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurorobotics/articles/10.3389/fnbot.2022.845955/full).
- **Assessment:** Modern hardware makes larger tests feasible; differentiability makes equivalence analyses possible; neither removes the state-settling cost. PC may be valuable for neuromorphic/local adaptation constraints, but that advantage must be measured on the target hardware and end-to-end workload.

#### Wake-sleep and offline consolidation

- **Original computation:** A Helmholtz machine has a generative model and a recognition/inference model. “Wake” updates generative weights from data-driven latent samples; “sleep” generates synthetic samples and uses them to train recognition weights. [Hinton, Dayan, Frey & Neal, 1995](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~hinton/absps/ws.pdf).
- **Why it struggled:** The phase-specific updates do not generally optimize one shared likelihood objective; sleep samples from the model can poorly cover posterior states needed during waking inference. More compute increases sample count but cannot guarantee proposal quality or posterior coverage.
- **Modern descendants:** Reweighted Wake-Sleep uses multiple inference samples and importance weighting to improve gradient estimates and likelihood, addressing the estimator/recognition issue directly. VAE reparameterized variational learning is another related modernization, but should not be mislabeled as the same wake-sleep algorithm. Wake-sleep also remains useful outside neural density estimation: DreamCoder alternates task-solving and library growth with imagined/replayed tasks to learn reusable program abstractions. [Bornschein & Bengio, 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2751), [Kingma & Welling, 2013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114), [Ellis et al., 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08381).
- **Sleep-like replay prior art:** Tadros et al. (2022) interleave ANN task training with sleep-like offline noisy activity and local Hebbian-type updates, reporting reduced forgetting across several datasets. This is not the original Helmholtz wake-sleep objective, but it occupies broad “offline sleep replay plus local consolidation” claims. [Tadros et al., 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-34938-7).

#### Hybrid audit — HY22: PC inference/learning ↔ generative sleep replay

- **Source mechanisms:** PC contributes hierarchical prediction errors and iterative local state/weight updates; wake-sleep or continual generative replay contributes synthetic rehearsal when current data has moved on.
- **Exact coupling proposed for screening:** During online learning, cache compact layerwise residual statistics and a calibrated reliability estimate. During offline replay, generate prior-task sequences; weight each sample’s local consolidation by (a) whether it exposes a consequential prediction error and (b) whether the generator’s uncertainty estimate indicates that the synthetic sample is reliable. This attempts to avoid strengthening confident-looking but invalid self-generated examples while using local PC errors to route consolidation.
- **Prior-art collision and downgrade:** The broad coupling is no longer open: a 2025 arXiv preprint directly describes predictive-coding-based generative replay and compares it with VAE/backprop replay; 2022 PC continual-sequence work, sleep replay consolidation, and 2025 uncertainty-driven generative replay each occupy adjacent components. The 2025 PC-replay preprint is not treated here as validated evidence for its claimed accuracy gains, but it is direct prior art against novelty of “PC + generative sleep replay.” Uncertainty-driven replay is also already a named method family. [Nalagatla & Grandhe, 2025 preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.00619), [R2R, 2025 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04787).
- **What might remain distinct:** At most, a precisely defined reliability × prediction-error gate that changes *layerwise local plasticity* during offline rehearsal and uses calibration/coverage guarantees to control feedback loops. That is a narrow training rule, not a demonstrated new architecture. Novelty confidence: very low (~0.05); do not add it to the 31-card architecture slate.
- **Potential use:** Continual learning under distribution shift where old raw data cannot be stored, if generated rehearsal is useful but self-training drift is the dominant failure.
- **Likely failure modes:** PC’s settling cost may erase any replay benefit; generator calibration may be poor exactly on rare old modes; error × confidence gates can suppress useful high-surprise samples; replay weighting may duplicate uncertainty-based sampling; comparison can be confounded by optimizer/architecture differences.
- **Small CPU falsifier:** Train small sequential latent dynamical models on procedural trajectories with known rare modes and exact state labels. Compare PC without replay, PC with ordinary replay, PC with the reliability/error gate, VAE/reweighted-wake-sleep replay, and a PC+replay direct-prior-art baseline. Match model size, replay count, training examples, and wall-clock; report held-out sequence likelihood, old-mode coverage, retention after shifts, gate calibration, and total settling updates. The interaction is not worth pursuing if the gate loses at equal replay count, if confidence suppresses rare modes, or if any retention gain disappears after counting PC settling compute.
- **Status:** Prior-art search has found the core hybrid already. Keep this only as a falsifiable *mechanism ablation* if predictive coding independently earns a hardware/local-learning use case; do not market it as a new architecture.

**Updated archaeology ranking:** Boltzmann machines illustrate a hardware bottleneck that specialized samplers can materially reduce, but their learning mechanism is established. Predictive coding and wake-sleep show that newer optimization and data do not automatically eliminate algorithmic costs or objective mismatch. Neither case currently promotes a new architecture candidate. Literature only; no local training run and no GPU use in this pass.

### Boltzmann / Ising hybrid source-check correction — earlier direct precedents

The sparse-FPGA DBM revival must be placed in an already active hardware-learning line rather than treated as the first architecture/hardware combination.

- Aadit et al. introduced sparse, graph-colored Ising hardware in 2022 for probabilistic computing and optimization; its core contribution was the hardware/update schedule and throughput scaling, before the later DBM application. [Aadit et al., *Nature Electronics* 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41928-022-00774-2).
- Böhm et al. experimentally trained a small RBM with a time-multiplexed optoelectronic Ising machine in 2022. Noise injection was the exact sampler coupling that enabled approximate Boltzmann-temperature sampling; the 8×8 handwritten-digit task used 64 visible and 100 hidden units. This is direct prior art for an Ising sampler coupled to RBM weight learning, though much smaller than the later full-MNIST sparse DBM. [Böhm et al., *Nature Communications* 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-33441-3).
- A 2024 CMOS plus stochastic-magnetic-tunnel-junction prototype trained a 32-node, three-layer DBM on the full-adder truth table. Its aim was a proof of concept for asynchronous physical stochastic devices, not broad-scale image learning. [Singh et al., *Nature Communications* 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46645-6).
- A 2024 D-Wave study uses Equilibrium Propagation (EP) for supervised training on a physical Ising machine, including an MLP and a compact convolutional network mapped to chip connectivity. It adapts the nudge/free relaxation mechanism to a binary-spin annealer and reports MNIST/100-scale tasks. This directly occupies the seemingly attractive old-EP + modern Ising-hardware hybrid: its learning rule is physically aligned to relaxation, but the approach is already demonstrated and still entails chip embedding, repeated samples, and constrained binary states. [Laydevant, Marković & Grollier, *Nature Communications* 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46879-4).

**HY23 audit — Equilibrium Propagation ↔ physical Ising machine.** EP contributes a local two-phase learning rule; the Ising machine contributes native energy relaxation. Coupling: settle freely, perturb output states (“nudge”), settle again, estimate parameter updates from the state difference. This changes how gradients are obtained and lets hardware physics perform part of inference/credit assignment. Direct 2024 prior art exists, and the demonstrated model/data scale plus binary-state/annealing constraints limit the novelty and generality claim. **Reject as a new hybrid; retain as a historical bottleneck that modern hardware partially removed.**

**Revised HY21 novelty note:** “Use an Ising machine to accelerate Boltzmann sampling” is also directly established by 2022 sparse FPGA and noise-injected optoelectronic work. The 2023/2024 sparse-DBM contribution is an application-specific advance (hardware-aware sparse DBM training and conditional MNIST generation) inside that existing line, not a fresh sampler/optimizer coupling. The quantitative sampler result is relevant, while the broader architecture claim remains occupied. No hardware or training experiment was run here.

### Lead-verified correction — PC replay gate and direct hybrid prior art

The HY22 screening idea needs a tighter novelty boundary after primary-source review.

- **Direct PC-native replay and precision gate:** Fontaine & Alexandre’s predictive-coding neocortex model already implements sleep replay. It injects noise/cues into the top layer, pattern-completes a latent representation, then reinstates it in lower layers. To prevent bottom-up sensory error from undoing replay, it sets input-layer precision (and the corresponding error) to zero. This is a genuine precision switch, but it controls *sensory influence during replay*, not which memories get selected by calibrated uncertainty or prediction-error priority. Crucially, the paper calls the plastic update optional and says it does not use it because it is not studying episodic-memory consolidation; experiments are small MNIST digit-4/7 auto-associative recall, not continual learning. Thus do not claim the broad “precision-gated PC sleep replay” idea as new; the item-selection/plasticity-dose distinction is essential. [Fontaine & Alexandre, arXiv 2025; IJCNN 2025 version DOI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01987).
- **Uncertainty controls PC computation already:** Hybrid Predictive Coding combines amortized feed-forward inference with iterative PC settling and uses model uncertainty to adapt their relative influence/computation. This blocks generic claims that uncertainty-gated compute within a PC architecture is new. [Tschantz et al., *PLOS Computational Biology* 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10395865/).
- **PC plus generated old-task replay already implemented:** CLPC2 (Applied Soft Computing, 2026) couples a PC-trained classifier with VAE- or diffusion-generated samples from previous tasks. The replay schedule is task-driven and uses equal real/generated batch proportions in its reported setup, not a per-item uncertainty selector; nevertheless it is a direct continual-PC + generative replay collision. [Qiu et al., 2026](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1568494625015789).
- **Error-/utility-prioritized replay precedents:** Schillaci et al. already use prediction error to retain/replay episodes in continual learning. Barry & Love’s offline replay model learns which generated category samples to rehearse from their measured contribution to network performance. Both are outside PC-native sleep consolidation but show that “use error or value to choose replay” is not a new principle. [Schillaci et al., 2021](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13218-020-00700-8), [Barry & Love, 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9758580/).
- **Revised HY22:** The only plausible seam left is an experimentally specified joint rule that separates epistemic uncertainty from aleatoric noise and assigns both replay *content* and layerwise plasticity under a fixed offline compute budget in one continual PC learner. It must beat raw-PE replay, PC uncertainty-driven settling, performance-gain replay scheduling, and PC+VAE/diffusion replay at matched sleep updates. This is very narrow, low novelty, and not a new architecture class. Defer implementation until a literature check shows the precise rule is not already present. The unverified OpenReview lead from the subagent is not used as evidence.

### Old architecture archaeology — Adaptive Resonance Theory (ART/Fuzzy ART)

**Disposition:** ART was useful for its target niche and now has modern feature/graph/deep revivals. Hardware and self-supervised representations solve some old perception/throughput problems; they do not remove vigilance tuning, order sensitivity, coordinate dependence, or category growth. No new architecture candidate survives this pass.

- **Original mechanism:** ART stores category prototypes and compares each incoming pattern against them. Fuzzy ART complement-codes bounded inputs and uses elementwise-min/L1 match and a winner-selection rule. If the winning category’s match passes vigilance, its prototype is updated; otherwise a reset creates/searches another category. This lets online learning add new categories while preserving committed older ones. The 1991 Fuzzy ART paper describes fast, stable analog categorization and complement coding. [Carpenter, Grossberg & Rosen, 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0893-6080(91)90056-B); a later architecture description gives the online winner/vigilance/reset operation explicitly. [MPART, Kim et al., ICML 2021](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/kim21e/kim21e.pdf).
- **Why it was constrained:** Early ART systems had weaker perceptual features, small memory, and limited capacity to search many categories quickly. But the main limitations are architectural: high vigilance fragments data into many categories; low vigilance merges distinct patterns; category prototypes use an input-coordinate-dependent similarity rule; stream order and noise affect category creation; updating an encoder can invalidate prior category coordinates. More RAM/compute delays or speeds category search but does not choose a principled vigilance/geometry or prevent every noisy sample from becoming a new prototype.
- **What modern technology changed:** Deep/self-supervised vision encoders supply stronger feature vectors, and GPU vectorization can compare many prototypes at once. MPART (ICML 2021) directly maps pretrained BYOL features through parametric UMAP into bounded [0,1] features, complement-codes them, learns Fuzzy ART categories and a weighted topology, passes labels/uncertainty through the graph, and actively queries uncertain/representative incoming samples. This already combines modern representation learning, online ART, graph message passing, uncertainty, and active learning. Its experiments use an encoder/UMAP training phase; they do not show that ART itself learns robust raw pixels or eliminate category-count and feature-drift issues. [Kim et al., ICML 2021 paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/kim21e/kim21e.pdf), [supplement](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/kim21e/kim21e-supp.pdf).
- **Additional modern hybrids:** PAN (2023) combines pretrained CNN feature extraction, ART-II/BPART resonance and category memory, an experience pool, and gates for incremental knowledge updates; its evidence is primarily MNIST/Omniglot and is application-specific. DeepART (peer-reviewed 2025) inserts modified FuzzyART modules as fully connected or convolutional layers, uses local winner-take-all complement-coded updates, and uses a FuzzyARTMAP head for labels. Therefore “deep ART,” “CNN/ART,” “encoder + online resonance memory,” and “ART reduces forgetting” are not open broad architecture claims. [Zhang, Jiang & Xu, 2023](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/17483026231205009), [Petrenko et al., DeepART 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40472582/).
- **Vigilance adaptation is occupied:** Dynamic, per-category, uncertainty-aware, and iterative vigilance variants already exist. A modern proposal that merely lowers/raises vigilance based on confidence or noise would be a parameter-control variant; no new computational primitive was identified. Examples include [adaptive vigilance, 2013](https://doi.org/10.1109/IJCNN.2013.6706857), [uncertainty-aware interval type-2 fuzzy ART, 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2017.09.062), and [dynamic vigilance Fuzzy ART, 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2018.09.015).
- **Was ART bad or early?** Neither label alone fits. Its fast one-shot category creation and stable old prototypes remain attractive for online novelty/open-set tasks. Poor image representations and slower prototype search were partly historical; modern encoders and vector hardware help. Its vigilance/geometry/order tradeoffs persist and are not solved by more compute. ART is a specialist online category learner, not a demonstrated general replacement for deep representation learning.
- **Small falsifiable benchmark (no novelty claim):** Feed fixed, precomputed self-supervised features from a streaming class-incremental vision set to FuzzyART/FuzzyARTMAP. Compare (a) raw-pixel ART, (b) frozen-feature ART across a predeclared vigilance sweep and multiple stream orders, (c) online nearest prototypes, (d) a small online linear head, and (e) MPART/DeepART where reproducible. Match retained feature memory and query/compute budget. Report accuracy, false novelty/reset rates, category count and bytes, old-class retention after drift, sensitivity to order and vigilance, and inference/update latency. Falsify “modern features rescue ART” if it remains more sensitive or category-prolific than simple online prototypes at equal memory and fails to gain useful adaptation/retention. Use CPU on precomputed features; no GPU training is necessary for this test.
- **Hybrid audit HY24 — frozen self-supervised encoder ↔ ART category growth/topology:** The encoder provides semantic features; ART provides fast, local prototype updates; a graph supports neighborhood label transfer/querying. Exact combinations with BYOL+UMAP, ART, graph propagation, uncertainty, and active selection already exist (MPART); deep local ART modules are also direct prior art (DeepART). **Reject as a new hybrid.** Keep only the benchmark question: do better fixed features reduce ART’s category proliferation without increasing feature drift or erasing one-pass adaptation?

**Updated candidate slate:** Still C001–C031. No candidate was added for the PC replay gate, Ising/Equilibrium-Propagation hardware, or ART hybrids; each was demoted or retained as a bounded experiment because direct prior art is strong. The next useful archaeology targets are Adaptive Resonance variants only if the benchmark reveals an unexplained failure mode, plus unexamined pre-2000 architectures whose limitations were specifically hardware-bound. Literature-only updates; no experiment or GPU work was run.
