### Continuation log — replay boundary, adversarial re-ranking, and additional archaeology (2026-09-27)

#### Adversarial re-ranking of C026–C031

A fresh independent adversarial pass found no current candidate that warrants a **new broad architecture-class** claim. These estimates concern general architecture novelty, not possible application value.

| Rank for possible application work | Candidate | Novelty confidence | Main weakness |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | C029 / PDL, learned dependency-validity propagation | ~0.02 | Opaque-model invalidation remains a systems question; missing a dependency can silently stale an answer, while conservative audits may erase savings. |
| 2 | C031, violation-scoped homeostatic reorganization | ~0.02 | Local fault recovery might be useful, but ultrastability and fault-tolerant control already cover the trigger and reconfiguration pattern. |
| 3 | C027 / CCSC, counterexample-checked Soar chunking | ~0.01 | Soar chunking/filtering and CEGIS already cover the compile/check/repair loop. |
| 4 | C030, outcome-basin state machine | ~0.01 | Goal-conditioned bisimulation and set-based reachability goal abstractions cover its action-conditioned state signature. |
| 5 | C026 / PTM, predictive topology memory | ~0.01 | Predictive-state discovery and active test refinement already exist; the graph may only be a retrieval index. |
| 6 | C028 / LCRR, learned Copycat representation revision | ~0.01 | Copycat already revises representations during search; the proposed learned edit utility lacks a distinct edit calculus and learning rule. |

C030's closest collision is direct: goal-conditioned bisimulation learns state abstractions that preserve task behavior across goals, and a 2023 method discovers symbolic goal abstractions by grouping state sets with similar roles, approximating transitions through neural reachability, and refining abstractions while learning a hierarchical policy. Treat C030 as a rejected rediscovery unless it can show a concrete memory or interaction advantage over these methods. [Hansen-Estruch et al., ICML 2022](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/hansen-estruch22a.html); [Zadem et al., ICDL 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07675).

C031 is not ready for a useful falsifier because its mechanism leaves key decisions unspecified: how a violation is assigned to modules, which local parameters can change, how an update is accepted while preserving safety bands, and how intervention budgets are matched to global and model-based baselines. Without those, a simulation measures a hand-designed optimizer rather than C031. No simulation was run. If made precise, the smallest CPU study remains a three-loop plant with one actuator-gain fault; compare local reorganization, global ultrastability, adaptive PID, and model-based fault reconfiguration at matched probe budgets. Measure time outside viability bounds, recovery time, collateral change in unaffected loops, and false fault localization. Reject the application claim if localization does not improve the recovery/violation frontier. [Ashby, Design for a Brain](https://www.ashby.info/Ashby%20-%20Design%20for%20a%20Brain%20-%20The%20Origin%20of%20Adaptive%20Behavior.pdf); [Pitonakova (2013), ultrastable robotics](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/353115/); [example of online model identification and controller reconfiguration](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-47062-2_6).

The other checks consolidate existing rejection evidence: C026 overlaps predictive-state splitting and active test discovery; C027 overlaps Soar's overgeneralization filter and CEGIS; C028 overlaps Copycat/Metacat workspace revision plus learned codelet scheduling; C029 overlaps truth maintenance, Bayesian-network relevance updating, and incremental trace reuse. Retain them as benchmark prompts, not surviving broad architecture claims.

#### Replay novelty correction: uncertainty as a sampling energy is older than the PC/sleep idea

An ICLR 2022 submission appendix titled “Continual learning via uncertainty-based replay” treats predictive uncertainty as an energy landscape. It samples inputs from low-uncertainty regions by rejection sampling, labels them with the previous model, then replays them with the next task. Its example is two-task one-dimensional polynomial regression with a neural-network Gaussian-process kernel and no separate generator. This is a small proof-of-concept, not evidence for image-scale replay, calibrated epistemic uncertainty, predictive-coding learning, or layerwise plasticity allocation. It nevertheless closes the broad claim that uncertainty can drive pseudo-replay without a separate generative model. [ICLR 2022 submission appendix](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=u7UxOTefG2); the appendix is also reproduced in [Christian Henning's thesis](https://chrhenning.com/assets/pdf/PhD_Thesis.pdf).

The remaining PC-specific question is much narrower: can a PC learner distinguish epistemic uncertainty from irreducible/aleatoric error, then choose which episode to replay and how much plasticity to permit under a fixed offline-update budget? This is not a new replay principle and remains low novelty. If it earns implementation, use a CPU-scale compositional sequence stream with equal sleep updates and compare uniform replay, raw prediction-error priority, uncertainty selection, and marginal-utility selection. Measure retention, unseen-composition transfer, calibration, noise-driven false replay, and compute. Stop if it fails to beat strong selectors at equal updates or chases aleatoric noise.

“Replay to Remember” has now appeared in ECAI 2025 proceedings, first published online 25 August 2026. It combines a convolutional autoencoder, latent GMM, within-cluster dispersion thresholding, semantically guided synthetic replay, and cluster-level fine-tuning. This directly occupies cluster-uncertainty-guided generative replay; it remains a continual-learning pipeline rather than a new general computational class. Its performance claims should not be treated as settled without reproducing its task protocol, synthetic-data pipeline, and comparisons to strong continual-learning baselines. This caveat does not affect the prior-art collision. [Mandalika, Vardhan & Nambiar, ECAI 2025 proceedings (online 2026)](https://doi.org/10.3233/FAIA250808).

#### Old AI archaeology — blackboards, production systems, and dynamic rule execution

**Verdict: partly too early, partly intrinsically constrained.** Hearsay-II used a time-shared PDP-10 for speech-understanding. Modern processors, memory, simulators, and learned perception make larger workloads practical. But the 1980 authors already identified the enduring issue: uncertain evidence creates many competing hypotheses and knowledge-source actions, so search can grow combinatorially. Hearsay-II's scheduler considered the global hypothesis state, credibility, anticipated action, and processing time/cost; the main limitation was not just processor speed. Development ended with the DARPA speech program, while the system showed useful results within its constrained domain. [Erman et al., “The Hearsay-II Speech-Understanding System” (1980)](https://mas.cs.umass.edu/Documents/Erman_Hearsay80.pdf).

- **Blackboards:** independent knowledge sources post partial hypotheses to a shared state; an agenda scheduler chooses what to execute. This accommodates heterogeneous inference modules and opportunistic control. Central blackboard traffic can still slow work that specialized internal data structures would handle more efficiently; more compute does not make scheduler value estimates reliable or eliminate action-set growth.
- **Assumption-based truth maintenance:** ATMSs compile alternative assumption supports for derived claims. The same compilation can cause exponential label growth, and compact-label variants were studied in 1991. Hardware helps only when the required support family is not itself combinatorially large. [Collins & DeCoste, “CATMS: An ATMS Which Avoids Label Explosions” (AAAI 1991)](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/1991/AAAI91-044.pdf).
- **Rule matching and dynamic schedules:** Rete caches partial matches; TREAT and later Rete* methods make different memory/runtime tradeoffs. Current Drools Phreak delays matching, batches updates, tracks node/segment/rule readiness, and puts enabled goals on a priority agenda. Therefore lazy event-driven rules, incremental rule matching, and dynamic agenda order are established mechanisms. [Forgy, Rete (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(82)90020-0); [Drools Phreak documentation](https://docs.drools.org/latest/drools-docs/drools/rule-engine/index.html).
- **Modern learned revival:** Neural Production Systems (NeurIPS 2021) pair object-centric perception with differentiable production rules. Query/key matching binds a rule to entities; a rule-specific MLP updates entity properties. This supplies perception and trainable rule application that older symbolic systems lacked, but it is direct prior art for neural perception plus dynamic production-system execution. [Didolkar et al., “Neural Production Systems” (NeurIPS 2021)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/d785bf9067f8af9e078b93cf26de2b54-Abstract.html).

A low-confidence hybrid seam is to predict the downstream invalidation/recomputation cost of each candidate inference and include that estimate in a blackboard scheduler's utility score. Hearsay-II already estimated action effects and execution cost; metareasoning, learned scheduler heuristics, dependency tracking, and Phreak cover neighboring controls. This looks like a systems scheduling feature, not a new class. If worth an application study, use tiny diagnosis/constraint tasks with exhaustive correctness oracles; compare FIFO, Hearsay-style utility/cost, lazy demand-driven execution, and support-graph invalidation-cost scheduling at matched CPU budgets under low and high evidence churn. Measure answer quality, retractions/recomputations, and scheduler overhead; reject if matched-quality CPU savings are absent or low-churn performance regresses.

#### Old AI archaeology — evolutionary and developmental neural architectures

**Verdict: hardware limits were real but incomplete.** NEAT evolves topology and weights together; CPPNs/HyperNEAT use compact coordinate-conditioned generators for spatially regular connectivity. Parallel evaluation and modern simulation make larger evolutionary populations and substrates feasible, but each candidate still costs task interactions and evaluation; the genome-to-structure mapping imposes a bias. Compute does not provide better credit assignment or make an unsuitable encoding express arbitrary structure. [Stanley & Miikkulainen, NEAT (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1162/106365602320169811); [Stanley, D'Ambrosio & Gauci, HyperNEAT (2009)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19199382/).

Several obvious old-plus-modern combinations already exist:

- Differentiable Pattern Producing Networks evolve topology but learn weights by gradient descent with Lamarckian inheritance. A denoising-autoencoder demonstration compresses 157,684 weights to roughly 200 CPPN parameters. [Fernando et al., “Convolution by Evolution” (GECCO 2016)](https://www.mlanctot.info/files/papers/gecco16-dppn.pdf).
- GPU-based differentiable gene-regulatory networks combine local SGD with evolutionary search; reject “GRN dynamics plus gradient learning” as a new coupling. [Wilson et al. (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05948).
- Neural Developmental Programs grow networks through learned local communication and have been explored under evolutionary, supervised, and reinforcement-learning objectives. Lifelong NDP adds activity/reward-dependent synaptic and structural plasticity, including spontaneous-activity-driven pre-experience development. These closely modernize the previously rejected growing-tissue family; evaluated tasks remain small relative to broad perception or language benchmarks. [Najarro, Sudhakaran & Risi (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08197); [Plantec et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09787).
- AutoML-Zero evolves complete small learning algorithms from primitive arithmetic operations. This is a modern continuation of algorithm evolution, but its restricted search space and evaluation budget are central to feasibility. [Real et al., ICML 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a.html).

**Hybrid verdict:** evolved topology plus gradient learning, local development plus reward plasticity, and GRNs plus SGD are directly occupied. No new candidate is added. A possible CPU revival benchmark would use procedural navigation: train on small grids, test larger grids and held-out obstacle layouts, then lesion a small number of nodes/edges. Compare a fixed controller, equal-capacity redundancy, NEAT, HyperNEAT, and one developmental program at matched environment interactions and evaluation compute. Measure success, transfer, damage recovery, graph size, and CPU time. Falsify the developmental-prior claim if transfer/recovery does not improve at matched budgets or if gains disappear after graph-size control. Keep this as a revival benchmark, not an architecture novelty claim, and defer execution until a reproducible reference and fair budget are fixed.

#### Research state and experiment/resource record

- C001–C031 remain the full slate; this pass added no new broad architecture. Blackboard scheduling, neural production systems, and evolutionary/developmental learning remain archaeology/revival benchmarks.
- The bounded experiments still worth considering are C031 fault recovery (not sufficiently specified), a low-novelty PC replay-selector study, and CPU revival benchmarks for ART or developmental networks. C029 stays theoretical until conservative invalidation is auditable.
- At that earlier checkpoint, work was literature-only and no code/local training/GPU experiment had run. Since then, the C012 CPU prototype has run (details and resource record below); no GPU process was started, and GPU state was not queried because the pilot was CPU-only.
- Before future GPU work, check current memory and process ownership, keep this process at or below about 5.5 GB VRAM with roughly 1 GB headroom, and never interrupt Claude or another process.
### Continuation log — independent audit of C003, C007, and C012 (2026-09-27)

The independent adversarial ranking was checked against primary sources. None of the three broad-slate candidates merits promotion. C012 has the most useful remaining empirical question, but its current description lacks the rule needed to test it.

#### C003 — Associative Fold Machine: reject as a new class

The proposed “typed, task-conditioned, persistent monoid” lies at the intersection of several established mechanisms: learned associative/commutative aggregators for GNNs, prefix scans for sequential-parallel neural models, and persistent annotated sequence structures.

Ong and Veličković explicitly learn associative commutative binary aggregators for GNNs. The 2026 Prefix-Scannable Models paper characterizes state-space recurrences through associative scans and generalizes prefix-scannable sequence models to non-associative aggregation with logarithmic memory. Hinze and Paterson's finger trees are persistent sequences with cached monoidal annotations; the annotations may be noncommutative and multiple measures can be maintained together. Therefore “typed,” “persistent,” “task-conditioned,” or “parallel fold” does not by itself identify a new primitive. [Learnable Commutative Monoids for GNNs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08541); [Yau et al., ICLR 2026](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/4fef2f009c960581664363987fbe34d5-Abstract-Conference.html); [Hinze & Paterson, Finger Trees](https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/ralf.hinze/publications/FingerTrees.pdf).

**Residual novelty gate:** an exact learned order-preserving algebra would need a guarantee not reducible to existing monoidal scans, prefix-scannable models, or measured persistent data structures. Approximate associativity regularization does not ensure chunking invariance; exact associativity by construction risks reducing to familiar algebra. No experiment is justified before such a distinct algebra and guarantee are specified. Demote C003 from architecture candidate to known operator/algorithm baseline.

#### C007 — Error-Correcting Belief Code: reject the broad idea

Error-correcting output codes already encode classifications redundantly. More directly, neural networks trained with noisy hidden units learned error-correcting representations in 1992. Coding-theoretic fault-tolerant computation already encoded a whole computation's inputs and outputs; 2022 work builds a universal fault-tolerant neural network from biological/grid-cell error-correction codes; function-correcting codes protect a specified computation's output despite errors to the encoded message. Recent DNN hardware work also combines error codes with learned inference paths and low-precision analog compute. These make “encode beliefs redundantly, propagate, then repair with a syndrome” a known mechanism family rather than a new architecture. [Judd & Munro, NIPS 1992](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/1992/hash/c361bc7b2c033a83d663b8d9fb4be56e-Abstract.html); [Spielman, FOCS 1996](https://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/spielman/Research/fault.html); [Zlokapa et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.12887); [Lenz et al., Function-Correcting Codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.03094); [Yu et al., COLA, ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/yu23a.html).

A possible future contribution would need a learned semantic code plus operations that provably preserve a correction radius through arbitrary-depth composition and improve the redundancy/compute tradeoff over coding and fault-tolerance baselines. C007 specifies neither a closure rule nor that guarantee. A syndrome detects code inconsistency; it does not say whether a consistent represented belief is epistemically wrong. No experiment is justified until a code, closure operation, and bound are explicit. Demote C007; retain coding, ECOC, HDC, and fault-tolerant circuits as prior art/baselines.

#### C012 — Jet Calculus Machine: demote as architecture; retain a methods gate

Forward Taylor jets are already the representation propagated by higher-order automatic differentiation. Taylor models attach a polynomial approximation to a domain plus a rigorous remainder bound, and compose those models. They are used to analyze neural-network controllers and reachable sets; polynomial neural networks/Taylor maps already simulate and fit learned dynamical systems. A 2025 Taylor-Model PINN uses symbolic higher-order Taylor terms plus a learned ODE remainder. Thus “propagate values and derivatives,” “carry local polynomial patches,” and “attach a validity region” overlap existing AD, numerical analysis, verification, and physics-informed modeling. [JAX Taylor-mode jet documentation](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/jax.experimental.jet.html); [Verisig 2.0](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-81685-8_11); [Ivanov et al., Polynomial Neural Networks and Taylor Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09986); [Nagesh et al., Taylor-Model PINNs (Neuro-symbolic Systems 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03860).

**Narrow remaining question:** can a model learn *sound and non-vacuous validity regions* for local dynamical patches from sparse, partially observed transitions? This is a learning-rule question, not a new jet architecture. A radius estimated or calibrated from finitely many samples is not a certificate without explicit assumptions or a sound bound on the unknown dynamics. Higher-order terms also grow rapidly with state dimension, while repeated composition can inflate the remainder until the bound is useless.

**Falsifier once a validity learner is specified:** on a two-dimensional damped pendulum with known dynamics, train order-2/3 local patches from sparse transition and derivative samples. Compare against sound Taylor-model propagation and a neural ODE. Measure bound coverage and width over a fixed rollout horizon, patch count, sample use, and CPU time. Reject if bounds are unsound or quickly vacuous, or if coverage per sample/patch does not improve over Taylor-model baselines. **This experiment is gated, not ready to run:** no validity-radius learning algorithm is currently specified.

#### Updated broad-slate disposition

C003 and C007 are rejected as broad architecture claims and do not merit standalone experiments. C012 is the strongest of this trio only as a narrowly scoped methods question; it remains low novelty and cannot be prototyped honestly until its validity-bound learner is defined. The architecture slate remains C001–C031. This was literature work only: no code, local training, or GPU experiment; no GPU process was started.

### C012 pilot protocol — empirical residual tubes on damped-pendulum dynamics (pre-run, 2026-09-27)

**Status:** Run a bounded CPU pilot as a methods sanity check, not as evidence for a new architecture. The proposed split-conformal residual quantile is already an established tool; it does not supply a sound deterministic validity radius, and it does not automatically give sequential or distribution-shifted rollout coverage. Prior art directly includes finite-sample marginal conformal prediction for regression [Lei et al. (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04173) and conformal verification/inflation of neural reachable tubes [Lin & Bansal, L4DC 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v242/lin24a.html). The pilot asks the narrower empirical question of whether one-step marginal calibration plus a sampled-Lipschitz recursive tube remains useful on a simple rollout.

**Predeclared setup:**

- Ground truth is the two-state damped pendulum, `dθ/dt = ω`, `dω/dt = -sin(θ) - 0.12ω`, advanced one step by fixed-step RK4 with `dt = 0.05`.
- Train on 48 one-step transitions with input states sampled uniformly from `[-1.2,1.2]^2`. Fit (a) a global linear transition, (b) a global quadratic transition, and (c) four locally weighted quadratic patches blended smoothly by Gaussian weights. No derivatives are provided.
- Fit each predictor only on the training split. Use an independent set of 160 transitions from the same uniform input distribution to calibrate the 90% split-conformal Euclidean residual quantile, with rank `ceil((n_cal+1)*0.90)`.
- Evaluate one-step marginal coverage on 4,000 independent uniform states. Separately roll out 128 initial states sampled uniformly from `[-0.8,0.8]^2` for 40 steps. For each predictor, propagate a heuristic radius by `r_0=0`, `r_(t+1)=L_hat*r_t+q`, where `q` is its held-out residual quantile and `L_hat` is the largest finite-difference Jacobian norm over a dense grid on the calibration box. Track one-step coverage, per-step rollout coverage, final error coverage, final radius, and radius divided by the box diagonal.
- Repeat with 12 independent random seeds. All parameters above are fixed before observing results. The dense-grid `L_hat` is explicitly an empirical surrogate, not a formal Lipschitz certificate; therefore the propagated set will be called an *empirical tube*, not a sound bound.

**Falsification/interpretation:**

- The split-conformal claim is only relevant for a future input exchangeable with the calibration inputs. Later rollout states are dependent on earlier states and may follow a different distribution, so loss of per-step coverage is expected to expose the gap between one-step marginal coverage and sequential validity.
- If one-step coverage misses 90% by more than sampling variation under the matched uniform distribution, first audit the quantile implementation and randomness. If tube coverage degrades over the horizon, or the radius approaches/exceeds the operating-box diameter, this simple residual-plus-Lipschitz recipe fails as a useful rollout validity method. If it covers and remains narrow, that is a small benchmark result only: it does not prove soundness or novelty.
- This experiment cannot validate a broad architecture claim. Direct conformal reachability prior art is already established; any new contribution would need a distinctly specified learning rule for sound, useful validity sets beyond conformalized tubes and ordinary Taylor-model remainder propagation.

### C012 pilot result — split-conformal residual tube sanity check (2026-09-27)

**Outcome:** Completed the predeclared CPU pilot. The result does not promote C012 or its conformal residual method. It shows that the simple heuristic can be empirically narrow on this smooth, low-dimensional system at this horizon; the much stronger coverage later in rollout is expected because the radius compounds one-step residual allowances, and is not a formal guarantee.

| Predictor | One-step coverage, target 90% | Rollout coverage at steps 1 / 10 / 20 / 40 | Minimum step coverage | Mean final RMSE | Mean q | Mean sampled L | Mean r40 | r40 / box diagonal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Global linear | 89.80% (SD 1.44 pp) | 97.79 / 99.94 / 100 / 100% | 97.72% (SD 2.80 pp) | 0.05137 (SD 0.00690) | 0.00293 (0.00035) | 1.00156 (0.00022) | 0.12090 (0.01432) | 3.56% (0.42 pp) |
| Global quadratic | 89.40% (SD 2.45 pp) | 97.20 / 98.96 / 100 / 100% | 97.07% (SD 5.52 pp) | 0.05279 (0.00863) | 0.00312 (0.00034) | 1.00293 (0.00061) | 0.13228 (0.01462) | 3.90% (0.43 pp) |
| Four smoothly blended local quadratics | 89.41% (SD 2.59 pp) | 98.11 / 99.54 / 99.94 / 100% | 98.05% (SD 4.51 pp) | 0.04346 (0.00844) | 0.00282 (0.00041) | 1.00404 (0.00051) | 0.12214 (0.01756) | 3.60% (0.52 pp) |

Values are means over 12 independently seeded fits/calibrations; parenthesized values are standard deviations across seeds, not confidence intervals. Each seed used 48 training transitions, 160 independent calibration transitions, 4,000 one-step test states, and 128 held-out rollouts over 40 RK4 steps. Initial rollout states were sampled from `[-0.8,0.8]^2`; calibration and one-step test states were uniform over `[-1.2,1.2]^2`. No rollout state was outside that box at step 40. The reported stepwise coverage is empirical over the rollout ensemble; the change in input-state distribution across time means the one-step exchangeability condition does not establish it.

The local quadratic blend had the smallest mean terminal point RMSE among these three models, but its seed-to-seed spread overlaps the global baselines and the sample does not establish a robust advantage. All three reached 100% empirical tube coverage at step 40 while the radii remained small relative to the box diagonal. This is a favorable sanity-check result for the *heuristic on this smooth pendulum task*, not evidence of deterministic soundness: `L_hat` is a grid-sampled derivative maximum, not a certified supremum, and calibration quantile `q` is not a worst-case residual bound. The recursive inequality is therefore not a sound reachability proof.

**Prior-art update:** Conformalized reachability is directly occupied. Lin & Bansal (L4DC 2024) use split conformal prediction to verify neural reachable tubes and provide probabilistic safety guarantees; they also show the relation to scenario optimization. Wang et al. (2025 preprint) construct probabilistic reachable tubes with conformal prediction and state stepwise and cumulative guarantees for a tube-MPC controller. These systems differ in details from the present toy recurrence, but they eliminate the broad novelty claim “calibrate model residuals and use them to inflate a trajectory tube.” [Lin & Bansal (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v242/lin24a.html); [Wang et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03293). Split conformal's finite-sample marginal guarantee comes from exchangeability, not from the learned model being sound; it does not imply conditional, sequential, or shifted-distribution validity. [Lei et al. (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04173).

**Disposition:** C012 remains demoted as a new architecture and as a broad validity-learning claim. Retain only a bounded question: whether a specified method can provide *deterministic* non-vacuous local remainders from sparse dynamics data, or a clearly scoped sequential probabilistic guarantee under a named trajectory distribution, while improving tube width/sample cost over Taylor-model verification and conformalized reachability. This pilot provides a reproducible baseline and a negative novelty result; it does not answer that harder question.

**Resource record:** CPU only (Python 3.11.9, NumPy 2.4.6); measured experiment-body runtime 0.153 s across 12 seeds. Peak VRAM = 0 GB used by this run; no GPU process was started. GPU memory/processes were not queried because no GPU work was used, so whether Claude was concurrently using the GPU is unknown and irrelevant to this CPU-only run. Model/experiment size: 2D transition fits (three models, including four blended quadratic patches), 48 training points per seed, 160 calibration points, 4,000 one-step test points, 128 rollouts × 40 steps. Peak system RAM was not measured.
### Lead-verified correction — the C012 recurrence is direct 2026 prior art

The independent audit found a much closer collision than the earlier generic conformal-reachability references: Bakhtiaridoust, Baumann & Deka’s June 30, 2026 preprint, *Uncertainty Quantification via Invariant-Measure Conformal Prediction* (imCP). The paper's multi-step method calibrates one-step residuals using independent calibration transitions from an invariant measure and propagates the resulting conformal quantile through a Lipschitz predictor. It proves the same recurrence used in the pilot, `r_(h+1)=L*r_h+q`, equivalently `r_h=q Σ_(i=0..h-1)L^i`. Under its assumptions it proves a simultaneous horizon-`h` coverage lower bound `1-min(1,hα)`. The paper separately proves rolling one-step coverage at each fixed time when the state distribution remains invariant. [Bakhtiaridoust, Baumann & Deka (2026), arXiv:2606.31607](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31607); [full text, methodology and Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.31607v1).

The match is exact at the method-family level, not just a neighboring idea. This pilot's empirical update is a direct implementation of the same mathematical propagation rule. Its important differences are shortcomings, not novelty: it uses a uniform-box calibration distribution that is not invariant for the damped pendulum; its initial rollout distribution is narrower than calibration; and its maximum `L_hat` is sampled on a grid rather than certified. The pilot therefore cannot inherit imCP's guarantees. imCP itself is a preprint, but its timestamp and method are documented primary prior art, so the mechanism is occupied regardless of publication status.

Additional lead-verified context: Knuth et al. (RA-L/ICRA 2021) already use probabilistic Lipschitz bounds on the difference between learned and true dynamics to define trusted regions and safety/reachability guarantees. [Knuth et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08993). Cleaveland et al. (AAAI 2024) calibrate trajectory-level error regions across multiple time steps to reduce the conservatism of separately calibrated per-step intervals. [Cleaveland et al.](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/30089). Ma et al. (2026 preprint) combine conformal uncertainty intervals for unknown dynamics with reachability analysis for safe control. [Ma et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03799).

**Disposition update:** close the broad C012 residual-tube novelty question as rediscovery. Keep the CPU pilot only as a local reproduction/sanity baseline. Any future work must target a precisely different result—for example, a deterministic sound, non-vacuous local remainder learned from sparse data under explicit regularity assumptions, or a sequential guarantee under a deployment distribution not covered by invariant-measure calibration—then compare against Taylor-model verification, imCP, trajectory-level conformal prediction, and conformal reachability. No candidate is promoted. The pilot's favorable empirical coverage cannot establish this gap or novelty.

### Old-plus-old hybrid audit — ART match tracking × predictive coding

**Source architectures.** Adaptive Resonance Theory (ART) combines bottom-up feature evidence with a category's top-down expectation. A mismatch can reset the active category and trigger a search, which is the stability–plasticity mechanism. Predictive-coding networks instead represent hierarchical predictions and prediction errors, iteratively updating latent activities and sometimes synaptic weights to reduce those errors.

**Tempting coupling.** Let an ART category select a local generative/predictive-coding model. Its top-down expectation initializes local inference; bottom-up residuals update local activities. If the residual remains beyond a learned criterion, raise ART vigilance, search for a better category, or create a new one. Permit synaptic learning only after a match/resonance, retaining stable old categories while adapting within the selected model.

**Why the obvious hybrid is not new.** ARTMAP was explicitly presented as “Predictive ART” in 1991. It uses two ART modules plus an associative map, and a target prediction error increases vigilance just enough to trigger category search/creation through “match tracking.” This is not modern variational predictive coding, so the two theories should not be conflated; nevertheless, the headline interaction “prediction error controls category granularity while local ART learning preserves prior categories” is already implemented in a pre-deep-learning architecture. The source also describes top-down learned expectations, bottom-up input, match/reset, and trial-by-trial predictive-error control. [Carpenter, Grossberg & Reynolds (1991), *ARTMAP*](https://sites.bu.edu/steveg/files/2016/06/CarGroRey1991NN.pdf), especially §§1.7–1.8; [distributed ART and predictive learning (1997)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360809700004X).

**What modern tools change / what they do not.** Modern differentiable or inference-learning PC networks can provide continuous hierarchical generative predictions that old ART feature vectors could not easily represent; pretrained perception could supply a better metric for vigilance. Those components make a larger benchmark practical, but ARTMAP already occupies predictive-error-driven category refinement. Simply replacing its hand-designed prototypes with a deep PC encoder is a component modernization, not a distinct architecture.

**Only possible residual seam (low confidence):** use *multi-step action-conditioned trajectory residual structure*—not a single supervised label mismatch—to decide which category dimension to split, and jointly allocate a new local generative model only when the residual is both repeatable and causally discriminated by an action. That might couple predictive-control evidence to category growth more selectively than scalar match tracking. This wording is still underspecified and likely intersects predictive-state discovery, adaptive system identification, and active automata learning; no candidate is promoted before those collisions are searched.

**Smallest falsifier if the seam survives further prior-art search:** a CPU two-mode nonlinear controlled process where one rare action reveals a persistent dynamics change and unrelated observations remain stable. At equal interaction, parameter, and update budgets compare ARTMAP/fuzzy ART on transition labels; an online predictive-coding model; a simple ART-front/PC-head cascade; and the action-conditioned residual-gated joint learner. Measure multi-step prediction after the shift, retention of the old mode, recovery sample count, category/model count, and inference/update operations. Reject the coupled mechanism if it fails to beat the best separate or ARTMAP baseline on accuracy-versus-memory/update cost, or if noise creates categories as fast as informative action-conditioned residuals.

**Verdict:** useful pairing to understand and benchmark, but the broad mechanism is an old rediscovery. No new class enters C001–C031.

### Independent invention pass beyond C001–C031 — lead-verified rejections

A fresh invention pass proposed three directions from older computational traditions. I checked the nearest primary sources before disposition; none adds a new broad class.

#### Dynamic neural fields × symbolic/relational binding

A tempting mechanism is to represent variables/roles as locations or peaks in continuous neural fields, bind fillers to roles, and let attractor dynamics perform parsing and control. This is already directly explored: *Language Processing with Dynamic Fields* (2008) maps recursive syntactic structures into tensor-product/filler–role representations and describes their transient processing through coupled dynamic fields. *Universal Neural Field Computation* (2013) maps a universal Turing machine into a dynamic-field automaton. A 2013 DFT architecture connects fields with sensors, motors, working memory, decision, and autonomous learning. Thus field dynamics plus symbolic binding, universal symbolic computation, and embodied closed-loop processing are established combinations; modern implementation might improve throughput or sensing, not make that combination new. [beim Graben et al. (2008)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19003475/); [beim Graben & Potthast (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3550); [Sandamirskaya (2013)](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2013.00276/full).

**Potential practical probe, not a novelty claim:** compare fields plus binding against a symbolic planner and recurrent neural model on noisy generated scenes/commands, measuring compositional generalization, robustness, latency, and memory under equal compute. Do not prioritize until a specific advantage over the above field architectures is identified.

#### Ashby ultrastability

The proposal—fast regulation inside a viability region plus a slower trial-and-error reorganization loop when essential variables leave bounds—is the same historical ultrastability mechanism already represented by C031's violation-scoped homeostatic reorganization. New optimization inside the outer loop would be a modernization, not a new architecture. Keep only the previously documented fault-recovery falsifier against adaptive control and homeostatic RL; do not create a duplicate candidate.

#### Self-replicating neural networks in artificial-chemistry populations

A population in which networks apply to/train one another can exhibit self-replicating weight configurations and attractor basins. Gabor et al. directly formalize neural self-application, self-training, robustness to noise, and interacting “soup” populations. [Gabor et al., *Self-Replication in Neural Networks*, Artificial Life 28(2), 2022](https://doi.org/10.1162/artl_a_00359). This is a valuable artificial-life substrate but does not specify how task-relevant skill is acquired or selected; adding task fitness becomes evolutionary computation, while omitting it leaves no broad-use objective. No architecture candidate or experiment is added.

**Pass verdict:** the strongest field/symbolic idea has direct old prior art; the other two are duplicates of C031 or a published artificial-life mechanism. No new candidate was added. This pass was literature-only and CPU/browser-side; GPU usage was zero and the device was not queried.

### Old AI archaeology — cybernetics, self-maintenance, and conversational learning

An independent survey examined several cybernetic and organizational traditions not yet consolidated in the ledger. The question was whether the core computation disappeared for lack of compute, or whether its goals and learning rules remained underspecified. Lead checks of the cited papers found no new broad architecture class; the strongest bounded revival experiment is a CASTE-inspired test of procedural teachback.

| Tradition | Original computation and historical limit | What modern technology changes | Verdict and closest work |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Viable System Model (VSM)** | Recursively organizes operations, coordination, internal control, environmental planning, and policy/identity. It is a design framework for viable organizations, not a concrete general learner with an explicit update algorithm. | Software agents, service telemetry, and simulation can instantiate larger managed systems and automate monitoring. They do not decide how to derive the VSM roles or turn variety into a learned policy. | Not simply too early; an organizational/control scaffold, not a new AI computation. Software-oriented VSM architectures and autonomic-management applications predate current AI. [Herring & Kaplan, *The Viable System Model for Software*](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=1058b698ab4a9158ac8e0473b20c31cb6041d0da&repid=rep1&type=pdf); [Stoyanov et al. (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICAS.2006.22). |
| **Autopoiesis** | Local production and repair processes regenerate the components and boundary that sustain the system. A minimal computer model was published in 1974, so the idea was not waiting for modern compute. | Differentiable cellular automata and large simulators make optimization and larger damage-repair experiments practical. A 2026 preprint, Minary, supplies a formal distributed self-maintenance primitive. | Self-maintenance still does not specify a task objective, skill acquisition, or useful selection among behaviors. Modernization exists; treat it as a component/testbed and compare against neural cellular automata, not a new general learner. [Varela, Maturana & Uribe (1974)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4407425/); [Growing Neural Cellular Automata (2020)](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/); [Connor & Defant, Minary (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04501). |
| **Rosen relational biology / (M,R)** | Abstract mappings encode metabolism and repair as a self-referential closure. The main barrier is formal interpretation, computability, and mapping to measurable biological processes—not raw machine speed. | Modern process-algebra, communicating X-machine, and cell-realization work give concrete computational realizations to compare. They do not settle claims about what counts as a faithful realization. | Too abstract for an AI architecture without explicit data, objective, and learning rule. Direct computational realizations already exist, while the theoretical status is debated. [Palmer et al., *(M,R) system as an X-machine* (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtbi.2016.08.007); [computational realization discussion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0303264723000217). |
| **Second-order cybernetics / Ashby Box** | The observer is inside the loop and must infer how its own actions affect a nontrivial, potentially changing machine. This is a system-identification and control problem, not a general learning rule by itself. | Cheap simulators make observer/controller ablations and online reconstruction straightforward. A 2020 Ashby Box implementation already synthesizes an observer that reconstructs its own function. | Modernization is real, but the general mechanism overlaps adaptive control, dual control, online system identification, and C031. No new architecture. [*Learning the Ashby Box* (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1108/K-06-2019-0439). |
| **Anticipatory systems / anticipatory classifier systems** | Condition–action–effect rules predict consequences and use them to choose current actions. The difficulty was model quality and planning/search, not the abstract availability of computation. | Modern simulators, GPU model learning, hindsight data, and model-based RL improve prediction and imagined planning. | Dyna, MPC, model-based RL, and anticipatory classifier systems already cover the mechanism. No new class; useful as historical lineage for C001/C015. [Butz, *Anticipatory Learning Classifier Systems*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4615-0891-5); [ACS2 with hindsight replay (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09400). |
| **Synergetic computer** | Slow order parameters steer fast state variables toward stored patterns; demonstrated for associative memory, recognition, attention, and logical operations. Early implementations faced modest hardware, but the method is still mainly prototype-based pattern completion. | Modern compute allows broader image experiments and hybridization with learned features. Synergetic neural networks are still being applied, including to SAR recognition. | Not a forgotten general architecture; it sits near associative memory and dynamical pattern recognition. The hard limit is capacity/generalization, not only hardware. [Haken, *Synergetic Computers and Cognition*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-22450-2); [modern synergetic network for SAR (2023)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10006923/). |
| **Pask's Conversation Theory / CASTE** | CASTE tracked a learner's topic relations and strategy, regulated uncertainty through dialogue, and used teachback/explanation as evidence of understanding. Its papers also describe evolving the topic domain by adding nodes to an entailment structure. The original system taught probability theory; topic structures and tutorial rules were hand-authored, limiting breadth. | Procedural simulators, generated curricula, cheap interaction, and learned learner models can automate larger domains and test query policies. These remove cost of experimentation, not the need to specify reliable semantics for explanations or a graph-construction rule. | Best bounded revival test, but the core is established and neighboring active program learning/curriculum methods are close. It is a revival of a learning protocol, not a novel architecture. [Pask & Scott, CASTE (1973)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0020-7373(73)80008-2); [Pask, Scott & Kallikourdis, conversation theory and evolving domains (1973)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0020-7373(73)80002-1). |
| **Numa-Rete** | A 12×12 photocell/circuit mesh counted opaque objects despite variation in size, position, and shape. Larger hardware was contemplated; funding and the specific device ended. | Cheap sensors and parallel hardware make local filters trivial to scale. Convolution, morphology, and object detection already generalize the local-property idea. | An important early parallel-vision device, not a new computational class. Increasing resolution would not itself add semantic reasoning. [University of Illinois Biological Computer Laboratory exhibit](https://distributedmuseum.illinois.edu/exhibit/biological_computer_laboratory/); [Asaro, history of BCL](https://www.peterasaro.org/writing/Asaro%20HVF%26BCL.pdf). |

#### CASTE revival experiment gate

The specific claim worth testing is **sample efficiency**, not novelty: on a finite procedural concept domain, does requiring an executable teachback and using a prerequisite/entailment graph to choose the next lesson reduce oracle queries or improve transfer to held-out compositions over an active program-learning baseline? Use a short Boolean/program grammar with an exact interpreter; give both methods identical examples, simulator access, grammar, interaction budget, and compute. Compare (a) CASTE-inspired graph plus executable teachback and uncertainty-regulated topic selection, (b) active program synthesis with counterexample queries, and (c) random curriculum. Measure queries to exact program recovery, accuracy on deeper unseen compositions, calibration of the learner-state estimate, and CPU time. Falsify the revival claim if teachback/graph control does not beat the strongest baseline on query efficiency or held-out composition accuracy at equal access, or if gains disappear when the baseline gets the same prerequisite graph. The graph-evolution mechanism is excluded from the first test because CASTE already describes it and active curriculum construction is a separate collision zone.

This is a **methods/revival experiment only**. No code was run in this pass; a defensible executable definition of teachback and matched active-program baseline must be fixed before implementation. No GPU was used or queried because there was no GPU experiment. No subagent edited the notebook; findings were consolidated and source-checked here.

#### CASTE hybrid novelty check — teachback × active program synthesis

The possible hybrid is an entailment graph choosing a learnable subprogram, a learner submitting executable teachback, and a verifier supplying counterexamples that update the learner estimate and the next query. This would change lesson scheduling based on executable semantic failures, rather than merely attaching a dialog interface to a program synthesizer. Direct checks close the broad novelty claim more firmly than the initial pass: CASTE already tracked topic relations, used mechanically checked explanations of a relation and its derivation, and described topic-graph growth. Error-Based Simulation (EBS) already runs an erroneous learner model to expose counterexample-like behavior and explain violated constraints; a model-building learning environment coupled EBS with robust simulation. COMMAND jointly infers a prerequisite graph and student model from performance data. Machine-teaching research optimizes examples and concept order over compositional programs. Together these occupy the central graph + executable model + diagnostic simulation + adaptive curriculum combination. I found no clear source for the exact learner-specific rule that distinguishes a missing prerequisite, a wrong procedure, or a bad domain model from one counterexample, but that would be an application-level diagnostic mechanism, not a broad AI architecture. **Reject as a new hybrid; leave no prototype scheduled** unless this instructional application becomes a priority. ### Old AI archaeology — local memories, tuple evaluators, and product units

This pass concentrated on older mechanisms whose limitations may plausibly have involved sparse memory, small processors, or training cost. Several were already modernized or absorbed; the “too early” hypothesis survives only in scoped applications, not as broad novelty.

| Architecture | Original computation and historical limitation | What has changed / closest modern form | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Neocognitron (1980–82)** | Unsupervised hierarchical S/C cell maps build shift-tolerant visual features by local competition and pooling. The original used much smaller data and hardware than current vision systems. | Backpropagation, large datasets, GPUs, and convolutional weight sharing made the hierarchy broadly trainable; modern CNNs occupy the hierarchical local-feature and pooling mechanism. | Strong example of “born early and absorbed,” rather than an abandoned architecture awaiting revival. A local unsupervised adaptation variant would be a continual-learning mechanism question, not a new neocognitron class. [Fukushima (1980)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7370364/); [Fukushima & Miyake (1982)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0031320382900243); [detailed 1988 account](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0893608088900147). |
| **CMAC (1975)** | Continuous controller inputs activate several overlapping memory addresses; output is the sum of stored values, updated locally. It offered fast associative control lookup, but memory scales poorly with dimensions and original updates can converge slowly. | Sparse tables, hashing, parallel lookup, and learned features reduce memory/throughput barriers. Multiresolution neural hash grids also store trainable feature vectors in addressable sparse tables and let a small MLP decode them, but this is an analogy and graphics-specific method, not a direct CMAC revival. | Old mechanism remains useful for real-time low-dimensional control; no general architecture novelty. A CPU plant-tracking comparison could test adaptation/interference versus CMAC, tile coding, RBF, and tiny MLP at fixed memory, but defer until a concrete deployment advantage is identified. [Albus (1975), primary abstract](https://www.nist.gov/publications/new-approach-manipulator-control-cerebellar-model-articulation-controller-cmac1); [slow convergence analysis (1990)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-6670(17)52750-0); [Instant-NGP hash grid (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.05989). |
| **N-tuple systems** | A set of overlapping short patterns each indexes a value table; their values are summed and trained by temporal difference/self-play. This works especially well where the state has a small discrete geometry, but pattern tables do not transfer naturally to arbitrary continuous perception. | CPU self-play already made the method competitive in Othello. A 2022 paper couples TD n-tuple value functions with MCTS at test time for Othello, Connect Four, and Rubik's Cube, reporting a strong CPU-trained Othello agent. | Modern compute is not required for the narrow game niche, and the apparent old-plus-modern hybrid (tuple memory plus tree search) is already direct prior art. Preserve as a strong CPU baseline for discrete game/search tasks; no new class. [Lucas (2008)](https://repository.essex.ac.uk/3820/); [Scheiermann & Konen (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13307). |
| **Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM)** | Sparse distributed encodings, distal-context segments, and sequence prediction provide online learning without a separate gradient-training stage. The proposed advantage is streaming adaptation, not raw compute. | A carefully tuned 2020 time-series comparison found LSTM/GRU could exceed HTM by >30% at lower runtime on its tasks and found that temporal components were not always responsible for accuracy. A 2026 smart-meter comparison instead reports near-equal clean point accuracy, lower CPU runtime, and greater noise stability for HTM under its specific online setup. | Do not summarize as “HTM loses” or “HTM wins”: results are workload/protocol-specific. Modern hardware does not automatically repair task-dependent capacity or representation limits. It remains a useful streaming/online baseline, not a general new architecture. A fair follow-up must match preprocessing, training access, adaptation cadence, timestamps, tuning budgets, and noise/drift. [Empirical HTM/RNN comparison (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2018.09.098); [smart-meter comparison (2026)](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-5903/18/4/222). |
| **Pi-Sigma / higher-order product networks (1991)** | Linear sums feed multiplicative product outputs to represent selected higher-order interactions with fewer units than a dense polynomial expansion. Products can create numerical sensitivity and interaction growth. | Autodiff/GPU training improved practicality, while multiplicative integration and multiplicative LSTMs made input-dependent products a trainable recurrent primitive. | Product-based neural computation was revived, not forgotten; broad novelty is occupied. A narrow interpretable sparse-product model would need a measured advantage over multiplicative gates, polynomial networks, and low-rank feature interactions. [Shin & Ghosh (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1109/IJCNN.1991.155142); [Wu et al., Multiplicative Integration (NeurIPS 2016)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2016/hash/f69e505b08403ad2298b9f262659929a-Abstract.html); [Krause et al., mLSTM (2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.07959). |

GMDH has already been covered in the historical register; the additional check supports its existing disposition: candidate-unit search became cheaper with GPUs, but selection over repeated validation sets can overfit, and symbolic regression, polynomial networks, and AutoML now cover much of the construction mechanism. More hardware does not by itself improve the model-selection signal. No new candidate was added from this pass.

### CMAC revival pilot — preregistered CPU experiment (2026-09-27)

This is a small **architecture-revival benchmark**, not a novelty experiment. It tests the historically plausible practical claim that distributed local table updates can adapt quickly to a local change while changing predictions elsewhere less than a globally shared MLP. It cannot establish a general advantage or a new model class.

- **Task:** online regression on a smooth two-dimensional control-like function over `[-1,1]^2`. After 4,000 examples, one compact region changes via a smooth localized perturbation; continue for 4,000 more examples. Training inputs are uniform, with fixed Gaussian observation noise. The test set is fixed and separates the changed region from its unchanged complement.
- **CMAC:** eight offset tile codings over the two coordinates; one active scalar per tiling; 1,152 total address weights; online normalized error update divided across active addresses.
- **Baseline:** two-hidden-layer tanh MLP with 30 units per layer (1,051 scalar parameters), online SGD, same examples, same stream length. No replay, reset, or task label is available to either learner.
- **Runs and measures:** ten fixed random seeds; report test RMSE before and after the change; changed-region adaptation error over the first 1,000 post-change examples; unchanged-region retention error over the same interval; final changed/global error; parameter counts; CPU runtime. Use identical streams and noise for both methods.
- **Falsification:** the local-update advantage is not supported if CMAC does not reduce the early post-change error in the affected region, or if it obtains that gain only by materially worse final changed-region accuracy or materially higher unchanged-region error than the MLP. If it helps only because of the chosen feature grid or learning rate, the result is inconclusive; no tuning is permitted after seeing the aggregate results.
- **Limits:** approximate parameter count is not a compute match. Python implementation latency includes loop/indexing overhead and cannot stand in for optimized hardware. The MLP uses a learned global representation while CMAC has a fixed grid. A favorable result would motivate a matched-budget control study; an unfavorable result rejects only this setup.

The protocol is fixed before execution. Use CPU only; no GPU inspection is needed unless the plan changes to GPU.

Its post-change unchanged-region RMSE remained high (`0.1270 ± 0.0165` after 4,000 updates), evidence that this fixed one-sample SGD configuration had not learned the original function before the shift. ### CMAC follow-up — matched local RBF protocol (pre-run, 2026-09-27)

The previous result may only show that a fixed local representation fits this smooth low-dimensional target better than the selected MLP. To test whether tile-coded CMAC contributes anything beyond local basis functions, compare it against a Gaussian RBF lattice with the same coefficient count and the identical shift/stream task.

- **RBF memory:** 32×36 fixed centers over `[-1,1]^2`, 1,152 scalar weights. For each input, use the nearby Gaussian basis functions within `3σ`, normalize active feature values to sum to one, predict their weighted sum, and update those weights by normalized LMS. This is a conventional local function approximator, not a new architecture.
- **Tuning:** five independent stationary streams (seeds 2200–2204), 4,000 examples each. Select `σ ∈ {0.07, 0.10, 0.14}` and update rate `α ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.6}` by minimum mean noise-free validation RMSE. Freeze before any drift evaluation. Require mean validation RMSE ≤ `0.08`; otherwise report the baseline as unqualified and stop the comparison.
- **Evaluation:** fresh seeds 2700–2709; same CMAC implementation, training stream lengths, localized shift, test regions, and metrics as the prior CMAC pilot. No tuning on these seeds. Report adaptation curves, unchanged-region error, and final error. If RBF matches CMAC within across-seed variability, treat the effect as generic local-basis bias, not a CMAC-specific advantage.
- **Limits:** memory is matched by coefficient count; computation/update operations are not. This probes representational/locality bias and does not establish high-dimensional control value or broad architectural novelty.

CPU only; no GPU experiment is planned, so GPU state need not be queried.

**RBF baseline qualification:** the tuning pass selected `σ=0.14`, `α=0.1` (mean stationary validation RMSE `0.01911 ± 0.00156`; next best was `σ=0.10`, `α=0.1`, RMSE `0.02303 ± 0.00109`). It clears the pre-set `0.08` gate by a wide margin. Freeze these values for the fresh-seed comparison. Tuning used five streams, 4,000 points each, Python 3.11.9 / NumPy 2.4.6, CPU runtime 4.388 s; GPU was not used or queried, RAM was not measured.

### Hybrid archaeology — ACS2 anticipatory rules × hindsight replay

This is a direct old-plus-modern coupling, verified from the primary 2026 preprint. **Source mechanisms:** ACS2 uses condition–action–effect classifier rules to learn an explicit action-conditioned model, with anticipatory learning, reinforcement updates, and genetic generalization. Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) was developed for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning: if the intended goal fails, later states from the trajectory are relabeled as virtual goals. **Exact coupling:** ACS2HER invokes goal relabeling after failed episodes, stores original and hindsight transitions in replay memory, then re-runs the classifier system's anticipatory learning (ALP), reward learning, and genetic rule generalization on those transitions. This changes which rule effects are reinforced, when structural learning runs, and the size/composition of the classifier population; it is more than putting an LCS and a neural HER module side by side.

**Prior art and scope:** replay had already been coupled to ACS2 as ACS2ER (GECCO 2022), followed by episode-based replay (IEEE Access 2023); the 2026 preprint presents the first ACS2/HER goal-relabeling integration. It is direct prior art for that precise hybrid, but the work is marked preliminary and tests only small discrete Maze 6 and FrozenLake tasks. [Butz & Hoffmann, ACS2 (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1177/1059-712302-010002-01); [HER (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01495); [ACS2 with experience replay (GECCO 2022)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3520304.3533996); [episode-based ACS2 replay (IEEE Access 2023)](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3269879); [ACS2HER (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09400).

**What the coupling changed in the reported experiments:** on deterministic Maze 6, HER increased the rate of learned reliable transitions, but rule populations exceeded 3,000 classifiers versus roughly 474 in standard ACS2, and some exploration settings took up to 3,746 seconds versus 36 seconds for ACS2. On stochastic FrozenLake, HER variants achieved fewer successful goals than ACS2 and ACS2ER, even though some reached shorter paths during exploration; high-intensity settings exceeded 22,000 seconds versus about 13 seconds for ACS2. The authors identify limited test environments, incomplete goal-strategy search, statistical robustness, stochastic sensitivity, and runtime/population overhead as limitations. These are the paper's reported figures and should be treated as preliminary, not independently replicated.

**Hybrid verdict:** this is a meaningful interaction between an old rule-learning substrate and a modern relabeling strategy, but it is already directly published and tightly scoped. The strongest result is also a caution: dense hindsight signals can amplify classifier growth and can mislead learning under stochastic dynamics. Keep ACS2HER as a benchmark when studying interpretable rule learners or sparse-reward exploration; do not add it as a new broad architecture candidate. A follow-up worth considering would compare HER strategies and confidence-weighted virtual-goal rule updates on larger stochastic tasks at matched wall-clock and classifier-memory budgets. The main claim would be falsified if faster transition-rule acquisition does not improve success per unit compute, or if stochastic virtual goals continue to increase model size without reliable predictive rules.
