#### AR-01 — NARS: non-axiomatic, resource-bounded reasoning

- **Original mechanism.** NARS' early reports date to 1993/1994; its 1995 dissertation describes a substantial system. Instead of fixing axioms or assuming unlimited theorem proving, it stores statements with evidence-sensitive truth values (frequency and confidence), uses rules for deduction, induction, abduction, analogy and revision, and schedules questions, goals and beliefs under finite time and memory. NARS 4.1 time-shares multiple tasks, selects premises by priority, adjusts priority from inference feedback, and can return a provisional answer while continuing to search for a better one. [Wang, *From inheritance relation to nonaxiomatic logic* (1994)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0888-613X(94)90021-3); [NARS 4.1 (2000)](https://cis.temple.edu/~pwang/Publication/NARS-41.pdf).
- **Primitive / representation / repeated operation.** The units are concept-terms and evidentially weighted statements. An inference cycle chooses a task, relevant concept/belief and rule; it emits a revised or derived task/belief, adjusts memory/priority, then yields. Knowledge resides in a changing concept network. Inputs are experiences, questions and goals; outputs are revisable answers or executable operations. Learning and inference are the same ongoing process, not separate offline stages.
- **Was it bad or early?** Not simply early. Its defining challenge is deliberately finite knowledge and compute, and it already has incremental input, uncertainty and bounded search. Faster CPUs/RAM/GPU perception can improve plugins, but do not remove term-generation and inference branching, semantic grounding or evidence calibration. The hard question is whether its priority scheduler spends scarce computation better than strong task-specific anytime search and active-inference baselines.
- **What changed / prior modernization.** NARS remains active. Its 2022 perception paper proposes active, goal-directed sensing and representing perceptual experience in the same memory; it also explicitly describes perception as ongoing work with open problems. OpenNARS for Applications (ONA) adds event-driven sensorimotor reasoning and application/robot interfaces. Later work tests operant adaptation; a 2024 NUTS paper applies NARS to small-sample word recognition. These are narrow integrations, not proof of general perception or learning. [Unified perception and cognition (2022)](https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2022.806403); [ONA architecture and control (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-64300-3_6); [NUTS, NARS and Speech (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17874); [Machine Psychology with ONA (2024)](https://doi.org/10.3389/frobt.2024.1440631).
- **Use case / expected advantage / weaknesses.** It could provide online belief revision and anytime decisions in changing, partially known environments without retraining a global model. Its vulnerabilities are combinatorial inference, term/variable representation, perception grounding, and the need to calibrate evidential truth and priority on real tasks. It may outperform on small structured streams with frequent contradictions and hard deadlines; no broad result establishes this.
- **Novelty judgment.** AIKR, experience-grounded logic, priority scheduling, online belief revision and a unified reasoning/learning loop are established. **Confidence that the architecture is new: 0/5.** A narrow open question is how to calibrate the compute cost and downstream value of different perceptual operations so reasoning can request a useful next observation; active perception, NARS attention and ONA already make the broad hybrid an established direction.
- **Small falsifier.** In a toy task with ambiguous scenes, sensors of different cost/noise, and a mid-run task change, compare ONA-style priority allocation with round-robin sensing, fixed active-perception policy and a value-of-information oracle at matched sensing/inference budgets. Measure task success per cost, adaptation time, belief calibration and missed deadlines. Reject if priority feedback does not improve the success/cost frontier or leaves a large oracle gap. This tests an implementation claim, not architecture novelty. **No experiment run.**

#### AR-02 — Neural Engineering Framework / Semantic Pointer Architecture (NEF/SPA)

- **Original mechanism.** NEF is a neural compiler: populations represent real-valued vectors through nonlinear encoders and decoders; alternative decoders implement transformations; recurrence implements state dynamics. SPA builds cognitive functions from composable high-dimensional semantic-pointer vectors. Spaun (2012) integrated perception, working memory, action selection and motor output in an approximately 2.5-million-neuron model across eight tasks. [NEF overview](https://compneuro.uwaterloo.ca/files/publications/stewartAISB.2012.pdf); [Spaun (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1225266).
- **Primitive / learning / inference.** A neural ensemble represents a vector; learned or analytically selected connections compute functions of it. Recurrence plus semantic-pointer binding stores structured concepts/sequences. Input is a sensory stream or vector state; output is another state, decision or motor signal. Decoders can be solved from target functions, and local error-driven rules or differentiable optimization can tune selected connections. Inference is continuous state evolution and learned transformation, not token decoding.
- **Was it bad or early? What changed?** This was not blocked only by lack of arithmetic: the large multi-task model existed in 2012. Simulator cost and the labor of specifying networks were real limitations. Nengo 2 improved benchmark simulation speed about 50× over Nengo 1.4. Later graph optimization reduced one Spaun benchmark from 8,926 to 1,886 seconds per simulated second; one OpenCL GPU LIF configuration reached about 66 seconds per simulated second, still far from real-time Spaun. [Nengo 2 (2014)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3880998/); [Nengo graph optimization (2017)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5415674/). NengoDL adds CPU/GPU simulation, Keras/TensorFlow components and optimization; Nengo has neuromorphic deployment backends. SPA/NEF remains active: a 2026 preprint integrates spiking walking and arm control in simulated humanoid locomotion, while hardware deployment remains future work. [NengoDL](https://www.nengo.ai/nengo-dl/); [Nengo neurorobotics (2020)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2020.00461); [Steffen et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11034).
- **Potential advantage / failure modes.** The method offers interpretable transformations, explicit state, and a path to neuromorphic control. Nengo lowers the cost of implementing a specified function; it does not automatically discover useful cognitive programs or provide scalable perception. High-dimensional population costs, long temporal credit assignment and differences between smooth training and spike-time inference remain. No matched evidence establishes broad capability or energy advantage over modern dense models.
- **Novelty and falsifier.** SPA/NEF, vector-symbolic composition, population transforms, GPU simulation and differentiable neural modeling are all direct prior art. **Confidence in a new class: 0/5.** A small navigation/control test with a sensor shift could compare hand-specified NEF transformations, trainable NengoDL transformations and a matched recurrent network on held-out compositions, recovery, latency and memory. Reject an advantage if it disappears at matched data, task interface and hardware.

#### AR-03 — Artificial immune systems

- **Original mechanism.** Negative-selection algorithms learn detectors that avoid known “self” patterns and flag unmatched or distant inputs. Clonal-selection methods copy and mutate detectors that match selected samples. Immune-network and dendritic-cell variants add interaction, diversity or context from multiple signals. Forrest et al. proposed self/nonself discrimination for computer security in 1994. [Forrest et al. (1994)](https://doi.org/10.1109/risp.1994.296580).
- **Primitive / information / use.** Detectors and memory cells encode regions/patterns, usually as bit strings or vectors. Inputs are normal/reference samples or a stream; outputs are an anomaly score, class or evolved detector set. Learning rejects self-reactive detectors or clones/mutates detectors by affinity; inference compares new input with this set. This is a specialized one-class/online-search mechanism, not a broad cognitive architecture.
- **Was it bad or early?** Older hardware hurt detector generation and matching, and modern vector accelerators or learned embeddings can make those cheaper. But more FLOPs do not remove the geometry issue: random detectors poorly cover sparse high-dimensional spaces; generation can be expensive; “non-self” is not one coherent distribution; and drift can turn yesterday's self pattern into tomorrow's anomaly. Later NSA variants explicitly add grids, triangulation, density and revised stopping rules. [High-dimensional NSA analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2017.09.005); [grid-based NSA](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2013.08.013).
- **Modernization / prior art.** AIS remains active. A 2022 paper combines negative and clonal selection for multi-class anomaly detection; a 2026 Applied Soft Computing paper proposes an AIS-style continual learner. This confirms a living specialized method family, not an undiscovered general architecture. [NSA/CSA anomaly detection (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2022.108838); [APC-CLCM (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2026.115123).
- **Modern hybrid audit addendum (2026-09-27).** The strongest limitations were not just a lack of compute: a 2009 idiotypic-network detector already proposed online updating for changing normal behavior; Immuno-Net RAILS already couples deep image-classifier features to clonal/exemplar search for adversarial robustness (a static-learning study); continual-classification methods already add immune memory during testing; and a 2026 RL-DCA learns feature assignments to danger/safe/pathogen signal categories. These close broad immune-network × online anomaly learning, immune memory × continual classification, neural features × clonal selection, and RL × dendritic-cell signal adaptation as new-architecture claims. Their application results do not solve whether an unfamiliar event is harmful, how to prevent poisoning, or whether gains persist under realistic drift. [Lau et al. (2009)](https://www.cs.york.ac.uk/rts/static/papers/R%3ALau%3A2009.pdf); [Wang et al., Immuno-Net RAILS (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02842); [CLCMNLD (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106423); [RL-DCA (2026)](https://doi.org/10.32604/cmes.2026.079034).
- **Novelty and falsifier.** Detector populations, immune memory, clonal adaptation and danger signals are known; confidence in a broad new class is **0/5**. On a synthetic drifting stream with rare anomalies, compare NSA/CSA with matched one-class density models, kNN, replay and online classification at equal memory/update cost. Measure false alarms on benign drift, rare-event recall, forgetting, detector count and compute. Reject if gains vanish after controlling representation and thresholds. **No experiment run.**

#### AR-04 — Tsetlin Machine: finite-state automata learning propositional clauses

- **Why it is included.** This omitted model class is relevant because its learning primitive is integer-state automata rather than gradient descent. Automata choose to include/exclude Boolean literals; resulting conjunctions vote for or against outputs, and reward/inaction/penalty feedback changes the automaton states. It dates to 2018, so it is a modern alternative rather than forgotten pre-deep-learning AI.
- **Repeated operation / information.** It stores explicit disjunctive-normal-form clauses over Boolean literals. Each labeled example produces local feedback; automata move between include/exclude states; clauses are evaluated and their vote returned. Convolutional, regression, reinforcement and relational variants exist. [Granmo, Tsetlin Machine (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01508).
- **Has hardware changed the picture?** Yes for one bottleneck: a massively parallel asynchronous implementation reports up to 50× faster learning and near-constant time for 20–7,000 clauses on a Tesla V100 over its tested range. This is a direct modernization, not an open claim that GPU-friendly automata are new. [Abeyrathna et al., ICML (2021)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/abeyrathna21a/abeyrathna21a.pdf). Continuous-feature automata and convolutional TMs/accelerators also exist. [Sparse continuous representation (2021)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/10/17/2107); [CTM accelerator (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.micpro.2023.104949).
- **Weaknesses / potential use.** It could be useful for low-power interpretable Boolean or relational patterns. It needs useful Boolean or discretized features; clause learning does not itself supply general perceptual features; many clauses may be required; stability can depend on feedback and representation settings. Variants reduce but do not eliminate the feature bottleneck.
- **Novelty and falsifier.** Automata, clauses, convolutional forms and GPU-parallel variants occupy the class. **Novelty confidence: 0/5.** A narrow test could compare Tsetlin, XCS and a compact recurrent model on online Boolean rule drift, matching observations and memory; track recovery and rule stability. Reject broad generality if gains require hand-coded Boolean features or disappear on held-out compositions. Do not promote as a new class.

#### AR-05 — Stochastic Diffusion Search

- **Original computation.** A population of agents retains partial hypotheses for a decomposable pattern-match/search problem. Each iteration an agent tests a cheap piece of its hypothesis; successful agents recruit peers through direct communication, while unsuccessful agents adopt another hypothesis. Clusters of partial successes identify promising candidates. The lineage begins with Bishop's 1989 thesis, with later formal resource-allocation analysis. [Bishop (1989), thesis record](https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.236643); [Nasuto, Bishop & Lauria, steady-state analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0202007).
- **Why early / why not general.** Cheap independent partial tests map naturally to parallel hardware, and large populations are now easier to run. But the method depends on decomposing a candidate score into cheap tests whose partial success predicts global quality. It searches hypotheses; it does not learn a rich representation or objective. More compute accelerates the metaheuristic without fixing poor factorization or deceptive subproblems.
- **Prior art / falsifier.** SDS is a known search algorithm adjacent to ant colony, particle swarm and evolution, not a new learner. On noisy transformed-pattern matching, compare against random-restart, hill-climbing and beam search at equal objective-evaluation budgets; reject if it does not improve success-per-evaluation or runtime. **No experiment run.**

**AR-05 modernization and hybrid source check (2026-09-27).** The family was not simply discarded for lack of hardware: a 2000 technical report already studied parallel implementation and spiking-neural realizations; a 2009 peer-reviewed paper specified NESTER, a spiking network intended to perform SDS-like partial-feature memory search. The 2013 review catalogs pattern matching, continuous optimization, robotics, medical imaging, and hardware variants. Formal analysis later characterizes global convergence and expected steady-state allocation of agents under stated search assumptions. However, those results depend on decomposable partial evidence: local tests must provide enough signal that mutually consistent hypotheses identify the best global match. The stability proof does not remove false optima when this assumption fails, nor the communication/coordination cost in weakly connected or heterogeneous spaces. Direct hybrids are also established: SDS has been combined with particle swarm optimization and differential evolution for continuous optimization; SDS with n-tuple RAM was used for facial feature identification/tracking; a connectionist spiking variant already treats the mechanism as a neural search model. Thus GPUs/parallel hardware can accelerate testing and diffusion, but do not turn a search heuristic into a representation learner or broad model class. Class novelty remains **0/5**. Keep only as a comparator when partial-factor search is a natural workload, and charge neighbor selection, communication, and failed hypotheses against full objective evaluations. [Al-Rifaie & Bishop, review (2013)](https://doi.org/10.2478/pjbr-2013-0021); [Nasuto & Bishop, steady-state analysis (2002 preprint / 2015 journal)](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0202007); [Nasuto et al., spiking SDS/NESTER (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2008.03.019); [SDS–PSO/Differential Evolution hybrid source review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2212683X15000158).

#### AR-06 — Stigmergic memory in recurrent networks

- **Mechanism.** A shared memory surface accumulates deposits/removals from activity; this changed surface influences later updates and coordinates processing indirectly. Galatolo et al. made this a recurrent-neural memory in 2019, testing supervised MNIST with rows or pen-stroke sequences. [Galatolo et al. (2019)](https://doi.org/10.5220/0007581508300836); [paper PDF](https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2019/75815/75815.pdf).
- **Potential strength.** Persistent external traces could coordinate asynchronous components without all-to-all state transfer and preserve information when recurrent hidden state is overwritten.
- **Weakness / novelty.** Ant-colony pheromone, blackboards and shared-memory networks are established, and the specific RNN already exists. Its early evaluation does not establish long-lag memory. Traces can form stale loops, slow recovery after shifts, or encode just another recurrent state in a costly substrate. No broad new architecture.
- **Falsifier.** Test delayed sequence recall with interference and distribution shift; compare SM-RNN with LSTM/GRU, linear state-space and shared-memory baselines at matched parameters/update budgets. Measure recall vs delay, interference, adaptation and wall time. Reject if the effect is confined to short MNIST sequence proxies. **No experiment run.**
- **Modern revival and prior art addendum (2026-09-27).** The mechanism was not merely waiting for neural hardware. By 2014, synthetic pheromones had already been used as persistent environmental state for reinforcement learning, and Phe-Q learning was an earlier multi-agent example. Xu et al. later coupled digital pheromone to independent RL as an indirect communication medium, with local conflict-avoidance networks and federated policy training, and tested decentralized shape formation. Habanero (2024) automatically designs pheromone controllers and tests eight real robots across four missions. Its authors identify continuous pheromone intensity/decay and direct-versus-indirect communication as open design questions. Recent preprints apply deep RL to robot congestion coordination and use trained stigmergic agents to control ant-swarm phase behavior through the shared pheromone field. A separate 2025 model formally connects nematode pheromone-mediated aggregation to cross-learning and reports that stale traces can trap the system; a minority of pheromone-insensitive exploratory agents restores switching in its simulations. Thus shared environmental traces plus learned policies are directly established, and added compute does not remove stale-feedback, trace-capacity, credit-assignment, or task-specificity problems. [Barbosa et al. (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1155/2014/932485); [Xu et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TNNLS.2021.3056418); [Aina & Ha (2025 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03592); [Vellinger et al. (2025 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20095); [Pitteri et al. (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17709).

#### AR-07 — Membrane/P systems

- **Primitive.** Nested or graph-structured membranes hold multisets of symbolic objects. Local multiset-rewrite rules apply in parallel; objects cross membranes, rules may have priorities, and some variants divide or dissolve compartments. [Păun, *Computing with Membranes* (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1006/jcss.1999.1693).
- **Historical weakness / technology change.** Some theoretical variants give polynomial-step solutions by consuming exponential space. Parallel hardware can speed simulation of a finite P system and membrane systems have been combined with ML subroutines, but simulation on conventional hardware still pays for synchronization, state growth and hand-designed rules. Complexity results do not imply practical learning advantages. [Păun et al. (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0303-2647(00)00143-X).
- **Verdict / falsifier.** This is an established unconventional model of computation, not a general learning architecture. On a finite rule-learning task, compare a learned P-system controller with the same rule set executed as a multithreaded worklist and conventional symbolic state machine, including rule search and memory. Reject if its parallel semantics yield no end-to-end advantage after excluding exponential-space shortcuts.

#### AR-08 — Neuroendocrine robot controllers

- **Original mechanism / modernization.** Slow hormone-like variables modulate neural circuits or plasticity while fast feedback loops produce movement. A 2012 ultrastable controller predates modern DL; a 2022 physical hexapod combines a central pattern generator, artificial hormone network and unsupervised input-correlation learning to adapt to unpredictable terrain. [Ultrastable controller (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1177/1059712312462249); [physical hexapod controller (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TNNLS.2021.3119127).
- **Was it merely early?** Modern simulators, sensors and robots help test richer disturbances. But this mechanism already demonstrated physical online adaptation, so there is no evidence it disappeared only due to weak historical hardware. More compute has not turned it into broad reasoning or representation learning.
- **Weakness / falsifier.** Hormone dynamics, stability envelopes and modulatory credit can be hand-designed; no evidence they give a universal inductive bias. Compare against adaptive PID, matched CPG and online model-based control under equal sensors/energy; measure violation time, recovery, actuator energy and collateral change. Reject broad claims if benefits stay task-specific.

#### AR-09–11 — Independent invention attempts that collided with known mechanisms

The inventing subagent returned five mechanisms; no files were edited by it. I checked the central prior-art claims before recording them.

- **Oscillator-phase binding (AR-09):** feature units use oscillator phase; local excitation/global inhibition synchronize features of one object and separate competing groups. Direct prior art is LEGION, whose 1997 paper binds image pixels using phase and whose successors study segmentation, attention and noisy scenes. [Wang & Terman (1997)](https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1997.9.4.805). A noisy two-object test is possible, but the mechanism and synchronization costs are known.
- **Nonlinear dendritic temporal units (AR-10):** branching cable dynamics, local voltage and synaptic eligibility let each cell compute/learn temporal feature conjunctions. A detailed pyramidal-cell model already learned spatial/temporal feature-binding tasks using a dendrite-derived local rule. [Jones & Kording (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroscience.2021.07.036); [Jones et al., Neuron (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2021.09.044). Temporal XOR could test an inductive-bias advantage over point neurons, but this is a unit-level hypothesis, not a new general model class.
- **Compositional lens-update learner (AR-11):** source structures and task views are linked by bidirectional lenses; edits to a view propagate into the source while maintaining round-trip laws. Lenses are already connected categorically to compositional supervised learners; bidirectional transformations are mature prior art. [Fong & Johnson, *Lenses and Learners* (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.03671). Keep only as a narrow experiment seed if correction traces can induce robust update policies without a hand-authored schema. Generate nested records with invariant-preserving edits; compare fixed lenses and one-way learning on violations, collateral edits and sample count. Do not claim novelty yet.
- **Stigmergic artifact memory** was also independently proposed; ant-colony, blackboard and AR-06 prior art closes the broad idea. A graph-allocation task could still benchmark trace coordination against Ant System and a central scheduler.
- **Tsetlin finite-state clause learning** is recorded under AR-04; it is an established architecture and a useful Boolean-rule baseline.

### Hybrid audit — NARS resource allocation × active perception

- **Source mechanisms and exact coupling.** NARS/ONA contributes priority-driven task/belief scheduling, evidence revision, goals and operations under limited resources. Active perception chooses what, where or how to sense. The proposed deep loop is: reasoning identifies which uncertainty blocks a goal; the scheduler budgets a concrete sensor computation/action; returned evidence revises beliefs and priorities; learned reliability/cost affects later allocation.
- **Why it is tempting.** A neural front-end may spend compute on irrelevant pixels or process all modalities before context is known. Reasoning can identify which evidence would separate candidate explanations; sensing can acquire it. The interaction changes when perception runs and which observations enter learning.
- **Prior art.** NARS' 2022 perception paper already describes perception as goal-directed and active, sensor/actuator operations, and attention-based feature selection in a shared reasoning process. ONA has event-driven sensorimotor reasoning; robotics has a long active-sensing/value-of-information line; a 2022 NARS/neural-detector system combines deep visual detection/tracking with adaptive NARS over perceptual sequences. [Unified perception (2022)](https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2022.806403); [NARS + deep detection for collision warning (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15076); [active-sensing source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2963579/).
- **Possible seam, low confidence.** A learned value-of-computation rule allocates internal perception operations (crop, frame rate, resolution or modality) according to expected reduction in action-relevant evidential uncertainty; later outcomes calibrate both inference priorities and sensory costs. The high-level idea is established. Any novelty would have to lie in this specific calibrated coupled update and performance under equal budgets.
- **Small falsifier.** In a simple partially observed robot task, make low-resolution vision cheap and high-resolution crops or tactile probes costly. Compare fixed sensing, learned active sensing, ONA-like priority without cost learning, and the full coupled rule with the same base encoder and compute budget. Randomize lighting and sensor costs midway. Measure goal success per latency/compute, false-belief persistence, calibration and recovery. Reject if the full loop fails to beat the strongest active-sensing baseline or needs a hand-coded value table. **No experiment run; a CPU simulator suffices for an initial test.**

#### AR-12 — Polyscheme: synchronized focus traces across unlike algorithms

- **Original mechanism.** Cassimatis et al. describe algorithms from unlike formalisms as strategies that request a sequence of common operations over a shared focus. A focus denotes a proposition with time and world arguments; it is an interlingua, not the system's only data structure. At each focus, all specialists report opinions, read the other specialists' opinions, update their private memories/inferences, and can request the next focus. A focus manager schedules this loop. The 2007 implementation used a simple queue. The paper demonstrates case-retrieval suggestions changing a WalkSAT search state, constraint checking correcting a mismatched case, and a perception specialist injecting new evidence during inference. [Cassimatis et al., AAAI 2007](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/2007/AAAI07-241.pdf); original [Polyscheme thesis record](https://www.media.mit.edu/publications/polyscheme-a-cognitive-architecture-for-integrating-multiple-representation-and-inference-schemes/).
- **What it computes / unit / communication.** The unit is one scheduled focus fixation. It binds a proposition, time interval and hypothetical world; specialist algorithms each produce an opinion and local changes in response, then enqueue follow-up focuses. Communication happens through opinions on the common focus and private specialist state, not through a large shared blackboard. With (S) specialists, the paper's all-pairs opinion exchange is (O(S^2)) per focus in its direct form; a practical redesign would need typed subscriptions or sparse routing and must be checked for changed semantics.
- **Knowledge and learning.** Knowledge lives in specialist-owned structures: scripts/cases, constraints, probabilistic networks, sensor state, etc. The architecture can retain cases and update specialized knowledge, but it does not provide a common learned representation or a general learned focus policy. Algorithm selection is mostly encoded in specialist `ModifyFM` strategies; the illustrated manager is queue-based. This is a deliberately small control substrate rather than end-to-end learning.
- **Inference and use.** Run the focus loop, let each specialist update/infer on the selected proposition, and continue while the goal, resource bound, or stopping condition permits. The original use cases span occlusion-aware robot tracking and path recovery, probabilistic/PCFG parsing, and heterogeneous data retrieval. It may help when a fast but brittle case/script system and a slower flexible search/inference system must repair one another at intermediate steps.
- **Historical limits and what changed.** The paper's motivating robotics task found a full SAT physical model infeasible even on a coarse grid, while a case path gave a fast initial guess that constraint search repaired. That is a real scale bottleneck, but the more general adoption friction is specialist engineering: every specialist must implement compatible Store/Opinion/Match/focus-update behavior, and the shared proposition/world semantics are demanding. A central focus synchronizes every specialist, so latency and communication grow with specialists/fixations. GPU parallelism could batch independent local specialist calculations and learned perception/simulation; it does not remove semantic mapping, synchronization, or poor scheduler choices. Modern simulators and learned dynamics make richer hypothetical-world specialists practical, but learned world models can drift and hallucinate.
- **Closest prior art and novelty judgment.** Polyscheme is itself direct prior art for heterogeneous algorithmic hybrids under a shared focus scheduler. Soar's impasse-driven problem spaces, ACT-R/CLARION, blackboards, and metareasoning overlap portions; Polyscheme's distinctive historical mechanism is that each algorithm is a control strategy over synchronized focus traces, not merely a component chosen at a coarse boundary. There is no new architecture here. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 for Polyscheme revival; 1/5 for the narrow scheduler experiment below.** It is worth a small CPU test as a revival/control study, not as a proposed new general model class.
- **Potential narrow seam.** Replace the queue with a learned focus scheduler estimating expected goal progress, uncertainty reduction, wall-clock cost and specialist staleness; specialists propose typed foci, and the scheduler meters them under a budget. Keep specialist memories private and share only focus evidence. This changes computation scheduling, but value-of-computation, metareasoning, active sensing, and learned planning policies are broad prior art. The only potential distinction is whether cross-specialist evidence on the *same partial hypothetical branch* yields useful work reuse and calibrated cost/progress estimates that a standard planner does not obtain. Treat this as a testable implementation question, not a novelty claim.
- **Small falsifier.** CPU-only partially observed maze with changing obstacles; implement reactive safety, case-script retrieval, symbolic constraint search, and a learned transition predictor. Compare fixed pipeline, fixed module switching, original queue focus, learned cost/progress focus, and an oracle focus schedule under equal specialist operations and simulator calls. Track success, time-to-replan after a reveal, redundant repeated branch work, stale contradictory opinions, starvation, and runtime. The claim fails if the adaptive focus has no Pareto gain over the strongest fixed schedule or if gains disappear when simulator/search calls are matched. This experiment has **not** been run.

#### HY-23 — Polyscheme focus traces × learned world-model planning (broad hybrid rejected)

- **Constituents.** Polyscheme contributes synchronized opinions and specialist-requested focus; Dyna/world-model planning contributes learned dynamics and planning updates during interaction; case/script and constraint specialists contribute fast proposals plus consistency checks.
- **Exact proposed coupling.** A focus is keyed by a hypothetical branch/world ID and state proposition. The learned dynamics specialist predicts a successor or uncertainty for the currently focused branch; a case specialist may propose a multi-step script on that same branch; a constraint specialist rejects or repairs inconsistent predicted states; each specialist can request the next focus under a shared compute ledger. The coupling should let a case jump-start model-based planning while constraints invalidate local errors, with other specialists reusing an already simulated branch instead of duplicating it.
- **Why the combined behavior differs from a simple side-by-side system.** All methods revise or inspect the same branch at each focus; the scheduler can redirect computation mid-inference as evidence or disagreement changes. A one-shot retrieval-then-plan pipeline cannot feed every intermediate search step back through all specialists. This is still exactly the sort of adaptive algorithmic hybrid Polyscheme was built to express.
- **Closest prior work.** Polyscheme itself already interleaves case-based reasoning, search, and perception, and supports alternate worlds. Dyna directly couples acting, model learning, and planning; modern latent world-model agents (including Dreamer-family work) plan through imagined rollouts. The proposed composition mostly restates known mechanisms. [Sutton, Dyna (1990)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/1990/hash/d9fc5b73a8d78fad3d6dffe419384e70-Abstract.html); [Dream to Control (2018)](https://research.google/pubs/dream-to-control-learning-behaviors-by-latent-imagination/).
- **Advantage and failure modes.** Possible gains: avoid duplicated imagined rollouts, correct model errors with explicit constraints, and recover quickly by reusing similar plans. Risks: focus synchronization/branch bookkeeping can cost more than duplicated cheap rollouts; correlated model/case errors evade constraints; a bad manager can starve a useful method; scheduler learning can overfit one maze; imagined branches can grow combinatorially.
- **Minimal experiment / decision.** Use HY-23's maze falsifier above and report saved model calls per success, branch-repair rate, and equal-budget solve rate against Dyna-style model-based planning, case retrieval + planner pipeline, and simple Polyscheme queue. Reject if only raw unbudgeted runtime improves, if planner quality is unchanged, or if standard cache/memoization gets the same reuse. No GPU needed. **Disposition: demote to a low-cost architecture integration experiment; no new-class claim.**

#### AR-13 — 4D/RCS hierarchical real-time control

- **Original mechanism.** RCS organizes recursive control nodes, each with sensory processing, a world model, value judgment, and behavior generation. Lower levels operate over short, fine-grained horizons while upper levels handle abstract concepts and longer plans; model predictions/evaluations feed plan selection and feedback loops at each level. [Albus et al., 4D/RCS reference model, NIST (2002)](https://www.nist.gov/publications/4drcs-reference-model-architecture-intelligent-unmanned-ground-vehicles); [NISTIR 6910](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.IR.6910).
- **Historical issue versus compute.** It was designed for real-time robotics and applied in UGV/control work, not simply abandoned for lack of GPUs. The NIST abstract explicitly states that at the time only lower levels had been fully implemented; the hard part is completing and validating the high-level hierarchy and its module interfaces. New perception encoders, learned world models and cheap simulation can help fill modules, but they do not decide the hierarchy, preserve calibrated predictions across scales, or guarantee safety.
- **Modernization/prior art.** Hierarchical reinforcement learning, behavior trees, options, receding-horizon MPC, and learned hierarchical world models already modernize parts of the approach. A faithful RCS revival should be a baseline in control research, not a fresh architecture label. Possible open seam: continual automatic discovery of hierarchy boundaries and contracts between its sensory/world-model/value/behavior modules.
- **Small falsifier and verdict.** CPU grid-robot simulator with two/three RCS levels versus behavior tree + flat planner under matched action and planning budgets, testing unseen obstacle dynamics and task switching. Measure task success, reaction delay, replans, recovery and unsafe actions. Reject a hierarchy advantage if it does not improve the reaction/planning trade-off or only works with hand-written decomposition. **Established architecture, 0/5 broad novelty; revival benchmark only.**

#### AR-14 — BDI practical reasoning and intention management

- **Original mechanism.** Beliefs, desires and intentions are explicit dynamic stores plus an event queue. A practical loop updates beliefs, generates options, deliberates/adopts intentions, selects a plan from a library, executes a step, and reconsiders or drops intentions when they are satisfied or no longer achievable. The 1995 practical architecture explicitly avoids implementing the full temporal/modal theory as an unconstrained theorem prover because reasoning time could be unbounded and destroy reactivity; it uses a compact executable interpreter instead. [Rao & Georgeff, ICMAS 1995](https://cdn.aaai.org/ICMAS/1995/ICMAS95-042.pdf).
- **Historical issue versus compute.** This was not primarily starved by hardware. The central trade-off is deliberation boundedness versus expressivity, and the dependency on hand-authored plan libraries, event handling and intention reconsideration rules. Faster CPUs help bounded reasoning, but unbounded deliberation remains unbounded and more generated plans can worsen choice/reconsideration.
- **Modernization/prior art.** BDI remains a deployed agent-programming family. Satori (2024 preprint) pairs BDI user modeling with a multimodal LLM for proactive AR guidance; it is direct application-level BDI+LLM prior art, though not necessarily a general BDI agent architecture. Modernization can use learned perception or plan generation behind the BDI interface, but “LLM proposes plans; BDI commits/executes” is not a new computational class. [Satori](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16668). A specific testable seam is learning when intention persistence should be interrupted from outcome and switching-cost feedback while enforcing safety constraints.
- **Small falsifier and verdict.** CPU hidden-state task with interruptions, stale beliefs, and changing goals; compare fixed BDI commitment, reactive replanning, and a learned interruption/reconsideration rule under the same plan library and deliberation budget. Track completed goals, unnecessary reversals, stale-intention errors and response latency. Reject if gains require hand-coded goal-specific exceptions or the learned rule fails under goal distribution shift. **Established; 0/5 broad novelty.**

#### AR-15 — Case-based reasoning cycle

- **Original mechanism.** Retrieve a similar prior case, reuse/adapt its solution, revise/evaluate it against the current task, and retain the corrected case. Memory and adaptation—not only nearest-neighbor lookup—are the central computational cycle.
- **Historical issue versus compute.** Large case bases made indexing and similarity expensive, but the harder limits are semantically useful similarity, structural alignment, solution adaptation and avoiding harmful case accumulation. ANN indexes and learned embeddings address retrieval speed; they do not guarantee that a retrieved case is adaptable or that retaining it improves future behavior.
- **Modernization/prior art.** End-to-end/neural CBR, neural case adaptation, and deep embedding retrieval have directly modernized this line. The 2023 EACL end-to-end CBR study uses retrieve/reuse but identifies adaptation as difficult and often omitted in practice. [ECBRF (EACL 2023)](https://aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.255.pdf); [Ye et al. on neural case adaptation (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07095). A new general architecture claim would be false. Candidate seam only: online learning of *repair operators* with explicit invariants and counterfactual failure credit, rather than just a learned retrieval metric. This overlaps program synthesis and repair.
- **Small falsifier and verdict.** Generate structured planning cases with controlled feature shifts and invariant-preserving solution edits. Compare fixed similarity + hand adapter, learned retrieval only, retrieval plus learned repair, and matched parametric planner under equal memory/update budgets. Measure held-out composition solve rate, collateral edits, repair steps, retention interference and latency. Reject if retrieval improves but final solution validity/generalization does not. **Established; 0/5 broad novelty, keep as retrieval/adaptation baseline.**

#### AR-16 — Constraint propagation with search

- **Original mechanism.** Represent variables with finite domains and relations; repeatedly remove values unsupported by neighboring constraints (node/arc/path consistency); propagate domain changes and branch/backtrack when local propagation stalls. [Mackworth, “Consistency in Networks of Relations” (1977)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(77)90007-8).
- **Historical issue versus compute.** Constraint propagation is efficient and valuable but incomplete; exact search remains combinatorial in the worst case. Faster hardware changes constants, and modern CP/SAT solvers are highly optimized, but cannot erase worst-case complexity. The challenge is choosing useful decompositions/branch variables and handling distribution shift.
- **Modernization/prior art.** Neural and RL branching heuristics, learned CSP solvers and learned policies inside CP solvers already target these bottlenecks: [PDP (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01969), [Neuro# (AAAI 2021)](https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/17474/17474-13-20968-1-2-20210518.pdf), [learned variable ordering for CSP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10762). This overlaps the notebook's Constraint Crystal work, so no separate candidate is promoted.
- **Small falsifier and verdict.** CPU graph-coloring and Latin-square families varying treewidth and train/test generators; compare AC-3+MRV, CP-SAT and learned branching under matched wall time/node budgets with exact validity. Measure solved instances, nodes, model overhead and out-of-distribution degradation. Reject a learned benefit if node reductions do not translate to equal-budget solves or vanish on shifted instances. **Established reasoning primitive; 0/5 broad novelty.**

### Hybrid correction — NARS budgeted reasoning × cost-sensitive active sensing

An adversarial prior-art audit found a closer collision than the prior paragraph recorded: Tan's 1991 **CS-QL** directly couples cost-sensitive sensor-feature selection, a task-dependent state description, and Q-learning. It selects cost-effective sensing features and updates the state representation and policy jointly. Its experiment assumes a finite deterministic environment, known feature costs, and noiseless sensors; it also reports a stability/learning-cost trade-off when state descriptions are refined. [Tan, AAAI 1991](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/1991/AAAI91-121.pdf).

This does **not** collapse exactly to NARS/ONA: CS-QL is a task-dependent perceptual representation plus action-value learner, not a general evidence-weighted reasoning system with NARS' resource-budgeted concept/task semantics. But it closes the broad “reasoning chooses costly sensing and jointly learns from the result” novelty claim. ONA's global priority mechanism does not, in the cited description, make sensor invocation cost an explicit learned quantity. The residual seam—online learning under noisy sensors and drifting/nonstationary latency, with goal-conditioned sensor value inside a shared budget scheduler—is a conventional extension to cost-sensitive active sensing/value-of-information, not a new architecture class. **Revise novelty confidence to 0.5/5.**

- **Experiment retained only as a narrow coupling test.** Small partially observed gridworld with noisy cheap sensing, accurate costly zoom, changing goals, and drifting observation latency. Compare default ONA-like prioritization, ONA plus a separately computed cost-sensitive value-of-information controller, a Tan-style joint task-dependent representation/policy, and the proposed common priority scheduler under matched sensor/inference budgets; include an oracle-cost upper bound. Log success, sensing cost, latency and recovery when goals/costs shift. Falsify coupling if the scheduler does not beat the strongest decomposed/joint baseline outside seed noise or only beats default prioritization. CPU-only; not run.
