Compare BACON-style trend/constancy transforms and an active-query variant with symbolic-regression/AI-Feynman-style search at equal simulator calls and evaluation work. Add realistic noise and nuisance variables; score exact law recovery, query count and transfer to unseen equation forms. Reject the modernization if gains require hand-added transformations, disappear under noise, or lose to symbolic regression at matched query budget. **Not run.**

#### HY-35 — BACON regularity discovery × EURISKO meta-heuristic search (rejected as a new class)

- **Source mechanisms and exact coupling.** BACON contributes evidence-driven construction of derived numeric terms and hypotheses. EURISKO contributes an explicit agenda and heuristics that can propose, specialize and revise other heuristics. A deep coupling would turn BACON’s transformations, residuals and hypothesis failures into typed evidence slots; EURISKO-style meta-heuristics would use that evidence to revise which feature transformations to generate, which experiments to query, and how competing laws are scored. Revised search heuristics would then steer the next BACON-like observation/transform cycle. This changes both representation growth and data acquisition, rather than merely chaining output from one program to another.
- **Why behavior might differ.** The system could adapt its equation vocabulary and experiment policy from the same feedback, allowing a failed law to revise both a feature transformation and the next query. This couples object-level discovery to control of the discovery process; either source system alone uses a more fixed search language or priority scheme.
- **Prior art and rejection.** The generic hybrid was proposed in 1985 by Paul R. VanArragon: his *Automated Discovery* report explicitly suggests incorporating BACON-like systems into an overall EURISKO-like system so they could combine in discovering knowledge. That report proposes the integration rather than implementing this exact loop. Modern symbolic regression already develops transformation grammars, meta-search and active queries; AI Feynman recursively creates simpler derived datasets, and current automated-discovery systems couple hypothesis generation with experimental testing. Thus the broad combination is not new, while the proposed typed evidence-to-meta-heuristic update has not yet been specified tightly enough to claim a surviving mechanism. **Novelty confidence: 0.05/5; reject generic hybrid, preserve only as a falsifiable design pattern.** [VanArragon, 1985, Waterloo report CS-85-14](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/research/tr/1985/CS-85-14.pdf); [AI Feynman](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7159912/); [2025 review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10994-025-06955-2).
- **Small disproof test.** Use the AR-39 simulator suite with a typed grammar and held-out equation families. Compare fixed BACON, BACON plus EURISKO-style heuristic mutation, grammar-guided symbolic regression, and an active symbolic-regression baseline at matched query/evaluation budgets. Measure held-out law recovery, queries to distinguish competing forms, rule reuse across equation families, invalid transformations and runtime. The coupling fails if it only wins with oracle transformation rules, does not improve query efficiency or transfer, or spends more compute changing its heuristics than it saves in search. **Not run; no architecture claim survives yet.**

### Scientific structure inference archaeology — DENDRAL and Meta-DENDRAL

#### AR-40 — DENDRAL / Meta-DENDRAL (1964–1980s): constrained graph hypothesis search plus domain-model-directed rule induction

- **Original computation.** Heuristic DENDRAL takes a molecular formula and mass spectrum and proposes molecular graphs. Its 1968 description divides the program into preliminary inference, data adjustment, a nonredundant structure generator, a rough forward mass-spectrometer predictor, and an evaluator that compares predicted with observed peaks and ranks candidates. The generator uses data-derived required/forbidden substructure lists and spectral constraints to prune the graph search. The source reports execution on a PDP-6, about 80,000 words of memory, and an initial noncyclic structure generator; it explicitly names poor handling of ringed structures and its formative fragmentation theory as limitations. It also warns that heuristic constraints can bypass the correct structure and that outputs often remained a shortlist, not one uniquely established answer. [Buchanan, Sutherland & Feigenbaum, 1968/1969 primary paper](https://digirepo.nlm.nih.gov/ext/document/101584906X920/PDF/101584906X920.pdf).
- **Meta-level learning.** Meta-DENDRAL is a related but distinct system, not merely DENDRAL’s performance module. Given spectra from molecules whose structures are known, it uses INTSUM to reinterpret peaks and summarize evidence, RULEGEN to search a constrained grammar of possible fragmentation rules, and RULEMOD to test negative evidence, specialize/generalize, merge and remove redundant rules. The 1977 account reports expert-judged rules and explicitly frames domain-knowledge acquisition as the bottleneck; this is a useful early example of learning symbolic mechanisms from observations, with the search space tightly bounded by chemistry and rule syntax. [Feigenbaum, “The Art of Artificial Intelligence: Themes and Case Studies of Knowledge Engineering,” IJCAI 1977](https://www.ijcai.org/Past%20Proceedings/IJCAI-77-VOL2/PDF/092.pdf); [Buchanan et al., 1976 Meta-DENDRAL paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00436a017).
- **What it represented and did repeatedly.** The primary inference unit is a partial chemical graph constrained by valence and evidence; the meta-learning unit is a candidate subgraph-to-fragmentation production rule with positive and negative support. DENDRAL repeatedly extends/prunes graph hypotheses, simulates spectra and reorders surviving structures. Meta-DENDRAL repeatedly maps spectral peaks to possible bond-break events, expands supported rule patterns and rejects rules contradicted by data. Inputs are spectra plus formula (DENDRAL), or spectra plus known molecular structures (Meta-DENDRAL); outputs are ranked structures, or interpretable fragmentation rules with evidence summaries.
- **Learning, inference and memory.** DENDRAL’s data-sensitive constraints and hand-authored chemistry heuristics guide inference; its forward predictor supplies a check on candidate graphs. Meta-DENDRAL performs bounded symbolic induction over rule descriptions. Memory is explicit: graph hypotheses, constraint lists, spectra, rule candidates, evidence counts and accepted rules. The system can learn after deployment in the limited sense that new spectra/rules can update an explicit rule base, but each expansion requires domain-valid vocabulary, measurement interpretation and safeguards against inconsistent rules.
- **Was it bad or early?** Hardware was a real constraint: a large graph search and knowledge program ran within PDP-6 memory and compute limits. Modern memory, fast graph algorithms, parallel search, high-resolution MS/MS, larger curated spectral databases and simulation can ease candidate generation and evaluation. But speed did not cure the deeper limits: underdetermined spectra, false pruning from brittle constraints, incomplete fragmentation theory, limited chemical/ring coverage, instrument/domain shift, and expert effort in selecting useful representations. The 1993 retrospective attributes DENDRAL’s competence to detailed chemical knowledge, supporting the view that the bottleneck was never compute alone. [Lindsay et al., 1993 retrospective](https://web.mit.edu/6.034/www/6.s966/dendral-history.pdf).
- **Modernization and nearest prior art.** This architecture has already been modernized in its own application. Competitive Fragmentation Modeling learns probabilistic fragmentation transitions; CFM-ID 4.0 combines a learned fragmentation module with explicit class-specific rules and reports gains for supported chemical classes, with little or no benefit when the rule base does not cover the domain. [CFM-ID 4.0](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465). The MassSpecGym benchmark now provides 231,000 curated spectra for 29,000 molecules and structure-aware splits for de novo graph generation, retrieval and spectrum simulation. [MassSpecGym, NeurIPS 2024](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/c6c31413d5c53b7d1c343c1498734b0f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf). A 2026 bioRxiv preprint, AIMe/DeepMS2Reasoner, couples a graph Transformer that scores fragmentation actions with explicit chemical operators, feasibility checks and fragmentation-DAG propagation; treat it as a preprint, not settled validation. [AIMe preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.05.743095v1.full).
- **Potential advantage and residual.** DENDRAL remains a strong design pattern where exact combinatorial outputs, hard domain constraints, forward simulation and inspectable explanations matter. A tightly scoped modern study could ask whether learning which *partial-graph constraints are safe to apply early* reduces search without false-pruning under noisy spectra and scaffold shift. But learned graph/action ordering, learned fragmentation and neuro-symbolic pruning already occupy much of that territory. No general new architecture or sufficiently distinct coupling survives this prior-art pass. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as a class; retain as archaeology, not a candidate.**
- **Small falsifiable CPU prototype (planned, not run).** Use a tiny acyclic C/N/O graph grammar (4–8 heavy atoms) and a known stochastic fragmentation simulator. Compare (i) exhaustive canonical graph enumeration plus spectrum scoring, (ii) DENDRAL-style required/forbidden-subgraph pruning plus symbolic forward prediction, and (iii) a learned partial-graph prioritizer that may reorder expansions but cannot prune. Hold total predictor calls fixed; train on some functional groups and test held-out combinations under peak deletion/noise. Measure top-k exact-graph recovery, expansions, false-prune rate, runtime and abstention on isomers with indistinguishable spectra. Reject any proposed learned-guidance advantage if it fails to reduce expansions at matched accuracy, sacrifices correct-structure recall under modest noise, or only works with hand-supplied oracle constraints. This tests search economics, not architecture novelty.

#### HY-36 — DENDRAL-style symbolic constraints × learned fragmentation/action scores (rejected as a new hybrid)

- **Source mechanisms and coupling.** The symbolic side represents legal graph edits, chemical constraints and explicit fragmentation rules. The learned side scores candidate fragmentations from graph and experimental context. In a genuine coupling, the scorer assigns mass over actions generated by a symbolic operator set; only feasible actions enter a probability-weighted fragmentation DAG, and downstream spectrum agreement updates the action scorer.
- **Why it could behave differently.** It would make the learned component allocate search over a structured, chemically legal transition space while the symbolic component carries exact atom accounting and removes impossible trajectories. A separate graph predictor appended after an LLM or classifier would not realize this mechanism.
- **Prior art / decision.** This coupling is directly instantiated by CFM-ID 4.0’s rule-based-plus-learned modules at a coarser level, and more closely by the 2026 AIMe preprint’s neural action likelihoods coupled to deterministic fragmentation operators, chemical-feasibility checks and DAG mass propagation. Meta-DENDRAL already separated rule induction from performance use. The exact proposed couplings are therefore not new; a future contribution would need an independently justified update rule or a demonstrable new search/learning behavior, neither of which has been identified. **Novelty confidence: 0.05/5; reject generic hybrid.** [CFM-ID 4.0](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465); [AIMe preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.05.743095v1.full).
- **Small disproof experiment.** On the AR-40 simulator, compare rule-only, learned-action-only, and coupled search at matched transition budgets on held-out scaffolds. Measure exact structure top-k, chemically invalid path rate, expansion count, spectrum score and rule transfer. The coupling is not useful if it does not improve held-out accuracy or search cost at the same budget, or if gains disappear under spectral noise.

- **Continuation/resource update:** This pass verified the original Heuristic DENDRAL paper, Meta-DENDRAL's primary IJCAI description and JACS record, the 1993 project retrospective, CFM-ID 4.0, MassSpecGym and the AIMe 2026 preprint. AR-40 is recorded as archaeology, not promoted; HY-36 is rejected as a generic hybrid. Literature review only: no prototype or GPU experiment ran, GPU use and peak VRAM were both 0 GB, and live GPU occupancy was not sampled because no GPU experiment was started. Before any future GPU work, inspect VRAM and process owners and enforce the shared 5.5 GB target and 1 GB headroom. Next: continue into analog/continuous-time and less-covered cognitive/control architectures; source-check any independent leads before promoting them. C001–C031 remain untouched.

### Optical, analog-sensory, and context-sensitive cognitive architectures

#### AR-41 — Optical / holographic associative memory (1970s–1990s): diffraction-based content-addressed recall

- **Original computation and unit.** A volume hologram records interference information linking an input pattern to an output pattern. Illuminating the recorded medium with a cue reconstructs the associated output through diffraction, so many spatial products are computed in parallel. A 1989 two-layer optical memory added thermoplastic holographic plates and a liquid-crystal light valve for gain and thresholding; its feedback loop made recognition and associative completion a stable dynamical state. This is a physical optical-memory architecture, distinct from C006's vector-symbolic use of the word *holographic*. [Hong & Psaltis, 1986](https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lo/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/OL_11_812_Dec1986.pdf); [Hsu, Li & Psaltis, 1989](https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?uri=OAM-1989-WJ1).
- **Input, operation, output and storage.** Input is an optical pattern; repeated linear diffraction and, in feedback variants, nonlinear thresholding produce one or more reconstructed stored patterns. Knowledge resides in interference gratings and the optical interconnection geometry. Training/write operations record pairs or networks of associations; inference is illumination, propagation and optional feedback convergence. It suits low-latency content-addressed image recall, pattern completion and optical correlation when memory is spatial and sensor/compute stay in the optical path.
- **Historical limit and what changed.** Optical parallelism and interconnect fan-out were real strengths, but storage was not unbounded: Hong and Psaltis derived a capacity bound from hologram space-bandwidth product and showed that multiplexed exposures create crosstalk that degrades recall fidelity. Analog precision, writable/erasable media, nonlinear thresholding, optical-electronic conversion and limited depth were additional issues. Modern spatial-light modulators, integrated photonics, better optical nonlinearities and GPU simulation make systems easier to prototype; they do not remove information-capacity, crosstalk or I/O limits.
- **Modern prior art and novelty.** This is a hardware revival of associative memory, not a new general model class. A January 2026 *Physical Review Applied* paper experimentally implements two- and four-body dense associative memory interactions with a nonlinear-optical Hopfield network and reports improved pattern storage on MNIST. [Musa et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1103/7jh8-2vny). A June 2026 arXiv preprint proposes a two-volume-hologram cascade with a nonlinear coded plane that computes the modern Hopfield softmax-retrieval map; it explicitly rests on dense-associative-memory theory rather than a new retrieval primitive. The complete cascade is not an integrated experimental demonstration: the preprint outlines a proposed recording medium and demonstrates only some component functions. [Brady & Neory, 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18492). Thus any residual is a physical device/material, recording-medium or throughput contribution, not a retrieval-model contribution. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as an AI architecture; useful physical-computing archaeology.**
- **Small CPU falsifier (planned, not run).** Generate correlated and uncorrelated binary patterns and simulate (i) one-shot linear holographic correlation, (ii) correlation-plus-threshold feedback, (iii) classical Hopfield, and (iv) dense-Hopfield retrieval under equal pattern and operation budgets. Sweep overlap, cue corruption, and additive/crosstalk noise; measure exact recall, false attractors, iterations and capacity. If optical equations provide no recall or operation-count advantage after charging threshold/feedback and storage fidelity, the revival claim is only a hardware-implementation question. Energy and latency advantages still require physical measurements.

#### AR-42 — Mead–Mahowald silicon retina and Lyon–Mead analog cochlea (1980s): continuous-time computation at the sensor

- **Original computation and unit.** The 1988 silicon retina computes a logarithmic response to incident light, spatially smooths receptor values through a resistive network, and amplifies the local-minus-smoothed contrast. A fabricated 48×48 array reproduced several retinal bipolar-cell characteristics. The analog cochlea uses micropower CMOS and cascaded, nearly linear second-order filters with controllable Q to approximate cochlear traveling-wave frequency analysis, including adaptation and active gain. The repeated unit is a local analog circuit/filter coupled to neighboring or frequency-ordered units. [Mead & Mahowald, 1988](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/fmtk4-y3964); [Lyon & Mead, 1988](https://doi.org/10.1109/29.1639).
- **Input, output, learning and memory.** Light or sound enters directly at the device; analog state evolves continuously and emits contrast or frequency-channel signals for downstream recognition/control. The circuits mostly encode fixed physical priors rather than learn an open-ended model. Knowledge lies in circuit topology, time constants, biases and the sensor's adaptation state; inference is local continuous-time transduction and filtering. Their natural use is low-latency, low-power sensing under wide illumination or bandwidth limits, not general reasoning.
- **Was the idea bad or early?** These devices were not failures waiting on GPU-scale compute: the architecture depends on specialized analog VLSI and close sensor coupling, and in fact used contemporary CMOS effectively. Early chip area, fabrication, mismatch, tuning and fixed task scope constrained deployment. The cochlea lineage was actively improved: a 1992 revision targeted dynamic range, stability, mismatch and compactness; a 2010 silicon-cochlea pair supported online-learning sound localization; CAR-FAC later reached real-time FPGA implementation but its authors noted that no model yet reproduced all cochlear characteristics together. [Watts et al., 1992](https://doi.org/10.1109/4.133156); [Chan et al., 2010](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2010.00196); [Thakur et al., 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00504). Modern event cameras and neuromorphic auditory front ends improve fabrication, processing, simulation and available datasets. The 2008 DVS already reports asynchronous pixel-address events when local relative intensity changes cross threshold; modern event-driven robotics integrates such sensor output with online visual attention. [Lichtsteiner, Posch & Delbrück, 2008](https://tilde.ini.uzh.ch/~tobi/wiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?media=lichtsteiner_dvs_jssc08.pdf); [Rea et al., 2013](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2013.00234/full). A 2025 physical-computing speech recognizer combines analog temporal feature extraction with a separate analog in-memory CNN classifier, showing a useful modern front-end/classifier division rather than cochlear computation replacing higher-level learning. [Nature, 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09501-1). The DVS-to-dynamic-field integration is also explicit in a 2013 DFT paper already covered elsewhere in this notebook, so it is not a new hybrid. [Sandamirskaya, 2014](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2013.00276/full).
- **Assessment.** Modern technology revives these ideas as useful *front ends*, not general architectures. By construction, change-only event streams do not report unchanged absolute scene content; the DVS paper reports a nonzero array mismatch in event thresholds, and later cochlea work still identifies dynamic-range, stability and device-mismatch constraints. Analog cochlear filters do not supply broad learned audio semantics, and even later CAR-FAC models trade off sharp tuning, dynamic range and gain. The representational restriction is often an advantage for efficiency, but limits transfer. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as a general model class; retain as sensor-side computation archaeology.**
- **Small CPU falsifier (planned, not run).** On recorded or procedurally generated high-dynamic-range motion, compare event-native tracking with a frame reconstruction plus conventional tracker at matched observation bandwidth and end-to-end latency. Measure target error, reaction delay, event/byte rate, and pause/illumination-change failures. Reject a useful revival claim if information savings vanish after reconstruction or tracking degrades materially during static pauses. This evaluates a front-end utility claim, not a model-class novelty claim.

#### AR-43 — DUAL (1994): context-gated symbolic microprocessors with spreading activation

- **Original computation and unit.** DUAL is a hybrid architecture in which each small agent has both a symbolic processor/knowledge fragment and a connectionist activation value. Links spread activation; current activation controls whether declarative content is visible and how quickly that agent's symbolic procedure runs. The set of active agents and their coalitions emerge from context rather than being fixed as separate task modules. [Kokinov, ECAI 1994](https://hps.elte.hu/~zemplen/materials/sofia2000/personal/kokinov/dual_mul.pdf); [Kokinov, “The Context-Sensitive Cognitive Architecture DUAL”](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0wj7w24k).
- **Input, operation, output and memory.** Input is a task or percept that activates relevant agents in a persistent graph of concepts, operations and relations. Activation repeatedly changes which symbolic structures can participate and how much computation they receive; the active coalition produces an inference, analogy or judgment. Long-term knowledge resides in the agent/link graph; working memory is the currently active subset. Learning can adjust associative links and agent structures, but those structures and symbolic procedures remain largely designed representations.
- **What modern hardware changes.** Parallel CPU/GPU hardware makes thousands of simple agents cheap to simulate, but the original work already contemplated large populations. The central challenges are representational engineering, how activation maps to processing speed, calibration/stability of spreading dynamics, human-behavior evaluation, and transfer beyond analogy/deduction tasks. More compute can scale the simulation but cannot determine a useful knowledge decomposition or certify that a low-activation fact is safely ignored.
- **Prior art / disposition.** DUAL itself is prior art for tightly coupled symbolic and connectionist agents, context-sensitive knowledge visibility and dynamic computation allocation. AMBR, Copycat/Metacat, blackboards and other cognitive architectures cover nearby analogy, activation and opportunistic scheduling mechanisms; the micro-level symbolic-agent/activation coupling is a precise DUAL signature, not a new candidate. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as a class; retain as archaeology.**
- **Small CPU falsifier (planned, not run).** Construct graph-deduction tasks with relevant rules, distractor rules and a changing goal cue. Compare activation-gated variable-speed symbolic agents against the same rules under a fixed scheduler at matched rule-firing budgets. Measure accuracy, irrelevant firings, missed necessary facts and latency as distractor load grows. Reject the efficiency claim if context gating misses correct low-activation knowledge or saves no work under equal budgets.

#### AR-44 — Dörner's PSI / MicroPsi (1980s–2010s): drives and modulators regulate cognition and action

- **Original computation and unit.** PSI models cognition, motivation and emotion as a coupled control process. Needs or drives influence which goals are selected; modulators alter activation, persistence/selection thresholds, attention, retrieval and planning resolution. MicroPsi turned parts of the theory into situated agents built from spreading-activation node nets, sensor/actuator links, memory, behavior and planning components. Its 2003 report explicitly states it was a prototype, and that the original low-level image-perception mechanism was not included. [Bach, “The MicroPsi Agent Architecture,” 2003](https://cognitive-ai.com/publications/assets/MicroPsiArchitectureICCM03.pdf); [Dörner & Güss, “PSI: A Computational Architecture of Cognition, Motivation, and Emotion,” 2013](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1037/a0032947).
- **Input, operation, output and memory.** Inputs include external percepts and internal body/need variables. The system repeatedly updates needs, modulators and node activations; goal/action selection then changes perception, planning depth and behavior. Output is a selected action or plan. Memory is a semantic/episodic node network with active access regions and learned associations. The central loop can adapt online as needs and environment change, but the concepts, drives, node types and modulator semantics are strongly designed.
- **Was it simply early?** Faster simulation, modern robots, game worlds and machine-learning components improve experimental reach, but PSI's main historical obstacles were theory formalization, nonstandard representations, missing broad perception/language and weak computer-science evaluation. MicroPsi 2 was rewritten as a software framework and OpenPsi implemented PSI-inspired motivational control in OpenCog; adding drives to an agent is therefore already explored. [MicroPsi 2, 2012](https://researchgate.net/publication/259870874_Artificial_General_Intelligence_-_5th_International_Conference_AGI_2012_Oxford_UK_December_8-11_2012_Proceedings); [OpenPsi, 2013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2012.11.003). More compute does not establish that drive variables improve objective selection or avoid oscillation.
- **Assessment.** Useful as an explicit motivational-control baseline where internal resources, competing goals and uncertainty matter. It is a cognitive architecture, not a new generic model class; CLARION, BDI systems, hierarchical RL and active-inference approaches already cover many relevant couplings. No distinct learning or memory mechanism survives. **Novelty confidence: 0/5; keep as archaeology, not a candidate.**
- **Small CPU falsifier (planned, not run).** In a symbolic resource world with shifting needs and uncertainty, compare PSI-like drive-regulated goal switching with a single scalar-reward controller and fixed-priority goals under equal action/planning budgets. Measure time outside viability bounds, adaptation time, goal-switch oscillation and retained behavior when needs recur. The revival claim fails if drive regulation cannot improve recovery or stability without hand-tuned goal schedules.

- **Continuation/resource update:** Source checks verified the 1986 holographic capacity/crosstalk limits, a 1989 optical feedback memory, 2026 optical dense-memory work, the silicon retina and cochlea primary records, the 2008 DVS, DUAL's own papers, and MicroPsi/PSI descriptions. AR-41–AR-44 are recorded as old mechanisms with current descendants or direct prior art, not new candidates. No prototype or GPU experiment ran: GPU use and peak VRAM 0 GB; no GPU process snapshot was taken because this pass used literature review only. Before any GPU experiment, inspect memory/process ownership, cap this work near 5.5 GB, and keep about 1 GB headroom. The planned CPU falsifiers are comparative utility tests; none establishes novelty by itself.

#### HY-37 — Soar problem-space learning × constraint propagation × learned branching (rejected)

- **Source mechanisms and interaction.** Soar contributes symbolic states, production-rule learning and problem-space control; constraint programming contributes propagation and complete search; a learned branching policy would allocate search over variables/values. CHS-Soar already integrated a generalized constraint representation and propagation into Soar and learned domain-independent texture heuristics across map coloring and job-shop scheduling. A GNN/RL variable-ordering policy and RL+CP branching solvers are later direct prior art. [Bittle & Fox, CHS-Soar, 2009](https://doi.org/10.2991/agi.2009.15); [Song et al., 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10762); [Cappart et al., AAAI 2021](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16484).
- **What a true coupling would do.** The learned policy would choose a variable from the live propagated constraint state; Soar would turn successful cross-domain texture decisions into symbolic chunks, which would then affect future branching. This is more than putting a neural scorer beside a solver, but both constituent couplings already exist at close range.
- **Verdict / cheap falsifier.** Reject as a new class. A CPU comparison could train on small graph-coloring instances and test held-out graph families plus job-shop scheduling: compare CHS-Soar texture chunks, learned GNN branching and their integrated version under equal propagation calls. Transfer fails if the integrated system does not reduce nodes without extra propagation or if the learned policy does not outperform strong CP heuristics. **Novelty confidence: 0/5.**

#### HY-38 — Blackboard knowledge-source agenda × learned deadline/value scheduler (rejected as generic hybrid)

- **Source mechanisms and coupling.** Blackboard systems let independent knowledge sources update shared hypotheses and goals; a modern scheduler could estimate each source's time, expected solution improvement and deadline risk, then change the execution budget online. This coupling changes computation scheduling and solution granularity rather than merely appending a planner to a model.
- **Direct prior art.** Decker et al.'s real-time approximate-processing blackboard already tracks predicted task duration/results, channels, control goals and a real-time scheduler; it changes approximation level, postpones low-priority work or drops tasks to satisfy deadlines. That is a close architectural match to budget-aware learned scheduling, decades before modern learned priority policies. [Decker et al., *Real-Time Control of Approximate Processing*, 1991 technical report](https://web.cs.umass.edu/publication/docs/1991/UM-CS-1991-050.pdf).
- **Verdict / cheap falsifier.** Reject “blackboard + adaptive scheduler” as a novelty claim. A remaining utility test would add an online learned estimate of cost and benefit to a task scheduler under nonstationary workload; compare fixed priorities and the original duration/result estimates at equal operation budgets. Retire the scheduler upgrade if it fails on held-out workload mixes, starves useful knowledge sources or only wins when given more total computation. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 for the broad coupling.**

#### HY-39 — FORR advisor voting × reward-causal object perception (demoted; exact coupling not shown new)

- **Source mechanisms and coupling.** FORR has multiple advisors, representations and rationales; it learns their reliability and decision weights. A reward-causal object module could identify which tracked objects explain reward changes, then alter advisor relevance or trigger focused sensing. This would feed object-level causal credit into the action-rationale scheduler.
- **Prior-art collision.** FORR already learns advisor weights, useful knowledge and new advisor rules, with a tiered/voting decision process. Separately, Li et al. (2022) describe a self-learning cognitive architecture that tracks objects and uses causal dependence between object trajectories and reward sequences to select relevant objects for reinforcement learning; FORR-based work also learns spatial affordances. [Epstein, FORR and self-awareness, AAAI 2004](https://cdn.aaai.org/Symposia/Fall/2004/FS-04-01/FS04-01-004.pdf); [Li et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2022.02.029); [Epstein et al., learned spatial affordances](https://repositories.cdlib.org/uc/item/13s0r6rm).
- **Verdict.** The exact merge was not found, but both proposed learning/control mechanisms are already present in adjacent systems, so a component assembly is not enough. Demote pending a specific cross-level credit assignment rule showing that object-reward evidence changes which advisor computations are run, with useful transfer under matched action/sensing budgets. **Novelty confidence: 0.1/5; no candidate promoted.**
- **Cheap falsifier.** In a small maze with changing obstacles and occlusions, compare fixed FORR advisors with reward-causal object relevance and sensing. Match observation and action budgets; reject if gains vanish on held-out layouts or come from extra observations.

### Fresh candidate probes from independent invention pass

#### C032 — Query-driven abstract-state refinement (rejected: abstract interpretation + CEGAR)

- **Idea / primitive / represented information.** Maintain a sound over-approximation of possible concrete world states in an abstract domain (for example, intervals plus discrete predicates) and refine the abstraction only when the current query cannot be answered uniformly. The unit is an abstract set with a sound transfer map; it represents uncertainty and reachable states rather than one latent estimate.
- **Repeated operation, input and output.** Propagate the abstract state through candidate actions, check whether all represented concrete states agree on the requested safety or outcome query, and split the smallest responsible abstract component if they do not. Input is an uncertain state set, transition model and property query; output is a certified answer/action or a refined counterexample-guided abstraction.
- **Learning, inference and memory.** Classical abstract interpretation and CEGAR are algorithmic analysis methods rather than learned model classes. One could learn transition transformers from interaction, but certification then requires sound bounds; otherwise the safety claim is lost. Inference is sound abstract propagation plus spurious-counterexample analysis. Memory stores the lattice/domain, transition summaries and refinement predicates.
- **Use, possible advantage and weaknesses.** This could support safe control or debugging by spending computation only on distinctions relevant to the current query. The weakness is decisive: abstract interpretation is foundational work from 1977, and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement is established since 2000; neural-network verification already combines abstraction and refinement. Learned decision-relevant splits are a narrow verification technique, not a new general architecture. State explosion, coarse bounds and certification of learned models remain hard. **Novelty confidence: 0/5; reject as a class.** [Cousot & Cousot, 1977](https://www.di.ens.fr/~cousot/COUSOTpapers/POPL77.shtml); [Clarke et al., 2000](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs357/cegar.pdf); [CNN-Abs, 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01978).
- **Small falsifiable probe.** CPU-only uncertain grid-world or 2D point-mass with hidden hazards; compare fixed interval reachability, standard CEGAR and learned split priorities against exact enumeration. Match expansion budgets and measure certified safe actions, refinement count and runtime. A learned policy is not useful if it cannot preserve the same safety guarantees or uses no fewer refinements than standard CEGAR. **Not run.**

#### C033 — Incremental formal-concept closure engine (rejected: established Formal Concept Analysis)

- **Idea / primitive / represented information.** Treat data as a binary object–attribute relation. The computational unit is a closed extent–intent pair under the Galois connection: a set of objects and exactly the attributes shared by those objects. Repeated closure operations build a concept lattice and exact implication structure.
- **Input, output and operation.** New categorical examples update only affected parts of the lattice; a query retrieves minimal concepts or implications covering its attributes. Input is a stream of discrete objects and named properties; output is a canonical concept hierarchy or implication set.
- **Learning, inference and memory.** Incremental lattice construction is the learning procedure; closure and traversal are inference. Memory is the incidence table plus the lattice graph. Updates can be local on typical data, but the lattice has exponential worst-case size.
- **Use, advantage and weaknesses.** The niche is exact, interpretable, incremental taxonomy/rule discovery when features are already categorical and meaningful. It does not solve perception, feature induction or noisy continuous representation. Wille’s formal concept framework and incremental lattice-update algorithms from 1994–95 directly establish the mechanism. **Novelty confidence: 0/5; reject as a class.** [Wille, 1982](https://hal-lirmm.ccsd.cnrs.fr/lirmm-04895826v1/document); [Godin, Missaoui & Alaoui, 1995](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1467-8640.1995.tb00031.x); [incremental concept formation, 1994](https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-3975(94)90195-3).
- **Small falsifiable probe.** CPU-only categorical concept streams with held-out conjunctions and controlled concept drift. Compare incremental FCA, a decision tree and an association-rule learner under matched memory/update time; measure update latency, lattice growth, implication stability and held-out composition. Retire the utility probe if lattice growth dominates or its exactness offers no stability/interpretability benefit under modest noise. **Not run.**

### Pulse-coupled visual computation archaeology and hybrid screen

#### AR-45 — Pulse-coupled neural networks (PCNNs; 1990s–present): feature grouping through synchronized bursts

- **Original mechanism.** Eckhorn et al. (1990) modeled stimulus-linked oscillations as interacting neural assemblies: local feature-driven units communicate through forward feeding and lateral/backward modulatory links, so assemblies with compatible activity can synchronize. Johnson’s 1994 image-processing formulation became known as a pulse-coupled neural network; it studies both strong-coupling synchronous bursts and weaker-coupling traveling waves that encode image geometry. The mechanism is temporal grouping: membership is expressed through phase, burst timing and the resulting pulse maps, not solely through a static activation vector. [Eckhorn et al., 1990](https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1990.2.3.293); [Johnson, 1994](https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.33.006239).
- **Unit, information, operation, input and output.** A unit is a pulse-generating cell with a feedforward drive, linking/modulatory input, internal activity and threshold/refractory state. It represents local image evidence and temporary synchrony-based grouping. Repeatedly integrate input and local coupling, update the threshold/state, and emit a pulse; the time series or selected pulse frame is the output. Inputs are image or sensory features; outputs include similarity groups, image decompositions, segments, edges or object proposals. Do not conflate the 1990 linking-field model, the simplified 2D PCNN image algorithm and later trained PCNN neurons: they share a lineage but have different equations and goals.
- **Learning and memory.** Classic PCNNs generally use designed coupling kernels and manually selected parameters, with no separate data-driven training stage; transient membrane/link/threshold state carries short-term dynamics. Modern DPCNN work replaces LIF units in deep SNNs with PCNN neurons and uses spatiotemporal backpropagation, learned inter-channel coupling and receptive-field/time-dependent batch normalization. That is a direct modernization of the neural dynamics, not proof that the classic image algorithm learns a general representation. [Yi et al., *Deep Pulse-Coupled Neural Networks*, 2024 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08649).
- **Was it bad or early? What changed?** This architecture was not primarily blocked by slow processors: it was simulated and used for image processing before GPU-era deep learning, and an optical hybrid demonstration was reported by 1994. The enduring friction is the hand-set dynamical parameters and the difficulty of establishing stable, interpretable behavior across scenes; a 2023 dynamics analysis says seven parameters are commonly hand-set and notes the lack of a generally accepted parameter theory. Current autodiff, surrogate-gradient training and GPUs make richer learned PCNNs practical, and the 2024 DPCNN preprint is evidence of an actual revival. Yet these tools add an optimization recipe, not a unique broad inductive advantage; performance and efficiency claims need matched SNN/ANN controls and replication. [2023 PCNN dynamics/parameter analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2023.107101).
- **Use, potential edge, and failure modes.** Potential niches include grouping fragmented/noisy visual evidence, asynchronous perception, and low-label image segmentation/fusion where temporal co-firing has a useful grouping bias. Synchrony could form transient groups without preassigned object slots and may communicate beyond explicit local wiring through traveling waves. Risks include parameter sensitivity, extra sequential latency, unstable or input-dependent grouping, poor absolute-scene representation, expensive time-step simulation on ordinary CPUs/GPUs, and no demonstrated generalization benefit over convolutional or spiking baselines. Surveys document many application-specific PCNN variants, while a 2023 visual-perception paper reports that synchronous-oscillation cues alone were insufficient for its segmentation setting and that its model had computational-efficiency limitations. [Wang et al., 2010 review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imavis.2009.06.007); [2023 *Scientific Reports* PCNN visual-perception study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-39376-z).
- **Closest work and novelty verdict.** PCNN itself is prior art for synchrony-based grouping. Johnson’s 1994 article already reports invariance experiments and an optical demonstration; a 1999 PCNN object-detection pipeline already performs PCNN smoothing, iterative segmentation, controller-guided region removal, and object identification. DPCNN now supplies a learned deep-SNN revival; standard SNN learning, recurrent vision, dynamic fields, and the already logged visual-routine work cover adjacent temporal perception and active control. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as a general model class; retain as archaeology and as a possible low-cost front-end baseline.** [Ranganath & Kuntimad, 1999](https://doi.org/10.1109/72.761720).
- **Small falsifiable prototype.** CPU-only 32×32–64×64 procedurally generated shapes with broken contours, distractor edges, moderate pixel noise, and held-out rotations/contrast changes. Compare one faithful classical PCNN, a static threshold-plus-connected-components baseline, and a small LIF-spiking/local-recurrent baseline. Match operation count or report time steps and neighborhood updates separately; tune parameters only on training seeds. Measure object grouping F1/adjusted Rand score, transformation stability, latency, parameter sensitivity across seeds and noise levels. Falsify the revived-computation claim if PCNN does not improve held-out grouping at matched work, or if the gain requires a narrow hand-tuned parameter setting. **Planned, not run.**

#### HY-40 — PCNN synchrony × task-composed visual routines (demoted empirical hybrid)

- **Source mechanisms and exact coupling.** PCNN contributes transient phase-coherent feature groups. Ullman-style visual routines contribute task-chosen sequences such as select-anchor, trace, search and compare. Proposed coupling: the current routine’s spatial result gates the PCNN linking field; the resulting synchronized group ID becomes the target/anchor for the next routine operation; task reward or a comparison error updates the linking gain and the next-operation policy. Thus object grouping changes which routine runs and the next routine changes which pixels can synchronize.
- **Why it could behave differently.** This loop could bind visually separated but task-related fragments into an object-specific temporal group, then reuse that group as working state while performing a multi-step query. A possible gain is fewer pixels or less fixed slot machinery for a cluttered partially occluded relation task; the cost is serial dynamics and a new stability problem. A synchrony mask followed by a routine controller without feedback would be a side-by-side assembly and is not the proposed mechanism.
- **Prior art and novelty.** PCNN linking fields already group visual regions and a 1999 PCNN object-detection system already uses iterative segmentation plus a control module to retain or discard regions. Ullman’s visual-routine hypothesis has direct active-vision implementations, and RELEARNN (already logged under AR-34/HY-32) learns short visual-operation sequences with local reward and a persistent spatial focus. DPCNN already adds learned coupling across feature channels. I found no primary-source demonstration of this exact two-way reward-conditioned coupling, but the pieces are close, and “visual synchrony plus a routine” alone is not a new architecture. **Novelty confidence 0.1/5; demote to a narrowly controlled empirical hybrid, not a candidate class.** [PCNN object detection, 1999](https://doi.org/10.1109/72.761720); [Rao & Ballard, active visual routines, 1995](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(95)00026-7); [Mollard et al., 2024](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012030).
- **Falsifier.** On CPU relational scenes with distractors, occlusion and operation sequences held out at test time, compare (a) fixed PCNN segmentation plus a fixed routine, (b) learned routine with static frame/feature masks, and (c) the bidirectional reward-conditioned coupling. Equalize pixel access, routine count, episodes and neighborhood updates. Report relational accuracy, pixels/time steps per answer, group-identity switches and cross-task transfer. Reject the coupling if accuracy or compute gains vanish at equal budgets, if pulse synchrony changes group identity under harmless perturbations, or if reward learning overfits the exact operation sequences. **Not run.**

### Recursive structure encoding archaeology

#### AR-46 — Recursive Auto-Associative Memory (RAAM; 1988–1990): recursively compress and reconstruct variable-size trees in fixed-width codes

- **Original computation and unit.** Pollack's RAAM consists of a compressor and reconstructor trained together. The compressor maps a pair of fixed-width child patterns to one same-width pattern; applying it bottom-up recursively creates a fixed-width code for an arbitrarily sized fixed-valence tree. The reconstructor learns to decode each parent vector into its children, recursively until terminal symbols are reached. The computational unit is a learned parent-to-child-pair transform, repeatedly applied over tree depth; external stack/control supports recursive traversal and a terminal test. [Pollack, NeurIPS 1988](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/1988/file/5fd0b37cd7dbbb00f97ba6ce92bf5add-Paper.pdf); [Pollack, *Recursive Distributed Representations*, 1990](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(90)90005-K).
- **Information, input, output, inference and memory.** It represents syntactic/semantic composition and subtree identity in continuous fixed-width vectors whose distances can reflect structural similarity. Input is a tree over terminal vectors; output is its root code, with reconstruction or subtree access performed by repeatedly applying the decoder along a path. Knowledge resides in the shared encoder/decoder weights and learned latent patterns; temporary traversal state resides on external stacks. This is a structured representation method, not an unconstrained content-addressable file cabinet.
- **Learning and possible uses.** The original learner applies backpropagation to encode/reconstruct local tree pairs; because internal targets depend on currently changing weights, its training environment is nonstationary (“moving target”). It can learn vectors that retain enough detail to reconstruct structure while organizing related phrases near one another. Potential uses include compositional parsing, structured memory, variable-size program/scene trees, and analogical retrieval over trees. A fixed-width code might make structured objects compatible with similarity-based neural processing; it does not by itself yield a general reasoner.
- **Was it bad or early?** Better autodiff, optimizers, GPU batches and synthetic grammars could make larger experiments and more stable optimization practical. However, Pollack already used backpropagation, and his paper explicitly called for analysis of moving-target convergence and how reconstruction tolerance sets maximum tree depth. It also warns that reconstruction errors grow recursively, that terminal-code geometry affects generalization, and that finite-precision vectors cannot store arbitrary structure without exploiting regularity. Its language demonstration used a small engineered grammar and a small example set. Modern hardware helps test and optimize the representation, but cannot remove the finite-width/capacity tradeoff or supply productive symbolic generalization automatically. [Pollack 1990, further-work and representation analysis](https://www.dlsi.ua.es/~mlf/nnafmc/papers/pollack90recursive.pdf).
- **Modernization and closest prior art.** Linear RAAM directly attempted to improve structure generalization with linear units and Oja's rule, reporting generalization to novel tree structures; recursive autoencoders and TreeLSTM-style models learn over trees; neural program interpreters, NPI, and modern neuro-symbolic reasoning already execute compositional structures. These make RAAM a historical architecture with descendants, not an unoccupied class. A precise revival question is whether modern optimizers and large generated grammars materially improve depth/generalization while preserving one fixed-width distributed code, compared with linear RAAM and contemporary recursive encoders. [Sperduti et al., Linear RAAM, 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2005.01.005); [Tai et al., TreeLSTM, ACL 2015](https://aclanthology.org/P15-1150/); [Reed & de Freitas, NPI](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06279); [Li et al., neuro-symbolic reasoning, ICLR 2024](https://yzhu.io/publication/generalization2024iclr/paper.pdf).
- **Strength, weaknesses and novelty.** The distinctive historical strength is joint compression and decompression: a vector is trained to be both similar enough for neural computation and structurally decodable. Main risks are depth-sensitive reconstruction, hidden-vector collisions, moving-target optimization, external recursion/control, terminal-test fragility and weak generalization outside generated structures. **Novelty confidence: 0/5 as a general architecture; retain as a serious revival baseline because the historical bottleneck is unusually testable.**
- **Small falsifiable CPU prototype.** Generate binary trees from a compositional grammar, hold out combinations and depths, and train a faithful RAAM at small widths. Compare original nonlinear RAAM, linear RAAM, a modern recursive encoder/decoder, and exact AST-plus-stack manipulation. Measure exact reconstruction by depth, subtree-query accuracy, collisions, compositional generalization, parameter/storage cost, optimizer stability and CPU time. The revival claim fails if modern training cannot improve held-out depth/composition over the linear and recursive neural baselines without widening the code or storing external per-tree structure. **Planned, not run.**

#### RAAM pilot protocol — optimizer and depth generalization (CPU-only; pre-run)

- **Question.** Does a modern optimizer reduce the original RAAM's documented moving-target instability and improve out-of-depth tree reconstruction at a fixed code width, or does the fixed-width recursive bottleneck dominate?
- **Fixed toy setup.** Four one-hot terminal symbols; one shared nonlinear compressor `R^(2d) → R^d` with `d=12`, one shared decoder `R^d → R^(2d)`, and a leaf/internal terminal classifier. Train on 512 random binary trees with maximum depth 3; test on held-out trees at depths 1–5. Recompute every internal code from the current compressor each update and train local pair reconstruction losses plus terminal/internal labels. Three paired initialization seeds; 150 full-data epochs each.
- **Comparison and measures.** Compare SGD with learning rate 0.1 and momentum 0.3 (matching the historical paper's typical values) against Adam at 0.003. Same initial weights, trees, examples, architecture, and update count within each seed. Measure training reconstruction loss, exact recursive tree recovery at each test depth, code collisions/terminal errors, run time, and across-seed variance. This is a small diagnostic, not a faithful reproduction of all 1990 training details and not evidence of broad utility.
- **Decision rule and resources.** If Adam only improves training loss but does not improve exact reconstruction on unseen structures/depths, record that optimization did not remove the representational bottleneck; if it improves depth generalization, the result justifies a larger RAAM-vs-linear-RAAM/TreeLSTM study, not a novelty claim. Python 3.11.9, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, CPU only, GPU unavailable to the run; no GPU model, batch, or VRAM usage. **Pre-registered; not yet run.**

### Prior-art correction to nonlinear-dynamics archaeology

- **AR-37 / WLC learning and sequence memory are more occupied than the earlier summary implied.** Seliger, Tsimring & Rabinovich (2003) already learn pattern projection and competition matrices in a two-layer winnerless-competition network so it can associatively retrieve prerecorded sequences. Arena et al. (2006) use stimulus-dependent WLC trajectories for classification. Kiebel et al. (2009) combine stable heteroclinic channels with online Bayesian inversion for recognizing hierarchical sequences. Calvo Tapia, Tyukin & Makarov (2018) learn motor-motif transitions by rewiring WLC couplings online from a teacher and demonstrate robot behavior. Therefore generic “WLC plus learned transition matrix,” “sequence readout,” “Bayesian decoder,” or “motor-motif learner” hybrids are established; keep WLC as a useful dynamical baseline, not a new class. [Seliger et al., 2003](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.67.011905); [Arena et al., 2006](https://doi.org/10.1109/CNNA.2006.341601); [Kiebel et al., 2009](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000464); [Calvo Tapia et al., 2018](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.97.052308).
- **Cheap future falsifier only.** If a narrower online, reward-only transition adaptation rule is proposed, compare it with a fixed WLC plus readout, the 2003 learned competition matrix, and an echo-state network on a sequence grammar whose transitions change. Reject if it cannot adapt with fewer examples while retaining stable transitions and held-out sequence performance. This proposed rule is not currently specified or promoted.

- **Continuation/resource update:** Lead-verified archaeology now adds AR-45 (PCNN) and AR-46 (RAAM). HY-40 records a low-novelty PCNN/visual-routine coupling experiment; no new architecture candidate is promoted. The WLC follow-up audit confirms direct sequence memory, classification, hierarchical recognition and online motor-learning prior art; this correction is recorded above. CPU falsifiers for PCNN, HY-40 and RAAM remain planned, not run. No GPU work ran or was started, so GPU usage/peak VRAM were 0 GB; live GPU occupancy was not checked because no GPU experiment was needed. Before any future GPU experiment, inspect memory/process ownership and keep within the shared 5.5 GB target and headroom policy.

### RAAM CPU pilot result — training fit is inadequate for a generalization verdict

- **Execution.** Ran the pre-registered pilot with 512 training trees, four terminal symbols, code width 12, a 625-parameter shared encoder/decoder/classifier, 150 full-data epochs, and three paired seeds. Tests used 80 balanced trees per depth (1–5). PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, CPU only. SGD (lr 0.1, momentum 0.3) and Adam (lr 0.003) used identical trees and initial weights within each seed. The measured comparison took 27.4 seconds total; a separate 8.0-second Adam diagnostic inspected training-tree recovery. The first exploratory decode attempt had a loose recursion bound and no usable output; the reported rerun limited recursion to test depth + 1 to contain malformed decodes. That depth limit only returns failure for nonterminating/overdeep predictions; exact outputs still require the model's own terminal decisions. Runtime comparisons are therefore not reported.
- **Results.** Mean final combined training loss was about 0.162 for SGD and 0.074 for Adam. Mean exact held-out recovery by depth was: SGD 0.10 at depth 1 and 0 at depths 2–5; Adam 0.98 at depth 1, 0.05 at depth 2, and 0 at depths 3–5. In the separate seed-101 Adam diagnostic, exact training recovery was 100% for depth-1 trees, 19% for depth-2 trees and under 1% for depth-3 trees, despite 0.0202 local reconstruction MSE and perfect internal-vs-terminal classification.
- **Interpretation.** Adam lowered the local loss but neither optimizer fitted the training structures deeply enough to test held-out depth generalization. The result exposes error accumulation and the gap between local pair reconstruction and exact recursive structure recovery in this small setup; it does **not** falsify RAAM's representational claim or show that modern optimization cannot help. Treat the pilot as a failed/inadequate reproduction, not evidence for a model-class decision.
- **Next falsifier.** Revise the diagnostic so training exact recovery reaches at least 95% through the training depth before testing unseen depths. Then compare local pair loss against recursively decoded end-to-end structure loss and a wider code, with the same generated trees; include linear RAAM and an exact AST baseline. If no setting achieves stable training recovery without extra per-tree memory, then the revival claim is weak. If train fit succeeds but deeper generalization fails, the fixed-width capacity/compositionality limit becomes the sharper question. This follow-up is not yet run.
- **Resource log.** Main run: CPU, 512-tree full batch, 150 epochs, 3 seeds × 2 optimizers, 625 parameters, 27.4 seconds measured. Diagnostic: CPU, one seed, same width and schedule, 8.0 seconds wall time. PyTorch build was CPU-only; GPU use 0 GB and peak VRAM 0 GB. No GPU process snapshot was taken because no GPU experiment was started; live occupancy remains unknown. No process belonging to another research agent was inspected or changed.

#### RAAM follow-up protocol — recursively decoded training loss (CPU-only; pre-run)

- The first pilot failed its training-fit gate. Test a specific training modernization: retain the same shared fixed-width encoder/decoder but, from each training-tree root, recursively feed the decoder's *predicted* child codes through subsequent levels and apply structural-code reconstruction plus terminal/internal supervision along the known training tree. This backpropagates through accumulated decoding error; it changes the training objective and is a component of modern recursive autoencoders, not a novelty claim.
- Re-run the local-pair objective as control and the recursive-rollout objective with Adam (0.003), same `d=12`, tree corpus, 512 trees, three seeds, 150 epochs and parameter count. Report exact recovery on training trees by actual depth and held-out full trees at depths 1–5; do not interpret test depth until the training-fit gate reaches 95% through depth 3. The experiment is falsified as a useful optimization fix if recursive supervision cannot reach the fit gate or if training fit improves but test generalization remains at zero beyond seen depth.
- CPU-only PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. No GPU model or process will be started; no GPU occupancy snapshot is needed for this CPU run. **Pre-registered; not yet run.**

#### RAAM follow-up result — recursive rollout supervision did not rescue training fit

- **Harness correction.** An initial follow-up attempt failed with a local implementation type error (a frontier list was passed to a linear layer); it ran for about 8.5 seconds and produced no valid comparison. I corrected the harness and reran the pre-registered comparison. Discard the failed attempt's partial output.
- **Execution and results.** Corrected CPU-only run: PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, `d=12`, 625 parameters, 512 training trees, 40 held-out trees per depth, 150 epochs, three seeds, Adam 0.003. It compared the local-pair objective against recursively decoded rollout supervision. Total wall time was 62.0 seconds. Local-objective train exact recovery by depths 1/2/3 was seed 101: 1.00/0.143/0; seed 202: 1.00/0.212/0.007; seed 303: 0.937/0.162/0.007. Rollout train exact was seed 101: 0.438/0.095/0.007; seed 202: 0.191/0.030/0; seed 303: 0.302/0.108/0.010. No condition approached the pre-set 95% training-fit gate through depth 3. Held-out exact recovery was nearly all zero beyond depth 1; rollout also lowered depth-1 test recovery in these seeds. Together with the first pilot, this is enough to pause RAAM experiments at width 12. A future revival attempt should first improve train recovery, perhaps by testing a wider code and a better specified leaf/internal decoding scheme against linear RAAM and an exact AST baseline; do not spend GPU time before a CPU setup clears the training-fit gate.
