#### Old-architecture archaeology — Hierarchical Temporal Memory (AR-86; C018 follow-up)

**Status:** HTM remains a distinctive, useful online sequence-memory mechanism, but not a new architecture. A modern visual front-end and HTM temporal memory have already been coupled directly in GridHTM; the broad “deep perception + HTM for online sequence/anomaly learning” hybrid is therefore occupied.

1. **Original computation.** HTM’s spatial pooler maps binary inputs to sparse distributed representations through competitive overlap/inhibition, Hebbian synapse-permanence updates and homeostatic duty-cycle control. Temporal memory subdivides columns into context-sensitive cells with distal segments that learn transitions; cells can be active and predicted together when sequence branches remain ambiguous. The main unit is a sparse context-conditioned transition; local synapses and cell states store sequence history. At inference, input matching and local prediction update an SDR and prediction-mismatch/anomaly signal. [Cui, Ahmad & Hawkins (2015/2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05463); [Cui, Ahmad & Hawkins, spatial-pooler analysis (2017)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5712570/).
2. **Learning and deployment.** The spatial pooler and temporal memory learn online with local Hebbian-like rules; no global backpropagation is required. That permits post-deployment adaptation to streaming data, but also means encoder drift, overlearning, and regime mixing must be handled without a unified gradient objective. A frozen feature/semantic encoder is often assumed.
3. **Why it struggled historically.** Sparse computation did not guarantee cheap computation: proximal/distal synapses create irregular memory accesses, inhibition and branching state updates, and maintaining many context segments grows memory. The algorithm also depended on a semantically useful input encoder; raw vision is not converted into stable, overlap-preserving SDRs by HTM itself. Parameters such as sparsity, boosting, segment thresholds, permanence changes, context depth, and anomaly aggregation are sensitive. These are partly software/hardware issues, but representation and calibration are deeper limits.
4. **What modern technology changed.** GPU parallel implementations of the spatial pooler and custom flash/NVM hardware for spatial pooling demonstrated acceleration/storage-local execution. CUDA-like dense kernels can parallelize overlap calculations, while sparse temporal-memory updates remain branch- and memory-bound. Larger datasets and modern pretrained encoders relieve the weak-perception problem, but a frozen encoder can change output codes under domain shift and invalidate stored sparse synapses. [parallel SP implementation (2016)](https://www.scitepress.org/papers/2016/57066/57066.pdf); [non-volatile HTM spatial pooler (2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02792).
5. **Modernization already performed.** GridHTM uses PointRend with a ResNet-101 ImageNet-pretrained backbone to segment cars, maps segments into SDR-friendly grids, and sends them through per-cell spatial poolers and temporal memories. It demonstrates the direct old/new connection, but its evaluation uses a single stationary-camera VIRAT video plus synthetic frame skips/repeats; the paper notes that aggregated anomaly scores are difficult to threshold, high-framerate motion can cause contextual loops, anomaly scores jump at cell entry, and longer real video datasets were future work. Thus prior art closes the generic coupling without proving scalable performance. [Monakhov et al., GridHTM (2022)](https://arxiv.org/html/2205.15407). A 2018 HTM+one-shot distance-learning system is another direct deep/HTM integration. [Zou et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICME.2018.8486447).
6. **Scale and hardware.** Spatial overlap/inhibition is amenable to parallel bit operations and tensorization. Temporal memory relies on sparse, context-dependent segment matching and online synapse updates, with irregular reads/writes that can be bandwidth-limited and poorly utilize dense GPU kernels. NVM/neuromorphic substrate may fit its locality, but requires technology-specific implementations. HTM’s strengths are potentially useful for low-label streaming anomaly/sequence adaptation; it is not a general-purpose replacement for visual representation learning or long-range planning.
7. **Potential residue and novelty.** A more precise question is whether HTM-style context branching, not a simple one-state recurrent predictor, improves *online recovery after encoder/scene drift* at matched sparse memory, adaptation samples, latency, and false alarm. The central mechanism (SDR overlap + local transition learning) is established, and encoder+HTM is published, so this is at most an evaluation/engineering hypothesis. Novelty confidence: **0/5 for HTM class; 0/5 for generic visual encoder × HTM; 1/5 for an unspecified drift-safe interface.**
8. **Small falsifier and decision.** A CPU symbolic-stream pilot can first test context branching under changing transition laws; any visual demonstration should then compare frozen pretrained features + HTM, GridHTM, online encoder + HTM, and equal-parameter GRU/streaming baselines. Measure anomaly ranking, false alarms under normal drift, adaptation samples, memory growth, and time to recover. Reject the specialist-revival claim if context branching does not improve recovery at matched false-alarm rate and resource use, or if encoder changes make HTM synapses stale. Do not call this a new architecture; retain HTM as a baseline for online sequence learning.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — neural fields, continuous-time recurrent nets, and cellular neural dynamics (AR-87)

**Status:** The broad continuous-time/local-dynamics idea was partly born before convenient compute and training tools, but has already been substantially revived. It remains valuable for continuous sensorimotor dynamics and local spatiotemporal modeling; no general architecture candidate survives.

- **Original computation.** Amari’s neural fields model continuous activity over space, where local excitation and lateral inhibition can form persistent bumps, moving localized activity and pattern transitions. Continuous-time recurrent neural nets and real-time recurrent learning (RTRL) update a dynamical state and can train online without a fixed sequence boundary. Chua–Yang cellular neural networks hard-wire local analog cells to perform fast spatial signal operations. These architectures represent functions of space/time and local state; their repeated unit is a continuous differential update or locally coupled circuit rather than a token or layer. [Amari (1977)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00337259); [Williams & Zipser (1989), RTRL](https://gwern.net/doc/ai/nn/rnn/1989-williams-2.pdf); [Chua & Yang (1988), Cellular Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1109/31.7600).
- **Why they historically struggled.** Simulation of spatially dense fields was expensive; analog circuit programmability, precision, calibration, and device mismatch constrained what could be learned on-chip. RTRL’s exact online sensitivities require nonlocal communication and expensive computation, as the original authors acknowledge. Neural fields often relied on hand-chosen kernels and had limited mechanisms to learn task representations; stable inference may require delicate parameter tuning. Thus hardware was a real bottleneck, but online credit assignment, objective design, stability, and representation were also fundamental.
- **What changed and what is already revived.** GPUs/autodiff make local field simulations differentiable and parallel; neural operators learn maps between function spaces. Liquid Time-Constant Networks use state-modulated learned time constants in continuous-time recurrent units; closed-form continuous-time models (CfC) approximate LTC dynamics without a numerical ODE solver and report at least order-of-magnitude speedups over ODE-based continuous-time models in their evaluated tasks. Neural Cellular Automata learn shared local update rules through differentiable rollouts and model transient/stable pattern formation and PDE dynamics. [Neural Operators (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.08481); [LTC (AAAI 2021)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16936); [CfC (Nature Machine Intelligence 2022)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-022-00556-7); [NCA spatiotemporal learning (PLOS Comp Bio 2024)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11078362/).
- **Hybrid audit.** Local continuous state plus learned update is already NCA/Neural PDE; adaptive time constants are LTC/CfC; event-driven synchrony and asynchronous cellular automata are established. NCA uses a random per-cell update mask during training to survive asynchronous updates. Locally adaptive CA already couple state to rule changes. These occupy generic “continuous field + local neural update + asynchrony/adaptation” proposals. [Growing NCA (2020)](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/); [locally adaptive CA (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07067); [event-triggered neural control with scheduling](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=djVlAgkRFO).
- **What may remain different.** A model could learn a *state-dependent local compute hazard*: each region estimates whether skipping its next update will create downstream prediction loss, communicating/update-triggering only when that risk exceeds a shared resource price. This changes the computation schedule, not just the cell dynamics. But sparse gates, event-triggered control, adaptive CA, random asynchronous NCA and learned neural events are adjacent enough that no novelty claim is warranted. Hardware cost also matters: deciding whether to update each cell may itself require evaluating a gate everywhere, and irregular updates can erase GPU efficiency.
- **Small falsifier.** If this numerical-method comparison is ever run, freeze one learned transition law and compare synchronous NCA, random-mask asynchronous NCA, a fixed sparse update rate, the 2004-style adaptive policy, and a learned local hazard against the same dense-step reference trajectory. This prevents schedule changes from being mistaken for an architecture gain when asynchronous stepping changes the learned discrete-time semantics. Count local-rule evaluations separately from trigger, queue, synchronization, and wall-time costs; test shifted pulse timing, perturbations, grid-size changes, stability, and error. The reported 4–5× speedup for Zhu et al. is confined to its cardiac examples. Falsify if a scheduler fails to save total measured cost at equal error or is unstable under shifts. No architecture claim remains.
- **Disposition.** Neural fields/continuous-time dynamics are substantially modernized, not a general lost AI architecture waiting only for more compute. HY-71 is superseded by HY-73: direct per-cell adaptive-timestep and event-triggered scheduling prior art demote the learned-hazard concept to an optional simulation-method comparison. No model-class candidate survives and no experiment has run.

#### HY-70 — visual encoder × HTM online sequence memory (reject as new hybrid)

- **Source mechanisms.** A modern vision model supplies semantic object/segment features; HTM spatial pooling maintains sparse codes while temporal memory learns local sequence transitions online from them.
- **Exact interaction/prior art.** GridHTM directly uses a PointRend/ResNet101 segmenter to generate per-object/per-cell inputs and uses online spatial-pooler/temporal-memory adaptation. HTM also predates this with encoder/spatial-pooler/temporal-memory pipelines, and HTM has been integrated with one-shot distance learning. The coupling improves HTM’s input representation, but does not alter its online learning rule or remove the need for stable SDR overlap semantics. Generic deep-perception + HTM for video sequence/anomaly detection is occupied.
- **Failure modes and disproof test.** A pretrained encoder’s domain shift may scramble overlap codes; segmentation errors can trigger false anomalies; the published demonstration has limited video coverage and acknowledged threshold/context problems. Compare GridHTM, frozen encoder+HTM, online encoder+HTM, and matched online recurrent predictors on multi-scene drift with long normal streams and rare anomalies. Reject any utility claim if it cannot improve adaptation/false-alarm tradeoff at matched labels and memory. No new-class claim is retained.

#### HY-71 — learned local event hazard × neural field/NCA (superseded; demoted by HY-73)

- **Coupling.** Combine an NCA/neural-field local dynamical rule with a predictor that estimates the error risk of skipping each location’s next update. The hazard controls when a cell computes, when its changed state is transmitted to neighbors, and which local rollouts receive training credit. This differs from random update masks by making compute contingent on expected downstream consequence; it differs from a standard locally adaptive CA by changing the update schedule rather than only changing local rules.
- **Complementarity.** Neural fields/NCA provide local dynamics and parallel simulation; asynchronous CA/event-triggered control provide sparse scheduling; a learned hazard could spend computation where long-range effects or fast local change make it useful. The hoped-for benefit is lower average active-cell work at a fixed trajectory error on systems with mostly quiet regions and sparse propagating changes.
- **Prior art and caution.** HY-73 found asynchronous adaptive local steps for cellular automata (2004), per-neuron variable-step integration (2005), learned event-triggered control (2025), learned ODE step controllers, asynchronous NCA and differentiable spike-event queues. No exact same combination was verified, but that is not evidence of novelty. Novelty confidence: **0/5 for an architecture class**, **1/5 for the exact CA-specific scheduler coupling**, **2/5 possible value for sparse physical simulation**, and **0/5 as a general intelligence class**.
- **Small falsifier (CPU, deferred; not run).** If a simulator application warrants it, compare synchronous NCA, random asynchronous NCA, Zhu et al.’s local activity/derivative step policy, a standard adaptive local ODE integrator, and learned hazard scheduling on small reaction-diffusion/wave tasks. Match rollout error; charge trigger calculation, queue and synchronization work; test timing/grid/stiffness shifts and long-horizon stability. Reject practical value if it does not beat the best numerical baseline at equal accuracy and measured wall time. The broad event-triggered CA/neural-computation prior-art search has now been done; no unique learning rule currently justifies a prototype.

#### AR-08 / C031 follow-up — homeostatic RL and viability are modernized, not a new control architecture

Ashby’s Homeostat was both too early in available computation and limited by its global random reorganization: the fully cross-connected system could not retain partial adaptations and could adapt implausibly slowly. The original author states that partial successes need preservation and that excessive connectivity prevents their accumulation. Later modular homeostatic RL explicitly gives each drive its own learner and reports better sample efficiency and out-of-domain robustness than a monolithic DQN on its tested homeostasis task. Continuous HRL uses neural function approximation and HJB dynamics; a 2024 study reports deep homeostatic agents trained from visual inputs. These are direct modern revivals, so “modernize Ashby with neural networks” is not new. [Ashby, *Design for a Brain*](https://www.ashby.info/Ashby%20-%20Design%20for%20a%20Brain%20-%20The%20Origin%20of%20Adaptive%20Behavior.pdf); [Dulberg et al. (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06608); [Laurençon et al. (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06580); [Yoshida et al. (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608024003034).

**Hybrid seam (HY-72; demoted):** modular homeostatic specialists could be gated by a learned viability-margin model; after a persistent safety-margin decrease, only the specialist with the largest estimated causal effect on the failing internal variable would reorganize. Barrier-function safety filters and learned viability-boundary approximations already cover the basic coupling. The remaining question is whether localized adaptation preserves unaffected drives better under a changing plant, but this is a benchmark extension to C031, not a new class. Compare scalar-reward RL, modular-drive RL, barrier-filtered RL, and localized adaptation at matched action/probing budgets; reject if it does not improve safety/recovery without hand-coded fault-to-module mapping. No experiment run. [VBOC (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07535); [Parker et al. PCT review (2020)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32092312/).

#### AR-88 — Minsky's Society of Mind (1980s): nested agencies as a conceptual architecture

- **Original computation.** Minsky frames intelligence as societies of small, individually mindless processes (“agents”) grouped into agencies, with agencies decomposable into lower-level societies. The 1979 K-line memo gives one real algorithmic proposal: designate an event as memorable after goal success; create a K-node/K-line linked to currently active agents; later reactivate only a partial state within a level band, leaving lower-level perception and higher-level current goals able to revise it; recursively connect new K-lines to already-active K-nodes; and use cross-exclusion to preserve competing dispositions. The repeated operation is sparse local activation plus context-bounded partial-state reinstatement. The theory also recognizes a physical/communication crossbar problem and proposes sparse local communication as a scaling principle. [Minsky, “K-Lines: A Theory of Memory,” MIT AI Memo 516 (1979)](https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.803/pdf/aim-516.pdf); [Minsky, *Society of Mind*, publisher excerpt and metadata](https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Society-Of-Mind/Marvin-Minsky/9780671657130).
- **Learning, memory, and historical limits.** This is more than a metaphor, but it does not define a complete task-general learning system. The K-line paper leaves open how success is judged “memorable,” how a goal is linked to a K-node, how activation strengths and partial reinstatement are computed, how the agent repertoire is acquired, and how conflicts are resolved. Minsky explicitly calls the unrestricted K-line connectivity a crossbar problem and says a general solution may not exist; sparse specialist communication is his proposed direction. Modern sparse graphs, large memory and concurrent simulation reduce those implementation costs, but do not supply the missing learning, cueing, and arbitration policies. The useful hypothesis is narrower: context-banded retrieval of methods/active specialist subsets may transfer better than replaying whole episodes while preserving response to current evidence.
- **Modernization already exists.** A 1996 storytelling implementation directly translated Minsky agencies into cooperating/competing software agents and represented partial states, K-lines, frames and other coordination structures on a blackboard. Hearn later implemented a declarative K-line programming language that compiled to a connectionist-style network and structurally changed as new memories formed; a simulated creature learned basic walking/posture behavior. The project identified its simple world and immature short-term memory as limits, while navigation and problem solving remained future work. In 2023, Natural Language-Based Societies of Mind used heterogeneous neural/LLM agents communicating in natural language and demonstrated prototypes for VQA, captioning, image generation, 3D generation, egocentric retrieval, embodied exploration and language tasks, up to 129 members. The paper is now journal-published (2025). It reports no benefit from more than two interaction rounds in one 3D setting; at least one text-to-image evaluation is qualitative, and the experiments do not establish cost-matched broad benefit or shared agent learning. A 2024 AAAI Symposium paper also proposes cognitive-architecture/LLM integration patterns including a Society-of-Mind/LIDA-motivated agency approach. [Brenner et al., ICMAS 1996](https://cdn.aaai.org/ICMAS/1996/ICMAS96-056.pdf); [Hearn, MIT CSAIL K-line language report](https://publications.csail.mit.edu/abstracts/abstracts05/hearn/hearn.html); [Zhuge et al., NLSOM (2023; journal version 2025)](https://doi.org/10.26599/CVM.2025.9450460); [Romero et al., AAAI Symposium (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaaiss.v2i1.27706).
- **What might remain and novelty.** Heterogeneous specialists with nested subskills and sparse reinstatement are a useful design vocabulary, but none is unique: blackboards, Soar/ACT-R, DUAL, LIDA, PSI, behavior-based robotics and modern modular or multi-agent systems instantiate overlapping organization. NLSOM directly occupies the obvious modern LLM-agent interpretation. Singh’s review traces derivational analogy directly to K-lines: replay retrieves the earlier problem-solving search tree, including failed branches, rather than only the final answer; retrieval, adaptation, indexing and how to record failures were open implementation questions. Singh also found no then-existing literal combination of connectionist representation with structured case-based reasoning. This makes the analogy useful for narrowing a test, but discounts broad episodic-reinstatement novelty (see AR-62 for the original mechanism and this section for later implementations). An architecture could differ only by a precise, task-general mechanism for learning agent boundaries, activation conditions, credit and partial-state memory jointly; that mechanism is not supplied by the original theory, and without it “society” is a broad metaphor. Confidence: **0/5 for a new class; 0–1/5 for any unformalized learning-rule residue**. Do not promote or repackage agent orchestration as an architecture class. [Singh, “Examining the Society of Mind,” *Computing and Informatics* 22 (2003)](https://cai.type.sk/content/2003/6/examining-the-society-of-mind/1332.pdf).
- **Small falsifier if revisited.** In a CPU-only compositional symbolic domain with reusable subroutines, compare exact trajectory replay, ordinary case retrieval, ungated K-line reinstatement, and context-sensitive partial reinstatement under the memo’s fixed level-band rule; include Soar chunking or a learned module router as a modern baseline. Give all methods identical specialist set, memory capacity, environment access and primitive-operation budget. Test held-out task recombinations with changed observations/goals; measure success, transfer, search operations, interference from stale methods and activation cost. Falsify the specific K-line hypothesis if level-banded partial reactivation does not beat full replay/case retrieval at matched cost, or if its gains depend on hand-designed specialists/cues. This is a methods study, not a model-class novelty test, and no run is currently justified.

#### HY-78 — Society-of-Mind organization × modern heterogeneous neural specialists (reject as a new hybrid)

- **Coupling considered.** Keep specialist processes in nested agencies, use K-line-like partial-activation memories to reinstate successful subsets under related cues, and allow macro/micro agents to exchange typed results and alter one another's activation.
- **Prior art and decision.** Minsky's own theory supplies the hierarchical society and K-line memory; Hearn's working K-line language adds a self-modifying network implementation, while the 1996 implementation translated the theory directly into a blackboard multi-agent system. NLSOM (2023; published 2025) couples heterogeneous neural modules through a common natural-language protocol, with hierarchical and democratic/leader-agent variants. The 2024 AAAI cognitive-architecture integration paper explicitly says its Society-of-Mind-motivated agency approach is “not a novel architectural approach” and leaves inter-agent communication, coordination and hierarchy as open questions. A new name, typed messages, or learned routing would not distinguish the mechanism unless the coupling changes a specified learning rule or computational guarantee. Broad coupling is rejected; no experiment is scheduled.
- **Potential narrow test only.** In one structured domain, compare sparse K-line reinstatement against episodic replay and learned module routing under the same specialists, calls, memory and solver. Reject if benefit is not in held-out recombination or if it requires extra specialist calls. No broad model-class claim remains.

### Selectional neural architectures revisited — 2026-09-27

#### AR-89 — Theory of Neuronal Group Selection (1978–1990s): selection among overlapping recurrent repertoires

- **Original computation and represented information.** Edelman’s theory of neuronal group selection (TNGS; Neural Darwinism) treats development and learning as selection over variable, overlapping groups of neurons. A primary repertoire supplies diverse circuits; experience alters synaptic efficacies so groups that contribute to adaptive behavior become more likely to participate; recurrent “reentry” among mapped perceptual and motor regions correlates distributed activity. Donnett and Smithers grounded the proposal in a sensorimotor robotics architecture: visual/sensor patterns activate feature and combination-response repertoires, reciprocal connections couple recognition maps to motor groups, and success at touching a perceived object reinforces the correlated ballistic motor response. [Reeke, Edelman & Sulzbach, “Selective Neural Networks and Their Implications for Recognition Automata” (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1177/109434208700100105); [Donnett & Smithers, NeurIPS 1989](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1989/file/274ad4786c3abca69fa097b85867d9a4-Paper.pdf).
- **Primitive, operation, I/O, learning, memory, inference.** The proposed unit is a recurrently connected neuron group, with group identity/function partly induced by activity and plasticity; groups communicate through overlapping or reciprocal map-to-map connections and reentrant loops. Inputs are sensory populations and adaptive consequences; outputs are perceptual categories and action-group activity. Learning is activity/experience-dependent synaptic modification that changes which groups win future selection; there is no single global loss or explicit address-based memory. Inference is ongoing population activation and recurrent correlation. Knowledge resides in the primary/secondary repertoires, their synapses and cross-map coordination. The original papers leave substantial details to particular models, so this is a theory family rather than one fully standardized algorithm.
- **Was it bad or early?** In the 1989 robotics paper, sensory input was still simulated on an IBM PC/AT and the authors explicitly identified serial computation as a major obstacle because the selectional system would be computationally intensive. This is a genuine hardware-era limit: GPUs, parallel simulation and current simulation toolchains make population-scale experiments much more practical. But the same paper’s robot task and feature detectors were narrow. The enduring issue is not simply speed: the theory does not give a general rule for defining/selecting group units, evaluating adaptive usefulness under delayed consequences, avoiding redundant groups, or assigning credit through reentrant loops. A critical review also records disputes over whether group-level Darwinian selection is distinct from ordinary synaptic selection/group formation. More computation cannot settle those conceptual and algorithmic questions. [Donnett & Smithers, lines 189–193](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1989/file/274ad4786c3abca69fa097b85867d9a4-Paper.pdf); [Doolittle & Bapteste et al., “Selectionist and Evolutionary Approaches to Brain Function: A Critical Appraisal” (2012)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3337445/).
- **What changed and what has already been modernized.** Parallel hardware can simulate diverse recurrent populations and modern learned encoders could improve perception; synthetic environments can provide repeated sensorimotor episodes, while differentiable surrogates may help tune parameters. Those aids risk replacing the distinctive local selection mechanism if global gradients do the real work. Direct implementations predate modern accelerators: the 1987 selective-network work reports recognition, categorization, generalization and tracking models; the 1989 robotics paper applied the principles to adaptive perception-action coordination. A 2023 arXiv proof of concept explicitly combines group selection with randomly initialized Hopfield networks, using their convergence/recognition behavior as group-level selection and showing repeated-symbol category learning on binary Latin letters. The authors characterize it as a proof of concept, not state-of-the-art recognition. Thus “TNGS × modern associative Hopfield units” is already occupied at the exact mechanism level, albeit only in a very small domain. [Stepanik (2023 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18789).
- **Closest research, novelty and value.** Closest neighbors include competitive/constructive neural networks, Hebbian or reward-modulated plasticity, population coding, evolutionary robotics and associative memories; these explain components but are not all equivalent to the proposed biological theory. The explicit Hopfield-group selection combination is direct prior art. No new broad class survives. A possible residual is a precise sensorimotor learning rule where recurrent group selection—not a globally optimized selector—creates and stabilizes cross-modal action-perception assemblies under delayed reward. That is a narrow empirical mechanism, currently underspecified and low confidence (**0/5 for class novelty; 1/5 for that residual**). It is not worth pursuing as a general architecture before a complete group birth/retirement, reward-credit and communication rule is fixed.
- **Small falsifiable prototype.** If that rule is made executable, use a CPU two-context sensorimotor toy with overlapping feature groups, reciprocal perception/action maps, delayed reward, and a later cue-to-action remapping. Compare (a) specified local group-selection plus reentry, (b) the same recurrent population with fixed groups and reward-modulated Hebbian plasticity, (c) a matched winner-take-all/competitive learner, and (d) a small neuroevolution baseline; equalize units, interaction budget and tuning effort. Measure first-task learning, transfer after remapping, retained behavior, group diversity, number of active groups and operations per action. Falsify the specific benefit if group selection gives no transfer/retention gain at matched cost, collapses to one group, or gains only because it has more tunable capacity. This tests one operationalization, not the truth of TNGS. No run.

#### HY-79 — Neural group selection × Hopfield associative groups (reject: explicit modern prior art)

- **Source architectures and coupling.** TNGS contributes variable overlapping groups selected by experience, with recurrent interaction/reentry; Hopfield networks contribute recurrent associative dynamics whose convergence can make an active group recognize a pattern. The proposed coupling lets the recognition/convergence behavior of each Hopfield group determine which group is strengthened or selected after repeated input, with a second level forming categories from selected groups.
- **Why it changes behavior / prior art.** This is not just placing a Hopfield memory beside a selection controller: the Hopfield relaxation itself is the selection signal used to alter the population of groups and form abstract categories. However, Stepanik’s 2023 preprint already gives this exact mechanism and demonstrates it on repeated binary letter patterns. Its scope is narrow and the paper disclaims state-of-the-art aims, but the central hybrid is not new. GPUs, larger image encoders and broader synthetic data could test scaling; they do not restore hybrid novelty. Reject as a candidate. [Stepanik (2023 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18789).
- **Small disproof / optional replication.** If revisited for replication, compare the published Hopfield-group rule against a single Hopfield memory, fixed ensemble/voting, and a conventional prototype learner at matched memory and compute; test corrupted glyphs, compositional shapes and sequential category overlap. Drop practical interest if selection merely clusters prototypes less efficiently or lacks gains outside the hand-binarized symbol task. No experiment scheduled.

HY-79 rejects that exact old-modern hybrid as already published. Neither track produces a new broad model class.

### Neuroevolution, generative encoding and heredity compatibility — 2026-09-27

#### AR-90 — NEAT, HyperNEAT and developmental encodings (1990s–2026): evolve a compact genotype, grow a network phenotype

*Cross-reference:* This source-checked expansion complements AR-48, which already covers Cellular Encoding, Kitano grammar growth, L-systems and modern developmental plasticity. It is not a new architecture family.

- **Original computation.** NEAT starts each candidate with a small neural controller, then evolves topology and weights together. Historical markings support crossover between structurally different genomes, while speciation protects new topology innovations from immediate competition with mature networks. HyperNEAT evolves a compositional pattern-producing network (CPPN) that maps the spatial coordinates of neural endpoints to connection weights, allowing a compact genome to generate repeated/symmetric connectivity. Developmental encodings generalize the genotype-to-phenotype process from a coordinate function to repeated local growth/rewriting/chemical dynamics. [Stanley & Miikkulainen, NEAT (2002)](https://direct.mit.edu/evco/article/10/2/99/1123/Evolving-Neural-Networks-through-Augmenting); [Stanley, D’Ambrosio & Gauci, HyperNEAT (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1162/artl.2009.15.2.15202); [Stanley & Miikkulainen, developmental-encoding taxonomy (2003)](https://nn.cs.utexas.edu/?stanley:alifej03=).
- **Representation and repeated operation.** Knowledge during search resides in a population of genotypes and their expressed networks. At each generation, the search evaluates candidate policies on task inputs, selects by fitness, crosses/mutates genomes, and grows/decodes new phenotypes; after deployment, ordinary NEAT/HyperNEAT controllers are static unless a separate plasticity rule is included. Their advantage is search over structure and regularity: a compact generator can reuse one discovered pattern across many edges, while direct encodings allow local irregular changes.
- **Was it bad or early?** This is a surviving method family rather than a failed model. Its historic cost is repeated population evaluation and irregular genome bookkeeping. In a 1989 predecessor experiment, a different selectional circuit explicitly hit serial-compute limits (AR-89); for evolutionary encoding, much of the cost is environmental rollout count and hard fitness landscapes, not simply arithmetic. Modern GPU simulation removes a real wall-clock bottleneck: TensorNEAT tensorizes variable-topology populations, reports up to 544× runtime speedup over NEAT-Python on HalfCheetah with a 10,000-member population on an RTX 4090, and supports NEAT/CPPN/HyperNEAT. But this comparison uses a fixed padding cap of 50 nodes/100 connections and 24-GB GPU hardware; it proves faster execution in those workloads, not better sample complexity, broader searchability, or superior learned behavior at equal rollout budgets. More compute cannot make a wrong substrate geometry useful or fix a fitness landscape with no accessible improving mutations. [TensorNEAT (2025, accepted ACM TELO)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08339).
- **Was developmental structure actually useful?** Yes, in some regimes: indirect CPPN encodings reuse geometric regularity, while direct encodings can express exceptions more easily. That complementarity was already combined explicitly. The 2017 HybrID work switches from indirect to direct encoding after regular patterns are found; Auto-Switch-HybrID removes the manual switch point; Offset-HybrID keeps both the CPPN and a direct offset vector active at once. Earlier common-genetic-encoding and DSE approaches add further direct/indirect alternatives. Hence “shared generative rule plus per-edge exceptions” is established, not a new hybrid. [Helms & Clune, *PLOS ONE* (2017)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5363933/); [Kitano/CE/DSE overview and experiments (2011)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3161195/).
- **Modernization and present prior art.** Modern work meta-learns developmental genotype-to-phenotype maps for quality-diversity/searchability (2024); LNDP couples developmental topology growth with activity/reward-dependent lifetime structural and synaptic plasticity (2024); MorphoNAS uses local morphogen/reaction-diffusion rules to grow small networks and is journal-published in 2026; a GECCO Companion 2026 study characterizes Hebbian/anti-Hebbian plasticity on 50,000 morphogenetically grown controllers and includes co-evolution of plasticity settings with developmental architecture. This closes generic “add learned development,” “add lifetime plasticity,” and “make the developmental code learnable” directions. [Montero et al., ALIFE 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09020); [Plantec et al., LNDP (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09787); [MorphoNAS (2026 journal version)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13785); [Medvid et al., GECCO Companion 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03386).
- **New controlled evidence against easy revival claims.** A preprint submitted 14 September 2026 matched a direct, static generative, and temporal developmental encoding on genome size (34), adult-controller size (34), optimizer, mutation/crossover, environments and evaluations across 30 paired evolutionary runs. In one simulated locomotion task, temporal development did not reliably beat direct encoding in final training or out-of-distribution fitness. It substantially increased phenotype diversity and attenuated early developmental damage, but reduced mutation viability and genotype–phenotype locality and sharply harmed crossover offspring fitness/viability. The paper is one benchmark and not a general verdict, but it directly shows why “more generative development” is not automatically more evolvable; representation compute also differed, with 3,072 development operations per phenotype versus none for direct encoding. [Saoud, “The Cost of Becoming” (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17606).
- **Disposition.** NEAT, HyperNEAT and development are useful search/encoding methods with direct descendants. Hardware materially improves throughput; it does not convert these into a new inference architecture or remove evaluation/sample complexity, geometry bias, or inheritance pathologies. Broad architecture novelty **0/5**. Retain AR-48 as archaeology and the narrowly defined HY-80 mechanism below as a low-confidence method question, not a promoted model class.

#### HY-80 — reversible compression of direct exceptions into a developmental generator (speculative; low-priority test only)

- **Source architectures.** HyperNEAT/CPPN provides a compact reusable geometric generator; HybrID/Offset-HybrID provides direct local edits when the generator misses irregularities; continual learning and sparse exceptions contribute bounded per-context correction memory.
- **Exact coupling considered.** Maintain a shared generative base plus local residuals. When the same residual motif recurs across contexts or shifted substrates, test whether it can be encoded as a low-complexity update to the shared generator; transfer that repeated pattern into the genotype, then clear or reduce only the now-explained local residuals. One-off exceptions remain local. If future contexts contradict the absorbed pattern, allow residuals to reappear rather than irreversibly overwriting the base. The hypothesized new behavior is movement in both directions between shared regularity and local exceptions, changing transfer/compression while preserving one-off adaptation; ordinary Offset-HybrID evolves generator and offsets simultaneously but does not itself specify this evidence-triggered consolidation-and-reversal rule.
- **Prior art and risk.** The broad hybrid is occupied: HybrID already has switch-based and concurrent generator-plus-offset variants; direct/indirect encodings can evolve in a common genome; DSE/CE and learned developmental maps occupy constructive representations; DPPNs and Lamarckian neuroevolution transfer learned phenotype information into genomes; LNDP and recent MorphoNAS work already couple development with lifetime plasticity. A targeted source check found that the 2017 HybrID paper explicitly describes irreversible one-way conversion as losing the ability to exploit newly encountered geometric regularities, proposes preserving both CPPN and offsets to keep adapting, and says passing acquired patterns back through the genome would require epigenetic inheritance or phenotype-to-offspring communication. This does not itself specify recurrence-triggered bidirectional consolidation of individual residuals, but it names the key conceptual seam as a recognized open mechanism, so an absence claim would be weak. The proposal may reduce to Lamarckian inheritance, model compression, or incremental system identification. Novelty confidence **0–1/5**; methods-level only if a precise algorithm beats the established no-consolidation Offset-HybrID baseline.
- **Possible advantage and failure modes.** It could retain recurring structural changes in a compact shared rule, transfer them to new layouts, and keep rare events as sparse exceptions. It may instead overfit a few contexts, cause catastrophic generator drift, absorb noise, need an expensive inverse-encoding fit, or lose the compact generator’s lineage compatibility. The 2026 matched comparison makes inheritance compatibility and locality mandatory outcomes, not optional side metrics.
- **Small falsifiable CPU prototype.** Use synthetic connectivity targets with a known repeated coordinate regularity, a recurring motif of local edge exceptions, and independent one-off exceptions. Compare (1) fixed generator plus residual table, (2) full direct connectivity storage, (3) Offset-HybrID-style generator plus offsets with no consolidation, and (4) the proposed recurrence-triggered fit/transfer/clear rule with a rollback test after a regime reversal. Match target observations, number of update opportunities and storage budget; charge generator fitting, validation and rollback cost. Measure held-out layout error, adaptation steps after shifts, bytes retained, corruption of one-off cases and recovery after reversal. Falsify the residue if it cannot save memory at matched held-out error, if recurring exceptions fail to transfer, or if consolidation harms old contexts more than the no-consolidation baseline. This tests a storage/adaptation rule, not a general AI architecture. A first CPU smoke test below supports only the known-motif compression premise; the matched consolidation/rollback comparison remains unrun.

#### HY-81 — intervention-distinction-preserving episodic memory for causal control (demote; component coupling is occupied)

- **Source mechanisms.** Continual Bayesian model selection can keep a bounded episodic buffer chosen to preserve data points whose statistics distinguish competing model classes; active causal RL can alternate interventions that learn/update a causal graph with policies that exploit it; CAASL learns an adaptive intervention policy to improve causal-graph estimation. A newer 2026 preprint applies causal interventions to selecting which memories should influence an LLM answer, though its objective is answer robustness rather than maintaining a causal-model posterior. [Nagy & Orbán, “Episodic memory for continual model learning” (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01169); [Cai et al., “Learning by Doing” (2024/2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04869); [Annadani et al., CAASL (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16718); [Srivastava, Causal Memory Intervention (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17641).
- **Exact coupling considered.** Keep a bounded set of past intervention episodes; score each episode by its contribution to posterior distinctions among causal-graph hypotheses that differ on high-impact control decisions. Choose future interventions using both task utility and the graph uncertainty induced by the retained data. When memory is full, evict episodes only when their removal minimally changes those distinctions. This makes memory contents affect the graph posterior, the graph posterior affect the next intervention, and the selected intervention change which future episodes are worth retaining.
- **Mechanistic difference and possible advantage.** It narrows ordinary replay/model-selection memory to interventional evidence that distinguishes graph hypotheses, including rare interventions that reservoir sampling or task-return ranking could discard. The potential value is under a hard memory cap after regime changes, when preserving one causal contrast may matter more than retaining many frequent transitions.
- **Prior-art collision and decision.** The three central operations already exist separately and close together: hypothesis-discriminating sample retention for continual model selection; intervention-updated causal RL; active causal experimental design; and, in a different LLM domain, intervention-based memory selection by causal effect on answers. I did not verify a source that explicitly combines *graph-posterior discrimination* with *eviction utility for intervention episodes* under a hard lifelong memory cap. That is a narrow absence from this targeted check, not evidence of novelty. The proposal is a principled objective for coupling established memory and active-learning components, not a new computational substrate/model class. Novelty confidence **0–1/5**; retain as an optional algorithm comparison only.
- **Small falsifier.** Use a small partially observed system with two causal regimes, competing DAG hypotheses, delayed control reward and a strict episodic buffer. Compare full-history oracle, reservoir sampling, the published model-selection memory objective, an active-causal policy with no history-aware eviction, and the coupled retention/intervention rule. Charge all graph-posterior updates, interventions and retained bytes. Measure posterior calibration over DAGs, number of interventions needed to detect a regime shift, downstream control regret and recovery after misleading/noisy interventions. Reject the method if it cannot beat the strongest single-component baseline in either graph identification or control at equal memory and interaction budgets, or if sufficient causal summary statistics remove the need for retained episodes. No experiment run.

#### HY-82 — counterexample-driven automaton growth inside recurrent networks (reject: direct extraction prior art)

- **Proposed idea and coupling.** Train a recurrent neural controller on sequence behavior; use a formal automata learner to find a distinguishing query/counterexample; split or reconfigure neural recurrent states so the learned continuous machine better matches the discrete automaton. The hoped-for behavior is a model that combines neural tolerance with a symbolic state machine that generalizes and can be checked on long sequences.
- **Direct prior art.** Weiss, Goldberg and Yahav’s ICML 2018 method already uses Angluin’s L* exact learner for automata extraction, with a trained RNN serving as the query oracle; it obtains distinguishing counterexamples/queries to refine the DFA describing the RNN’s state dynamics. Earlier recurrent-net work addresses finite-automaton identification, and NNPDA (AR-64/HY-49) explicitly trains a continuous recurrent controller and then extracts a discrete pushdown automaton. Thus the simple counterexample/extraction loop is established. A new mechanism would need to specify how discrete counterexamples change the neural architecture or learning rule beyond state abstraction/extraction; merely saying “grow units on a split” does not provide that rule. [Weiss et al., ICML 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09576); [Gabrijel & Dobnikar (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0893-6080(02)00221-6); [NNPDA 1993, AR-64](https://api.drum.lib.umd.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/58808e6a-dddf-4ac5-9765-6c6206e64f6c/content).
- **Closest neighboring lineage.** Stochastic Distinguishing Experiments (SDEs) actively select distinguishing experiments and update predictive tests/states after surprise; sPOMDPs use those tests to split/refine predictive-state partitions. Those already occupy the broad active-query × hidden-state-refinement direction, while AR-74 covers active automata learning and HY-49 covers continuous neural stacks plus counterexample-guided PDA repair. [Collins & Shen, 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2017.07.005); [Collins & Shen, 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bica.2018.04.005).
- **Small falsifier if a precise mechanism is proposed.** On held-out regular and visibly pushdown languages, compare L* with an RNN oracle, query-guided DFA/RNN extraction, ordinary RNN training on counterexample strings, and the proposed architecture-splitting loop. Match oracle queries, training examples and total state/unit budget; test exact classification on long generated strings and report extraction cost. Drop any neural-growth claim if the loop only reproduces the already-known extracted DFA, adds parameters without reducing queries, or fails to improve long-string generalization. No new class and no experiment run.

#### AR-01 modernization addendum — NARS language interfaces and evaluation remain the hard problem (2026-09-27)

- **What modern technology changed.** NARS was designed to manage scarce inference steps itself; more arithmetic does not directly answer the original resource-allocation question. Its own 2015 capability/limitations material says NAL had a specification and implementations, but called for more testing, a stronger theory of “thought economy,” automatic knowledge acquisition, and systematic NARS+ combinations. These are objective/control and interface gaps, not just slow 1990s computers. [Wang, AGI-NARS conclusion (2015)](https://cis.temple.edu/~pwang/AGI-NARS/2015-KFU/09-Conclusion.html).
- **Modern language connection already exists.** NARS-GPT is an open implementation that uses GPT-4 as a language channel into OpenNARS for Applications: it maps natural language to Narsese, then leaves explicit belief revision, evidence-based NAL calculations, long-term storage and inference to NARS. It supports optional bounded memory with usefulness ranking. This proves feasibility of the broad LLM-language-front-end × NARS-reasoner coupling, but its repository description is not a controlled broad reasoning evaluation. [NARS-GPT repository](https://github.com/opennars/NARS-GPT).
- **New evaluation work.** A 2026 preprint introduces NARS-Reasoning-v0.1, a 1,000-example benchmark pairing natural language with FOL forms and executable Narsese, plus a deterministic compiler for a useful logical subset and a Phi-2 LoRA proof of concept trained for True/False/Uncertain classification. This advances data and executable evaluation for the older system, but does not test open-world online learning, sensorimotor grounding, priority scheduling under hard budgets, or broad task transfer. [Gabriel & Wang, “From Natural Language to Executable Narsese” (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18873).
- **Disposition.** Keep the old architecture as a serious prior-art and reasoning baseline; do not promote modern LLM translation, neural term similarity or a larger memory as architecture novelty. A useful research program would compare supported/unsupported/contradictory conclusions on executable Narsese tasks at matched latency and memory, but only after controlling for the accuracy of the language-to-formal translation. No experiment run.

#### HY-80 CPU smoke experiment — known fixed generator basis (limited positive; not a novelty test)

- **Question tested.** In a deliberately favorable synthetic layout task, can a shared generator fitted to repeated coordinate structure predict a recurring edge motif on unseen layouts better than a zero-residual/direct-cache baseline, while using fewer scalar slots than directly storing positive training edges?
- **Setup.** CPU-only NumPy run, 12 random seeds. Per seed, 12 training layouts and 12 held-out layouts; 20 nodes/layout and all 380 directed non-self edges. Each node has a random scalar coordinate. Target edge residual is 1 for the recurring known rule `source_x < 0.30 AND target_x > 0.70`, plus two randomly selected one-off positive residual edges per layout outside that motif. The 100 fixed Gaussian RBF centers form a 10×10 grid over the two endpoint coordinates, with sigma 0.17 and ridge penalty 0.02. The model is fit jointly to all training edges. A training residual entry is counted as remaining direct storage when absolute fit error exceeds 0.45. This is a supervised, known-coordinate-prior toy; recurrence detection and basis search are not learned.
- **Results.** Held-out MSE for predicting zero residual on unseen layouts: 0.096729 ± 0.009793 across seeds. Shared RBF held-out MSE: 0.014647 ± 0.001104, an 84.9% relative reduction. Paired mean absolute MSE gain was 0.082082 (approximate 95% t interval [0.076184, 0.087980], n=12). Motif-edge MSE remained 0.054087 ± 0.011869; non-motif MSE was 0.010646 ± 0.001451, so the generator still misses part of the recurring motif. A positive-edge direct table averaged 432.9 scalar slots in the training layouts; 65.9 above-threshold residual slots remained after fitting the generator, for 165.9 total generator-plus-residual slots and 61.4% ± 5.4% savings versus that direct positive-edge table.
- **Interpretation.** This validates only that a hand-chosen smooth function approximator can compress and transfer an explicitly recurring low-dimensional rule in this toy. The zero-residual baseline is the transferable behavior of a direct cache when the held-out layouts have new edge identities; it is not a claim that direct storage cannot fit training data. Storage counts are scalar slots, not byte-accurate memory or equal-compute accounting. The test omits the proposed part that might be distinctive: detecting recurring residuals, deciding when to consolidate them into a generator, preserving one-off edits, and reversing consolidation after regime changes. It also omits Offset-HybrID as a matched comparator. No novelty implication.
- **Resource and reproducibility record.** Python 3.11.9, NumPy 2.4.6, CPU only, 12 seeds, 0.617 s reported runtime, GPU not used, peak VRAM 0 GB. No GPU occupancy/process check was taken because no GPU experiment was imminent; live shared usage remains unknown. The run used in-memory code piped to Python and created no experiment artifact. A follow-up must compare fixed generator + cache, Offset-HybrID-style offsets without consolidation, and evidence-triggered reversible consolidation under matched observation/update and storage budgets, then introduce motif drift and check old-context damage/recovery. Stop this line if consolidation cannot improve the Pareto frontier over no-consolidation offsets after charging fit/validation/rollback cost.

#### HY-84 — confidence-triggered expansion of NEF/SPA representations (demote; allocator is established)

- **Source mechanisms.** NEF uses a specified population of neurons to represent vectors and approximate transforms; SPA uses fixed-width semantic-pointer vectors for binding/unbinding and cleanup. ART and resource-allocating networks grow categories/units when an input fails an existing match criterion. The proposed coupling would let low SPA cleanup margin trigger local growth of the implicated NEF ensemble, with allocation targeted only to overloaded semantic roles.
- **Exact claim and expected behavior.** The hoped-for gain is lower neuron count at equal retrieval quality: preserve high capacity for ambiguous or frequently used pointers, while cheap pointers use smaller ensembles. This is dynamic resource allocation over an existing neural/vector-symbolic computation, not a different basic computation. More neurons in a fixed-width ensemble can reduce neural representation/decoding error; they do not remove cross-talk caused by bundling too many items in the fixed-width vector. Widening one vector locally is generally incompatible with bound vectors/relations in the same algebra and could require vocabulary/memory re-encoding.
- **Prior-art check and novelty judgment.** Low-match-triggered category allocation is central to ART vigilance; Platt’s 1991 Resource-Allocating Network adds a computational unit when an unusual pattern is presented. VSA capacity analyses explain width-dependent retrieval/bundling limits; HDC/VSA literature already separates fixed-width working representations from larger external associative memory. Nengo's public `Ensemble` API takes fixed `n_neurons` and `dimensions` when building each ensemble and exposes weight/encoder learning rules, but this source review did not establish that dynamic ensemble growth is impossible or absent across all backends. In any case, the general “low confidence → add capacity” rule is prior art; at most the exact neural-readout-versus-algebraic-noise allocator is a task-specific engineering question. Class novelty **0/5**; method novelty **0–1/5**, pending exhaustive search not warranted before utility evidence. [Carpenter et al., Fuzzy ART (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0893-6080(91)90056-B); [Platt, Resource-Allocating Network (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1991.3.2.213); [Kleyko et al., VSA capacity analysis (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10352); [HDC/VSA memory separation (2023)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9869149/); [Nengo Ensemble API](https://www.nengo.ai/nengo/v3.0.0/frontend-api.html).
- **Strongest advantage and failure modes.** A local allocator might spend neurons where repeated cleanup is ambiguous, improve robustness per active neuron, and avoid globally raising dimension. But cleanup margin conflates finite-neuron noise, algebraic bundling cross-talk, input grounding error and true ambiguity. It can allocate capacity to unfixable error; structural growth can require recompiling downstream transforms or replaying old associations; a fixed larger network may be simpler and more efficient.
- **Small falsifiable test.** Synthetic role–filler retrieval with two independently swept factors: (a) neural decoder noise/population size and (b) number of bindings bundled at a fixed VSA width. Compare fixed-small, fixed-large, confidence-triggered neuron growth, wider-vector, and SDM/external-memory controls. Fix total neuron/byte budgets where meaningful; separately report representational changes, reconstruction overhead, retrieval accuracy, held-out role/filler compositions, active neurons, latency and forgetting after new roles arrive. Falsify utility if margin does not distinguish neural approximation error from algebraic overload, if growth helps only by spending more total resources, or if the fixed-small system plus external memory dominates. No experiment scheduled; low priority until a cheap simulation shows a meaningful equal-budget advantage.

#### HY-80 prior-art follow-up — the residual-to-genotype seam is anticipated conceptually

The primary HybrID source makes the unresolved transfer problem explicit. It describes Auto-Switch-HybrID's one-way indirect-to-direct switch as irreversible and unable to rediscover geometric regularities after a task/environment change; Offset-HybrID retains both CPPN and direct offsets, enabling broad generator changes plus local edits. The authors specifically say that passing learned patterns into the genotype would require epigenetic inheritance or communication of learning to offspring, and list this as future research. Their tested Offset-HybrID evolves both encodings at once; it does **not** perform evidence-triggered online identification of repeated residual motifs, clear the now-explained exception entries, or reverse that consolidation when evidence changes. Thus the exact policy remains unverified, but the high-level missing direction is anticipated and its most natural implementation sits inside established Lamarckian/epigenetic neuroevolution. Keep HY-80 as a low-cost methods benchmark only, and compare any implementation against Offset-HybrID plus ordinary Lamarckian inheritance before making novelty claims. This prior-art result lowers enthusiasm; it does not justify expanding the toy smoke test into expensive work. #### Old-architecture archaeology — von Neumann constructors, self-reproducing automata, and Evoloops (AR-91)

- **What the older architecture computes.** Von Neumann's universal constructor is a local automaton that reads a description, constructs the described machine, and copies the description so the offspring can itself reproduce. The design separates a constructor, a copier, and a control description; the important computational idea is that a machine can contain an executable description of itself without confusing “copy this description” with “execute this description.” The 1966 posthumous volume formalizes a 29-state cellular substrate; Codd later reduced the state count. In the 1990s, Langton's loops and Sayama's nine-state Evoloop made compact local self-reproduction and heritable interaction-driven variation simulable. Evoloop used no global fitness function: collision, dissolution, and differing reproduction rates produced population-level selection. [von Neumann, *Theory of Self-Reproducing Automata* (1966)](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/MAS.865/topics/self_replication/VonNeumann.pdf), [Codd, “A system of universal cellular automata” / simplified replicator (1968)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0019995866902208), [Sayama, “A New Structurally Dissolvable Self-Reproducing Loop Evolving in a Simple Cellular Automata Space” (1999)](https://bingdev.binghamton.edu/sayama/papers/ALIFE5-4-343.pdf).
- **Unit, information, and repeated operation.** A finite-state cell updates from its neighborhood. The wider construction is represented as a spatially embedded genome/tape plus local construction-control state. Repeated local updates copy the description, build the described configuration, and let descendants interact. Input is a seeded configuration and boundary/resource conditions; output is a population of self-copying structures. “Inference” is not the central objective: replication, repair, or survival is the behavior being computed.
- **Learning and memory.** The original constructor does not learn by gradient descent. In Evoloop, variation enters through interactions and imperfectly robust replication; selection is realized through differential persistence and reproduction. Heritable information lives in the loop/genome, while transient construction state lives in cells. Modern differentiable neural cellular automata can instead learn local update rules for a specified morphogenesis/regeneration objective, but training for a target form is distinct from open-ended evolution of the rule.
- **Why it may have been early, and what changed.** Space/time requirements and debugging a large discrete machine were formidable on 1940s–60s hardware; later CA models proved easier to simulate but often had hand-designed rules and highly constrained worlds. Parallel GPUs, cheap large grids, automatic differentiation, and differentiable simulators remove much of the simulation bottleneck and make local rules trainable. They do not by themselves supply a useful open-ended objective, cumulative functional complexity, or robust transfer between environments. The modern neural-CA literature already covers learned self-organization and regeneration [Mordvintsev et al. (2020)](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/), and a 2023 preprint reports inheritable mutation and genetic drift in neural CAs [Sinapayen (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13043).
- **Current direct collision.** A September 2026 preprint gives each cell a tiny neural network and copies/mutates its weights during replication; it reports 1,680 short runs and 24 long runs, with self-maintaining populations in 20 of the 24 long configurations and a phenotype/genotype-diversity tradeoff. This is direct prior art for the obvious constructor × neural-CA hybrid, though its abstract establishes ecological persistence/diversity rather than task-directed skill, cumulative open-ended capability, or broad intelligence. Treat those latter claims as untested, not as results. [Jain, Reimers & Nichele, “Self-Replicating Neural Cellular Automata” (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19902); broad historical context and unresolved definitions are reviewed in [Sayama & Nehaniv, “Self-Reproduction and Evolution in Cellular Automata: 25 Years After Evoloops” (2025/2026)](https://direct.mit.edu/artl/article/31/1/81/124368/Self-Reproduction-and-Evolution-in-Cellular).
- **Was it bad or too early?** Mixed. Local self-copying and heredity were sound computational abstractions and are now experimentally accessible. The claim that this substrate naturally yields open-ended, generally useful intelligence remains unsupported; limited rule spaces, resource competition, and absence of a task-relevant selection signal can yield persistent but behaviorally trivial ecosystems. More compute addresses experiment scale, not the missing mechanism for cumulative useful innovation.
- **Novelty judgment.** No new architecture claim. Core constructor/copy separation is classical; compact evolving CA descendants and trainable neural CAs are established. Any remaining contribution would have to specify a new, testable mechanism by which task-relevant behavior changes heritable construction rules while preserving replication stability. Novelty confidence for the broad direction: 0/5.
- **Small falsifier if revisited.** At equal cell-update budgets, compare a hand-coded Evoloop, a shared-rule regenerative NCA, and a weight-inheriting self-replicating neural CA under random local damage and a changing navigation/foraging objective. Measure replication viability, repair, task score, and whether innovations persist across generations. Falsify the “heritable self-organization helps general behavior” claim if replication survives but task performance does not improve over the shared-rule or non-heritable baseline, or if any gain disappears when total updates and mutation opportunities are matched. CPU-first on small grids; GPU is optional only after live process/VRAM inspection.

#### Hybrid rejection — von Neumann constructor × neural cellular automaton (HY-85)

- **Source mechanisms and coupling.** The constructor separates a copier and construction policy encoded in a genome; a neural CA gives each local site a learned neighborhood-to-state update rule. The direct modern coupling lets a living cell copy a neighbor's local network weights with mutation, so the update rule itself is inherited through spatial reproduction. This changes genotype transmission rather than merely putting a CA next to a neural controller.
- **Why it behaves differently and the closest work.** It can generate spatially embodied lineages whose policy and morphology coevolve under local competition. The mechanism is already instantiated by neural-CA mutation work in 2023 and the 2026 self-replicating neural-CA preprint above; classical Evoloop supplies earlier non-neural local heredity. This is a real interaction, but not a new one.
- **Advantages and failure modes.** Local parallelism, cheap mutation, and open-ended population dynamics are attractive for self-repairing materials or evolutionary simulation. Main risks are extinction, neutral drift, mutation load, task reward requiring global coordination, and apparent “diversity” without cumulative capability. Evaluation can mistake ecological persistence for intelligence.
- **Disposition and falsifier.** Reject as a novel hybrid (novelty 0/5). A worthwhile replication would add matched task-directed selection and heritability ablations; the central claim fails if copied weights increase lineage diversity but not held-out task competence or damage recovery at equal update budget. No experiment run in this continuation.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — counterpropagation networks (AR-92)

- **Original computation.** Hecht-Nielsen's 1987 counterpropagation network composes Kohonen competitive learning with a Grossberg outstar associative output layer. A winner-take-all/prototype layer learns an input-space partition; its active unit then selects or interpolates an associated output prototype. It acts as a learned lookup/interpolation table rather than a deep feature hierarchy. [Hecht-Nielsen, “Counterpropagation Networks” (1987), Optica primary record](https://opg.optica.org/ao/abstract.cfm?uri=ao-26-23-4979).
- **Representation and operation.** Input vectors are represented by prototype/codebook locations; outputs are stored as associations to winning prototypes. Repeated operation is nearest-prototype competition followed by an outstar readout. Learning is local: competitive updates move the winning input prototype, while associative updates adjust its output weights toward the target. Inference is a fast competition and weighted output lookup. Knowledge resides in codebook and association weights; no episodic external memory is required.
- **Historical weakness and modernization.** The design was attractive when backpropagation was expensive and its local stages trained quickly, but memory grows with prototype count, distance-based partitioning becomes difficult in high dimensions, and prototype coverage/generalization depend on presentation order and density. GPUs and modern optimizers make larger codebooks cheap, but do not remove the geometric curse or turn local lookup into compositional extrapolation. RBF, vector quantization, SOM, prototype learning, and local mixture models occupy neighboring territory.
- **Novelty verdict and test.** Archaeologically useful but not a new architecture class (0/5). A tiny CPU test could compare counterpropagation, RBF, and a compact MLP on smooth interpolation with a shifted input-density distribution, matching parameter and memory budgets; the class's practical claim would be falsified if its fast local fitting does not yield a robustness/latency advantage over these controls. No experiment run.

#### Open source lead — Crossbar Adaptive Array (CAA)

An independent archaeology report flagged Bozinovski's Crossbar Adaptive Array (CAA, circa 1981/82) as absent under that exact name. The available evidence so far is a later author retrospective describing a crossbar of action preferences and valence/emotional evaluation, plus a reported “genetic environment” that supplies initial state-to-valence associations. The cited original 1981/82 source has not yet been recovered, so do not treat the algorithm or its self-learning claims as primary-source verified. Broadly it appears close to associative actor-critic/intrinsic-value mechanisms already covered elsewhere. Keep as a source-recovery lead, not a candidate; if the primary text is found, test whether the valence mechanism learns anything beyond a hand-coded prior at equal interaction and memory budgets. [Bozinovski retrospective (2018)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1877050918323020).

#### Hybrid collision audit — active sensing, intention learning, program synthesis, spiking prediction, and classifier systems (HY-86–HY-90)

**HY-86 — predictive coding × active sensing (reject as broad novelty; retain a narrow mechanism comparison).** Predictive latent-state estimation is coupled to actions chosen to reduce expected posterior entropy; new observations then change what the agent learns. Sharafeldin et al. give an end-to-end architecture, demonstrating maze exploration and active visual sampling with downstream classification. Their implementation uses a deep generative VAE and Monte Carlo approximation to information gain; it is not the standard iterative MAP predictive-coding inner loop. The direct coupling therefore occupies generic predictive-perception × uncertainty-driven sensing, but a controlled comparison of iterative local-error inference against amortized VAE inference under sensor shifts remains a useful empirical question. Reported limitations include a small task set, discrete action enumeration, and dependence on the chosen generative model. Broad novelty 0/5; narrow comparison is a replication question, not an architecture claim. Small falsifier: on procedurally shifted foveated scenes, equalize sensor views and compute; compare amortized VAE, iterative PC, random selection, and a greedy information-gain oracle. Reject any claim of better adaptation if the iterative mechanism does not improve held-out classification or exploration efficiency under matched resources. [Sharafeldin et al. (2024)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11240181/).

**HY-87 — Fusion ART × intention/BDI × reinforcement learning (reject; direct 2010 hybrid).** cBDI-FALCON already has separate desire, intention, and reactive Fusion-ART modules. The reactive module learns state/action/value behavior; the intention module learns action-sequence associations with context and goals, refines plans from reinforcement, and prunes low-confidence plans. The authors report a concrete limitation: strict plan matching reduces plan reuse and causes fallback to reactive TD-FALCON, with limited sensing reduction. A modern ART-state cache or learned intention scheduler is not novel at this granularity. Novelty 0/5. If any narrow revisit is justified, compare plan retrieval under context shifts at equal experience against the original reactive fallback, measuring reuse, sensing, and regret; otherwise keep as rejection. [Tan et al. (2010), cBDI-FALCON](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2009.11.012).

**HY-88 — analogy dynamics × program synthesis (demote; broad coupling occupied).** Copycat-like structural analogy plus executable synthesis is an intuitive hybrid, but analogy-guided synthesis already has retrieval → AST-based abstraction/“revelation” → program-reasoning stages in SynthoMinds. This is not an exact transplant of Copycat's parallel codelet/temperature dynamics, so that narrower search-control policy is not disproved; it needs a precise algorithm and a control against ordinary AST retrieval and grammar search before it merits candidate status. The broad “analogy helps synthesis” claim is not new; confidence ≤1/5. Small falsifier: few-shot DSL transformations requiring relational transfer, charge invalid programs and runtime, and ablate stochastic codelet competition against the same retrieved abstractions with deterministic search. [Gou et al. (2024), SynthoMinds](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jss.2024.112140).

**HY-89 — predictive coding × continual spiking learning (reject as generic hybrid; exact prior art).** Spiking Neural Coding Networks already combine continuous-time guess-and-correct activity updates with local synaptic updates, process data as a one-pass stream, and report lower forgetting on split-task classification than several tested continual-learning baselines. Later PC-SNN and DiffPC papers extend local spiking predictive learning. This overlaps the existing AR-45/AR-78 predictive/spiking archaeology and HY-61/62 predictive-coding hybrid audits; log it as a source-checked collision rather than a new candidate. Hardware may improve event-driven energy use, but the historical-to-current premise and basic learning coupling are already occupied. Novelty 0/5. A replication would need to test stream shifts and realistic neuromorphic energy/latency against strong replay and continual-learning baselines; it would not establish architecture novelty. [Ororbia et al. (2023), Spiking Neural Coding for continual streams](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2023.126292), [N'dri et al. (2024), survey of spiking predictive coding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05386).

**HY-90 — learning classifier systems × deep perception (reject as generic hybrid; multiple direct precedents).** XCSR has already consumed deep-network-compressed input as continuous-valued rule conditions; Matsumoto et al. report that the covering mechanism can improve classification on their benchmarks. DCAXCSR uses a deep classification autoencoder as compressor/decompressor around XCSR. N-XCS goes further by putting a neural network in each classifier's condition and adjusting it by backpropagation after covering or genetic crossover fails to match an input. Thus a learned encoder feeding evolutionary rules, or neural plasticity inside the rule match, is not a new broad combination. Exact joint credit assignment or continual rule/feature coevolution could remain a methods question, but would need controls against these systems and XCS with replay. Novelty 0/5 for the generic coupling. Tiny falsifier: rare outlier-state detection with representation drift; compare fixed-feature XCS, XCSR on deep compression, N-XCS, and joint encoder/rule updates at equal memory and interaction budgets. Reject the coupling if the joint model does not improve shifted-state coverage without sacrificing accuracy or rule interpretability. [Matsumoto et al. (2017), XCSR with deep compression](https://doi.org/10.20965/jaciii.2017.p0856), [Hayashida (2019), N-XCS](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecj.12209), [DCAXCSR record](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/xcsr-based-on-compressed-input-by-deep-neural-network-for-high-di).

#### AR-91 primary-methods follow-up — neural CA heredity is direct and narrowly scoped

I inspected the full 2026 preprint rather than relying only on its abstract. Each grid site holds its own two-layer network with 44 parameters (40 mutable weights); on clone events it inherits a uniformly selected living neighbor's network and perturbs weights with bounded uniform noise. The reported runs have no external task or objective beyond the local viability/liveness gate. The authors explicitly say their “open-endedness” is descriptive genotype novelty, not a claim that a formal open-ended-evolution criterion is met; they also state they did not evaluate genomes on an external task. The diversity labels are operational coarse-grainings, and the sole agent capacity is 44 parameters. Therefore this paper directly closes the old-constructor × per-cell-NCA inheritance idea, while leaving a substantial gap between persistent lineage diversity and capability accumulation. The strongest low-cost next test is to add a controlled changing task plus damage, log parentage, and measure held-out skill and repair—not another diversity-only sweep. This is a single-version preprint and its results need independent replication. [Full preprint, methods and scope/limitations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19902).
