#### C029 prior-art follow-up — dynamic neural inference already reuses activations (2023)

Sharir & Anandkumar's Incrementally-Computable Neural Networks directly address updating a model output when a document changes: vector quantization discretizes intermediate activations so small perturbations do not propagate, enabling reuse of cached values. Their VQ-OPT experiment reports comparable document-classification accuracy and 12.1× median fewer arithmetic operations across atomic edits, with a smaller 4.7× average reduction for complete revision pairs. [Sharir & Anandkumar (2023), primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14988). This is a more direct architecture-level precedent for incremental inference than general database materialized-view maintenance. It does not learn an explicit semantic dependency graph or certify which outputs are safe to retain; it instead changes the model's intermediate representation so insignificant changes are filtered. It nevertheless closes the broad C029 claim that neural conclusions can be selectively recomputed after input edits. Any residual should be framed as a correctness-aware systems method for sound dependency certificates or conservative fallback under opaque/online models, not a new learning architecture. A fair falsifier would compare full recomputation, VQ incremental inference and learned dependency invalidation on edit streams with known causal change cones, matching output error, model size and wall-clock; count audit/fallback work. Reject if the learned graph ever silently preserves a stale conclusion or if its audit cost erases the reuse savings. No experiment run.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — Qualitative Process Theory and QSIM (AR-114; 1984–present)

**Original computation.** Forbus's Qualitative Process Theory represents physical processes (flow, heating, contact, motion, etc.) with explicit process schemas and causal influences. QSIM, developed by Kuipers, represents each variable using a finite *quantity space* of meaningful landmarks and intervals plus a direction of change; qualitative differential equations (QDEs) encode constraints such as addition, multiplication, derivatives and monotonic relations. Given a QDE and an initial qualitative state, the simulator repeatedly proposes successor states, constraint-filters them and outputs a branching behavior graph/tree rather than a single numerical trajectory. This lets one model stand for a family of ODEs consistent with incomplete knowledge. [Forbus, *Qualitative Process Theory* (MIT AI TR-789, 1984)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/a48814a2-9d2b-4694-9e7a-0d5b3b019d7f); [Kuipers, *Qualitative Simulation* (AIJ 1986, author-hosted reprint)](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~kuipers/research/pubs/Kuipers-aij-86.html); [QSIM overview](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~kuipers/research/qsim/qsim-overview.html).

**Was it bad or merely early?** It was not primarily a compute-limited learner. The core simulator is symbolic, constraint-based search and worked on 1980s hardware. Its guarantee is one-sided: for a correctly specified QDE and a valid abstraction of the initial condition, each concrete ODE solution has a corresponding qualitative behavior in the simulator's output. This is coverage, not a probability distribution or calibrated uncertainty estimate. The same abstraction can admit spurious behaviors; the original paper shows local qualitative simulation cannot always eliminate them, and later work proves soundness and completeness cannot both be guaranteed for expressive QSIM vocabularies. Ambiguous models also generate large trees. More GPU throughput can speed search or a learned front end, but cannot restore quantitative detail discarded by abstraction, identify useful landmarks without data/assumptions, or turn branch enumeration into calibrated probabilities. [Kuipers (1986), original analysis](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~kuipers/research/pubs/Kuipers-aij-86.html); [Yılmaz & Say, *Causes of Ineradicable Spurious Predictions* (2011)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.0020).

**Modernization already tried.** QSIM's own lineage already includes Q2/Q3 quantitative annotations, adaptive landmarks and time points, trajectory envelopes, abstraction changes and filtering methods that preserve formal coverage where assumptions hold. The field also moved beyond manual models: Genmodel, Qoph, ILP-QSI and other QDE learners infer constraints from qualitative or numerical traces. Qoph supports noisy data and can introduce unmeasured intermediate variables; that does not establish robustness to arbitrary missing sensor channels or irregular time gaps, and its search/model count grows with noise. The 2010 survey covers decades of QDE model-learning systems. Gaussian-process methods have also learned ODEs with qualitative structure. A 2025 diagnosis paper couples ASP-QSIM outputs to observed traces for conformance-based monitoring and fault detection, evidence that this is an active specialist method rather than an abandoned class. [QSIM overview and extensions](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~kuipers/research/qsim/qsim-overview.html); [Pang & Coghill, QDE learning survey (2010)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3659653/); [Qoph, *Learning Qualitative Models of Physical and Biological Systems* (2007)](https://digitalarchive.library.bogazici.edu.tr/bitstreams/1b8d970e-c9aa-4a1e-b30a-d4e6c07dd9df/download); [Liu et al., *Learning ODE Models with Qualitative Structure Using Gaussian Processes* (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.05364); [Das et al., QSIM monitoring and diagnosis (DX 2025)](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/01oasics/oasics-vol136-dx2025/html/OASIcs.DX.2025.4/OASIcs.DX.2025.4.html).

**Use, strengths and failure modes.** The method remains plausible when users know coarse causal structure but not reliable parameters, and they care about event order, direction, thresholds or safe/unsafe possibilities more than exact trajectories: diagnosis, fault monitoring, process control and explanation. It can represent a set of possible dynamics structurally, with readable constraints and explicit alternative futures. It is weak when a task requires precise magnitudes, many interacting variables, or calibrated probabilities over branches. Engineers must identify observed variables, select landmarks and provide or learn from a typed vocabulary of qualitative relations; QDE learning does not automatically solve this grounding problem. Converting noisy, sparsely sampled measurements to qualitative states is itself uncertain. Stress tests with missing observed channels and irregular gaps should be labeled as new tests, separate from Qoph's demonstrated unmeasured-intermediate-variable and noise results. Quantitative hybridization and adaptive refinement already exist in the QSIM line; a newly named version is not an open gap.

**Novelty and possible hybrid.** QPT/QSIM is established architecture archaeology, not a new model class (novelty 0/5). A learned perception/landmark front end feeding QSIM is not sufficient novelty: neural physical-concept discovery, QDE learning, GP qualitative structure and ASP-QSIM monitoring already address adjacent pieces. The exact broad coupling must therefore not be promoted under a new name. A remaining *benchmark question*, not a claim of invention, is whether a modern, uncertainty-aware QDE learner can retain QSIM's useful trajectory-coverage behavior with fewer spurious branches on noisy partial observations than historical QML baselines, without needing expert-specified landmarks.

**Small falsifiable revival experiment.** Use small systems with analytically or exhaustively checkable qualitative behavior classes (for example, bounded linear or threshold-switched ODE families) and fixed observed-variable identities, sampling schedules and QDE relation vocabulary. Add measurement noise and held-out initial conditions; treat missing channels/irregular gaps as a separately labeled new stress condition. Compare (i) oracle QDE + QSIM as a *coverage ceiling*, not a data-matched competitor; (ii) a faithful Qoph/ILP-QSI-style learner followed by QSIM; and (iii) a specific GP posterior or interval-valued ODE learner whose calibrated trajectory sets are abstracted to the same event alphabet and forecast horizon. Match observed data, allowed model grammar, latent-variable allowance and prior knowledge in the learned-model comparison. Measure empirical event-sequence coverage against set size/behavior width, event-order recall, runtime and model size. Only call a branch spurious when its unrealizability is proved for the chosen system family; otherwise report it as “unwitnessed in a stated finite/interval audit,” since failure to find a numerical witness is not proof. Falsify a monitoring-utility claim if learned QDEs miss held-out events under modest noise, or their coverage-vs-set-size curve and runtime are worse than a calibrated numeric baseline. CPU-only is sufficient; no experiment ran and no GPU resources were used. **Disposition:** worth retaining as an archaeology/reference family and possible monitoring baseline; not worth continuing as a new architecture candidate absent a concrete application and mechanism.

#### Archaeology near misses — Contract Net and TAMER (no model-class candidates)

The independent scan also identified two absent-by-name approaches but they do not meet the architecture-class objective. Smith's 1980 **Contract Net Protocol** is a distributed task-allocation/communication protocol: a manager announces a task, capable peers submit task-specific bids, and an award assigns work; its concerns include message traffic, deadlines and local evaluators rather than a new learned computational unit. It persists in distributed and multi-robot allocation, so it was not waiting for GPU-era neural hardware. [Smith, *The Contract Net Protocol* (1980 primary paper)](https://cse-robotics.engr.tamu.edu/dshell/cs631/papers/smith80contract.pdf).

**TAMER** (2008) learns a model of scalar human evaluative feedback and chooses actions predicted to receive high feedback; the original uses supervised function approximation rather than temporal-difference RL. Deep TAMER already extends this to high-dimensional visual states and reports an Atari Bowling agent trained with 15 minutes of human feedback. The historical constraint was feedback delay, bandwidth and reward alignment, not insufficient compute; modern deep encoders already occupy the obvious modernization. [Knox & Stone, TAMER (2008 primary paper)](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~bradknox/papers/icdl08-knox.pdf); [Warnell et al., Deep TAMER (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.10163). Record these as established protocol and feedback-learning antecedents, not architecture candidates or novel hybrids.

An independent read-only scan found QPT/QSIM as the only substantial old-architecture coverage gap; the lead verified Forbus's 1984 MIT report, Kuipers's 1986 formal source, the QDE-learning survey and Qoph/GP successors, and a 2025 QSIM monitoring application. AR-114 records it as an alive, narrow symbolic dynamics/diagnosis family whose limits are abstraction, representation acquisition and spurious branching rather than hardware. **AR-114 adversarial correction.** An independent reviewer confirmed the source interpretation and tightened the proposed evaluation. QSIM's guarantee is one-sided coverage for correctly specified QDEs, not probability calibration; Qoph supports noisy data and unmeasured intermediate variables, not arbitrary missing sensors or gaps. The oracle-QDE arm is only a coverage ceiling, and raw QSIM branch count must not be compared to finite GP posterior samples. The revised protocol aligns event alphabets/horizons, calibrates a specified numeric posterior/interval baseline, matches observed variables and grammar, and labels finite-audit branches “unwitnessed” unless unrealizability is proven. Q2/Q3 and adaptive quantitative refinement already exist in the QSIM lineage. This correction changes the benchmark design only; AR-114 remains archaeology and no architecture/hybrid candidate is promoted. No GPU or experiment ran.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — saturation theorem proving (AR-115; OTTER/E lineage)

**Original computation.** Saturation provers turn a conjecture and axioms into clauses, maintain processed and unprocessed clause sets, select a given clause, derive consequences by resolution/paramodulation and related rules, then simplify, subsume or discard redundant clauses. The cycle seeks the empty clause or stops at a resource bound. Its state is explicit symbolic clauses and indexed terms; its repeated operation is inference plus heuristic search. There is no learned representation or training mechanism in classic OTTER. Useful outputs are machine-checkable proofs or failure within a search budget; applications include formal mathematics, verification and reasoning over axioms. [McCune, OTTER 3.3 Reference Manual (primary system manual)](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0310056).

**Was it bad or early?** The mechanism was useful on 1980s/90s hardware and remains a strong exact reasoner, but proof search can grow combinatorially. Faster processors and memory help throughput, indexing, term rewriting and larger search budgets; they do not remove the search explosion or guarantee that a useful clause is selected. The modern neural revival is already direct: Loos et al. train networks on proof traces to guide E's processed-clause selection; ENIGMA learns clause ranking in E; TRAIL represents the prover state and inference choices as an RL policy; a 2025 study trains efficient clause selection inside Vampire. Neural evaluation can itself cost latency, so the scoring speed must be measured against the inferences it saves. [Loos et al. (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06972); [ENIGMA (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06532); [TRAIL (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.03906); [Suda (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07792).

**Novelty / hybrid disposition.** This is a mature symbolic search method, not a new general learning architecture; learned clause selection and RL guidance are occupied. A generic neural-controller-plus-saturation-prover is rejected (0/5 novelty). No surviving unexplored mechanism is identified here. Retain as an archaeology case showing that modern compute and learned control can improve a useful old algorithm without turning it into a distinct broad model class.

**Small falsifiable prototype.** On a small public first-order benchmark slice, compare a fixed classical given-clause schedule with a compact learned ranker trained only on disjoint proof traces. Hold prover, inference rules and wall-clock budget constant; measure proof rate, inferences, peak RAM and per-selection latency. Falsify practical utility if reduced inferences do not improve proof rate or time after scoring overhead. This tests learned-guidance value, not novelty. CPU is sufficient; no experiment was run.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — Warren Abstract Machine (AR-116; execution substrate near miss)

**Original computation.** Warren's 1983 abstract Prolog instruction set specifies memory areas, registers and instructions for term construction/unification, calls, choice points and backtracking. The engine can be compiled to native machine code, interpreted as bytecode, implemented in firmware/microcode, or mapped to a dedicated processor. Facts/rules remain program data; the WAM is the execution state and control substrate, not a learned knowledge model. Its output is the bindings or failure yielded by Prolog execution. [Warren, *An Abstract Prolog Instruction Set* (SRI primary report)](https://www.sri.com/publication/cyber-formal-methods-pubs/an-abstract-prolog-instruction-set/); [report PDF](https://www.sri.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/641.pdf).

**Was it bad or early?** It was partly motivated by a hardware-performance problem: Prolog's unification and reversible search were expensive on general-purpose machines. Warren explicitly considered bytecode, VAX microcode, firmware and a special Prolog processor. Modern compilers and CPUs make efficient WAM-like software execution practical; they improve constant factors, while large search trees and the difficulty of authoring/maintaining symbolic programs remain. This was primarily a successful runtime/compiler design rather than a discarded general AI architecture.

**Novelty / disposition.** The exact WAM instruction/memory organization is established and widely taught; a WAM-inspired accelerator is a processor design, not a broad model class. The 1983 report and historical archive make the hardware story explicit. [SRI report](https://www.sri.com/publication/cyber-formal-methods-pubs/an-abstract-prolog-instruction-set/); [Software Preservation Group Prolog archive](https://www.softwarepreservation.org/projects/prolog/index.html). No architecture candidate or hybrid is promoted (0/5). A modern WAM is worth using as a symbolic execution baseline, not as a new learning system.

**Small falsifiable revival test.** If a concrete symbolic workload appears, benchmark a maintained WAM compiler/interpreter against a simple tree-walking Prolog interpreter and a general-purpose logic engine on unification-heavy, recursive and backtracking-heavy programs. Match semantics and report throughput, memory and engineering cost. This can test the hardware/runtime lesson but does not support a broad AI-architecture novelty claim. No experiment was run.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — Graphplan (AR-117; planning/search near miss)

**Original computation.** Graphplan grows alternating proposition and action layers from an initial state, annotating fact/action pairs that are mutually exclusive (mutex). Once goal facts appear without mutex, it searches backward through the graph for a shortest partial-order plan. It represents actions, facts, preconditions/effects and pairwise incompatibility; the repeated operations are layer expansion, mutex propagation and backward extraction. Classic Graphplan does not learn: rules and initial state are given, and inference is deterministic apart from search choices. It outputs an executable plan or reports no plan at a reached horizon. [Blum & Furst, *Fast Planning Through Planning Graph Analysis* (1997)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0004370296000471); [authors' Graphplan page](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~avrim/graphplan.html).

**Was it bad or early?** The planning graph is compact and mutex propagation prunes search, but extraction remains combinatorial and grounded action spaces can be large. More memory and compute help graph construction and search, but do not solve poor domain encodings or worst-case complexity. The approach was modernized directly: Blackbox converts the Graphplan structure and mutex constraints to SAT, performs general SAT simplification, then uses SAT solvers; learned neural heuristics for classical planning are also established. Thus a mutex graph coupled to learned search is not by itself an open hybrid. [Kautz & Selman, Blackbox (1999 primary paper)](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/selman/papers/pdf/99.ijcai.blackbox.pdf); [Liu et al., learned search-space-specific planning heuristics (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04019); [Liu et al., neural search policies (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.12200).

**Novelty / disposition.** Graphplan is a distinct planning algorithm, not a general learned model class, and its most obvious SAT hybrid and learned heuristic extensions are prior art. Reject as a new architecture candidate (0/5). A residual empirical question could compare its compact graph/mutex pruning with SAT or neural heuristic search on domains with strong pairwise exclusions, but that is planner benchmarking, not architecture discovery.

**Small falsifiable revival test.** On a fixed STRIPS benchmark subset enriched for pairwise mutex structure, compare original Graphplan, Blackbox-style graph-to-SAT and a modern learned-heuristic planner under matched hardware/time limits. Report solved instances, plan length, expansion count, memory and preprocessing cost. Falsify a Graphplan-specific advantage if mutex-rich cases do not yield lower total search cost after graph construction. CPU only; no experiment was run.

Learned theorem-prover guidance is direct prior art from proof-trace ranking through RL and efficient clause scoring; WAM is a mature logic-language runtime; Graphplan's mutex graph was explicitly coupled to SAT by Blackbox and learned planning heuristics are established. These entries close catalog gaps and reject generic learned-search hybrids without promoting candidates. No code or experiment ran. #### Control-theory archaeology — set-valued reachability state (AR-118; established representation, not a new model class)

**What it computes.** Instead of carrying one estimated state or a sampled posterior, set propagation carries a compact region of possible states (for example, an interval box, polytope, zonotope or bundle). Each update applies the dynamics to the full region, adds admissible inputs/model error and can intersect with an observation constraint. The output is a guaranteed overapproximation of what the system could reach, supporting bounds and safety checks. Set propagation is a mature method for continuous and hybrid systems, with applications in verification, controller synthesis and estimation. [Althoff, Frehse & Girard, *Set Propagation Techniques for Reachability Analysis* (2021 survey)](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-control-071420-081941).

**Was it bad or early?** This family is not mainly waiting for modern neural compute: its central limits are conservative set growth, nonlinear overapproximation, representation choice, and dependence on a dynamics model. CPUs and GPUs accelerate matrix and set operations, but a faster loose bound may remain useless for decision-making. Learning the dynamics from data was already coupled directly to set propagation in matrix-zonotope methods: Alanwar et al. derive guaranteed reachable-set overapproximations for unknown linear systems from noisy data and extend the method to nonlinear systems (2021). Neural-network verification also now uses reachability/abstract interpretation and projection-based latent set representations; this is adjacent verification rather than proof that latent set propagation solves general state estimation. [Alanwar et al. (2021, primary paper)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v144/alanwar21a.html); [Blaas et al., ICLR 2026, latent-space sets for neural verification](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/14bb27f680bee45d83bc769738e7f9b5-Abstract-Conference.html).

**Architecture/hybrid audit.** A state unit could store a generator matrix and bounded coefficients; communication is set-valued transition, Minkowski addition, constraint intersection and occasional reduction/merging. Knowledge lies partly in learned dynamics parameters and partly in the current set. Learning can fit transition parameters while preserving a coverage condition; inference propagates sets. Data needs include trajectories and defensible noise/input bounds. This can help safety-critical robotics and diagnosis when false-safe predictions matter more than sharp point estimates. However, learned dynamics plus matrix-zonotope reachability already directly couples learning and set propagation. Calling a general set-valued observer a new architecture or a learned-model × zonotope hybrid is not justified (0/5 broad novelty). The unclosed practical question is whether learned nonlinear transition sets stay tight enough under partial observation and long horizons for a particular application.

**Small falsifiable prototype.** Generate low-dimensional partially observed switched-linear systems with known disturbances and bounded measurement noise. Fit dynamics from a fixed training trajectory budget; compare data-driven zonotope propagation, an interval observer and an ensemble of learned point dynamics at equal CPU time. Measure empirical state-set coverage, set volume/width, false-safe rate, and runtime across held-out regimes and horizon. Falsify the utility claim if near-complete coverage requires bounds too broad to distinguish safe from unsafe states, or if learned reachability is no sharper/faster than the observer. CPU-only is sufficient; the executed CPU smoke probe is recorded below. **Disposition:** retain as a robust-control representation and baseline, not a new broad AI class.

#### Hybrid audit — learned dynamics × guaranteed set propagation (HY-102; reject as already coupled)

**Coupling and proposed behavior.** The tempting hybrid would learn unknown dynamics from data while carrying a set of all transition models consistent with observations, then propagate state sets through that model set to return reachable bounds. The learned component contributes adaptation to unknown physics; zonotopes contribute explicit uncertainty coverage and safety-relevant bounds. Their interaction yields a family of reachable trajectories rather than a point rollout. This is a meaningful coupling, but Alanwar et al. (2021) already introduce data-driven reachability for unknown systems using matrix zonotopes, with guarantees for linear and extensions for nonlinear dynamics. The broad interaction is occupied, not merely adjacent. [Primary paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v144/alanwar21a.html).

**Verdict and test boundary.** Reject the hybrid as a novel architecture. Any remaining work should be application-specific: compare tightness, coverage and runtime for a new observation regime or nonlinear model class, clearly distinguishing a new algorithmic guarantee from applying known set propagation. The CPU falsifier is the AR-118 protocol; no new experiment was run and no candidate ID is warranted.

#### Computational-biology near miss — Cellular Potts / Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg (AR-119)

**Original mechanism and historical limit.** The Cellular Potts Model extends a large-Q lattice Potts system so one persistent cell identity can occupy many lattice sites. A local copy proposal changes the lattice; an adhesion/volume/perimeter energy difference and stochastic acceptance govern the update. Sorting and tissue-scale patterns emerge from cell-level interactions. It represents cell identity and local interfaces, updates them through stochastic energy-based dynamics, and outputs tissue morphology. The seminal 1992 paper demonstrated sorting driven by differential adhesivity. [Graner & Glazier, *Simulation of Biological Cell Sorting Using a Two-Dimensional Extended Potts Model* (1992 primary paper)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2013).

The original method was already runnable on 1990s hardware; it was slow for large tissue-scale simulation, not unable to implement its core mechanism. That compute limit has been addressed directly: a 2011 GPU implementation reported roughly 80× speedup over serial and 3D lattices up to 256³; a 2023 GPU method reports 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speedup while preserving local update statistics and simulating millions of cells. [Tapia & D'Souza, GPU parallelization (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpc.2010.12.011); [Sultan et al., tissue-scale parallel CPM (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09317).

**Novelty / disposition.** CPM is a useful stochastic tissue simulator and its cell-identity representation is more expressive than a basic one-site-per-cell cellular automaton. It does not supply perception, general task semantics or a general learning rule; parameters and biological terms are supplied or fitted for specific domains. The current GPU era has revived its intended simulation scale, but does not convert it into a broadly useful AI model class. Nearby notebook coverage of amorphous computing and reaction chemistry does not make the CPM a new class. Reject as a general architecture candidate (0/5); keep as a simulator if a biological prediction task calls for it.

**Small falsifiable domain test.** Given microscopy-derived initial tissues and a fixed parameter-fitting budget, fit a CPM on a subset of cell-sorting trajectories and predict held-out cell rearrangement and morphology. Compare a non-CPM object/cell-based simulator on held-out geometry and time points. Falsify CPM utility if behavior requires manually encoding the target outcome, or held-out prediction does not improve at matched runtime and calibration. No experiment was run.

A non-neural primitive scan added set-valued reachability as a missing representational family and Cellular Potts as a computational-biology near miss. Reachable-set propagation is established in control/verification; learning unknown dynamics through matrix-zonotope reachability is direct prior art, so HY-102 rejects a generic learning × guaranteed-set coupling. Cellular Potts is an established cell-identity lattice simulator, and direct GPU implementations have already removed much of its scale bottleneck. Neither is promoted as a general architecture; AR-118 retains a narrow safety/coverage benchmark question, AR-119 is relevant only to tissue simulation. #### AR-118 CPU smoke experiment — zonotopes retain correlation better than interval boxes on a known linear system (2026-09-27)

**Question.** On a small linear system with bounded disturbances, does a correlated set representation avoid some of the geometric inflation caused by axis-aligned interval propagation while retaining coverage? This is an expected property of zonotopes, not a new architecture claim.

**Setup.** CPU-only NumPy, fixed seed 118, 50,000 Monte Carlo trajectories, 12 steps. Dynamics were x[t+1] = A x[t] + w[t], with A = [[1, 0.7], [0, 1]], initial uncertainty represented by independent generators diag(1, 0.25), and each disturbance coordinate bounded by ±0.02. Propagated the exact linear zonotope without generator reduction and its enclosing interval box. Exact 2D zonotope area was computed from generator pairwise determinants; box area from propagated coordinate radii. The interval box was checked against all sampled trajectories. Sample coverage for the zonotope follows by construction because each trajectory uses coefficients inside the same generator bounds; no independent membership solver was run.

| Horizon | Zonotope area | Interval-box area | Box / zonotope area | Sampled trajectories in interval box | Zonotope generators |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.115600 | 1.290600 | 1.157× | 100% | 4 |
| 4 | 1.576800 | 2.460480 | 1.560× | 100% | 10 |
| 8 | 2.500480 | 4.841280 | 1.936× | 100% | 18 |
| 12 | 3.842720 | 8.357440 | 2.175× | 100% | 26 |

**Interpretation and limitations.** In this deliberately favorable correlated linear case, the zonotope's exact area was about 64% of the interval box at step 4 and 46% at step 12 (2.175× smaller box-to-zonotope ratio), while the box contained every sampled path. This validates only the geometric point that preserving correlations can yield tighter reachable sets than coordinatewise intervals. It does not test unknown dynamics, nonlinearities, switching uncertainty, partial observations, safety decisions, or comparison with other set representations; generator count grows linearly here and can become costly under nonlinear propagation or reduction. No result files were created.

**Resource record.** Runtime approximately 1.4 s for the CPU command; 50,000 trajectories × 12 transitions. CPU only, peak VRAM 0 GB, CUDA not initialized. No GPU processes were inspected or touched because no GPU experiment was planned; live occupancy/Claude sharing remain unknown. Only `Codex_Research.md` was edited. **Disposition unchanged:** useful baseline evidence, zero broad architecture novelty.

#### Oscillatory relaxation archaeology — oscillator Ising machines (AR-120; 1990s–2026)

**Original computation and representation.** Early phase-locked-loop neural networks stored and recalled oscillatory patterns as phase-locked attractors. Oscillator-based Ising machines later used coupled self-sustaining oscillators for combinatorial optimization: an oscillator phase near 0 or π encodes a binary spin; programmable couplings encode a weighted graph/QUBO; subharmonic injection locking (SHIL) encourages binarization. In studied symmetric coupling regimes, a Lyapunov function is related to the Ising Hamiltonian. Noise injection and a gradual SHIL schedule can help trajectories escape some shallow minima before settling. Output is a low-energy spin assignment, not a general perceptual or language representation. [Hoppensteadt & Izhikevich, PLL neural network (2000 primary paper)](https://www.izhikevich.org/publications/pllnn.pdf); [Wang & Roychowdhury, OIM (2019 primary paper)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07163).

**Unit, operations, learning and memory.** The unit is a phase oscillator. Units communicate through weighted phase couplings; a digital simulation integrates phase equations, while physical devices use analog coupling elements and SHIL. Repeated inference is coupled phase relaxation under a fixed problem Hamiltonian. The original OIM solver uses couplings specified by the optimization instance; it has no general dataset-driven learning rule. A 2026 neural-memory paper changes the learning setup: it connects equilibrium stability to Hamiltonian energy and uses Hamiltonian-regularized eigenvalue contrastive updates (HRECM) to make desired 0/π equilibria stable attractors. This is direct learned-coupling prior art, but the paper reports numerical validation rather than a physical online learning demonstration. [Cheng & Lin, *Training oscillator Ising machines to assign the dynamic stability of their equilibrium points* (Phys. Rev. E 2026)](https://doi.org/10.1103/h63g-kfnp).

**Was it bad or early?** The primitive was implementable before GPUs: 2019 CMOS electronic prototypes supported programmable couplings up to 240 spins. Historical friction was analog device and programmable-interconnect control, phase calibration and measurement. Current devices improve fabrication, calibration and simulation, but current hardware analyses still report quadratic coupling and weight-memory requirements for fully connected networks. A GPU can simulate phases and train couplings, but does not guarantee physical energy/latency advantage or remove nonconvex optimization difficulty. [Wang, Wu & Roychowdhury (2019 hardware prototypes)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10211); [oscillator-computing review (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44335-024-00015-z); [digital ONN coupling-scaling analysis (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20680).

**Closest work, distinction and verdict.** Phase-coded binding in AR-09/SHRUTI and PCNN synchronization in AR-45 use coherence to bind/group features; OIM instead treats phase as the binary optimization state and physical relaxation as search. This is an omitted family distinction, not novelty: PLL associative memory, physical oscillator Ising machines, learned oscillatory networks and 2026 HRECM already occupy the mechanisms. Potential niches are optimization instances that map efficiently to sparse analog couplings, or associative memory with a clear phase-attractor advantage. Failures include local minima, annealing sensitivity, encoding/programming/readout cost, analog mismatch, and O(N²) couplers for dense graphs. Broad architecture novelty: **0/5**. No candidate is promoted.

**Small falsifiable prototype.** CPU-only simulate N=16–32 phase oscillators on associative patterns. Compare Hebbian Hopfield, random/untrained OIM, and HRECM-trained OIM; match pattern count, coupling norm, update budget and cue corruption. Measure recall, stable/spurious attractors, basin size, phase/coupling perturbation sensitivity and ODE evaluations. Falsify utility if HRECM does not enlarge correct basins at equal coupling budget, or gains disappear under simulated device perturbations. This is a reproduction/robustness study, not a novelty test; no experiment ran.

#### Hybrid audit — oscillator Ising relaxation × stability-contrastive coupling learning (HY-103; direct 2026 prior art)

OIM contributes continuous phase relaxation with binary 0/π equilibria and a Lyapunov/Ising-energy relation. HRECM contributes a training objective that adjusts coupling weights according to equilibrium stability: the 2026 paper connects equilibrium eigenvalues with Hamiltonian energy, then uses a contrastive eigenvalue loss with Hamiltonian regularization to stabilize target patterns. This changes coupling learning and memory inference, rather than merely placing a classifier beside an oscillator solver. Cheng & Lin already publish the interaction, with numerical validation, so reject as a new hybrid. Likely advantages are larger retrieval basins shaped by stability; failures include noisy eigenvalue estimates, spurious equilibria, local minima, mismatch between simulated energy and hardware noise, and quadratic coupling cost. [Primary PRE paper](https://doi.org/10.1103/h63g-kfnp). The AR-120 CPU protocol is a possible reproduction; no separate experiment or candidate ID is warranted.

#### Hybrid collision audit — Rete partial joins × learned probabilistic predicates (HY-104; systems method, no new model class)

**Coupling.** Rete retains partial matches for rule conditions and propagates changes through affected joins. Neural/probabilistic predicates could emit weighted facts from an image or stream; changed facts update rule matches and derivations, while gradients follow provenance to the predicates. This would alter inference scheduling and credit assignment by reusing partial rule state under sparse updates. It could suit streaming scene understanding or monitoring.

**Prior art and disposition.** Neural Datalog Through Time creates time-varying neural states for derived facts from Datalog provenance; differentiable change semantics for recursive Datalog derive how query outputs update under input changes. Combined with Rete’s original incremental matching, these occupy the central mechanisms. The exact execution-engine implementation with learned soft predicates may remain a systems comparison, not a general architecture (0/5). [Forgy, Rete (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(82)90020-0); [Mei et al., Neural Datalog Through Time (ICML 2020)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/mei20a.html); [Alvarez-Picallo et al., incremental recursive Datalog semantics (ESOP 2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06069).

**Cheap falsifier.** On a synthetic streaming scene graph with hundreds of facts and depth-2–4 rules, compare full differentiable reevaluation with persistent partial-match/delta propagation for 1%, 10%, and 50% fact changes per update. Check identical outputs and input gradients; measure latency, memory, join fanout, deletion and negation costs. Falsify the execution benefit if updates become dense, cached joins erase speedups, or a changed predicate forces a near-global rebuild. CPU only; no experiment ran.

#### Hybrid collision audit — heteroclinic sequence memory × differentiable transition learning (HY-105; broad coupling occupied)

A modernization might represent event state by metastable saddles and dwell time, then learn transition stability/topology from observed sequences. This would change transition memory and adaptation, not just add an RNN readout. The broad learning direction is occupied: Seliger et al. learned sequence projection/competition matrices in winnerless-competition networks; Voit & Meyer-Ortmanns (2019) infer heteroclinic topology and eigenvalues from trajectories by adapting a template; later sequence-recognition and robot motor-motif work add Bayesian inference or online coupling rewiring. Gradient tuning of the same transition dynamics is an optimizer choice, not a distinct model class. [Seliger et al. (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.67.011905); [Voit & Meyer-Ortmanns (2019)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fams.2019.00063); [Kiebel et al. (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000464); [Calvo Tapia et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.97.052308). Reject the broad hybrid and cross-reference HY-52/AR-37. A CPU benchmark could compare dwell-time extrapolation and route retention against a GRU on variable-duration branching sequences; falsify any useful claim if it needs a hand-built state graph or loses transfer after online transition insertion. No experiment ran.

#### Truth-maintenance archaeology correction — JTMS versus ATMS, modern alternatives, and label-size limits (C029/C020 cross-reference)

The existing TMS notes establish prior art for learned dependency validity, but the JTMS/ATMS distinction deserves a compact record. Doyle’s justification-based TMS (JTMS/TMS) maintains one current belief context: each datum carries justifications and an IN/OUT status, so retracted support invalidates dependent beliefs and contradictions can trigger dependency-directed backtracking to responsible assumptions. It was motivated by problem solvers that must act under incomplete information, later revise assumptions, and explain why beliefs or actions were supported. [Doyle, IJCAI 1977 primary paper](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/77-1/Papers/035.pdf); [Doyle, *A Truth Maintenance System* (1979)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(79)90008-0).

De Kleer’s assumption-based TMS (ATMS) changes the unit of maintenance: instead of choosing one context and backtracking among alternatives, it labels each derived node with minimal consistent sets of assumptions under which it follows. Justification antecedent labels combine by set-union/product; alternative justifications add environments; nogood-containing environments and nonminimal supersets are removed. This compiles shared derivations across many contexts, which can be effective if many alternatives will be examined. It can lose to ordinary propagation/backtracking when only one context or solution matters; de Kleer’s own analysis describes this workload dependence. [de Kleer, *An Assumption-Based TMS* (1986)](https://dekleer.org/Publications/An%20Assumption-Based%20TMS.pdf); [de Kleer, *Problem Solving with the ATMS* (1986)](https://dekleer.org/Publications/Problem%20Solving%20with%20the%20ATMS.pdf).

**Structural limits and modern alternatives.** A node may have exponentially many minimal supporting environments, so required output can itself use exponential time and space. This is not just an underpowered-Lisp problem. CATMS (1991) explicitly compresses labels to address explosions, trading label propagation for assumption-closure work. Elkan’s 1990 analysis contrasts ATMS exponential worst-case behavior with linear per-query Boolean-constraint-propagation TMS, while noting that precomputed labels can win when labels are small and queried often; nonmonotonic TMS inference is NP-complete. Darwiche’s d-DNNF compilation supports literal assertion, retraction and flipping and implements complete TMS/belief revision in tractable time for compiled bounded-structure theories; compilation itself may still grow exponentially. Incremental SAT solvers instead retain a base formula and learned clauses while testing contexts under temporary assumption literals; conflicts can identify a sufficient subset of assumptions without eagerly materializing every minimal support. This is a different update/explanation trade-off, not a way around worst-case combinatorics. [CATMS (1991 primary paper)](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/1991/AAAI91-044.pdf); [Elkan, *Truth Maintenance* (AAAI 1990)](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/1990/AAAI90-164.pdf); [Darwiche, d-DNNF and TMS (2000)](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0003044); [MiniSat incremental solver paper](https://minisat.se/downloads/MiniSat.pdf); [incremental SAT proof certification (LPAR 2024)](https://kfazekas.github.io/papers/FazekasPollittFleuryBiere-LPAR24.pdf).

**Verdict and bounded CPU probe.** JTMS and ATMS are useful, distinct symbolic architectures, but both are mature; SAT, d-DNNF and incremental dataflow occupy much of the repeated belief-update task. Do not reopen C020/C029 as a new model class. If a workload requires many alternative explanations, test k independent pairs of assumptions a_i/b_i, derive x_i from either and q from all x_i. The ATMS label for q has 2^k minimal environments, while the factored Boolean representation AND_i(a_i OR b_i) remains compact. Compare exact ATMS propagation against d-DNNF and incremental SAT for repeated context queries and assumption changes; measure label count, memory, preprocessing and update/query latency against exhaustive truth tables at small k. Falsify an ATMS revival claim if label expansion dominates before repeated-query amortization or factored alternatives preserve exact answers at lower total cost. No code or experiment ran.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — active inference as a perception/action architecture (AR-122; established framework, not a new class)

**What it computes.** An active-inference agent maintains a generative model relating hidden states, actions and observations. Perception updates a posterior over hidden states and model parameters to reduce variational free energy; action either changes sensory input to reduce current prediction error or selects policies by expected free energy. In discrete-state formulations, expected free energy trades off preferred outcomes (pragmatic value) and expected information gain (epistemic value). Thus action and sensing arise within the same probabilistic inference loop, with learned memory in the generative model and posterior sufficient statistics. Early implementations used small hand-specified state spaces; later continuous and deep variants learn latent state representations from high-dimensional observations. [Friston, Daunizeau & Kiebel, mountain-car demonstration (2009)](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0006421); [Friston et al., active inference and epistemic value (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1080/17588928.2015.1020053); [Friston, Parr & de Vries, graphical belief propagation (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1162/NETN_a_00018).

**Was it bad or early?** The 2009 demonstration used low-dimensional, structured dynamics and a hand-defined desired-state distribution. Deep generative models and GPUs later made image inputs and larger learned state spaces more feasible: a 2020 study learned representations end-to-end from camera frames and demonstrated deep active inference for robot navigation. Robotics reviews document applications to state estimation, planning and control. This resolves part of the old perception bottleneck, not the need to choose a generative-model structure, priors/preferences, policy horizon, and approximation scheme. Candidate-policy enumeration can grow exponentially with action horizon; approximate inference can be brittle or costly; poor prior preferences can encode a poor objective. The 2009 paper itself frames its mountain-car result as a proof of concept and discusses how the desired equilibrium density constrains the apparent objective-free formulation. [Çatal et al., deep active inference (2020 workshop paper)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.03220); [Lanillos et al., robotics and artificial-agent survey (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01871).

**Use and closest prior art.** The framework is useful for partially observed robotics, active sensing, exploration and cognitive modeling when information gain and goal preferences should be represented explicitly. Its strongest potential advantage is one shared belief-update and action-selection model that can seek informative observations while pursuing preferred outcomes. It is closely related to Bayesian model-based RL, POMDP planning, Bayesian experimental design, control-as-inference and predictive coding. Active inference is already a substantial established theory/framework, not an abandoned model awaiting modern hardware. Its distinctive objective and message-passing interpretation are known; novelty confidence as a new broad model class: **0/5**. AR-78’s predictive-coding coverage overlaps with the neural-inference mechanism, but does not replace this separate agent-level description.

**Small falsifiable revival test (CPU, not run).** Use a partially observed T-maze with an uncertain cue and a hidden transition reversal. Compare an expected-free-energy policy, an otherwise identical Bayesian planner with the epistemic term removed, a matched information-gain bonus planner, and an exact small-POMDP oracle. Share the same generative model, prior preferences, policy horizon, observations and computation budget. Measure successes after reversal, trials needed to identify the changed transition, belief calibration, action count and inference cost. Any claim of a distinct practical benefit fails if expected-free-energy selection does not improve adaptation or compute over the matched Bayesian information-bonus baseline, or if gains depend on hand-tuning preferences to the test outcome.

#### Hybrid collision audit — deep generative perception × active inference (HY-107; direct prior art)

Deep generative perception can encode camera observations into latent beliefs; active inference can use those beliefs to choose sensing/action policies by expected free energy. That coupling changes the input representation and enables active control from image observations. It is already directly demonstrated by Çatal et al. (2020), with continuous/robotic active-inference variants and predictive-coding hybrids nearby. The combination may be useful for embodied control, but it is not a novel architecture class. Risks include learned latent-model errors, costly policy evaluation, sensitivity to prior preferences, and weak comparisons against matched model-based RL. Reject the generic hybrid (0/5); the AR-122 T-maze experiment only tests the claimed action-selection advantage, not hybrid novelty.

#### Fuzzy cognitive-map source correction — nonlinear edges and delays predate KA-FCM; FRM is a narrow bipartite variant (AR-77 addendum)

The AR-77 wording that KA-FCM answers the old monotonic-edge limitation was too broad. Kosko’s 1988 primary paper already describes differential-Hebbian updates that correlate time derivatives of node outputs, alongside signed feedback graphs and nonlinear node activations. Hagiwara’s Extended FCM (1994) explicitly adds nonlinear causal relationships, time-delay weights, and conditional weights; Carvalho and Tomé’s 1999 Rule-Based FCMs represent non-monotonic causal relations with fuzzy rules and a fuzzy carry-accumulation operator. The modern KA-FCM contribution is more specific: placing learned univariate B-spline functions on edges as its causal-transmission parameterization. Its current record is IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems 34(6), 1884–1892 (2026), not an unpublished preprint. Broad nonlinear FCM edges and delay modeling are old prior art; spline-edge parameterization is the narrow modern mechanism. [Kosko (1988 primary paper)](https://sipi.usc.edu/~kosko/HiddenPatterns.pdf); [Hagiwara, Extended FCM (1994)](https://doi.org/10.1541/ieejeiss1987.114.3_367); [Carvalho & Tomé, Rule-Based FCM (1999)](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=01b8b56a84edb0307ce22573eec7fedde06e6fdf&repid=rep1&type=pdf); [Salmeron, KA-FCM (IEEE TFS 2026)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TFUZZ.2026.3680681); [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05136).

Fuzzy Relational Maps (FRMs), described by Kandasamy and Sultana around 2000 and in the authors’ 2004 book, are a related but narrower construction: concept nodes are divided into disjoint domain and range sets, and a rectangular bipartite relation propagates between them without within-side links. This can encode a known cause/effect partition compactly, but it is a topology restriction and specialist interpretable model, not a new general learner. A useful optional CPU comparison would test FRM against same-budget unrestricted FCM on genuinely bipartite synthetic systems and then on systems with within-side edges/confounding; a gain that vanishes outside the assumed partition is just inductive-bias matching. No experiment was run. [Kandasamy & Smarandache, author-hosted FRM book (2004)](https://fs.unm.edu/NRM.pdf); [University of New Mexico record](https://digitalrepository.unm.edu/math_fsp/150/).

#### Old-architecture archaeology — hierarchical task-network planning (AR-121; established planning architecture)

**Original mechanism.** HTN planning starts from an initial world state and a task network. Tasks are primitive actions or compound tasks; methods replace a compound task with a partially ordered network of subtasks when method conditions hold. A planner repeatedly selects a task and applicable method, checks ordering/state interactions, and expands until only executable primitive actions remain. The result is constrained by both world-state operators and the supplied task hierarchy. Domain methods encode reusable procedural knowledge about how a task may be accomplished. ABSTRIPS (1974) is an early related abstraction hierarchy; NOAH and later HTN systems develop decompositional planning, while Erol, Hendler and Nau formalize a sound and complete procedure (UMCP) in 1994. [Sacerdoti, ABSTRIPS (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(74)90026-5); [Erol, Hendler & Nau, UMCP (1994)](https://www.aaai.org/Papers/AIPS/1994/AIPS94-042.pdf); [Bercher, Alford & Höller, hierarchical-planning survey (IJCAI 2019)](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/2019/875).

**Was it bad or early?** HTN planners were already practical on pre-deep-learning hardware; SHOP2 earned a distinguished-performance award at the 2002 International Planning Competition. The persistent trade-off is knowledge engineering and search completeness: useful methods can make search efficient by specifying structured task decompositions, while incomplete or over-restrictive methods can hide valid plans. Broader HTN formalisms have high worst-case complexity, and method branching can still explode. Modern CPUs, RAM and GPUs accelerate search and trace processing, but do not supply correct task vocabularies, method preconditions, or hierarchies that transfer across domains. The 2019 survey emphasizes that hierarchical planning contains distinct formalisms with different expressivity and complexity, so comparisons must name the precise formalism. [Nau et al., SHOP2 (JAIR 2003)](https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.1141); [Bercher et al. (2019)](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/2019/875).

**Modernization and closest work.** HTN is still actively researched. HTN-MAKER learns methods from classical planning problems, solution plans and annotated tasks; HDL learns from expert plan traces; Word2HTN uses semantic vectors to group plan atoms while inducing hierarchies; later work learns methods from landmarks, repairs incomplete methods, and uses MCTS or domain-independent heuristics to select decompositions. Recent work also connects language-model heuristics or proposed decompositions to HTN. These results directly occupy generic “use modern learning to acquire or select HTN methods.” LLM-generated methods may reduce authoring calls, but transfer and correctness still depend on formal preconditions, grounding and downstream plan validation. [HTN-MAKER (AAAI 2008)](https://www.cse.lehigh.edu/~munoz/Publications/AAAI08.pdf); [HDL (ICAPS 2006)](https://www.aiinternational.org/Library/ICAPS/2006/icaps06-048.php); [Word2HTN (2018)](https://doi.org/10.3233/AIC-180756); [learning/refining HTN methods (AAAI 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i06.6557); [MCTS-guided HTN (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2021.107067); [HTN planning with LLM-generated heuristics (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07707); [online learning of HTN methods with LLM planning (2025 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12901).

**Use, limitation and novelty.** HTN is useful in robotics, workflow execution and planning assistance when experts can supply reliable task recipes and outputs must respect procedural constraints. Its strongest potential advantage is search guidance and interpretable decomposition. Main weaknesses are authoring cost, hierarchy/vocabulary mismatch, method incompleteness, poor transfer, and potentially expensive branching. HTN itself is mature and is not a general data-trained perception/reasoning architecture. A generic “learned decomposition policy × HTN planner” is also occupied by method learning, learned heuristic selection, MCTS and recent language-guided variants. Broad novelty: **0/5**. Retain it as a planner baseline and an example where modern compute cannot erase the knowledge-acquisition bottleneck.

**Small falsifiable revival test (CPU, not run).** Use two small domains with compositional task shift, such as logistics and blocks world. Compare hand-authored HTN, trace-learned methods, a current heuristic- or MCTS-guided HTN, and a classical planner under equal state expansions and training-plan budgets. Hold out new combinations of familiar subtasks and one changed precondition. Measure valid-plan rate, plan length, expansions, method count, annotation/authoring time, and recovery after execution failure. The claim that modern learning reduces the old knowledge burden fails if learned methods need near-complete hand annotations, fail on held-out compositions, or cost more to validate than the search they save.

#### Hybrid collision audit — learned decomposition and method scheduling inside HTN (HY-106; broad coupling occupied)

The proposed interaction would use execution outcomes to revise method preconditions and choose among decompositions online, while retaining explicit task structure for constraint-respecting plans. This changes planner search and method memory, but it is not an unexplored bridge: HTN-MAKER and HDL learn methods from plans, later methods refine incomplete hierarchies, SHOP-h/MCTS select decompositions using heuristics or search, and 2025–2026 work already connects online method learning and language-model heuristics to HTN. A new optimizer or learned score is not a new architecture. Potential advantages are reduced method-authoring effort and lower search; failures include invalid or over-generalized methods, distribution shift, costly validation and language-model latency. Reject as broad novelty (0/5); only consider a domain-specific controlled comparison if autonomous skill acquisition is the target. The AR-121 experiment is sufficient to falsify the generic utility claim; no second experiment is scheduled.

#### Reversible structural commitments — transdimensional inference and edit-history reduction (AR-123; no architecture candidate)

**Proposed primitive under audit.** Keep an editable internal graph, schema, or neural topology; propose a discrete split/merge/add/delete/rewrite; store enough information to invert the edit; score the revised representation on later evidence; then commit or restore the prior version. The hoped-for capability is safe structural learning in which an agent can try representation changes without permanently losing earlier competence.

**Prior-art reduction.** The reversible part is not a single new computation:

- If edits sample changing-dimensional model hypotheses and are accepted according to a posterior target, reversible-jump MCMC already gives dimension-matching proposals and reversible transitions between parameter subspaces. This has been applied directly to neural-network size and basis-function count, and to dynamic Bayesian networks with changing hidden and input neurons. [Green, *Reversible jump MCMC* (1995)](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/82.4.711); [Andrieu et al., *RJMCMC Simulated Annealing for Neural Networks*](https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/publications/publication7540-abstract.html); [Sequential RJMCMC for dynamic Bayesian neural networks (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2023.126960).
- If edits enlarge or reshape a trained network while preserving its current function, network morphism and Net2Net already specify such transformations. NEAT and older topology-and-weight evolving networks search structural mutations while retaining alternative genomes in a population; their lineage and mutation records give an ordinary route back to ancestors. [Wei et al., *Network Morphism*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01670); [Chen et al., *Net2Net*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05641); [Stanley & Miikkulainen, NEAT (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1162/106365602320169811).
- If the goal is to undo a deployed edit exactly, versioned snapshots, inverse edit logs, and transactional commit/abort provide the state-management operation. For derived computations, self-adjusting computation records dependencies and reuses unaffected trace regions after input changes; differential dataflow already represents additions and retractions through signed updates. Those systems track and update computation, but they do not learn an architecture. [Acar, Blelloch & Harper, self-adjusting computation](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~guyb/papers/LAB12.pdf); [McSherry et al., Naiad/differential dataflow](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/composable-incremental-and-iterative-data-parallel-computation-with-naiad/).
- If the internal transition itself is required to be bijective, reversible computing and reversible neural blocks apply. They cannot recover information erased by a many-to-one edit unless the edit stores the lost information in an auxiliary trace. An exact undo log can therefore cost as much as retaining the removed state.

**Candidate-standard answers.** The proposed state is a representation graph plus edit metadata; an edit reads selected nodes/edges and validation evidence, writes a candidate graph and inverse record, and executes when a proposal policy selects it. Learning the proposal policy from prediction error or task reward is ordinary search/model selection unless the proposal state or acceptance rule adds another precise operation. Inference then runs the committed graph. Knowledge is in the graph, parameters, and version log. A broad claim that this is absent from attention, recurrence, memory, planning, or search does not survive: explicit editing is a data-structure operation, choosing edits is model search, evaluating edits is validation/inference, and restoring a version is rollback. The pieces do not supply a missing architecture primitive when placed together.

**Verdict.** `USE THE CLASSICAL MACHINE — NOT A NEW ARCHITECTURE`. Record as a cross-cutting reduction for the existing Reversible Scene Editor / Counterfactual Rewrite seeds, C034 reversible traces, and HY-80's residual-to-generator consolidation. HY-80's exact recurrence-triggered policy remains an untested methods question, but its underlying edit, inheritance, and rollback operations are already present in model selection, network morphism, neuroevolution, and version control. Broad novelty **0/5**; hybrid novelty **0/5**. No new C candidate is warranted. No experiment or test was run or prepared under the temporary restriction.

#### Hybrid collision — learned topology proposals × reversible transactional commit (HY-108; component composition)

A prediction-error learner could propose local topology edits, a validation objective could choose among candidates, and a reversible edit log could commit or undo the chosen change. This would couple proposal quality to later outcomes and protect exact restoration, but it does not change the underlying search transition: use informed reversible-jump proposals for posterior model selection, NEAT-style mutation/population search for reward optimization, or network morphisms when function preservation is required; use a transaction log for rollback. These mechanisms optimize different criteria, so the coupling still needs an explicit target distribution or acceptance objective. Without one, “commit when evidence supports it” is underspecified. Likely engineering benefits are lower recomputation and safer online updates; likely failure modes are proposal/search cost, validation leakage, stale inverse records, and logs large enough to eliminate memory savings. Closest prior art is the combination of transdimensional Bayesian neural-network search, dynamic architecture growth, function-preserving transforms, and established rollback/incremental-computation machinery above. Reject as a new hybrid (**0/5**); an application-specific system comparison is possible, but it would not show architecture novelty. No experiment was run.

#### Old-architecture archaeology — persistent visual identity from FINSTs to temporal object slots (AR-124; occupied representation need)

**Original operation.** FINSTs are limited-capacity visual pointers that individuate scene tokens independently of their feature descriptions and follow them as location and appearance change. Object-file accounts separately describe temporary records that retain reference to an individual while accumulating its current and recent features. These ideas distinguish “which entity?” from “what does it look like now?” and predate modern deep learning. [Pylyshyn, *The role of location indexes in spatial perception* (1989)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-0277(89)90014-0); [Kahneman, Treisman & Gibbs, *The reviewing of object files* (1992)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-0285(92)90007-O).

**Historical limit and modernization.** FINST theorized a small number of pointers and did not provide a general learned visual feature system, open-ended entity memory, or a complete algorithm for identity under ambiguous observations. Object-centric deep-learning work supplies learned appearance/state representations and temporal matching. Slot Attention provides entity-like slots; Loci-Looped learns to fuse predicted latent object states with pixel observations and revise them after implausible events; later work explicitly trains temporal consistency; and the 2026 Temporal Slot Activation paper learns per-slot activity that gates both state updates and decoder participation, aiming to prevent an occluded slot from drifting or explaining another visible object. Modern compute and self-supervised video data improve perception and allow larger temporal memories, but identity still depends on evidence that distinguishes competing assignments. [Locatello et al., Slot Attention (NeurIPS 2020)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2020/hash/8511df98c02ab60aea1b2356c013bc0f-Abstract.html); [Traub et al., Loci-Looped (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10372); [Manasyan et al., Slot Contrast (CVPR 2025)](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/papers/Manasyan_Temporally_Consistent_Object-Centric_Learning_by_Contrasting_Slots_CVPR_2025_paper.pdf); [Nguyen et al., Temporal Slot Activation (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13714).

**What is represented and learned.** A tracker maintains entity records with persistent IDs, estimated state/features, uncertainty, and a mapping from current observations or latent slots to those records. Each frame supplies detections/features; association matches them to existing entities, creates new records, or marks entities temporarily absent. Learning may improve detection, appearance embeddings, motion models, or matching scores. Inference is data association plus state estimation; memory is the entity table and temporal history. The architecture need not hide identity in weights, and the relevant operation is an explicit mapping/update of records.

**Novelty test and disposition.** “Persistent identities that survive changing features or occlusion” is already the target of visual indexing, object files, multi-object tracking, object-centric slots, and learned temporal slot lifecycle models. A generic slot-per-entity learner or persistent-identity memory is therefore occupied. More strictly, if two entity assignments yield identical observations and no motion, relation, stable key, or other invariant evidence distinguishes them, swapping their IDs leaves the data unchanged; identity is unidentifiable, not merely hard to compute. A new method could improve a defined association regime, but cannot resolve absent evidence by changing architecture terminology. `USE THE CLASSICAL MACHINE — NOT A NEW ARCHITECTURE` for the generic association problem; learned perception is a component. Architecture novelty **0/5**.

**Smallest useful test, if revisited after the no-test period.** Evaluate a specific encoder-change or long-occlusion regime against identity-aware tracking/data-association baselines and temporal object-centric models, holding the observations and memory budget fixed. Measure ID switches, re-identification precision/recall, calibration of “unknown identity,” and downstream state-prediction errors. Falsify a proposed mechanism if the gain disappears when the baseline receives the same learned features or if it forces false identity commitments on observationally ambiguous cases. This is a future literature/benchmark specification only; no test was run or launched.

#### Hybrid collision — persistent entity records × learned object-centric slots (HY-109; direct modern coupling)

Object-file/FINST-style records contribute stable references; learned slots contribute appearance and state inferred from video. This coupling can make each slot a persistent entity state and let predicted latent motion bridge temporary occlusion. Loci-Looped already integrates latent imagination with sensation for persistent what/where representations. Slot Contrast directly optimizes temporal consistency, while Temporal Slot Activation (2026) ties one learned visibility/activity signal to both slot-state preservation and decoder suppression. The latter is a deep coupling: the same lifecycle variable controls whether evidence updates a track and whether the absent track participates in explaining current pixels. It changes slot updating and reconstruction behavior, but is direct prior art for the broad proposed hybrid. Advantages include reduced identity drift and object permanence; failures include slot-capacity limits, mistaken reactivation, ID switches under crossings, and ambiguity when objects are observationally indistinguishable. Reject the generic hybrid (**0/5**); only a carefully bounded data-association regime could support a methods contribution. No experiment was run.

#### Continuation/resource update — structural rollback and persistent identity prior-art closure (2026-09-27)

This literature/formal-reduction pass closed reversible structural commitment as a new primitive: RJMCMC already crosses model dimensions, neural architecture search already grows and edits topologies, network morphism preserves functions under structural changes, and ordinary transaction/version logs restore prior state. Self-adjusting computation and differential dataflow cover reuse and retraction of affected derived computations. HY-108 records why coupling learned proposals to reversible commits remains a model-search/system design unless it supplies a distinct operation. AR-124/HY-109 checked the old FINST/object-file distinction against modern persistent-slot work, including Loci-Looped, Slot Contrast, and the 2026 Temporal Slot Activation mechanism; generic persistent identity is occupied and impossible without distinguishing evidence in symmetric cases. No architecture candidate was promoted. Literature only: no experiment or test was run, no benchmark or background job was started, and no GPU action was taken; attributable GPU use 0 GB. GPU/Claude process occupancy was not inspected, per the user's instruction. Only `Codex_Research.md` was edited.

#### Runtime creation of typed operators and symbols — DreamCoder, ILP, and schema-induction collision (AR-125; no architecture candidate)

**Question and exact operation.** Could an architecture create a new internal type, relation, or executable operator while learning, then reuse it as a first-class unit? A precise version would take examples or prediction residuals, synthesize a typed definition (signature plus executable body or relation schema), insert it into a persistent library, and make later inference/search operate over the enlarged vocabulary.

**Prior art from different traditions.** Inductive logic programming has long induced predicates and recursive relational programs from examples plus background knowledge. Meta-interpretive learning supports predicate invention, including higher-order invented programs; bottom-up MIL work explicitly treats invented predicates as reusable features. [Muggleton et al., Meta-interpretive learning (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10994-013-5358-3); [Cropper, Morel & Muggleton, higher-order predicate invention (AAAI 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v34i09.7113); [Hocquette & Muggleton, bottom-up predicate invention (IJCAI 2020)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2020/320).

DreamCoder gives a close modern architecture: solve example-specified tasks by program search, compress/refactor solved programs into new symbolic library abstractions, and train a neural recognizer on real and imagined tasks so future search can reuse the growing language. The abstracted program fragments are newly invented operators in the functional DSL; this changes the available representational vocabulary and future search cost. This is direct prior art for the broad “learn new operators and compose them” mechanism. [Ellis et al., *DreamCoder: Bootstrapping Inductive Program Synthesis with Wake-Sleep Library Learning* (PLDI 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3453483.3454080).

Open-Ended Dreamer extends library growth toward unsupervised, novelty-seeking program discovery. It alternates generation, selection, and abstraction to grow reusable program building blocks, and reports that greater exploration/stochasticity is needed to counter the bias induced by an expanding language. This makes “the system invents new symbols over time” still less distinctive; open-endedness is a search/objective challenge, not a missing symbol-creation operation. [Najarro & Risi, *Open-Ended Library Learning in Unsupervised Program Synthesis* (ALIFE 2023)](https://doi.org/10.1162/isal_a_00685).

Typed schemas have a parallel line: relation/entity extraction can generate schema labels, normalize them, store them in an evolving registry, and feed the registry into later extraction. DSE-RE (2026) directly couples LLM-proposed relation/entity types, semantic clustering, a dynamic schema registry, and iterative extraction. The language model is a proposal mechanism; the registry and clustering are explicit data structures. It is a domain-specific system rather than a general architecture, but it occupies the proposed “learn new types at runtime and reuse them” coupling. [DSE-RE, *Dynamic Schema Evolution with LLM for Iterative Relation Extraction* (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44230-026-00158-1).

**Historical limits and modern change.** Program synthesis and logic learning historically paid large combinatorial search costs, depended on a manually bounded primitive language or metarules, and needed clean examples/background predicates. Current processors, neural proposal models, e-graphs, and synthetic task generation improve search guidance and reuse. They do not supply correctness criteria, semantic grounding, or a principled choice among multiple equivalent abstractions. Expanding the symbol/type vocabulary can also grow the hypothesis space and create redundant or unstable concepts; the Open-Ended Dreamer analysis names the search-bias problem directly. C037 already covers learned rewrite rules/equality saturation, and DreamCoder already covers compression-based symbolic library growth, so a new “operators emerge from residuals” description would duplicate the notebook's program abstraction lane.

**Verdict.** `USE THE CLASSICAL MACHINE — NOT A NEW ARCHITECTURE`. Dynamic type labels reduce to schema induction/ontology maintenance; executable operator creation reduces to grammar induction, inductive program synthesis, predicate invention, and library learning; subsequent use is ordinary execution/search over a larger DSL. A new class would need a different semantics for creating, validating, or revising the symbols, not only a learned proposal policy. Broad novelty **0/5**. Do not promote a C candidate. No experiment or test was run.

#### Hybrid collision — LLM relation extraction × evolving typed schema registry (HY-110; direct 2026 application)

The LLM proposes entity/relation types and triples from text; semantic clustering consolidates synonymous labels; a schema registry stores the resulting type definitions and supplies them as context in the next extraction iteration. The interaction changes the representation vocabulary over time and feeds it back into perception/extraction. DSE-RE (2026) already directly describes this loop. Its likely utility is adapting information extraction to changing domains without a fixed ontology; likely failure modes are hallucinated or overbroad types, premature merging, inconsistent registry history, and schema drift. The loop depends on an LLM to propose semantics and on explicit registry/clustering code to manage them; it does not demonstrate a new general learning primitive. Reject as a new architecture (**0/5**); retain only as a domain-specific schema-management system. No experiment was run.
