- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — DECOMPOSITION PRESERVES PROPERTY.** A boundary that forbids the message is an information restriction, not evidence that ordinary modules cannot preserve the computation.

#### 5. Differentiable optimization layers and planners — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** a planner/optimizer embedded in a learned system so its solution feeds the next neural state and its sensitivity trains upstream modules.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** value, primal/dual solution, or selected plan feeds an action/output; a derivative or relaxed Bellman/optimization update returns a learning signal to the proposer or perception model.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** calling an opaque optimizer after a neural model preserves a one-shot answer but can lose gradient-through-decision behavior. Hard discrete search may also make the derivative unavailable.
- **Strongest restoration:** expose an adjoint/KKT sensitivity, use differentiable dynamic programming, or use a differentiable relaxation while preserving the same solver state and recurrence. These interfaces restore exactly the claimed derivative only for their stated conditions; a relaxation may change discrete semantics and must be evaluated as such.
- **Closest historical prior art:** dynamic programming, value iteration, optimal control, and differentiable programming of constrained optimization.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Value Iteration Networks embed learned value-iteration steps and train end to end; OptNet/CVXPYLayers differentiate through convex programs. [Value Iteration Networks (NeurIPS 2016)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/hash/c21002f464c5fc5bee3b98ced83963b8-Abstract.html); [Differentiable Convex Optimization Layers (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.12430).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** An opaque solver is not the strongest decomposition, and the stronger differentiable solver-in-the-loop architecture is already published.

#### 6. Neural-symbolic joint training and solver-in-the-loop inference — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** a neural front end and symbolic solver that exchange intermediate signals during learning and inference.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** neural predicates or proposals parameterize facts/actions; symbolic derivations, constraint outcomes, rejected steps, or proof success return as probabilistic gradients, supervised labels, or RL reward.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** a perception-then-solver pipeline may prevent proof/constraint outcomes from changing the neural representation; a neural answer without a checker loses symbolic soundness.
- **Strongest restoration:** expose the neural predicate probabilities and the derivation/solver result as explicit ports; use differentiable proof semantics, surrogate gradients, or RL over checked actions, while retaining the checker as a soundness boundary. These choices have different gradients and guarantees, so claims must name which one.
- **Closest historical prior art:** inductive logic programming, probabilistic logic programming, theorem proving, and neural-symbolic integration.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Neural Theorem Provers relax backward chaining/unification; DeepProbLog trains neural predicates through probabilistic logic inference; AlphaProof couples a policy/value network, tree search, Lean tactics, verified state transitions, and RL; IJCAI 2026 Neural Decision-Propagation makes solver decisions and fuzzy propagation a differentiable loop. [End-to-End Differentiable Proving (NeurIPS 2017)](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/6969-end-to-end-differentiable-proving); [DeepProbLog (NeurIPS 2018)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2018/hash/dc5d637ed5e62c36ecb73b654b05ba2a-Abstract.html); [AlphaProof (Nature 2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09833-y); [Neural Decision-Propagation for ASP (IJCAI 2026)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2026/425).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** The exact neural-to-symbolic and symbolic-to-learning signal paths are already instantiated. This does not imply that every newly specified checker, proof calculus, or resource guarantee is old.

#### 7. Learned optimizers and meta-learning — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** a learner whose own update rule is learned and whose task-level outcome changes its future updates.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** gradient/history features enter a recurrent or learned optimizer, which writes parameter deltas; an outer loss differentiates through the inner learning trajectory or trains an initialization for rapid adaptation.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** treating the optimizer as an external fixed routine removes learned update behavior; stopping the outer gradient removes the meta-learning signal.
- **Strongest restoration:** expose gradient, optimizer hidden state, parameter state, and update delta as an optimizer-module interface, and differentiate through the unrolled update or use the exact meta-objective. This preserves the mechanism without putting the update code inside the model's forward operator.
- **Closest historical prior art:** learning to learn and recurrent learned update rules; classical adaptive control and optimization already separate controller/plant state.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Andrychowicz et al. learn an LSTM optimizer from gradient trajectories; MAML learns initial parameters for rapid gradient adaptation; hierarchical learned optimizers extend scale and task structure. [Learning to Learn by Gradient Descent by Gradient Descent (NeurIPS 2016)](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/6461-learning-to-learn-by-gradient-descent-by-gradient-descent); [MAML (ICML 2017)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/finn17a.html); [Learned Optimizers that Scale and Generalize (ICML 2017)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/wichrowska17a.html).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** A newly parameterized optimizer or meta-objective could be a useful method, but “the learner's state changes its later learning” is occupied.

#### 8. External-memory read/write feedback, NTM/DNC, and associative test-time memory — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** an inference controller that can form and retrieve persistent internal state while processing a stream.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** controller emits address, allocation, erase, and write vectors; memory returns read vectors that affect the next controller state and later outputs.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** a separate database with only batch insert/query may lose differentiable addressing, temporal write order, allocation/link metadata, or read-dependent controller behavior.
- **Strongest restoration:** give a memory service the same address/soft-attention, write, erase, allocation, and temporal-link API and feed the returned read vectors into the next controller transition. That is the NTM/DNC organization even if deployed as separate software modules. For exact RAM rather than differentiable memory, compare the changed addressing semantics and cost model instead of equating them.
- **Closest historical prior art:** external stores, fast weights, and content-addressable memory.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Neural Turing Machines and Differentiable Neural Computers provide differentiable read/write loops; Titans learns a neural memory update at test time; the 2026 JMLR Test-Time Regression paper places softmax attention, linear attention, state-space models, fast weights, and online learners in an associative-memory/test-time-regression framework. [Neural Turing Machines (2014)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5401); [DNC (Nature 2016)](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature20101); [Titans (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663); [Test-Time Regression (JMLR 2026)](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v27/25-0903.html).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** The write-feedback loop is already a named architecture family; a resource advantage must be stated and matched separately.

#### 9. Mixture-of-experts and routing-by-agreement — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** an input-dependent computation path where expert outputs or lower-level votes modify later routing decisions.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** router scores select or weight experts; in routing-by-agreement, lower-level predictions iteratively change coupling weights based on agreement with higher-level outputs.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** independent experts without a shared router lose input-dependent specialization; a one-shot router may lose iterative agreement or capacity/load constraints.
- **Strongest restoration:** keep router state and score in a dispatcher, pass selected activations to expert modules, return outputs, and update routing scores with the same agreement/auxiliary-loss rule. This preserves sparse activation, expert gradients, and the iterative routing rule; communication overhead is measurable but does not erase prior art.
- **Closest historical prior art:** Jacobs et al.'s adaptive mixtures of experts (1991), with a gating network deciding which expert handles each example; capsule routing-by-agreement (2017).
- **Closest modern prior art:** Switch Transformers simplify top-1 learned MoE routing and study communication cost and training stability; 2026 CR-DMS explicitly couples differentiable module composition with representation-driven module growth. [Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1991.3.1.79); [Dynamic Routing Between Capsules (NeurIPS 2017)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/6975-dynamic-routing-between-capsules.pdf); [Switch Transformers (JMLR 2022)](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v23/21-0998.html); [CR-DMS (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092523122602477X).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** A different route objective or load-balancing loss is not an unoccupied coupling mechanism.

#### 10. Shared latent workspace, blackboard, and production-system feedback — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** specialists coordinate by writing partial results into a common state that changes which specialist or production executes next.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** board entries, confidence, agenda items, and rule firings make hypotheses globally visible and trigger follow-on operations; each write can change control scheduling.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** independent specialists with no common state lose cross-domain availability, opportunistic cooperation, and data-directed triggering.
- **Strongest restoration:** provide a shared evented blackboard/working-memory interface plus an agenda scheduler; make every specialist's partial result, confidence, and trigger visible. This restores the same information flow and control transitions. A modern shared latent vector may not preserve symbolic inspectability, but inspectability is not implied by generic “workspace coupling.”
- **Closest historical prior art:** HEARSAY-II and Hayes-Roth's blackboard control architecture; production systems with working memory, rule matching, and agenda control.
- **Closest modern prior art:** blackboard/global-workspace cognitive architectures and shared-workspace agent systems reuse the same central-state and specialist-trigger pattern; no current candidate has named a different write or scheduling rule.
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** The alleged lost path exists in the blackboard machine itself. [HEARSAY-II (ACM Computing Surveys 1980)](https://mas.cs.umass.edu/pub/paper_detail.php/229); [Hayes-Roth, A Blackboard Architecture for Control (1985)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(85)90063-3).

#### 11. CDCL conflict feedback — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** conflict-driven search in which a failed branch changes future search rather than merely returning failure.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** implication/conflict graph yields an asserting learned clause and a backjump level; the solver writes that clause into its persistent database, propagates it, and resumes from a non-chronological level.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** DPLL plus a post-hoc conflict analyzer that does not feed clauses back into the active database loses the learned constraint and future pruning. It can revisit the same conflicting region; equal SAT/UNSAT output is not equal search behavior or proof complexity.
- **Strongest restoration:** expose the implication graph and conflict to a clause analyzer; return the learned clause and backjump level; append to the same persistent clause database and rerun propagation before branching. This exactly restores the transition—this is CDCL.
- **Closest historical prior art:** GRASP introduced conflict-directed backtracking and conflict-based clause learning; resolution and nogood learning are predecessors, but neither alone is the complete transition loop.
- **Closest modern prior art:** CDCL is standard SAT architecture. Pipatsrisawat and Darwiche prove that practical CDCL proof systems p-simulate general resolution. That theorem does not prove a separation over DPLL alone; it establishes that clause-learning CDCL retains the power of the resolution proof system. [GRASP technical report (1996)](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs.cmu.edu/academic/class/15414-f06/www/resources/CSE-TR-292-96.pdf); [Pipatsrisawat & Darwiche, AIJ 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2010.10.002).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** This is the calibration control: a naive decomposition loses the important feedback, while the best ordinary decomposition restores it by implementing the already-known CDCL state machine. Do not kill a new proposal merely because DPLL computes the same final function.

#### 12. Theorem-prover clause/lemma learning and proof feedback — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** proof attempts produce reusable derivations or learned clauses that steer later proof search.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** a derived clause, failed branch constraint, subproof, or verified lemma is written into the active/passive proof state or persistent archive; future inference selection and closure use it.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** a prover that only reports success/failure to an external learner may lose the proof object, dependency conditions, and local subgoal state needed for sound reuse.
- **Strongest restoration:** return a checked lemma with its proof/dependency certificate to the prover's clause index or schema archive; refresh subsumption/selection state and continue. If updates must be sound, the checker and dependency scope belong in the interface. This retains rather than handwaves away the critical feedback path.
- **Closest historical prior art:** saturation provers already derive clauses and place them in active/passive sets; conflict-driven lemma learning and ILP systems such as Popper learn constraints from failed hypotheses.
- **Closest modern prior art:** ENIGMA learns clause selection from proof-search traces; theorem-proving systems use learned clause/tactic guidance; AlphaProof returns Lean-checked search outcomes to RL; the August 2026 ProofEvolve preprint explicitly stores kernel-verified proof sub-DAGs in a cross-problem schema library and recombines them in later search. [Learning Theorem Proving Components (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10034); [Popper: Learning Programs by Learning from Failures](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-020-05934-z); [AlphaProof (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09833-y); [ProofEvolve (preprint, 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26334).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE** for the generic learned-clause/verified-lemma feedback claim. ProofEvolve's exact design is cited as very recent prior art; this audit does not independently judge that paper's own novelty.

#### 13. Actor-critic and internal credit assignment — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** action generation and policy improvement use an internal evaluator whose errors train the policy that generated the data.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** reward and next-state estimate form a temporal-difference error; eligibility traces or policy gradients deliver it to actor parameters while the critic updates its value estimate.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** a fixed critic or a reward applied only after a complete episode loses the bootstrapped, temporally local credit signal and can raise memory/variance costs.
- **Strongest restoration:** make the critic return the same TD error and eligibility-weighted update to an actor module at the same transition; preserve the shared state and sampling policy. This is the actor-critic loop, whether implemented monolithically or as cooperating modules.
- **Closest historical prior art:** adaptive heuristic critics and Barto–Sutton–Anderson's actor-critic architecture (1983); Sutton's temporal-difference learning (1988).
- **Closest modern prior art:** actor-critic remains a standard reinforcement-learning architecture; learned critics, eligibility traces, and policy-gradient updates refine its estimator/control choices rather than inventing the feedback direction. [Barto, Sutton & Anderson (1983)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1983.6313077); [Sutton, Temporal-Difference Learning (1988)](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1022633531479).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** Delayed feedback can lose credit assignment, but the direct native coupling has decades of prior art.

#### 14. Active inference and perception-action feedback — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** inference selects actions that change the next observations used for inference.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** prediction errors update beliefs; beliefs and expected free energy update policy/action; the resulting action changes sensory input and future inference.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** a perception module followed by a fixed policy severs epistemic value, top-down predictions, and action-dependent sensing; independent optimization of estimation and control may not preserve the common objective.
- **Strongest restoration:** share the generative-model/belief state and expose the prediction-error and expected-free-energy messages to a policy/controller module that acts and returns new observations. This can preserve the loop; it may be a different algorithm if the approximate inference schedule or objective changes.
- **Closest historical prior art:** Bayesian filtering, belief propagation, optimal control, planning as inference, predictive coding, and active sensing.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Friston et al.'s active-inference process theory derives coupled perception, action selection, and learning from variational free-energy minimization; factor-graph accounts make the message schedule explicit. [Active Inference: A Process Theory (Neural Computation 2017)](https://doi.org/10.1162/NECO_a_00912); [The Graphical Brain: Belief Propagation and Active Inference](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29417960/).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** The closed-loop information path is central to a named, formalized architecture family.

#### 15. Forward inference that changes later learning or search — KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE

- **Candidate name:** an architecture whose ordinary inference steps mutate a memory, optimizer, proof archive, or routing state that changes future inference/learning.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** surprise, prediction error, gradient, failed search result, or checked derivation is written online; later queries read the updated state.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** frozen inference followed by offline retraining loses within-stream adaptation; non-persistent search feedback loses transfer between episodes/problems.
- **Strongest restoration:** put an explicit online update operator between steps and pass a versioned state to the next inference call. The separate memory/optimizer/proof store preserves the same chronology, writes, and reads if the interface is complete. If memory bandwidth, update cost, or interference is the claimed property, count and compare those resources.
- **Closest historical prior art:** fast weights, online learning, recurrent state, learning-to-learn, and case/derivation archives.
- **Closest modern prior art:** Titans and test-time training update associative memory at inference; NeurIPS 2025 Nested Learning frames optimizers as memory and presents a self-modifying Titans variant plus continuum memory; JMLR 2026 Test-Time Regression unifies attention, recurrent/state-space, and online-regression memory designs; ProofEvolve (2026 preprint) writes checked proof subgraphs into later search state. [Titans (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663); [Nested Learning (NeurIPS 2025)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/4309616aaed8e848009bc4a7ef73b493-Abstract-Conference.html); [Test-Time Regression (JMLR 2026)](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v27/25-0903.html); [ProofEvolve (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26334).
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE.** Online writeback is an established architectural pattern. A particular state type, update rule, stability theorem, or resource separation may still need its own audit.

#### 16. Generic “native coupling” without a named signal — KILLED — NO MATERIAL PROPERTY

- **Candidate name:** an unspecified architecture in which parts are “tightly coupled” and therefore supposedly more intelligent or adaptive.
- **Claimed internal signal / native coupling:** none typed; no producer, consumer, write point, or schedule is given.
- **Ordinary decomposition and alleged loss:** the only alleged loss is that breaking the system into modules might block some unspecified path. Since the interface is unspecified, no state transition or guarantee is available to compare.
- **Strongest restoration:** first define the signal and expose it through an explicit value/state/update interface. If the “native” property remains after that replacement, it is not coupling-specific; if it fails, name the missing field, timing, ordering, or resource bound and search that operation directly.
- **Closest historical prior art:** blackboard/workspace, message-passing, recurrent, differentiable, and solver-feedback architectures occupy the broad organizational motifs.
- **Closest modern prior art:** direct examples span MPNNs, DEQs, NTM/DNC, differentiable logic, actor-critic, CDCL, Titans/Nested Learning, and 2026 neural decision-propagation. Their diversity confirms that “feedback” is a family descriptor, not a single uncovered machine.
- **Architecture verdict:** **KILLED — NO MATERIAL PROPERTY.** This is the target class as stated, not a ruling that all future internally coupled architectures are impossible.

### Kill-test crosswalk

| Alleged primitive property | Exact established signal path found | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient flow | VJP/JVP and reverse-mode composition across module boundaries | Decomposition can preserve it |
| Recurrence / equilibrium | Explicit state feedback, root-finding, implicit differentiation | Direct RNN/DEQ/EP prior art |
| Shared state / external memory | Read/write interface and persistent memory state | NTM/DNC and shared-store prior art |
| Rich messages / message passing | Edge messages, reducers, repeated node-state updates | MPNN/NAR prior art |
| Differentiable relaxation | Soft or implicit derivative through optimization/planning | VIN and differentiable-solver prior art |
| Joint end-to-end training | Symbolic likelihood/proof outcome supplies neural gradients | DeepProbLog/NTP prior art |
| Learned routing | Router scores, sparse dispatch, expert results, agreement feedback | MoE/capsule prior art |
| Solver-in-the-loop | Search result/checker state/reward feeds the next policy or update | AlphaProof/NDProp and CDCL prior art |
| Blackboard/global workspace | Shared board writes trigger specialist or rule execution | HEARSAY-II / blackboard prior art |
| Learned control / actor-critic | TD error, belief, or expected-free-energy signal changes action | Actor-critic / active-inference prior art |
| Alternating optimization / meta-learning | Inner update state is visible to the outer loss/learner | Equilibrium propagation / learned optimizers / MAML |
| Forward inference changes future learning/search | Online update writes memory, optimizer, clause, or proof state | Titans, Nested Learning, CDCL, ProofEvolve |

### Interpretation, limits, and next action

The collision map rejects the slogan “the computation must be natively coupled” as sufficient novelty. It does not assert that a software interface is free: copying full states, transmitting gradients, synchronizing feedback, or verifying writeback can change wall-clock, bandwidth, memory, privacy, or fault-containment properties. Those are valid architecture claims only when specified and compared. A candidate cannot use a deliberately crippled interface as its decomposition baseline; it must compare against the richest ordinary interface that carries the exact signal and transition under discussion.

**CDCL calibration.** DPLL can decide the same Boolean function, but DPLL without learned-clause feedback is not CDCL's state transition. The useful separator is persistent conflict-derived information that changes later branching/propagation and the induced proof system. The strongest modular decomposition preserves that signal by inserting clauses into the active database and thereby reconstructs CDCL. This keeps both sides of the calibrated standard: final-function equivalence is insufficient, while a direct same-architecture prior is decisive.

**2025–2026 source check.** The recent papers sharpen rather than reopen the broad family: Nested Learning (NeurIPS 2025) explicitly couples nested optimization, self-modifying sequence updates, and continuum memory; Test-Time Regression (JMLR 2026) unifies several “native” associative-memory sequence layers by memory/update/optimization design choices; Neural Decision-Propagation (IJCAI 2026) puts learned decisions and fuzzy solver propagation in a loop; ProofEvolve (August 2026 preprint) feeds checked derivation subgraphs into future proof search; CR-DMS (September 2026) couples differentiable module selection with growth. These are newly dated prior-art examples, not independent judgments that each paper has no contribution. The relevant negative result is narrower: the generic coupling motifs have direct instances; any distinct contribution needs an exact residual transition/property comparison.

**Verdict.** No candidate receives **SURVIVES ARCHITECTURE PRIOR-ART ATTACK**. There is no current candidate for which a decomposition was shown to destroy a material property while every direct architecture prior was ruled out. No experiments, benchmarks, or compute-heavy jobs were run. No smallest test is assigned because nothing survived. If a concrete candidate later appears, the smallest decisive falsifier is to replace the native link with an ordinary typed interface carrying the same signal and persistent write, preserve update order and resource budgets, and check whether the claimed guarantee/learning transition survives; only then compare costs when a cost separation is the claim.

**Exact next action.** Take the next independently proposed mechanism only after writing: signal producer and consumer; exact state read/write; trigger and schedule; property/guarantee; and the strongest interface that could transport it. Search for that same transition in the historical and modern architectures above before proposing any experiment. Continue avoiding Claude and Cursor notebook contents as research input.

## AR-140 — Single-model learning-dynamics collision library (2026-09-27)

**Question.** Before anyone spends compute on a new learning-dynamics proposal, how much of the claimed property is already supplied by a known architecture, update rule, objective, or schedule?

**Method.** Organize collisions by the learning property, not by field. A candidate is not rejected because a universal machine could simulate it. It is rejected when a named architecture already has the transition, or when the strongest matched ordinary mechanism retains the important learning behavior. “Same final function” is not enough: credit flow, state evolution, online adaptation, interference, and resource law are checked separately.

**Top-line finding.** The broad properties in this phase are heavily occupied. No currently specified Codex candidate survives. In several groups, the exact learning rule is known; in others, the architecture is known even though an optimizer cannot reproduce its wiring; in still others, the supposed novelty is only an objective or schedule. Those are distinct reasons for closure.

### Historical controls: the filter must preserve real architectural differences

| Control | Native state/update and property | Calibration result |
|---|---|---|
| **Residual / skip pathways** | A block updates (h_{l+1}=h_l+F_l(h_l)); its Jacobian includes an identity route plus the block Jacobian. Identity mappings allow forward information and backward derivatives to pass across blocks directly. Highway networks add learned carry/transform gates. | This changes the optimization path and trainability; “same arithmetic” or an optimizer-only substitution does not recreate the skip edge. But ResNet and Highway are direct prior architectures, so a later claim to this property is occupied. [Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05027); [Highway Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00387). |
| **Attention** | Queries read values through input-dependent key compatibility and normalized weights. Self-attention gives token-to-token paths within a layer; recurrent models instead carry state through sequential steps. | Attention changes path length, information access, parallelization, and the resulting gradients. A plain optimizer does not add those paths. Transformer/self-attention and earlier attention/memory mechanisms are direct architecture prior art, not evidence that all other sequence models are equivalent. [Attention Is All You Need](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/7181-attention-is-all-you-%0Aneed.pdf). |
| **Backpropagation / reverse-mode AD** | Given a differentiable computation graph and scalar objective, reverse accumulation applies the chain rule to compute vector-Jacobian products and parameter gradients. | Exact global credit transport is a real learning operation, not “just a computer simulation.” It is nevertheless a known algorithmic primitive; an architecture claim must name a different transition or property. The chronology spans reverse-mode AD, control-theoretic adjoints, and neural-network backpropagation; the 1986 treatment made its representation-learning role explicit. [Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986)](https://www.nature.com/articles/323533a0). |
| **Recurrent state** | (s_{t+1}=f_	heta(s_t,x_t)) writes a persistent state that mediates later computation. The same weights are reused over time; BPTT/RTRL assign temporal credit by distinct exact or truncated mechanisms. | Recurrence changes information retention and serial compute. A feedforward optimizer cannot supply persistent state without adding recurrence or memory. RNN/LSTM/GRU/SSM families already occupy broad stateful-learning claims. |
| **Fast weights** | A fast matrix/state is updated from current activations and used by subsequent activations; slow parameters learn the programmer/update policy. | This is not generic “more parameters”: it creates within-sequence plastic state. But it is directly described by early fast-weight controllers/programmers and modern recurrent fast-weight models. Linearized attention has a formal fast-weight-programmer interpretation. [Schmidhuber (1992)](https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/fastweights/); [Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/schlag21a.html). |
| **Equilibrium models / equilibrium propagation** | In DEQ, a tied transition is iterated/root-solved to (z^*=f_	heta(z^*,x)), then differentiated implicitly. In equilibrium propagation, a free fixed point is followed by a target-nudged fixed point; state differences estimate the gradient of an energy objective. | These mechanisms change effective depth, state settling, memory use, and credit transport. A finite unroll or ordinary BP may be a useful baseline but is not automatically property-identical. Both exact families are established prior art. [Deep Equilibrium Models](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/hash/01386bd6d8e091c2ab4c7c7de644d37b-Abstract.html); [Equilibrium Propagation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05179). |
| **Diffusion process** | A learned score/denoiser is conditioned on noise level; sampling follows a reverse Markov chain or reverse-time SDE/ODE. | The iterative trajectory and solver can materially affect generation. But a new noise schedule, denoising loss, or sampler alone is an objective/process/solver change, not a new learning architecture. Score-SDE work explicitly relates the process and alternate numerical samplers. [DDPM](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2020/hash/4c5bcfec8584af0d967f1ab10179ca4b-Abstract.html); [Score-based Generative Modeling through SDEs](https://research.google/pubs/score-based-generative-modeling-through-stochastic-differential-equations/). |
| **CDCL (cross-domain control)** | Conflict analysis writes learned clauses into the active database; future propagation and branching consume them. | A solver returning the same SAT answer is not enough to establish equivalence. Removing the writeback changes later search/proof behavior; restoring it reconstructs CDCL. This remains the standard reminder to compare state transitions, not only input-output function. |

These controls pass the calibrated test: architecture can change learning/computation even when ordinary arithmetic is used. They are not candidates for rediscovery; their direct prior art is why the same claimed organization is occupied.

### Collision library organized by learning property

#### 1. Transporting credit across layers or time

- **Mechanism family.** Reverse-mode/backprop sends exact derivatives backward through the computational graph. Feedback Alignment (FA) and Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA) replace symmetric backward weights with fixed random feedback paths and rely on learned alignment; DFA broadcasts output error directly to hidden layers. Synthetic Gradients learn a predictor of a module’s future gradient so its update can proceed asynchronously. Target Propagation (TP/DTP) sends activation targets through learned inverse/autoencoder paths. Predictive Coding (PC) settles local prediction errors and, under specified constructions, can converge to exact backprop gradients. Contrastive Hebbian Learning (CHL) uses free and clamped activity differences; in a layered linear special case, Xie–Seung show equivalence to backprop up to a scalar. E-prop factors recurrent gradients into local eligibility traces and a learning signal. Forward-Forward replaces backward error propagation with local goodness objectives on positive and negative passes.
- **Closest architecture/mechanism.** For exact credit, reverse-mode AD/BPTT; for asymmetric broadcast, DFA/FA; for independently scheduled modules, Decoupled Neural Interfaces; for inverse-target signals, DTP; for local relaxation, PC/EP/CHL; for recurrent local traces, e-prop; for layer-local positive/negative learning, Forward-Forward. These are not interchangeable in all guarantees or scaling; each occupies its own specific mechanism claim. [DFA (NeurIPS 2016)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/hash/d490d7b4576290fa60eb31b5fc917ad1-Abstract.html); [DFA at modern scale (NeurIPS 2020)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2020/hash/69d1fc78dbda242c43ad6590368912d4-Abstract.html); [Synthetic Gradients (ICML 2017)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/jaderberg17a.html); [Difference Target Propagation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.7525); [Predictive Coding approximates backprop on arbitrary graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04182); [CHL/backprop equivalence](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12590814/); [E-prop](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17236-y); [Forward-Forward](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.13345).
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Standard BP/BPTT with SGD, momentum, AdamW, or checkpointing preserves exact chain-rule updates but not the locality/asymmetry/asynchrony claim. Conversely, a local credit method should not be declared equivalent merely because both eventually reduce the same supervised loss.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Layerwise local objectives and positive/negative goodness losses can create local updates, but changing the objective does not by itself establish a new architecture. Forward-Forward is a known algorithmic family; target-propagation losses likewise have direct prior art.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Keep backbone, initialization, data, parameter count, update count, and compute budget fixed; compare the proposed rule with BP, the closest FA/DFA or synthetic-gradient variant, and the closest local/settling rule. Measure not only final accuracy but gradient/update alignment, locality, synchronization, memory and wall-clock. For exact-gradient claims, test the update equation, not just a downstream task score.
- **Verdict.** Broad claims to local credit, non-symmetric feedback, short credit paths, asynchronous updates, or prediction-error credit are **KILLED — EXISTING MECHANISM / EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. A new learning rule can still be a contribution, but needs an exact operation plus a property not already supplied by these mechanisms.

#### 2. Preserving gradient paths, changing depth, and conditioning

- **Mechanism family.** Residual/skip paths preserve identity transport; Highway gates choose carry versus transform; attention adds content-dependent paths; gating changes effective connectivity; normalization changes activation/gradient scale and cross-example coupling; initialization methods such as Fixup can recover some deep-training stability without normalization.
- **Closest architecture.** ResNet/Highway/Transformer and normalized residual blocks. These examples show why “same function in principle” is too weak: derivative paths and input-dependent information flow are part of the learning system.
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Learning-rate tuning, momentum, Adam/AdamW, second-order/preconditioned updates, gradient clipping, and schedules can address optimization geometry or stability. They do not reproduce a missing identity path, attention edge, or gating state. Conversely, claims that BatchNorm uniquely supplies the training benefit are narrowed by alternatives such as Fixup. [Batch Normalization](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/ioffe15.html); [Fixup: Residual Learning Without Normalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09321); [Mean Field Residual Networks](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2017/hash/81c650caac28cdefce4de5ddc18befa0-Abstract.html).
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Auxiliary losses, norm penalties, and path regularizers may encourage similar behavior but do not instantiate the same wiring or invariant. Treating a loss as equivalent requires showing that it preserves the claimed transition, not merely the end metric.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Same depth/width and data; compare residual/highway vs non-skip with optimizer and initialization tuned separately, and BN/LN vs a non-normalized alternative such as Fixup. For attention or gates, compare with the closest sparse/dense routing or recurrent implementation at matched FLOPs and sequence length. Ablate the path/gate itself.
- **Verdict.** New claims of skip-gradient preservation, adaptive highway flow, content-based routing/attention, or normalization-based conditioning are **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. A claim that an optimizer alone recreates a missing path is not supported; architecture novelty is killed here by direct prior art, not by that false optimizer equivalence.

#### 3. Recurrent state, adaptive compute, continuous time, and implicit depth

- **Mechanism family.** RNN/LSTM/GRU/SSM updates write state for future steps. Adaptive Computation Time chooses how many recurrent steps to execute before halting. Neural ODEs replace a discrete layer stack with a learned continuous-time vector field and an adaptive numerical solver. DEQs solve an equilibrium of a weight-tied transformation and use implicit differentiation. Recurrent backprop, BPTT, RTRL, adjoint sensitivity, and implicit gradients are established ways to train these transitions.
- **Closest architecture.** Recurrent networks for explicit state; adaptive-computation recurrent models for learned depth; Neural ODE/CDE families for continuous-time transitions; DEQ/MDEQ for fixed-point depth. No optimizer-only scheme supplies persistent state or a fixed-point computation when the architecture lacks it.
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** BPTT/RTRL/adjoint/implicit differentiation differ in exactness, truncation, and memory/compute, but are training rules for known recurrent/continuous/equilibrium architectures. Gradient checkpointing and dynamic programming can trade recomputation for activation memory without changing the learned model’s state transition. [Memory-Efficient BPTT](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/hash/a501bebf79d570651ff601788ea9d16d-Abstract.html).
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Auxiliary ponder/halting losses or trajectory consistency terms tune step count/behavior; they do not create recurrence or equilibrium state.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Compare the proposed transition against the same cell unrolled to matched effective depth, a tied recurrent model, and a DEQ/ODE solver when applicable. Match tolerance, solver evaluations, memory and FLOPs; otherwise “adaptive depth” may simply spend more computation.
- **Verdict.** Generic learned recurrence, state accumulation, continuous-time evolution, adaptive depth, and implicit equilibrium claims are **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. A specific new resource law must be demonstrated against tied unroll, checkpointing, and root/ODE solvers; no such candidate is currently specified.

#### 4. Fast/slow state, plasticity, and learning during inference

- **Mechanism family.** Fast-weight controllers program short-lived synaptic state; differentiable plasticity meta-learns plastic coefficients; test-time training updates model parameters from unlabeled or self-supervised test data; test-time memory stores context via online optimization, associative retrieval, or recurrent state.
- **Closest architecture.** Schmidhuber’s fast-weight systems (1991–93), differentiable plasticity, linear-attention/fast-weight programmers, TTT layers, Titans, ATLAS, MIRAS designs, and HOPE/Nested Learning. This is a particularly crowded current area. The 2026 JMLR Test-Time Regression paper organizes softmax and linear attention, SSMs, fast-weight programmers, and online learners as associative-memory regression systems specified by memory, regressor, weighting, and optimization choices. The unification is a design map, not proof that all models have equal memory, update, or compute costs. [Differentiable Plasticity](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02464); [TTT provably improves Transformers as in-context learners (ICML 2025)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/gozeten25a.html); [Titans](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663); [ATLAS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23735); [MIRAS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13173); [Test-Time Regression (JMLR 2026)](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v27/25-0903.html).
- **2025–26 collision detail.** Titans uses a learned neural long-term memory alongside attention; ATLAS changes memory capacity and update context; MIRAS explicitly varies memory architecture, attentional bias objective, retention gate, and memory learning algorithm; Nested Learning treats components as multi-frequency optimization/memory levels and instantiates self-modifying HOPE; 2025 theory characterizes gradient-based TTT for in-context learning; a 2026 Fast Spatial Memory preprint stabilizes plastic test-time weights with a Fisher-weighted elastic anchor. The recent examples occupy broad “learn while processing,” “fast/slow state,” and “online memory update” claims. The elastic prior is also close to EWC/regularized online adaptation rather than an unoccupied state semantics. [Nested Learning / HOPE (NeurIPS 2025 paper)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24695); [Fast Spatial Memory with Elastic TTT (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07350).
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Online SGD/Adam on a fast parameter copy, MAML initialization plus a few inner updates, or a learned optimizer can reproduce parameter adaptation without a special neural memory module. These controls may not match a particular associative read/write topology or streaming complexity, which must be tested separately.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** TENT/entropy minimization, self-supervised TTT, test-time regression losses, and next-token/denoising objectives provide known adaptation signals. Loss-only novelty is not architecture novelty.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Same backbone and stream; match parameter/state bytes, memory reads/writes, gradient steps, tokens, FLOPs and latency. Compare against ordinary test-time fine-tuning, fast-weight programmer/linear attention, Titans/ATLAS/MIRAS or TTR as relevant, and an explicit external memory. Measure adaptation speed, retrieval, retention/forgetting, and state growth.
- **Verdict.** Generic fast/slow separation, test-time learning, test-time memory, and self-modifying sequence updates are **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE / MECHANISM**. Exact memory/throughput tradeoffs remain architecture-specific; they do not create a generic novelty opening.

#### 5. Meta-learned initialization and learned optimizers

- **Mechanism family.** MAML learns an initialization whose parameters improve after a few ordinary gradient steps. Learned optimizers use an RNN or other update model over gradient/history to emit parameter updates. Meta-learning may instead learn a local plasticity rule, an optimizer hyperparameter, a task embedding, or an architecture/controller.
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** This is often the closest match: MAML is a bilevel objective over initialization plus an inner optimizer; learned optimizers replace/tune the update rule; learned schedules alter when/how updates occur. [MAML](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/finn17a.html); [Learning to Learn by Gradient Descent by Gradient Descent](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/hash/5a7b238ba0f6502e5d6be14424b20ded-Abstract.html); [learned derivative-free optimizer](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/chen17e.html).
- **Closest architecture.** LSTM/attention/meta-learners that implement a learned optimizer, differentiable plasticity, and recurrent fast-weight programmers. MAML itself is deliberately architecture-agnostic and need not add learned parameters to the base architecture.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** The outer meta-objective changes which initialization or update sequence is preferred; it is not by itself a new architecture. Test-time objective learning and conjugate pseudo-label work show that even apparently bespoke adaptation losses can reduce to a principled transformation of the supervised loss. [Test-Time Adaptation via Conjugate Pseudo-labels (NeurIPS 2022)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/28e9eff897f98372409b40ae1ed3ea4c-Abstract-Conference.html).
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Same model, task distribution, inner update count, and outer compute; compare tuned SGD/AdamW, MAML/reptile-style learned initialization, and a learned optimizer. Evaluate transfer to held-out task families and sensitivity to longer horizons, not only meta-training episodes.
- **Verdict.** Broad “learn to learn,” “learn the optimizer,” “fast adaptation from initialization,” or “architecture and optimizer co-design” claims are **KILLED — EXISTING MECHANISM / OPTIMIZER ONLY**, unless a separate state transition or non-preserved architecture property is identified.

#### 6. Reducing interference and retaining old skills

- **Mechanism family.** EWC and Synaptic Intelligence penalize changing parameters important to previous tasks; GEM/A-GEM constrain new gradients against episodic memories; replay stores examples/logits; Progressive Networks or parameter-isolation methods add capacity; adapters/low-rank updates restrict the plastic subspace.
- **2025–26 collisions.** LCoTTA tracks the low-dimensional principal subspace of test-time gradients and projects updates into it to suppress harmful entropy-minimization samples (NeurIPS 2025). Elastic Test-Time Training uses a Fisher-weighted prior around an evolving fast-weight anchor for long-sequence adaptation (2026 preprint). These occupy claims of continual test-time adaptation via gradient geometry, online subspaces, and stability–plasticity gates. [GEM](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2017/hash/f87522788a2be2d171666752f97ddebb-Abstract.html); [LCoTTA](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/1b6f528fe522a956dce80d5b98be8cd5-Abstract-Conference.html); [Elastic TTT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07350).
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** EWC/SI/GEM/A-GEM, gradient projection, constrained optimization, or replay under an unchanged backbone.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Distillation, parameter-importance penalties, and replay losses alter the objective; they do not establish an architectural mechanism unless capacity/state is changed.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Same backbone and stream order; match memory bytes, added parameters, gradient steps, replay volume and inference/training FLOPs. Compare fine-tuning, EWC/SI, GEM/A-GEM, replay, parameter isolation, and the nearest low-dimensional gradient method. Include both retention and forward transfer; a low forgetting score obtained by blocking learning is not a win.
- **Verdict.** Generic stability–plasticity tradeoffs, protected subspaces, replay, and continual adaptation are **KILLED — EXISTING MECHANISM / EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. “Less interference” is not itself a novel property without a formal/empirical frontier improvement after matching memory and capacity.

#### 7. Dynamically changing parameter use and specialization

- **Mechanism family.** Mixture-of-experts learns a gate/router that assigns inputs or tokens to experts; sparse top-k routing changes active parameters and compute. Historical adaptive mixtures of local experts and hierarchical experts predate sparse Transformer MoEs. Switch simplifies to top-1 routing; balancing losses or assignment procedures regulate expert load. Router gradients can themselves be sparse or densified.
- **Closest architecture.** Adaptive mixtures of local experts (1990–91), sparsely gated MoE, GShard/Switch, BASE balanced assignment, and modern routed Transformers. [Hierarchies of Adaptive Experts (NeurIPS 1991)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1991/hash/59b90e1005a220e2ebc542eb9d950b1e-Abstract.html); [BASE Layers](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/lewis21a.html); [Dense Backpropagation Improves MoE Routing](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v262/panda24a.html).
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Router parameter updates, dense router gradients, balancing/assignment optimization; the expert-selection architecture remains the same.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Auxiliary load-balancing, entropy, specialization, or diversity terms. A new router loss/policy is not a new routing architecture by itself.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Dense model at same active FLOPs; top-k MoE with matched total/active parameters; compare routing policies at equal capacity, communication, and dispatch overhead. Measure specialization, load balance, quality, and wall-clock; report expert collapse and routing instability.
- **Verdict.** Generic dynamic parameter usage, expert specialization, and learned routing are **KILLED — EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. A new routing rule could be a method contribution; architecture novelty needs a new material compute/learning property beyond router policy or auxiliary loss.

#### 8. Local learning, eligibility, neuromodulation, and plastic state

- **Mechanism family.** Hebbian/CHL/EP rules use correlations or phase/activity differences; three-factor rules combine pre/post activity eligibility traces with a broadcast reward/error signal; e-prop gives a recurrent eligibility-trace factorization; differentiable plasticity learns which connections change; neuromodulation gates or scales plastic updates.
- **Modern collision.** Astrocyte-Gated Multi-Timescale Plasticity (AGMP, 2026) explicitly combines fast eligibility, modulatory teaching, a slow astrocyte-like activity gate, and stabilization in an online four-factor rule for continual spiking-network learning. It is a direct collision for a generic “slow local context gates fast plasticity to reduce forgetting” proposal. [AGMP (2026)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12886396/); [three-factor eligibility review](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05219).
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Per-synapse learned rates, meta-learned Hebbian coefficients, online gradient descent, e-prop learning signals, or optimizer state such as momentum.
- **Closest loss-only solution.** Reward prediction, local contrastive objectives, or auxiliary prediction losses can supply a modulatory signal; a new reward/loss does not create new eligibility or gate dynamics.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Same spiking/recurrent topology and stream; compare BPTT/RTRL where affordable, e-prop/three-factor, differentiable plasticity, and AGMP-style multi-timescale gating with matched state and update cost. Measure online learning, delayed-credit accuracy, retention, stability, and locality.
- **Verdict.** Broad local plasticity, eligibility × modulation, fast/slow synaptic state, and astrocyte-like slow gating are **KILLED — EXISTING MECHANISM / EXISTING ARCHITECTURE**. Exact domain implementations may still matter; the general learning-dynamics novelty claim is occupied.

#### 9. Objective or schedule changes mistaken for a new learning architecture

- **Mechanism family.** A new loss, negative-sample construction, denoising target, noise schedule, test-time entropy objective, learning-rate schedule, or number/order of updates may alter training behavior without introducing a new state/update architecture.
- **Closest mechanisms.** Forward-Forward has explicit precedent for positive/negative goodness objectives and forward-only local updates. DDPM/score-SDE provide explicit denoising objectives and reverse stochastic/ODE trajectories. Test-time adaptation already uses entropy, self-supervision, pseudo-labeling, distribution matching, and meta-learned objectives; for example, conjugate pseudo-labels connect test-time losses back to the training loss. [Forward-Forward](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.13345); [DDPM](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2020/hash/4c5bcfec8584af0d967f1ab10179ca4b-Abstract.html); [Protected Test-Time Adaptation](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/9b35a0a20d617dc68ae98a7a57df2f51-Abstract-Conference.html).
- **Closest architecture.** Preserve the same backbone and state machine; compare objective/schedule variants. If the method adds persistent online state or a new execution path, classify and test that component separately.
- **Closest optimizer-only solution.** Same loss with a tuned optimizer/schedule, and same optimizer with a tuned loss. These two controls isolate whether the effect is objective, optimizer, or architecture.
- **Strongest matched baseline.** Factorial matched comparison: fixed architecture × standard loss/optimizer, new loss only, new optimizer/schedule only, and the full method. Match tokens, gradient evaluations, sampling steps, and total compute. Include ablation of any claimed state path.
- **Verdict.** A benefit caused only by a loss, optimizer, or schedule is **KILLED — LOSS/OPTIMIZER/SCHEDULE ONLY** as architecture novelty. That result can still be a valid algorithmic contribution.

### Candidate screen, open questions, and exact next action

| Candidate / claimed property | Closest architecture | Closest optimizer-only solution | Closest loss-only solution | Strongest matched baseline | Verdict / decisive future test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No named new candidate is currently in scope. Generic possible residue: a future, precisely specified update rule that improves online adaptation and retention under fixed memory/compute. This sentence is a search question, not a candidate. | TTT/fast-weight programmers, Titans/ATLAS/MIRAS/HOPE, TTR, differentiable plasticity, AGMP, and the task-specific families above. | MAML plus ordinary inner SGD/Adam, learned optimizers, EWC/GEM/SI, or explicit gradient projection, selected by the exact claim. | TTT/TENT/entropy or self-supervised objectives, local contrastive/Forward-Forward losses, or the candidate’s equivalent objective with ordinary training. | Same backbone/data stream, same persistent-state bytes, parameters, update count, tokens, FLOPs and inference latency; compare to the closest exact architecture and separately ablate the proposed update path. | **Not a survivor.** There is no operation/state rule to test. After one is specified, the smallest decisive test is a single controlled stream with a regime shift and recurrence of an earlier regime; measure adaptation samples, old-regime retention, update/state cost, and compare to the strongest listed baseline. Do not run this generic test before a candidate exists. |

**Interpretation.** The literature demonstrates both sides of the project’s calibrated standard. An optimizer cannot recreate a missing residual edge, attention path, recurrent state, or equilibrium semantics merely by being more expressive; those native organizations changed learning/computation and are accepted architectural mechanisms. But all broad “shorter credit,” “learn at test time,” “fast and slow memory,” “reduce interference,” “local update,” “adaptive depth,” and “dynamic parameter usage” properties now have direct mechanisms or architecture families. No decomposition-only rejection was used where a direct architecture collision sufficed.

**Limits.** This is a collision map, not an exhaustive survey of every optimizer or plasticity paper. The 2025–26 sources are explicitly treated as direct prior art only for the property they state; a unifying framework does not prove equal resource behavior, and an abstract architecture claim cannot be declared equivalent without a matched state/update comparison. Dates and status in the notebook reflect literature visible on 2026-09-27.

**Resources.** Literature and source checking only. No experiments, benchmarks, CPU-heavy jobs, GPU work, or background jobs ran.

**Exact next action.** When a concrete single-model learning-dynamics candidate is available, first write its state, update equation, trigger, and measurable property; classify whether the change is architecture, optimizer, loss, or schedule; then choose the nearest comparator from this collision library. Reject the broad claim if the matched comparator preserves the state transition and claimed learning/resource behavior. Only after that screen leaves a specific residual property should a minimal falsifier be designed.

## AR-141 — Rediscovery filter and novelty gate for automated mechanism search

**Date:** 2026-09-27

**Status:** protocol design only. No candidate search, experiment, benchmark, training run, or compute-heavy job was executed or authorized.
**Question:** How can a small generated learning/update program be rejected as a rediscovery when its source syntax is unusual, while avoiding the false conclusion that every architecture is equivalent to any machine that can simulate it?

### 1. Audit object and threat model

The search unit is a complete, typed, state-transition program, not a name or a single equation. Normalize each candidate into an event graph with these entry points where present:

1. setup(input_metadata) → initial state
2. forward(input, state) → prediction, activations, read trace
3. objective(prediction, target, state) → scalar/vector losses
4. update(state, gradients, activations, inputs, targets, feedback, rng) → new state
5. adapt_or_infer(input, state) → prediction, new state
6. structural_event(state, evidence) → changed topology/state

Represent one transition as:

    (x_t, y_t, theta_t, z_t, h_t, G_t, A_t, E_t, R_t) → (prediction_t, loss_t, theta_(t+1), z_(t+1), h_(t+1), topology_(t+1))

Here theta is ordinary model parameters, z is optimizer/update state, h is persistent activation or memory state, G is gradient/error/target information, A is activation/input information, E is external memory or feedback, and R is explicit randomness. The representation must say which values are unavailable at each phase; otherwise a candidate can silently use labels, future gradients, held-out examples, or a hidden extra forward pass.

The first machine-readable artifact is a **fingerprint**, not a novelty verdict. Keep absent, present, and unknown distinct. Unknown is never treated as absent. The fingerprint describes source-level structure, dynamic behavior, and resource use; it does not require or infer a theoretical proof.

### 2. Machine-oriented collision library

The signatures below are practical recognizers. A match means “known-family collision or mandatory manual review,” not that every implementation in the family is identical. Variants that change epsilon placement, bias correction, reset scope, feedback learning, stochasticity, tensor shape, or update ordering must keep those fields in their fingerprint.

| Family | Recognizable observable signature |
|---|---|
| SGD | No persistent optimizer state; inject current gradient into parameters: theta' = theta - eta * g. |
| Momentum | Persistent velocity; linear decay plus current gradient injection: v' = beta*v + g, theta' = theta - eta*v' (or its explicitly recorded sign/scale variant). |
| Nesterov | Momentum state plus gradient evaluated at a lookahead parameter/state, or the algebraically equivalent corrected momentum update; record lookahead and the point at which the gradient is sampled. |
| RMSProp | Per-coordinate exponential second-moment state s' = rho*s + (1-rho)*g^2; divide current gradient by sqrt(s')+eps (record centering and epsilon placement). |
| Adam family | First and second moment state, exponential updates, bias correction, coordinatewise division by square-root second moment plus epsilon. Mark AMSGrad/max-state, decoupled weight decay (AdamW), rectification, clipping, and epsilon convention separately. |
| Adagrad | Monotone accumulated coordinatewise squared-gradient state S' = S+g^2; scale by 1/(sqrt(S)+eps). |
| Natural gradient | Gradient transformed by inverse/regularized Fisher or an equivalent local information metric; record metric estimator, damping, and solve. |
| K-FAC | Layerwise Kronecker-factored activation and output-gradient covariance state; inverse/root factors precondition the parameter gradient; record factor update cadence and approximation. |
| Shampoo | Per-tensor-axis accumulated gradient Gram matrices and inverse matrix roots; precondition by applying the per-axis root factors. |
| Mirror descent | Update in dual coordinates under a mirror map/Bregman geometry, e.g. grad(psi(theta')) = grad(psi(theta))-eta*g; record map and domain. |
| Exponentiated gradient | Positive/multiplicative update w' proportional to w*exp(-eta*g) with normalization or simplex projection; a recognizable mirror-descent specialization. |
| Proximal update | Gradient step followed by prox_(eta R) or an equivalent joint proximal operator; record regularizer and exact prox. |
| Projected gradient | Gradient step followed by projection Pi_C onto a stated feasible set; record projection metric, frequency, and whether it is exact or approximate. |
| PCGrad | Multiple task gradients; detect pairwise negative inner products and remove the conflicting component by projection before aggregation. |
| OWM | Store activation covariance/subspace information and project subsequent updates into the complement of prior activations to limit interference. |
| GPM | Retain gradient/representation subspaces (often bases extracted from activations); project new task updates away from protected bases. |
| EWC | Store parameter importance (usually Fisher-diagonal) and reference parameters; penalize quadratic displacement from the reference during later-task learning. |
| Eligibility traces | Persistent decayed local derivative/feature trace e_t = lambda*e_(t-1)+local_signal_t; later scalar TD/reward/error multiplies that trace to update parameters. Record trace horizon and modulator source. |
| Hebbian / Oja | Correlation-driven local update such as Delta w ~ y*x; Oja adds a norm-stabilizing term such as -y^2*w. No global loss gradient is required. |
| STDP-like | Synaptic update is a function of pre/post spike timing difference, typically signed exponentials on the two sides of zero; record event windows, traces, and reset behavior. |
| Three-/four-factor plasticity | Local eligibility or pre/post factors are multiplied by a global reward/error/neuromodulator; a fourth factor adds another local/context/modulatory variable. Record exact factor provenance, delay, and scope. |
| Reverse-mode AD / backpropagation | Reverse traversal of the forward computation graph applies vector-Jacobian products to propagate a scalar/vector loss cotangent to parameters and activations; shared intermediate cotangents accumulate at fan-out. Record tape/checkpointing, graph truncation, and whether the update is exact or approximate. |
| Feedback alignment | Backward hidden credit uses fixed random feedback matrices rather than the forward weights' transpose; forward weights still learn from that approximate credit. |
| Direct feedback alignment | Output error is projected directly to each hidden layer by fixed random feedback matrices; bypasses layer-by-layer transposed Jacobian transport. |
| Target propagation | Construct layerwise targets through learned approximate inverse maps or target-difference rules; update activations/weights toward those targets rather than ordinary end-to-end backprop alone. |
| Synthetic gradients | A learned module predicts a cut-point gradient/error from local state; the upstream block updates without waiting for the true downstream gradient. Mark prediction target, training signal, and interface location. |
| Predictive coding | Maintain latent neuronal states and prediction-error units; iterative local inference reduces mismatch between each state and top-down/bottom-up predictions, with local weight updates. |
| Equilibrium propagation | Settle an energy network in a free phase and a target-nudged phase; parameter update is a difference of phase statistics/correlations, often scaled by the nudge strength. |
| Forward-Forward | Layer-local goodness scores are increased for positive data and decreased for negative data; local forward-only objectives replace a global backpropagated loss signal. |
| Fast weights | Separate slow parameters from rapidly updated sequence/task-local matrix/vector state; write to fast state from recent activations and read it content-addressably in later forward steps. |
| Differentiable plasticity | Learn slow base weights plus plasticity coefficients; an eligibility/Hebbian trace changes effective weights online, and outer gradients train the plasticity rule. |
| Meta-learning | Outer state/parameters are optimized across tasks so that an inner learner adapts; fingerprint task boundary, inner update, outer objective, and whether gradients pass through adaptation. |
| Learned optimizer | A learned recurrent or coordinatewise rule reads gradients/parameters/history, stores hidden optimizer state, and emits parameter updates; the optimizer itself is trained across optimizees/tasks. |
| MAML-like adaptation | Shared initialization is updated on support data by one or more gradient steps; outer loss differentiates through the inner adaptation to improve query performance. |
| Test-time training (TTT) | At inference/test time, update model or auxiliary parameters using an unlabeled/self-supervised objective on test inputs; record reset/stream scope and whether predictions occur before/after update. |
| Test-time memory | Write test-time keys/values or latent records into persistent state and retrieve them to condition subsequent predictions; record addressing, write policy, reset boundary, and label access. |
| DEQ / implicit learning | Define hidden state as a fixed point z*=f_theta(z*,x); solve by iteration/root finding and differentiate through an implicit Jacobian solve rather than an explicitly stored layer stack. |
| Neural ODE / adjoint | Evolve continuous hidden state by dz/dt=f_theta(z,t); numerical integration controls the forward path and an adjoint/continuous sensitivity equation computes gradients. |
| Residual / highway paths | Add identity bypass y=x+F(x) or a learned gated carry/transform mixture; expose the direct state and gradient path and its gate. |
| Recurrence / gating | Persistent hidden state is fed from one time/depth step to the next; gates control write, retain, expose, or reset of that state (e.g. GRU/LSTM-style). |
| Attention | Compute content-dependent query-key scores, normalize them, and use them to mix value states; record token/state scope, causal mask, head structure, and whether weights are learned or data-routed. |
| Mixture-of-experts routing | Router scores inputs/tokens and dispatches top-k or dense traffic to expert-specific parameters; record capacity, overflow/drop behavior, balancing auxiliary losses, and whether routing gradients are hard or soft. |
| Structural growth / freezing | Runtime event adds/removes/duplicates/freezes parameter blocks, rules, units, experts, or edges on a criterion; record trigger, object birth/death, inheritance, and later plasticity. |
| Cascade-Correlation | Train candidate hidden units to correlate with residual error, add the best unit to the network, then freeze installed weights while training the output layer. |
| ART | Compare input/category match to a vigilance threshold; resonance updates a category, mismatch triggers reset/search and possibly a new category. |
| Continual-backprop / reinitialization | Track age/utility/activation or contribution; periodically select low-utility units/weights for reinitialization while preserving or restoring useful function. Record utility statistic, schedule, and state reset. |

#### Collision rule encoding

Each row can be compiled into a template predicate over the fingerprint. A predicate should return one of match, near_match, no_match, or unknown, plus the fields that caused the result. Example:

~~~yaml
family: momentum
requires:
  state:
    - {role: optimizer_velocity, lifetime: across_updates}
  update:
    - {reads: [optimizer_velocity, current_gradient]}
    - {writes: [optimizer_velocity, parameters]}
  operators:
    - linear_decay
    - gradient_injection
  order:
    - velocity_update_before_parameter_update
allows:
  parameterized_fields: [beta, learning_rate, gradient_scale, sign_convention]
review_if:
  - state_is_reset_per_example
  - velocity_is_nonlinear_or_input_conditioned
~~~

The library must record family variants, not only a single canonical textbook equation. A candidate can match multiple families (e.g. Adam plus weight decay); a composite match is still a rediscovery unless the combination creates a separately stated material architectural property.

### 3. Layered equivalence screen

The levels below are ordered by cost. Passing a level does not prove novelty. A positive match can reject or route the candidate; a failure to match only means “continue.”

#### Level A — sound syntactic canonicalization

Parse the generated program into typed SSA/event-graph IR. Before hashing or matching:

- alpha-rename temporaries and state slots by first-use/role, independent of source names;
- constant-fold exact constants and remove identities, dead assignments, dead state, unreachable branches, and unused outputs;
- inline trivial aliases and canonicalize update equations into explicit old-state/current-input/new-state form;
- canonicalize exact commutative/associative expressions only under a declared mathematical domain where the rewrite is sound;
- normalize scalar products and expose parameterized scales (e.g. eta * (2*g) as an effective scale) while retaining a witness mapping to the original parameters;
- identify duplicated state registers with identical initialization, reads, and writes;
- canonicalize equivalent tensor reshapes/indexing only when they preserve axis and broadcast semantics;
- record dependency edges from every write to every read, including time index and phase.

Do **not** silently reorder floating-point additions, stochastic operations, clipping, norm, projection, quantization, or stateful calls. Do not cancel or absorb an epsilon across a square root, denominator, clipping threshold, regularizer, or weight decay. Do not assume a rescaling is equivalent when it changes a constraint set, stability region, precision behavior, or resource count. If exact symbolic equivalence cannot be established under the candidate IR semantics, keep both forms and mark the rewrite as heuristic.

The output is a canonical IR hash plus a list of applied rewrites/proofs. Exact A-level identity with a library template is a direct collision. A-level non-identity is not evidence of novelty.

#### Level B — behavioral trajectory fingerprints

Run only as part of a future authorized search. This section defines the protocol; **it was not run**.

Drive each candidate and library reference with identical, exogenous signal tapes so that the update rule is tested without task-performance confounds. At minimum use:

- zero, impulse, constant, sign-reversed, alternating, sparse, and coordinate-basis gradients;
- isotropic, diagonal ill-conditioned, rotated ill-conditioned, correlated, and heavy-tailed gradient sequences;
- piecewise stationary and regime-switching gradient sequences;
- activation/input tapes independent of gradients, then tapes with controlled correlation;
- delayed scalar feedback / reward against stored local eligibility signals;
- reset, continuation, and repeated-task traces to expose state persistence and interference;
- parameter-scale, gradient-scale, coordinate-permutation, and orthogonal-rotation transforms.

Compare complete trajectories, not only final predictions or loss: parameters, every persistent state register, update norms/angles, forward outputs, read/write traces, and topology at every step. For a proposed state reparameterization, require an explicit state map and check that it commutes with initialization, every tested transition, outputs, reset, and resource accounting.

For deterministic programs use paired fixed traces and declared tolerances: exact equality for discrete states/topology; floating comparison with preregistered absolute/relative tolerances for numeric state; also report max normalized trajectory deviation so a single large state mismatch is not averaged away. For stochastic programs, first couple identical random tapes; then compare output/state distributions over preregistered tapes, not just means. A match on finite probes is a probable collision, not a proof; a mismatch is a witness that these implementations differ on that trace, not proof that the rule is novel.

AutoML-Zero already used a fast functional-equivalence fingerprint: it recorded predictions after 10 training and 10 validation steps on fixed examples, truncated/hashed the trace, and reused scores to remove duplicates. That is a useful throughput filter but is too weak for this gate because it can miss hidden-state differences that affect later transitions and can collide after truncation. Preserve the distinction explicitly. [AutoML-Zero, §3.2](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a/real20a.pdf)

#### Level C — structural and resource fingerprint comparison

Compare candidate to each behavioral match along the following axes; do not collapse these to “same function”:

- state-slot count, shape, dtype/precision, bytes, initialization, lifetime, reset boundary, and sharing scope;
- which signal each update reads: global gradient, local gradient, activation, input, target, synthetic gradient, reward/modulator, previous state, or external-memory read;
- gradient path and Jacobian dependence, including whether forward-weight transposes are required, fixed, learned, approximated, or bypassed;
- state update schedule, trigger, ordering, delayed writes, number of inner/outer/test-time transitions, and whether state changes before prediction;
- normalization, bias correction, clipping, projection/prox, constraint solving, fixed-point/root solving, and numerical tolerances;
- memory address generation, read/write timing, capacity, eviction, and persistence across examples/tasks;
- fast/slow parameter split, learned update policy, meta-gradient route, and train/inference asymmetry;
- parameter/topology birth, deletion, freezing, unfreezing, cloning, and reset semantics;
- forward/backward/optimizer/solver FLOPs, passes, peak activation/state memory, latency, and communication scope.

A same-state-transition match with equivalent resource behavior is an architecture collision. A difference in source code, module labels, or storage layout alone is a parameterization/implementation difference. A real structural difference proceeds only if it is the source of a precisely claimed, material property.

#### Level D — mandatory manual prior-art search

Only candidates that remain unresolved after A–C reach literature review. The reviewer must:

1. State the candidate as STATE + OPERATION + WRITE/TRANSITION RULE + GUARANTEE, including phase, trigger, and information available at that phase.
2. Search the exact equation/algorithm name and synonyms for every distinctive state variable, operator, signal path, and update ordering; search both modern terminology and historical vocabulary.
3. Search the relevant machine families from early cybernetics/symbolic AI, optimization, control, PL/AD, continual learning, neural plasticity, meta-learning, online learning, and hardware/physical computing.
4. Read the nearest primary paper(s), not only abstracts or review taxonomy; inspect appendices and code when needed to resolve an equation or state semantic.
5. Include direct architecture prior art as well as optimizer/loss/schedule reductions; compare state, transition, learning signal, guarantee, information flow, and resource scaling in a side-by-side table.
