### 7. Automated-discovery failure modes and calibration

1. **Rediscovery in an unfamiliar encoding.** AutoML-Zero's generic operation search rediscovered two-layer networks trained by backpropagation/gradient descent; its evolved candidates also surfaced familiar modern ingredients such as normalized gradients, weight averaging, bilinear interactions, and dropout-like behavior. The source-level collision is precisely why code novelty is not mechanism novelty. [Real et al., AutoML-Zero (ICML 2020)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a)
2. **Finite fingerprint mistaken for equivalence proof.** AutoML-Zero's fixed 10-train/10-validation prediction hash was an efficient population duplicate filter, not a proof over internal state trajectories. Our gate extends the observable object to the full state/write trace and keeps the finite-probe limitation explicit. [AutoML-Zero PDF, §3.2](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a/real20a.pdf)
3. **One-task memorization / evaluator leakage.** AutoML-Zero reports a single-search-task case that evolved the teacher prediction function and hard-coded its weights. This is a direct control for task-specific memorization: task diversity, held-out task families, limits on persistent constants/state, and locked confirmation are mandatory. [AutoML-Zero PDF, §4.1](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/real20a/real20a.pdf)
4. **Search grammar creates the apparent discovery.** A vocabulary of primitives, allowed state, update phase, and interface determines what can emerge. Report the full grammar and run known-family positive controls; do not describe “from scratch” as absence of inductive bias.
5. **Validation becomes training through adaptive selection.** Thousands of candidates repeatedly queried against a validation set can overfit it even when each individual evaluation is a legitimate holdout estimate. Use a locked final split and fixed query budget; standard holdout reuse is not safe under adaptive candidate generation. [Dwork et al., Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)
6. **Best-of-many and researcher selection bias.** FunSearch states that stochasticity led it to run several experiments for some problems and report the best result; its method also uses a scoring evaluator, a program database, and sometimes a known greedy skeleton. These choices can be appropriate for discovery, but the final claim must disclose the search budget, seed selection, skeleton, evaluator, and confirmation procedure. Its verified combinatorial constructions/heuristics are not evidence that an unrelated learning mechanism is novel. [Romera-Paredes et al., FunSearch (Nature 2024)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06924-6)
7. **Objective gaming / benchmark exploit.** Candidate code can exploit a proxy metric, data ordering, finite generator, or evaluator artifact without implementing the intended property. Audit high-scoring candidates on adversarial traces, enforce causal data access, compare intermediate transitions, and preserve a distinct confirmation evaluator.
8. **Overtuning the search/evaluation budget.** Hyperparameter and algorithm searches can tune to noisy validation estimates; recent work studies overtuning in HPO directly. This motivates equal tuning budgets and a confirmation set unavailable during search. [Schneider et al., Overtuning in Hyperparameter Optimization (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19540)
9. **A real algorithmic discovery is not automatically a new architecture.** AlphaTensor and AlphaEvolve show that structured search can find new, correct algorithms or improve resource-specific algorithms, while FunSearch can produce new verifiable mathematical constructions. This is evidence that automated search can discover genuine results, not a waiver of the separate architecture/prior-art test. [AlphaTensor (Nature 2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05172-4); [AlphaEvolve (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131)

**Interpretation:** Automated discovery is not inherently a rediscovery machine; it can find valid new algorithms. The gate should therefore neither promote a high score as novelty nor reject a candidate because its parts are computable. It must ask what exact state transition is new, what established family is closest, and whether the alleged learning/resource property survives matched substitution.

### 8. Novelty decision tree and allowed classifications

Apply this order. Stop at the first decisive rejection, but preserve any useful empirical result as an algorithmic observation.

1. **Can the candidate be parsed and audited?** If not, reject it as unverifiable; no novelty classification.
2. **Does Level A match a library rule or canonical equation?** If yes, classify it as a rediscovered optimizer, learning rule, or architecture according to the matched object. A combined match must be described as a system/pipeline unless its native organization adds a separately stated material architectural property.
3. **Do Levels B+C show the same transition/state organization or a commuting state reparameterization?** If yes, reject the corresponding primitive/architecture claim as an existing mechanism/architecture. A finite behavioral match alone is a collision flag requiring review, not an equivalence theorem.
4. **Is the only difference a parameterization, initialization, loss, optimizer, hyperparameter, schedule, clipping/normalization choice, or added capacity/state?** Classify it as a new parameterization, loss-only, optimizer-only, schedule-only, or capacity/state scaling. It may be an interesting empirical rule, but it is not promoted as a new architecture unless a distinct native state/update organization and non-preserved property remain.
5. **Does a matched known baseline recover the measured property?** If yes, kill that property as optimizer-restorable, loss-restorable, schedule-restorable, or pipeline-preserved. If it wins only because of more compute, data, state, parameters, lookahead, or ensemble averaging, label it benchmark exploit or unmatched comparison and reject the novelty claim.
6. **Does ablation/replacement of the claimed organization remove the property under matched budgets?** If no, label KILLED — NO MATERIAL ARCHITECTURAL PROPERTY. If yes, the property has a causal mechanism-removal witness; this still does not establish novelty.
7. **Does the property repeat on preregistered seeds and locked task families with uncertainty/effect thresholds fixed in advance?** If no, label interesting empirical rule / unconfirmed result, not a candidate.
8. **Does fresh Level-D review find direct historical or modern prior art?** If yes, label it a rediscovered architecture or the more precise existing-family classification. If no source is found but the search is incomplete, leave it unresolved; absence is not a pass.
9. **Only after all preceding gates:** use possible architecture candidate when the organization is new and the material property is not preserved by the strongest ordinary decomposition; use possible primitive candidate only when the same-operation/state-transition search also leaves an uncovered operation. The word “candidate” is mandatory; it is not a breakthrough claim.

Minimum pass conditions before an architecture label: not explained by known optimizer/loss/schedule; explicit novel state/update organization; removal loses the effect; strongest matched baseline fails to recover it at matched resources; fresh historical and current literature search finds no substantially same architecture; repeated confirmation over seeds/tasks. A single benchmark win is never sufficient.

### 9. Compact implementation procedure

~~~text
audit(candidate):
  sandbox_check(candidate)
  ir = parse_to_typed_event_graph(candidate)
  if ir is invalid or undeclared reads exist:
      return UNVERIFIABLE_OR_LEAKING

  canonical = sound_canonicalize(ir)
  fp = extract_fingerprint(canonical, runtime_counters, state_lifetimes)
  A = match_canonical_templates(canonical, collision_library)
  B = compare_paired_traces(candidate, known_controls, diagnostic_tapes)
  C = compare_state_signal_order_and_resource(fp, known_controls)

  if A contains exact known-family match:
      return REDISCOVERED_FAMILY, evidence=(A, fp)
  if B and C strongly match a family:
      return LIKELY_COLLISION_REQUIRES_LITERATURE_REVIEW, evidence=(B, C, fp)
  if candidate differs only by objective/optimizer/schedule/parameterization/capacity:
      return NON_ARCHITECTURE_RESULT, subtype=classify_difference(...)

  property = freeze_claim_and_metric(candidate)
  controls = select_strongest_architecture_optimizer_loss_schedule_controls(fp)
  if matched_control_recovers(property) or mechanism_removal_preserves(property):
      return ARCHITECTURE_CLAIM_KILLED
  if not replicated_on_locked_tasks_and_seeds(property):
      return EMPIRICAL_RULE_UNCONFIRMED
  literature = run_documented_primary_source_search(candidate, fp, property)
  if literature.has_direct_collision:
      return REDISCOVERED_ARCHITECTURE
  if literature.incomplete or any_required_field_unknown:
      return UNRESOLVED
  return POSSIBLE_ARCHITECTURE_CANDIDATE
~~~

The implementation should emit the canonical IR, fingerprint, probe trace IDs, collision-template hits, full compute/data counters, baseline specification, literature-query log, and final decision reason. Do not return a scalar “novelty score”: a weighted score lets a strong benchmark result compensate for a direct prior-art collision, which is not acceptable.

### 10. Disposition and next action

- **Novelty gate:** specified sufficiently to implement at the schema/template/probe level; still requires a frozen candidate grammar and exact runtime data-access contract before any run.
- **Candidate status:** none. This work designs a classifier and evidence gate; it does not claim a new optimizer, architecture, or primitive.
- **Experiments:** none run. Search, benchmark, training, and CPU/GPU work remain unauthorized.
- **Next action:** convert the schema and family table into versioned machine-readable templates; create known-family positive controls and blinded syntax aliases; freeze diagnostic traces, resource budgets, confirmation tasks, metrics, and holdout policy in a preregistration. Obtain explicit owner authorization before executing the search.


## AR-147 — OMD-0 T1 RET hostile prior-art and known-machine audit

Date: 2026-09-28
Scope: T1 retention under hidden nonstationary reuse, before any OMD compute. This is a target-level audit, not a proposal for a cache architecture or primitive.

### 1. Verdict and scope boundary

**SURVIVES AS OMD TARGET**

This verdict means only that the search target has not been closed by a verified, same-scope compact solution or architecture. It does not say that T1 is novel, that the proposed discovery instrument is a candidate, or that an extracted policy would count as an architecture. There is no learned mechanism yet.

The exact workload target is materially narrower than generic caching: capacity 16–32, hidden changes among rank drift, working-set phases, scans, loops longer than capacity, bursts, and periodic reuse, with no item IDs or regime labels supplied to the learner. The mechanism to be searched would attach two evolving state values to each resident slot and one global value, update them on hit/tick/miss events, and choose the minimum-scored resident on a miss. A hit event indexed by slot is already per-object feedback: the slot is the object’s current address in the cache even if semantic IDs are absent.

No audited reference implements that full contract and establishes robust performance on the stated held-out mixture. That is a narrow gap in scope, not a positive novelty result. Nearly every constituent operation and the broader train-to-compact-policy workflow have direct prior art. If an extracted rule only reduces misses, it is first a new cache policy / algorithm claim. It becomes an architecture candidate only if a material property of its state/update organization survives the controls in section 5.

### 2. Direct prior-art collision map

| Existing mechanism | Exact collision with T1 | Scope limit that remains |
|---|---|---|
| RLR (HPCA 2021) | Uses reinforcement-learning analysis to identify important cache features and derive a lower-cost replacement rule; the derived policy avoids carrying program-counter information through the datapath. This directly occupies learned policy → inspect → compact rule. [Paper record and DOI](https://experts.umn.edu/en/publications/designing-a-cost-effective-cache-replacement-policy-using-machine-learning/) | Hardware cache and benchmark workload setup; not the anonymous two-slot-state controller on this six-regime synthetic mixture. |
| Glider (MICRO 2019) | Trains an attention-LSTM offline, analyzes it, extracts a compact control-flow-history feature, then deploys an online SVM/perceptron-style predictor. The paper explicitly presents analysis of a powerful model as a way to derive a cheaper cache policy. [Primary paper](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~lin/papers/micro19c1.pdf) | The compact rule uses PC/control-flow features and is not a transplant of the proposed no-ID recurrent state. Still a direct methodological collision. |
| Genetic insertion/promotion vectors | Searches a finite priority-update program: a 17-entry vector describes insertion and promotion behavior, genetic search tunes it, and set dueling selects among vectors. This is compact event-driven rank-state search plus online policy selection. [Primary paper](https://people.engr.tamu.edu/djimenez/taco/pdfs/15-jimenez.pdf) | Static vector family and hardware setting; does not establish mixed-regime generalization for a recurrent state machine. |
| GRUMA (2025) | The title explicitly combines a GRU and multi-head attention for cache replacement. This is the closest named recurrent-cache collision and blocks any broad claim that recurrence in replacement is new. [DOI record](https://doi.org/10.1145/3729706.3729815) | The full paper was not accessible in this audit, so its state granularity, event updates, workload-switch coverage, and extraction behavior are unverified. Do not treat it as an exact kill without inspecting the paper. |
| LearnedCache (2026), 3L-Cache (FAST 2025) | LearnedCache trains a small perceptron to estimate page reuse time and deploys it in Linux. 3L-Cache uses online learned object-level eviction/value prediction at scale. These are strong learned-ranker baselines, beyond a generic GBM. [LearnedCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26168), [3L-Cache](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/fast25-zhou-wenbin.pdf) | They use object/page observations and features unlike T1’s strict anonymous event interface. |
| ARC and CAR | Maintain compact per-object recency/frequency evidence and a global adaptive parameter. ARC uses ghost-history feedback to balance recency and frequency and is explicitly self-tuning; CAR transfers this organization to clock state. These already couple local retention evidence to a shared regime-sensitive control. [ARC](https://research.ibm.com/publications/arc-a-self-tuning-low-overhead-replacement-cache), [CAR](https://research.ibm.com/publications/car-clock-with-adaptive-replacement) | Their inputs and ghost structures differ; they do not cover every hidden workload or guarantee optimality. |
| S3-FIFO and SIEVE | Compact event-driven per-object metadata already changes future eviction: S3-FIFO uses small/main/ghost FIFO queues and a small reuse counter; SIEVE uses a per-object visited bit and persistent hand. They target one-hit scans, lazy promotion, quick demotion, and practical scalability. [S3-FIFO](https://www.pdl.cmu.edu/PDL-FTP/Storage/FIFOqueues-SOSP23_abs.shtml), [SIEVE](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/zhang-yazhuo) | Fixed queue/bit rules do not implement the precise proposed recurrence. They are mandatory controls for its scan and reuse signals. |
| EVA and LHD | Both estimate object value from observed history and evict by a derived score. EVA models hit/lifetime distributions; LHD estimates expected hit density with conditional probabilities and adapts online. This directly occupies “approximate a value function then argmin.” [EVA](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~beckmann/publications/papers/2017.hpca.eva.pdf), [LHD](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi18/presentation/beckmann) | Their feature/histogram state is richer and usually object-aware; resource-matched versions remain to be built if T1 proceeds. |
| LeCaR, CACHEUS, H-MC | LeCaR mixes LRU/LFU experts with online regret feedback; CACHEUS combines complementary recency/frequency/scan/churn-resistant policies; H-MC (2026) formalizes no-regret LRU/LFU mixing with optimal switching cost. This occupies online expert adaptation, including a stronger comparator than a fixed per-regime selector. [LeCaR](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/hotstorage18/hotstorage18-paper-vietri.pdf), [CACHEUS](https://www.usenix.org/conference/fast21/presentation/rodriguez), [H-MC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07566) | H-MC’s expert set is LRU/LFU, and no result here proves optimal tracking for this six-regime family. |
| PolicySmith, CacheQuery, CacheCraft | PolicySmith uses LLM-guided code search/evolution to synthesize deployable cache heuristics; CacheQuery learns deterministic hardware replacement automata through membership queries and program synthesis; CacheCraft evolves compact KV-eviction scorers and ablates scorer vs structure. Automated compact rule search and extraction are already occupied methods. [PolicySmith](https://daehyeok.kim/assets/papers/policysmith-hotnets25.pdf), [CacheQuery](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09770), [CacheCraft](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14555) | PolicySmith optimizes per trace and has not demonstrated a single extracted rule robust on this hidden mixture. CacheCraft targets attention-derived KV retention rather than general object-cache recurrence. |
| S4-FIFO / LAH and SCION (2026) | LAH/S4-FIFO learns cache-level control settings for an established S3-FIFO datapath from workload/hit-position features. SCION selects among known cache policies using a small workload fingerprint and epochal adaptation. These are strong decompositions for global switching without placing a new learned object model on every decision. [LAH/S4-FIFO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27975), [SCION](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01055) | The published evaluations use production traces and their own feature contracts; abrupt hidden transitions within a short C=16–32 cache remain untested here. |

Prior-art conclusion: the broad components “online event state per resident object,” “global adaptive reuse control,” “argmin priority eviction,” “learned cache value,” “expert selection,” and “train/inspect/simplify or synthesize a compact cache rule” are all occupied. A future output with one of these semantics in new notation is rediscovery. The exact no-ID, tiny-state, held-out-switching contract is not verified as already implemented.

### 3. Compact optimality and closure

No audited result proves an optimal or near-optimal compact rule for the full T1 contract at capacity 16–32.

Important scoped results:

- Least Profit Rate (LPR) gives a constructive priority policy that is gain-optimal for a specified Hidden Markov Reference Model when its generator parameters are known; its score can be computed from those model parameters. This is a strong model-conditioned compact solution, not a solution to unknown drift and held-out hidden semi-Markov switches. [Bilardi and Versaci, arXiv:1109.6643](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6643)
- Static-frequency caching is asymptotically optimal for large caches under a broad semi-Markov-modulated request model, with an LRU near-optimality corollary under additional generalized-Zipf assumptions. This does not establish near-optimality for capacity 16–32 or a finite sequence of abruptly changing, held-out regimes. [Jelenković and Radovanović, 2009 paper](https://www.ee.columbia.edu/~predrag/mypub/frequency2009.pdf)
- ARC/CAR and online learning-to-cache provide adaptive practical policies; they do not give a uniform optimum for all six proposed regimes.
- A belief-MDP optimum is not a closure result unless it yields a deployable compact rule with the same information and resource contract.

Therefore, lack of an exact optimum keeps the target empirically open; it does not itself support architecture novelty. Any pilot would have to compare finite-C trajectories rather than cite asymptotic or model-known guarantees.

### 4. Strongest ordinary decomposition: D1–D5 plus additions

| Decomposition | Strongest form and how it could reproduce the signal | Audit status |
|---|---|---|
| D1: oracle best policy per regime | Select the best library policy with access to the true current regime. This is an unattainable upper bound and a diagnostic, not a deployable comparator. Include per-phase and transition costs. | Does not kill T1 by itself. |
| D2: online expert mixing | Run shadow states for ARC, CAR, LRU, LFU/LRFU, 2Q, CLOCK-Pro, SIEVE, S3-FIFO, LIRS, TinyLFU, LHD, and EVA; use LeCaR/CACHEUS/H-MC-style weights, fixed-share or tracking-the-best-expert, change-point restart, and switching-cost penalty. This reproduces a global regime signal as changing expert weights. Match/report shadow-state bytes and work. | Strongest policy selector. Compare both unrestricted and budget-matched versions. |
| D3: feature ranker trained on MIN | Train an online or offline ranker on the same traces with age, decayed frequency, interarrival/reuse distance, hit/miss and scan/burst indicators, ghost returns, queue/slot position, per-policy victim ranks, and short-window hit-position histograms. Include LRB/HALP/3L-Cache-style reuse/value prediction, not just GBM. | Stronger than the handoff’s original GBM proposal. |
| D4: program search | Search the same event interface over priority-update vectors, bounded FSMs, integer/real score recurrences, and policy callbacks; include GA insertion/promotion vectors, PolicySmith, and synthesis from a DSL. Distill/compile the winner to plain code. | Directly tests whether OMD contributes anything beyond search-space and optimizer choice. |
| D5: EVA/LHD-style value model | Estimate conditional expected hit density or reuse value per resident item; combine age-conditioned histograms with a shared calibration state, then evict the lowest estimate. | Strong value-function explanation for any score rule. |
| D6: learned cache-level controller | S4-FIFO/LAH or SCION-like controller uses cache-level hit-position, reuse, scan and burst summaries to adjust a small parameter set or select a policy, with epochal updates and hysteresis. | Important baseline for global state g and hidden regime change. |
| D7: known-source model oracle | When source parameters are exposed, run LPR or the best model-conditioned policy. Keep separate from the unknown-parameter online comparison. | Theoretical diagnostic only; not a fair blind baseline. |

A learned T1 rule can therefore reduce to (a) an expert selector, (b) a per-slot ranker or reuse-value estimate, (c) a global interpolation/gating parameter for familiar recency/frequency/queue heuristics, (d) a small finite-state replacement controller, or (e) a searched policy in an event-driven DSL. Low agreement with individual library policies is not evidence against these reductions: a new score may disagree while matching a mixture’s retention behavior or achieving only a loss-function/parameterization change.

### 5. Is OMD worth targeting?

The target remains narrowly worth a later, small falsification pilot because the full hidden-switch mixture, short capacity, slot-indexed anonymous updates, and two-local-state/one-global-state budget were not found together in a direct prior-art implementation. This is an opportunity to test a candidate policy class, not a presumption that a new architecture will emerge.

Reasons the chance is low:

1. RLR and Glider already establish the core OMD story—learn a cache decision rule, analyze the learned model, and derive a lower-cost deployable rule.
2. GA-evolved insertion/promotion vectors, PolicySmith, CacheQuery, and CacheCraft already search or infer compact cache policies.
3. ARC/CAR, SIEVE/S3-FIFO, and learned hit-density/value methods already possess local event updates and a global or shared adaptation path.
4. S4-FIFO/SCION make a natural global-state decomposition; a hidden g may just be a cache-level controller or expert gate.
5. Per-slot transition state is standard mutable priority metadata. A non-linear update map alone is not an architectural property.
6. The proposed tick callback updates every resident slot on each request. Unless it admits an exact lazy-clock representation, the learner pays O(C) recurrent updates per request. Compare against ordinary lazy age/decay representations and include update work in resource accounting.
7. The OMD model may be non-identifiable: hidden-state permutations and continuous reparameterizations can preserve behavior; trajectories constrain only visited regions. A symbolic fit over those trajectories may not identify causal transition semantics.
8. The slot-indexed hit signal is identity by location. The claim is anonymous semantic IDs, not absence of object-specific access.
9. “S1 beats the best single policy,” “S2 has low policy agreement,” and a g-dependent bifurcation are insufficient. A mixture, ranker, controller, or arbitrary score can satisfy all three without architecture novelty.
10. If the extracted policy is a new, robust cache replacement algorithm but ordinary state/ranker/expert baselines recover its measured property, classify it as an interesting policy/system result, not a new architecture.

Before any compute, the independent lane should pin down exact state observability, tick semantics, initialization/reset, slot permutation invariance, and whether the extracted code can reproduce the neural controller on counterfactual state/event interventions. No OMD-1 is frozen by this audit.

### 6. Nearest-miss family spot-check

- **Zero-delay low-rate coding:** Not a stronger open OMD target. Witsenhausen’s structural result already reduces finite-horizon coding for a kth-order Markov source to the last k source symbols plus receiver memory; later work formulates zero-delay coding as stochastic control and gives convergent RL/near-optimal finite-memory policies under predictor-stability assumptions. This direction is more mathematically occupied, though the cited results are scoped to Markov-source/channel models. [Witsenhausen 1979](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1979.tb02263.x), [Cregg, Alajaji and Yüksel 2024](https://mast.queensu.ca/~communications/Papers/cay-acc24.pdf)
- **Congestion control:** More directly closed as a learn/search/distill target. Remy generates deployable congestion-control algorithms from network/trafﬁc models and objectives; PolicySmith searches deployable cache and congestion-control policies; SymbolicPCC trains a neural TCP controller and distills it into symbolic rules. These leave a stronger prior-art footprint for policy generation and extraction than T1. [Remy](https://conferences.sigcomm.org/sigcomm/2013/papers/sigcomm/p123.pdf), [PolicySmith](https://daehyeok.kim/assets/papers/policysmith-hotnets25.pdf), [SymbolicPCC](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/file/4574ac9854d4defe3bf119d07b817084-Paper-Conference.pdf)

These spot checks support T1 as the least-closed of these targets, not as a likely survivor.

### 7. Final classification and boundary

**SURVIVES AS OMD TARGET**

- Directly occupied: event-updated cache priority, adaptive per-object history, shared/global control, rank/value eviction, learned or evolved cache policies, teacher-to-compact-policy analysis, and automated compact-policy search.
- Not established closed: one tiny ID-free recurrent controller with two local state values and one global value that robustly handles the exact hidden six-regime trace family at C=16–32, after comparison against D2–D7.
- No architecture or primitive is proposed. A future rule must be named and formalized only after it exists and survives the strongest matched decomposition.
- Recommendation: keep the target eligible for a bounded independent identifiability/extraction audit, then consider only the smallest CPU pilot if that audit finds the result identifiable and causal. Do not launch search or freeze OMD-1 on this audit alone.

### 8. Sources checked

Primary or official sources used above: [RLR paper record](https://experts.umn.edu/en/publications/designing-a-cost-effective-cache-replacement-policy-using-machine-learning/), [Glider](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~lin/papers/micro19c1.pdf), [genetic promotion vectors](https://people.engr.tamu.edu/djimenez/taco/pdfs/15-jimenez.pdf), [ARC](https://research.ibm.com/publications/arc-a-self-tuning-low-overhead-replacement-cache), [S3-FIFO](https://www.pdl.cmu.edu/PDL-FTP/Storage/FIFOqueues-SOSP23_abs.shtml), [SIEVE](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/zhang-yazhuo), [EVA](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~beckmann/publications/papers/2017.hpca.eva.pdf), [LHD](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi18/presentation/beckmann), [PolicySmith](https://daehyeok.kim/assets/papers/policysmith-hotnets25.pdf), [CacheQuery](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09770), [CacheCraft](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14555), [LAH/S4-FIFO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27975), [SCION](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01055), [LPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6643), [correlated semi-Markov static-frequency result](https://www.ee.columbia.edu/~predrag/mypub/frequency2009.pdf), [zero-delay coding](https://mast.queensu.ca/~communications/Papers/cay-acc24.pdf), [Remy](https://conferences.sigcomm.org/sigcomm/2013/papers/sigcomm/p123.pdf), and [SymbolicPCC](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/file/4574ac9854d4defe3bf119d07b817084-Paper-Conference.pdf). GRUMA’s DOI metadata was checked, but its full text was inaccessible; its exact coverage remains open.

## AR-148 — Coupled attention sinks and massive activations: hostile no-compute audit

**Scope and status (2026-09-28).** This is an anomaly, not an architecture candidate. I checked whether its proposed training-time causal loop needs a new computational mechanism. Verdict: **KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS** for architecture discovery. The verdict is a synthesis of scoped primary results and standard Transformer derivatives, not a claim that every onset layer can already be predicted quantitatively. No code, training, benchmarking or GPU use.

### Direct collision map

| Putative part of anomaly | Strongest primary collision and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Softmax/no-op sink and implicit bias | [When Attention Sink Emerges](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.10781) finds key-heavy, value-light sinks; a learned key with zero value relocates the sink, while unnormalized sigmoid attention suppresses it. [Massive Activations](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17762) finds near-constant bias use and replacement by explicit K/V bias slots without losing the reported language-model quality. Neither says all sinks have identical function. |
| Positional seed and super-neuron amplification | [Structural Origin](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06611) derives a causal-mask value-variance disparity, demonstrates sink relocation through variance/mask interventions, and links output projection, FFN super neurons and Q/K dimensional disparity. These interventions establish forward sufficiency in examined settings, not a universal training order; changing the mask also changes the computation graph. |
| **Training-time coupled loop itself** | [Active-Dormant Attention Heads](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.13835) analyzes attention-sink/value-drain mutual reinforcement in a toy Bigram-Backcopy Transformer, with a stable phase; in deeper toy models residual peaks and Adam participate, while its OLMo checkpoint study reports analogous dynamics. Its theoretical derivation is toy/task-scoped, but it is direct prior art for the claimed feedback organization. In the toy setting SGD removes residual peaks while sinks can remain, so a massive peak is not required for sink existence. |
| Gradient concentration and normalization gain | [Attention Sinks Induce Gradient Sinks](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17771) identifies the ordinary value-path transpose: if Y=AV then the value gradient is A-transpose times the output gradient; an attended token receives many query contributions. It derives the RMSNorm inverse-RMS Jacobian scaling and observes sink persistence when massive activations are reduced. This supports a backward mediator, not a unique cause of first emergence. |
| Layer-specific massive direction and downstream coupling | [A Single Layer to Explain Them All](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.08504) identifies an emergence layer where RMSNorm/FFN create a massive feature and residual propagation carries it forward. [Attention Sinks and Compression Valleys](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.06477) connects a dominant residual direction to spectral compression and co-onset with sinks. These are primarily within-model localization and downstream effects, not a prospectively identified new rule. |
| Architectural interventions | [Gated Attention](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.06708) reports that SDPA-output gating suppresses both sink and massive activation, whereas value gating suppresses the massive peak more than the sink. [Trigger-Conditional Softmax Sinks](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11487) proves a sink/no-op necessity in a specified softmax task/model and contrasts ReLU attention; its necessity result is not universal. |

### Strongest ordinary loop; reconciliation of apparently competing explanations

**Within a forward pass across layers:** the first causal position has a distinctive aggregation variance. Softmax must distribute mass, and a key with little useful value can serve as a no-op destination. Q/K learning and positional asymmetry can select that destination. An FFN can make a particular normalized direction unusually large in the residual stream; residual addition carries it to later layers, where its normalized *direction* can influence Q/K routing. Raw norm alone is not sufficient in a pre-norm model because RMSNorm rescales it. Subsequent output-projection and FFN effects can reinforce the chosen direction. [Structural Origin](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06611), [Massive Activations](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17762), [Single Layer](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.08504).

**Across optimizer steps:** a sink gathers backward value-path contributions from many queries by A-transpose multiplication. Gradient descent can therefore reinforce the features and Q/K alignment that maintain routing. A large residual RMS suppresses the normalized branch's local backward gain while the residual identity path still carries gradient. An implicit attention bias/no-op capacity makes the state useful enough to retain. The training loop is ordinary feedback through an existing Transformer graph, not a separate credit-flow channel. The older [Active-Dormant](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.13835) paper already treats sink/value-drain coupling as mutual reinforcement; [Gradient Sinks](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17771) adds an explicit backward/gain account. The complete chain is a plausible joint explanation, **not** a universally proven causal sequence for all models.

Thus A (forward variance or an early massive feature promotes later sink), B (sink concentrates later training gradients), C (softmax no-op pressure), D (implicit bias storage), and E (normalization-mediated branch gain) can be different stages or functions of one loop. Forward variance can seed sink formation while backward pressure subsequently grows/retains an outlier. Sinks persist after massive activations are reduced in value-scaling, value-gating and optimizer interventions because their softmax/no-op and Q/K incentives remain. Residual persistence and RMSNorm explain the outlier's durability and gain effects without positing a new state type. Evidence for each link is not evidence that one ordering is exclusive or universal.

### Architecture-discovery relevance

The remaining academic questions are quantitative selection: which token, residual direction and onset layer in a particular architecture/data/optimizer setting; how much of the selection is driven by mask variance versus gradient reinforcement; and whether the RMSNorm gain effect is adaptive regulation or a consequential side effect. [Hidden Dynamics of Massive Activations](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.03616) models training-checkpoint trajectories but reports harder timing/onset prediction than steady-state magnitude. A complete prospective theory would be valuable, yet all observed state, transitions and credit paths remain standard attention, residual/FFN, normalization and gradient descent. There is presently no precise architecture-level property that an ordinary Transformer decomposition fails to preserve. This closes the anomaly as **architecture-discovery evidence**, not as a topic of Transformer science.

### Proposed causal discriminator is not orthogonal

1. **Forward-only variance equalization.** Head-wise RMSNorm changes forward activations, backward Jacobians and conditioning; learned scales may add parameters. A causal-mask change also changes receptive fields. A fixed-checkpoint activation patch can isolate an immediate forward effect but cannot serve as an unchanged training intervention. Match variance, direction and norm separately; [Structural Origin](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06611) reports variance amplification succeeding where norm amplification did not.
2. **Backward-only sink-gradient attenuation.** The published [V-scale](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17771) rescales forward values using an added learned parameter, so it changes the value function, capacity and backward path; same-layer Q/K attention weights being unchanged is insufficient. A genuinely forward-identical custom backward Jacobian change would still alter effective learning rates on selected paths; compare global-gradient-norm-matched and non-sink-token controls, with token/head preselected rather than chosen after observing results.
3. **Explicit no-op/bias capacity.** A learned K/V slot changes parameter count, attention denominator, forward function class and optimization. A fixed key/zero-value slot avoids extra learned parameters but still changes softmax normalization and reachable functions. It cannot be crossed as an independent factor with unchanged capacity and forward behavior.

**Smallest cleaner academic discriminator, if ever authorized:** at a single fixed initialization and predeclared sink position/head, compare forward-identical selective value-path Jacobian attenuation against equal-norm global and non-sink-path attenuation; verify exact equality of forward outputs before any update, then compare sink persistence and later outlier growth under matched seeds, update counts and gradient scale. Separately use fixed-checkpoint activation patches to test immediate variance/direction-induced relocation. Do not claim the no-op slot as a clean third orthogonal factor. **Do not run this for the project now**: the ordinary-loop collision already removes the architecture-discovery rationale.

### Final disposition

**KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS.** The strongest alleged coupling is already instantiated by a known Transformer attention/residual/normalization/gradient circuit, with direct training-loop prior art. The unresolved universal selection/onset theory is descriptive and model-dependent; it does not imply a missing primitive or native architecture. Next no-compute hostile audit: **HYDRA / SELF-REPAIR**, the independent remaining anomaly. Do not stop anomaly-first research on the basis of this one closure, and do not train on this target.

## AR-149 — Transformer Hydra / self-repair: hostile no-compute audit

**Scope and verdict (2026-09-28): KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS.** The observed response to an inference-time ablation is real, including downstream components that change their output in a compensating direction. The direct prior art traces those changes through the ordinary Transformer compute graph. Neither passive rescaling alone nor independent static redundancy alone explains every case; their combination with input-conditioned downstream heads/MLPs does. This closes the anomaly as an architecture-discovery lead, without claiming universal quantitative prediction of each ablation response. No code, training, benchmarking, GPU or experiment.

### Strongest combined ordinary decomposition

For a residual network, the final state contains the input and the sum of component writes. Ablating an upstream write changes (1) the direct residual contribution, (2) every downstream component whose input reads that changed residual state, and (3) the final LayerNorm/RMSNorm denominator and, for LayerNorm, centering. A downstream head can change its query/key logits and thus its *own* softmax distribution; a downstream MLP can cross a nonlinear activation boundary; a suppressor of the original write can suppress less. Parallel and later heads may encode overlapping task information, while residual paths retain the input needed for a later head to perform the same partial task. Overparameterization supplies many such paths. These effects can add or cancel on a prompt-specific output direction. [Hydra](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.15771), [Explorations of Self-Repair](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.15390), [Copy Suppression](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.04625).

The magnitude classes need no additional operation: if the compensating logit change is smaller than the removed direct contribution, there is under-repair; if similar, near-complete repair; if greater, over-repair. The terms depend on the prompt's representation, head attention logits, MLP activation regions, and normalization denominator, giving prompt/component dependence. This is an **explanatory decomposition and inference**, not a fitted predictor for every head/prompt. Importantly, attention heads have independent softmaxes: ablating one head's *output* does not automatically reallocate probability across sibling heads. Redistribution requires a changed input to a later head (or an intervention inside the same head's logits). Calling every later response “passive softmax redistribution” would falsely erase genuine conditional computation.

### Primary prior-art collisions and limits

| Mechanism or evidence | Primary result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Original Hydra | [McGrath et al., *The Hydra Effect*](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.15771) show an ablated attention layer in Chinchilla 7B can increase a later layer's effect, with late MLP erasure decreasing. In their middle-layer factual-recall setting these compensate about 70% of the direct logit loss. Their model was trained without dropout, so dropout-specific failure training is unnecessary; the result does **not** prove a universal origin or a dedicated repair module. Their causal formalism separates direct, indirect and total effects. |
| Imperfect/over-repair, normalization, anti-erasure | [Rushing and Nanda, *Explorations*](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.15390) find noisy, prompt-dependent incomplete and occasional overcompensation across model families and pretraining-distribution prompts. Their clipped ratio suggests final normalization can account for substantial repair, around 30% of a head's direct effect in many settings, but is **not** an additive universal share of all repair. Sparse MLP neurons reduce their negative erasure after upstream ablation. They explicitly warn that internal ablation can be off-distribution. |
| Backup and suppressor paths | [Wang et al., IOI circuit](https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00593) document backup name movers and negative heads; the narrow IOI margin after main name-mover knockout falls only about 5%. [McDougall et al., *Copy Suppression*](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.04625) find negative heads account for 39% of self-repair in that setting and show Q-composition makes backup heads attend *more* to the needed name while suppressors attend *less*. The backup response uses information beyond the output-token unembedding direction, yet still follows ordinary residual-to-Q/K-to-OV paths. |
| 2026 conditional evidence | [Gong et al., *Conditional Co-Ablation*](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01940) recover documented IOI backups from primary-conditioned ablations and validate their causal contribution. Holding clean LayerNorm statistics fixed improves backup detection, with documented backups retaining roughly 80% of conditional growth. Geometry-matched wrong primary sets do not expose the same backups. Thus the response is more than passive normalization or generic perturbation magnitude. Its conditional query is a method for finding an existing circuit, not evidence of an extra architecture-level channel. The paper's intact-state non-identifiability result applies to its specified intact-state score class, not to a hypothetical full weights-and-input analysis. |
| Redundant paths and refinement | [Veit et al., residual ensembles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06431) show modest degradation under path/layer lesions in ResNets; [Jastrzębski et al., iterative inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.04773) study layerwise residual refinement; [Michel et al., head pruning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10650) find many trained Transformer heads removable with little test loss. These establish capacity for redundancy/refinement, but by themselves do not derive Hydra's head-specific compensation. The IOI and conditional-ablation work supplies that narrower circuit evidence. |

### Passive algebra versus active conditional response

**Passive:** final normalization rescales remaining residual terms; a removed positive write can also remove a learned negative downstream contribution (“anti-erasure”); multiple correlated writes preserve output information. Softmax changes are automatic *within a downstream head when its logits change*, not a global head-to-head renormalization. These paths can make a direct-effect estimate differ strongly from the total effect.

**Active in the descriptive causal sense:** backup heads and MLPs do change their computations conditional on the altered residual input. The normalization-frozen and matched-wrong-primary controls in the [2026 study](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01940) rule out an account based only on passive scaling or undifferentiated damage. In IOI, [copy-suppression analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.04625) traces this conditioning to the main heads' residual write changing downstream Q/K selection, then familiar OV copying or suppressing. “Active” therefore means ordinary learned conditional computation on a changed hidden state. No model detects a component failure, rewrites parameters, enters a distinct repair mode, or opens a new credit-flow pathway at inference time.

### Training-time origin and prediction boundary

The dropout-free [Hydra model](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.15771) rules out a **necessary** dropout-training explanation. It does not rule out a conservative account: gradient descent on a large residual model can learn overlapping features, repeated refinement, negative corrections and task-conditioned heads because all improve ordinary likelihood on intact examples. Ablation then leaves task cues in the residual stream while removing a partial answer or suppression cue; later circuits respond according to their already learned functions. [Rushing and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.15390) explicitly present iterative inference as a speculative explanation, not a demonstrated universal training cause. The 2017 residual iterative-inference analysis and 2016 residual-path lesion study make the account plausible, not a guarantee that every trained network repairs.

Existing work can conditionally identify specific backups once the primary set and relevant task are specified: the [IOI circuit](https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00593) and [conditional co-ablation](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01940) are concrete examples. There is still no general *prospective, intervention-free* formula that accurately predicts the compensator, repair magnitude and under/over-repair across all heads, prompts and models. That is an incomplete mechanistic model of a distributed network. It is not evidence for a missing architectural principle unless a precise residual phenomenon survives the complete known-path decomposition and shows new state/transition or credit organization; none is currently specified.

### Discriminator audit: proposed freezes and co-ablation

The proposed test does **not** independently separate all passive algebra from active conditional computation:

1. Freezing **final** normalization at clean statistics removes one readout-scaling channel. Freezing **all** intermediate normalization statistics changes the downstream computation under ablation and may change attention/MLP responses themselves. In LayerNorm, centering and scale must be specified separately; RMSNorm has no centering. The [2026 conditional study](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01940) already shows backup growth persists after clean-statistic freezing, so that particular passive-only explanation is falsified.
2. Freezing a downstream attention *distribution* removes its Q/K response, a principal ordinary conditional route. It still leaves changed values and MLP inputs; freezing all distributions changes the counterfactual function and can either hide or induce apparent repair. It is not an orthogonal “passive” control, and sibling heads never share a single softmax to freeze.
3. Co-ablating predicted backup/suppressor components establishes conditional causal load-bearingness, but non-additive final normalization, nonlinear interactions, off-distribution state changes and newly recruited tertiary components affect the joint result. The interaction is not a unique amount of “active repair.” Preselect backups on separate prompts and distinguish restoring the backup's clean *output* from severing only the primary-to-backup read path.

**Smallest cleaner conceptual discriminator, not to execute:** for a predeclared primary and downstream head on the same clean/ablated prompt pair, hold only the final readout normalization scale fixed and perform path-specific replay of the primary's residual message into that head's Q/K input while keeping its V input and all other downstream inputs on the ablated run; then swap the V path separately. Measure both the head's attention/output change and the final fixed-readout logit contribution, with a matched irrelevant edge and a resample-ablation donor from the same distribution. A downstream MLP requires analogous input-edge replay. This distinguishes specific Q/K, V and MLP conditioning from final readout rescaling, while still being an artificial counterfactual subject to interaction and off-distribution caveats. It **cannot by itself establish why training produced the circuit** or prove a dedicated repair mechanism. Existing IOI work already performs a close variant, so the project has no reason to run it now.

### Final disposition

**KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS.** Genuine downstream compensation exists, but its observed information flow is standard residual state → downstream normalization/Q/K/OV or MLP → final residual/readout. The absence of an exact universal predictor leaves interpretability work, not an architecture candidate. Next audit the final independent anomaly, **CONTINUAL PLASTICITY COLLAPSE**, with literature and reasoning only; do not end anomaly-first research before that audit.

## AR-150 — Continual plasticity collapse: final hostile no-compute anomaly audit

**Verdict (2026-09-28): KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS. ANOMALY-FIRST PHASE COMPLETE — 0 SURVIVORS.** Plasticity loss is empirically real, and neither dead units nor any other single scalar proxy universally explains it. The best combined account is ordinary nonstationary optimization acting through the trained parameter state, optimizer state, signal propagation and task-aligned tangent/curvature geometry. No evidence requires a new persistent state type or update channel. This is a project novelty verdict, not a claim of a complete universal theory of all plasticity failures. Literature and formal reasoning only; no code, experiment, training, benchmark or GPU.

### What is measured

- **Forgetting (A):** old-task performance falls after new-task training. It can occur while the model learns the current task perfectly and is not the target.
- **Current-task plasticity loss (B):** under the same new-task distribution, optimizer, schedule, data and fixed update budget, a previously trained checkpoint achieves worse current-task learning than a fresh same-architecture model, preferably on *training* loss as well as held-out performance. This is the target. [Dohare et al., Continual ImageNet](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07711-7) construct repeated binary tasks of comparable difficulty; [Lyle et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf) explicitly compare later-task fitting against a random initialization.
- **Slow optimization (C):** a shallower current-task learning-curve slope within the budget is one route to B, not synonymous with a worse achievable optimum. Lyle et al. find slower progress rather than an early high-loss plateau in one controlled RL-derived setting.
- **Representation collapse (D):** correlated or low-rank activations may cause or accompany B but are neither the definition nor a universal predictor.
- **Loss of gradient-responsive directions (E):** degraded Jacobian/empirical NTK or task-relevant curvature is a closer mechanistic description of *finite-budget* B. It is input-, task-, metric-, optimizer- and parameterization-dependent; rank alone is not a full prediction.

### Primary collision library and causal status

| Proposed cause | Best evidence; causal status and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Dead, saturated, dormant units | [Dohare et al. 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07711-7) track increasing constant units, weight magnitude and declining representation rank; continual backpropagation restores learning by replacing low-utility units. [Sokar et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/sokar23a.html) recycle dormant RL neurons (ReDo) and improve performance. This makes dormancy a **cause or partial mediator in those settings**, not a universal necessity: [Lyle et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf) find plasticity loss without saturation, and [Lewandowski et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.00246) show leaky-ReLU can lose plasticity with high maintained feature rank. [Kong and Sutton 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.01475) report a growing network retaining plasticity despite rising dead-unit proportion. |
| Preactivation shift and effectively linear (“zombie”) units | [Lyle et al., *Disentangling*](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18762) show abrupt task changes and stale Adam state can shift preactivations, kill ReLUs or leave units nearly linear while still passing gradients. This is a **causal route**, and shows responsiveness alone is insufficient. Layer normalization mitigates some shifts; the paper combines it with weight decay because one route alone does not close all cases. |
| Weight growth / norm | Weight decay and Shrink-and-Perturb help in [Dohare et al.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07711-7); [Lyle et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18762) identify weight growth as a separate route to sharp/unstable optimization. But [Lyle et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf) show norm–plasticity correlations reversing across environments; [Lewandowski et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.00246) report rising weight norm without loss in an identity-activation control and a plateau with loss in ReLU. **Partial mediator; norm matching alone is not a universal rescue or causal isolation.** |
| Duplicated/cloned features and representation rank | Low effective feature rank is observed in [Dohare et al.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07711-7), and deliberate fresh-feature injection restores some diversity. But [Lyle et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf) reverse rank correlations across tasks; [Lewandowski et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.00246) exhibit maintained high feature rank with continued loss. Exact duplicate units would reduce distinct local feature directions, an ordinary symmetry/parameter degeneracy. **Possible route and correlate, not a sufficient statistic.** |
| Frozen- and cloned-unit update manifolds | [Joudaki et al. 2026, Theorem 2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00304) directly formalize the putative persistent trainability restriction: under exact saturation or specified forward/backward clone symmetries, gradients remain tangent to lower-dimensional parameter manifolds, so ordinary GD/SGD cannot restore the missing update directions; dropout or gradient noise can break clone symmetry in their experiments. Their result is conditional on exact frozen/clone structure and does **not** prove every empirical plasticity decline lies on such a manifold; their paper separately treats near-manifold stability. The older network-singularity literature they cite already identified duplication/elimination plateaus. This is **direct same-mechanism prior art**, not a new state semantics. |
| Hessian, GGN, NTK and task-aligned gradient subspace | [Lewandowski et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.00246) find curvature-direction loss more consistent than dormant/norm/rank proxies and preserve directions with regularization. [Prakash et al. 2025/26](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.22335) find spectral collapse *before* a later task's learning failure, derive a finite-step contraction condition in a **linearized/frozen-gate ReLU model**, and relate its loss-weighted Gram matrix to generalized Gauss–Newton curvature. [Wu et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01913) add RL-specific gradient-magnitude decay from replay/nonstationarity. These are **mechanistic mediators and predictors within scope**. Empirical spectral co-movement, a scoped linear proof and a regularizer's success do not prove a universal causal master variable; the full Hessian also contains loss and residual terms, and different targets can align differently to the same kernel eigenspaces. |
| Old-task basin / optimizer history | [Lyle et al. 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf) show slower new-task optimization rather than plateauing at a bad local optimum in their examined setting; an “old basin trap” is thus **not generally established**. [Lyle et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18762) show stale Adam moments can trigger an abrupt harmful update and unit death after task switch: optimizer state is a **causal factor in that construction**. Resetting optimizer state does not repair dead/duplicated features or guarantee recovery elsewhere. |
| Abrupt shift versus gradual change | [Liu and Mou 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.09234) show output interpolation or task-mixture transitions largely mitigate plasticity loss in their studied streams, with residual loss in at least one case; their theorem assumes smoothness/local strong convexity. The interventions change intermediate data, labels, available examples and number/placement of optimization opportunities, so they do not isolate transition continuity alone or refute the abrupt-switch benchmark. **Environmental/optimization amplifier, not a universal artifact diagnosis.** |
| Known repair methods | [Plasticity Injection](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.15555) changes trainable directions while keeping predictions and trainable parameter count at the intervention; [ReDo](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/sokar23a.html), [continual backpropagation](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07711-7), [regenerative regularization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11958), normalization + weight decay [Lyle et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18762), and near-isometry methods [Rosseau et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09762) restore known gradient paths/conditioning to differing degrees. These are existing architectures, rules, losses or optimizers; mitigation alone cannot establish a missing primitive. |

### Strongest ordinary combined account

The task stream changes labels, inputs, targets or bootstrap targets. Prior gradient updates and optimizer moments place parameters in a different region from initialization. Abrupt switches can make stale moment estimates mis-scaled and move preactivations sharply. Some units die or saturate; others become nearly linear, and feature vectors may duplicate. Exact frozen/clone configurations can make lost update directions invariant under gradient steps, as [Joudaki et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00304) show under their stated assumptions. Weight growth and normalization choices change update scale and curvature. On the *new task's inputs*, these changes alter the Jacobian of outputs with respect to parameters, the optimizer's effective metric, the empirical NTK and the Hessian/GGN. A new target error with projection into weak tangent directions will then contract slowly within the fixed budget. This explains why fresh networks can learn later tasks faster, why fresh units/resetting can help, why normalization plus weight control is stronger than a single treatment, why first-layer renewal can propagate benefit by restoring upstream features, and why gradual transition can reduce destructive jumps. This is an **integrated causal interpretation** supported in pieces by the sources above, not a universal proven chain for every network.

The [first-layer replacement study](https://repository.tudelft.nl/file/File_f73ff6fe-dd51-49fe-b5e3-532099bda692) reports that first-layer-only continual backpropagation nearly matches all-layer replacement in its setting and associates this with stabilizing layerwise weight magnitudes. It is a narrower student thesis result, not evidence that first-layer reset is sufficient across architectures/tasks. Ordinary forward/backward signal propagation already makes an upstream bottleneck capable of limiting every later layer.

### Same present function, different future trainability: a no-compute counterexample

Consider one ReLU hidden unit with output `f(x)=v ReLU(wx+b)` on any input domain. Both parameter states `w=0, v=0, b=-1` and `w=0, v=0, b=+1` realize exactly the same present function `f(x)=0` on **all** inputs. They have the same architecture, parameter count, Euclidean weight norm and a freshly zeroed optimizer state. On a new constant nonzero target, the first state has zero output and hidden-parameter gradients, so ordinary gradient descent stays at zero; the second has `∂f/∂v=1` and can learn immediately. Nothing novel is hidden: the difference is the ReLU activation gate and tangent Jacobian at two parameter states. The example proves that present input-output equivalence does **not** determine future trainability, while also killing the inference that this fact by itself implies a distinct architectural “trainability state.” The parameter state, activation derivatives, optimizer moments and task data already supply the complete conventional state for the update rule.

For squared error in a locally linearized network, write the new-task residual vector as `r` and its output Jacobian as `J`; under plain gradient descent the next residual is approximately `(I - η J Jᵀ) r`. After K steps an eigendirection with eigenvalue λ contracts by `(1 - ηλ)^K` in the fixed-J regime. Thus the *alignment* of the new error with the fast eigenspace, the optimizer metric and the finite budget matter, not just total representation or Hessian rank. [Prakash et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.22335) formalize a scoped version. Beyond linearization, curvature and changing gates also matter; this formula is an explanatory local model, not a universal exact predictor.

### Architecture-sensitivity and proposed discriminator

Primary studies compare CNNs, MLPs, residual nets and RL agents and show that architecture/activation/normalization choices change susceptibility; they do **not** furnish the much stronger matched comparison of two different native organizations at the same present function, optimizer, trainable parameter budget, data/target path, compute and task-aligned tangent geometry. The no-compute counterexample already shows why holding only the current function fixed is insufficient. A generic architecture sensitivity to conditioning is an existing learning-dynamics property, not evidence of a new organization. The [near-isometry work](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09762) offers existing architectural/regularization remedies and explicitly notes its regularizer does not guarantee isometry under strongly saturating gates; it is not an unexplained residual here.

Perplexity's proposed four-way functionally matched comparison cannot cleanly vary saturation, duplicate structure and tangent rank independently: these often *determine* the local Jacobian and each other. Matching outputs on a finite sample does not match the function on the next task's support. Reparameterizations can preserve the function while changing Euclidean gradient dynamics and norm without adding a state type. Matching Hessian rank alone ignores eigenscale, target-error alignment, indefinite/full-Hessian terms and learning-rate stability. Keeping Adam moments versus resetting them changes the optimizer; interpolating tasks changes the intermediate objective/data and update opportunities. Clone/duplicate manipulations may change effective width and implicit learning rate even with the same nominal parameter count. Any observed difference after loose matching therefore remains ambiguous.

**Cleaner no-compute discriminator:** the exact ReLU pair above already separates current function from future learning while holding optimizer state, norm and capacity fixed, and reduces the effect to ordinary activation/tangent geometry. For the broader scientific issue, the existing [Lyle 2023 falsification study](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/lyle23b/lyle23b.pdf), [Lyle 2024 multi-cause interventions](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18762), and [Prakash spectral analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.22335) already reject universal single proxies and locate finite-budget failure within established optimization quantities. No new training comparison is needed for this project's architecture-discovery decision.

### Final classification and phase decision

**KILLED — ORDINARY KNOWN DYNAMICS.** This does not mean all future-learnability outcomes can yet be predicted prospectively from a small diagnostic panel. A narrow unresolved scientific question is whether task-aligned tangent spectrum, optimizer state and higher-order gate transitions together predict finite-budget new-task loss across architectures without hidden task-specific fitting. That question concerns ordinary gradient-learning theory and carries no present architecture-candidate status. **Recommendation A: stop anomaly-first research** rather than opening another broad survey or experiment on this anomaly. The other two retained anomalies were closed in AR-148 and AR-149. **ANOMALY-FIRST PHASE COMPLETE — 0 SURVIVORS.**

Width **2**; input dimension **2** in every case. Dense layer:

Float64 SVD is diagnostic only. 80-decimal mpmath produces an approximate inverse

floor/ceiling arithmetic, rigorous exponential Taylor remainder, and the analytic
mixed derivative chain rule. Exact rational parameters/inputs are enclosed.

For the selected square minor Jm and stored rational dyadic M, a verified bound
`||I-M Jm||_infinity < 1` implies invertibility by the Neumann series. Thus that
specific determinant is **nonzero**, without relying on a rounded determinant.
`verify.py` regenerates the entire interval Jacobian and independently calculates
the residual inequality using exact Python Fraction sums. This is a reproducible
computer-assisted certificate; no external cross-lane replication is claimed.

## Query duality and exact packing

Each full n-by-P output functional satisfies the exact rational identity
L_i=C_tilde B_i. The regenerated coefficient matrices are stored in the
consistency records. The norm bound yields

`D_C(S1,S2) >= max_i mu_i |Delta Psi_i|`

for arbitrary full sensitivity differences, including unselected residual
coordinates. Invertible W realizes the allowed gate vectors; their interval
containment is checked. Direct future injection cancels because the histories
have exactly the same h. No residual-coordinate vanishing is assumed.

Using the frozen rational mu and rho, `delta_i=17 epsilon/(8 mu_i)` and
`N_i=floor(2 rho_i/delta_i)+1` give 2 positions on each axis. For every one of
the six distinct Cartesian pairs the certified query-distance lower bound
is **17/8000 = 0.002125 > 2 epsilon = 0.002**. Four deterministic memory
states and therefore at least 2 bits follow in the declared local model.

on this actual witness (normal-normal, normal-tangent, tangent-tangent)
lie below the regenerated complete-box majorants. These supporting checks

## AR-164 — Robust-witness search and frozen joint certification

# Robust-witness search

## Classification and direct answer

**ROBUST-WITNESS SEARCH FINDS ONLY SMALL IMPROVEMENT**

At epsilon exactly1e-3, new dense width3 search witnesses certify3 jointly
nontrivial directions,8states,3bits versus the archived2directions,4states,2bits.
Its best untouched confirmation witness certifies only2directions,4states,2bits.
Dense width4 certifies3directions,8states,3bits in BOTH search and confirmation,
versus archived1direction,2states,1bit. These are improved sufficient lower
bounds, but still few directions compared with exact fixed-h dimensions63/144.
The frozen moderate/large criteria were not met; they were not changed.

Thus archived witnesses were not optimal for robust certification. This search
does NOT establish a large robust core or a global robust-dimension ceiling.
Filtering, chosen axes/prefixes, box grids and interval conservatism can miss
larger regions. The tested result supports only a modest local-witness gain.
Independent recurrence also improves, especially at width4, so this is not a
unique architectural benefit of dense interaction.

## Design and immutable inputs

Widths2/3/4, horizons11/22/37, frozen archived parameters, initial h=0,
the same dense and independent families. Dense P10/21/36 and exact supported

dimensions8/15/24. No parameter learning, architecture change or new width.

conventions and epsilon are unchanged. No GAS-0/server operation.

history perturbations were checked coordinatewise<=1, the existing local
patch domain. Future query preactivations remain[1/4,3/4] under the accepted
fixed-head convention; future inputs may differ from past-generator support,
exactly as in the accepted prior query family. No domain enlargement.

repair/preserved invalid campaign: **5bb034c**. Complete valid search/objective
sealed and committed **deb3a85** before confirmation. All18 histories/axes/

Stage1 emphasizes many strong fixed-h singular directions, not sigma_min.

lexicographic `(joint nontrivial packing directions, integer packing bits,

amplitudes/two profiles/two normal factors were frozen before results.
Only one selected recipe per winner is certified; no post-failure tuning.

cross-checked. Torch's existing CPU installation and all model servers were

## AR-165 — Robust-certificate tightness / true-dimension gap

# Robust-certificate tightness / true-dimension gap

## Classification and architecture gate

**CERTIFICATES ARE HIGHLY CONSERVATIVE — MANY MORE ROBUST DIRECTIONS APPEAR NUMERICALLY**

**MORE ROBUST-DIMENSION WORK NEEDED.** The tested machinery misses substantial
finite-error separation. However, a large binary grid is not a proof of an
equally large intrinsic continuous robust dimension, and no useful tight upper
bound was found. No architecture, learning experiment, or AMS is justified here.

## Procedural cleanup and freeze

Documentation-only cleanup commit **1e17cb8** precedes the new experiment.
ROBUST_WITNESS_SEARCH_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_20261001.md records both readings of the
ambiguous Moderate sentence. The historical Small label remains for provenance;
dense width 4 satisfies the less-strict width-local Moderate reading. All 144
expensive search finalists were SPSA descendants concentrated in few tracks;
the 10,000-history pools did not receive uniform expensive primary evaluation.
Winner/runner-up agreement within a track is weak evidence of independence.

Protocol, eight fixed endpoints, code and development tests frozen at **a218388**.
Implementation of declared CPU/raw checks: **7009d6d**. Same-product finer-grid
supplement declared before its measurement: **b081224**. Structural query and
precision diagnostic derivations: **cbe9b0d**. No old output is modified. The
source result remains 7cb9f3d. Frozen input/code hashes are in FROZEN_SETUP.json.

## Models, domain, epsilon and levels

Dense and independent recurrence at widths 3/4 and horizons 22/37, each with its
archived and frozen best-confirmation center. Same parameters, initial h=0,
parameter counts (dense 21/36; independent 15/24), input SD sqrt(3/32),
parameter-group RMS, normalized q=ones/sqrt(n), beta=max(1,||R||F), and future
preactivations [1/4,3/4]^n. **Primary epsilon = 1e-3** is a research diagnostic.
No secondary epsilon was used; the primary result is sealed in PRIMARY_FROZEN.json.

- Level A: accepted existing interval products; separately, a newly derived
  support-aware query margin on the SAME independent boxes.
- Level B: directly solved finite numerical grids and pairwise query distances.
  Critical pairs were checked at 60/100 decimal digits on CPU.
- Level C: failures of particular grids, sampled maxima, and a very loose
  rigorous covering upper bound. Numerical failure is not impossibility.

The larger-domain analysis uses fixed centers, normal correction coordinates
within [-1,1], tangent half-amplitudes 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, and raw history
coordinates within +/-1 of each frozen center. These are local perturbations,
not new central witness searches. The finest successful grids used amplitude 1,
4--8 times the old tangent amplitude. This increase MUST NOT be counted entirely
as proof slack. A separate experiment uses only the EXACT old projection boxes.

## Certified versus numerical comparisons

The large-grid column gives binary-grid coordinates / states / bits. The

## Same-box query bias: a rigorous improvement for the control

The actual permitted-query supremum is computed over all 2^n gate-box vertices,
by convexity of the vector norm. This is the SAME allowed future family; the
old certificate used an interior finite frame only as a lower-bound device.
In independent recurrence, each parameter column is supported in one state row.
The query norm becomes a weighted Euclidean norm on the supported coordinates.
The all-equal permitted 7/8 gate supplies a stronger joint dual inequality.
INDEPENDENT_QUERY_SLACK.md derives it; 256-bit outward intervals and rational
packing arithmetic verify the following new lower calculations without changing
old rho, axes, boxes, epsilon or results:

| Independent endpoint | Historical states | New support-aware lower states | New log2(states) | Margin gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| independent_n3_archived | 2 | 7 | 2.807355 | 4.618--4.618 |
| independent_n3_confirmation | 2 | 9 | 3.169925 | 4.604--4.604 |
| independent_n4_archived | 1 | 4 | 2.000000 | 5.485--5.485 |
| independent_n4_confirmation | 6 | 84 | 6.392317 | 5.126--5.394 |

In particular independent width-4 confirmation improves rigorously from 6 to
84 states, or log2(84) = 6.392317 bits (at least seven fixed-width binary bits).
Its numerical greedy same-box packing found 67 states; this is entirely
consistent because that search was not a maximum. The old dense 3-bit versus
independent 2.585-bit comparison cannot support a dense advantage.

The support-aware inequality includes every LEGALLY SUPPORTED residual
sensitivity coordinate; it excludes only mathematically impossible off-owner
entries. This new short derivation needs independent review, unlike the already
accepted old product geometry. No unrestricted dense claim is inferred.

   tested through 12. Remaining exact coordinates are explicitly untested.
J. Interval precision: increasing 192 to 256 bits gives identical binary64

K. Basis coding, finite sampling, greedy choices and state cap can affect
   estimates. Components interact, so no factorial causal decomposition is claimed.

Dense width-4 confirmation's fourth through twelfth candidate directions were

## AR-166 — Support-aware robust continuous dimension

# Support-aware robust dimension certification

## Classification and architecture gate

**MODERATE ROBUST CONTINUOUS DIMENSION CERTIFIED**

**MORE ROBUST-DIMENSION WORK NEEDED.** Maximum achieved epsilon-essential continuous
lower certificate is four. No useful ambient upper bound or uniform compression
structure is established; no architecture design follows.

## Contract, endpoints and provenance

Primary epsilon exactly **1e-3**, unchanged normalized gradient/query units:
input SD sqrt(3/32), frozen R/W/b RMS parameter scales, q=ones/sqrt(n),
beta=max(1,||R||F), future preactivation box [1/4,3/4]^n. Eight unchanged
dense/independent archived and confirmation histories, n3/T22 and n4/T37.
Parameters P_dense=21/36, P_independent=15/24 are explicitly different.
No history, model, architecture, width or error-contract search.

Preregis/code/chart freeze **f0c231e**, before official intervals. Already
preregistered numerical diagnostic implementation **1dbcdb6**. Source checkpoint
915d007, accepted support-aware result supplied by the owner as independently
audited. New dimension conversion is not a re-review of that result.

## What continuous robust dimension means

For a unique continuous curved lift of projection coordinates z in [-1,1]^r,
prove on the ENTIRE simultaneous section

    max_i b_i |z_i-z'_i| <= D_C(S(z),S(z')) <= M ||z-z'||_2,
    m=min_i(b_i)/sqrt(r) > 0, and every retained b_i > epsilon.

Thus every sufficiently separated pair is query-distinguishable. Opposite
points on the cube boundary have distance >2epsilon. Borsuk-Ulam then excludes
a continuous no-replay encoder in fewer than r real coordinates answering
every allowed query to epsilon. This finite-radius criterion is stronger than
positive midpoint rank, and is separate from discrete bits/states. The
anisotropic cube boundary avoids an unnecessary inscribed-ball sqrt(r) loss
in the antipodal test, while the displayed Euclidean m honestly retains it.
PROOF.md gives the full argument, inverse accounting and computational scope.

## Model-specific query geometry

Independent: exact full query distance is the weighted Euclidean norm of all
legally supported owner coordinates, with weights sech^2(1/4)R_ii/(sqrt(n)beta).
Certification uses the near-optimal permitted rational7/8-gate lower norm and
its reviewed dual margins. Every supported residual coordinate remains.

Dense: use the entire permitted gate-box vertex maximum numerically. The
strongest accepted certified finite-frame projection dual used here remains
valid for arbitrary full-tensor residuals. It is a lower certificate, not the
exact dense norm. No independent-only zero restriction is imposed on dense.
Both models keep the same future family and physical epsilon.

## Upper bounds and comparison

**NO USEFUL ROBUST-DIMENSION UPPER BOUND FOUND.** On a chosen r-subsection,
the whole-section bi-Lipschitz map fixes its intrinsic dimension to r and
supplies a section-specific entropy cover. It excludes all OTHER reachable
directions and is therefore not a global robust-dimension upper bound.
Structural ambient upper counts remain63/144 dense and15/24 independent.
No uniform low-rank tail/truncation estimate justifies a smaller ambient ceiling.

Independent exact support does not eliminate the observed robust credit state:
it admits moderate r4 at one fixed endpoint. Dense strongest achieved r3.
These are unequal lower certificates, not true maxima or capability/superiority
comparisons. Exact full dimension remains much larger than certified robust r.
